SO when we contemplate the visible world with its essence and the life of the Creatures, we find therein the likeness of the invisible Spiritual World, which lies hidden in the visible World: just as the soul in the Body; and by the same we see that the hidden God is near to all, and through all, and yet entirely hidden from the visible being.

2. We have an example in the mind <note>original: "gemoed," a term Böhme uses to describe the inner seat of human will, thought, and emotion.</note> of man, which is an invisible fire, that is inclined toward Light and darkness, that is, toward joy and sorrow, and in itself it is nevertheless neither: but it is only a cause for them, an invisible, intangible source-fire <note>original: "welvuur," meaning the wellspring or origin-fire of the soul's energy.</note>, and according to its own essence yet enclosed in nothing, but only in the will of life.

3. The Body cannot grasp the mind, but the mind grasps the Body, and leads the same in joy and sorrow; so too it is to be understood of the word and the power of God, which is hidden from the visible sensible <note>original: "bevindelijke," referring to things that can be experienced or perceived through the senses.</note> elements, and yet dwells through and in the Elements, and works through the sensible life, and essence; just as the mind in the Body.

# CHAPTER I.
## *What the Revealed God Is, and Concerning the Trinity.*

<margin>1.</margin> <image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial Z featuring a seated figure in a landscape within a square border.</image-desc>Whenever we wish to understand the new birth—what it is and how it occurs—we must first know what man is, how he is the image of God, and what the Divine indwelling is; also, what the revealed God is, of whom man is an image:

<margin>2.</margin> Whenever I contemplate what God is, I say: He is the *One*, in contrast to the creature; namely, an eternal nothing, like no creature, and yet everything. He has neither ground, beginning, nor place; and He possesses nothing but Himself alone. He is the will of the unground <term>unground|Dutch "ongrond," often translated as "Abyss" or "Abyssal." It refers to the absolute, bottomless nature of God before any creation or manifestation—a state of pure potentiality.</term>. In Himself, He is nothing other than a single unity. He requires no space or place. From eternity into eternity, He begets Himself within Himself. He is like no thing, nor resembles any, and has no particular place where He dwells. Eternal Wisdom, or understanding, is His dwelling; He is the will of Wisdom, and Wisdom is His revelation.

<margin>3.</margin> In this eternal begetting, we are to understand three things: first, an eternal will; second, an eternal mind of the will; third, the proceeding of the will and of the mind, which is a spirit of the will and of the mind.

<margin>4.</margin> The will is the Father; the mind is the vessel of the will—that is, the seat or dwelling of the will, or the *center* <note>original: "centrum," a Latin term used here to describe the focal point of divine activity from which all things emerge.</note> toward something—and it is the heart of the will; and the proceeding of the will and of the mind is the power and the spirit.

<margin>5.</margin> This threefold spirit is a single essence; and though it is yet no essence, but rather the eternal understanding, an origin of "something," it is nonetheless the eternal mystery <note>original: "verborgentheyd," literally "hiddenness" or "secrecy."</note>. Just as the understanding of man is not graspable, nor exists in time or place, but is its own graspability and seat—and the proceeding of the Spirit is the eternal, original contemplatability, being a delight of the Spirit.

<margin>6.</margin> That which has proceeded is called the delight of the Deity, or the eternal Wisdom, which is the eternal origin of all powers, colors, and virtues, whereby the threefold spirit, in this delight, desir-

<summary>This page introduces the nature of the revealed God and the Trinity, defining God as the "Unground" and the "One" who exists beyond time and space. The author explains the Trinity as a process of eternal begetting involving Will (Father), Mind (Heart/Center), and Spirit (Power).</summary>
<keywords>Trinity, Unground, Divine Wisdom, New Birth, Image of God, Mysticism, Begetting of God</keywords>

...is manifested, namely the powers, colors, and virtues <note>original: "verwen en deugden." In this mystical context, "colors" refer to the various qualities of divine light, while "virtues" or "powers" refer to the active properties of the Godhead.</note>, and His longing is an impressing <note>In the sense of making an impression or forming a likeness.</note> and a grasping of Himself; the will grasps the wisdom in the mind, and that which is grasped in the understanding is the eternal word of all colors, powers, and virtues, which the eternal will speaks out from the understanding of the mind, through the Spirit.

7. And this same speaking is the movement, or the life of the Godhead; an eye of the eternal vision; therein one power, color, and virtue recognizes the other in distinction, yet they all stand in an equal property, without weight, limit, or measure, and are also undivided from one another; all colors, powers, and virtues lie in a single [unity], and it is a distinct, mutually harmonious, birthing Harmony <note>original: "Harmonie." This suggests a musical resonance where the different aspects of God are distinct yet perfectly unified.</note>; or as I might put it: a speaking word, wherein all languages, powers, colors, and virtues are lying within the word or the speaking, and with the sound or the speaking they develop themselves and lead into a vision or sight.

8. That is now the eye of the abyss <term>abyss|Dutch "ongrond," literally "unground" or "bottomless." It refers to the absolute, undifferentiated state of God before creation.</term>, the eternal Chaos, in which everything lies—all that is eternity and time—and it is named: counsel, power, wonder, and virtue. Its proper name is God, or *Jehovah*, or *Jehovah* <note>The text provides two spellings: "Jehova" and "Jehovah."</note>. He is beyond all nature, beyond all beginning of any kind of being, a working within Himself, a birthing and finding or experiencing of Himself, without any suffering <note>original: "quaal." In Böhmean terminology, this can mean "quality," "source-heat," or "torment/suffering," referring to the active friction of existence.</note> from anything or through anything. He has neither beginning nor end; He is immeasurable; He cannot be expressed by any number in His width nor greatness; for He is deeper than any thoughts can express. He is nowhere far from anything, nor near to anything; He is through all and in all. His birth is everywhere, and without Him there is nothing else. He is time and eternity, ground and abyss, and yet there is nothing that comprehends Him, except for true understanding; such is God Himself.

# CHAPTER II.
## Concerning the Word or the Heart of God.

<margin>1.</margin> This is now what John says in the 1st Chapter: *In the beginning was the word, and the word was with God, and God was the word, the same was in the beginning with God* <note>A translation of John 1:1.</note>: the word, (**In**) is the will of the abyss; (**beginning**) is the grasping of the will, wherein He [Himself]...

# THE 3RD CHAPTER.

### *How an evil has arisen out of the eternal good, which in the good itself had no beginning toward evil; and of the origin of the dark world, or Hell, in which the Devils dwell.*

1. Since then, in the external world, light and darkness are seen, as well as pain and affliction, yet everything arises out of the eternal **Mystery** <term>Mystery|The *Mysterium Magnum*, or the hidden, chaotic source of all possibilities from which God brings forth manifest reality.</term>—that is, out of the internal Spiritual world—and the internal Spiritual world arises out of the eternal birthing and speaking word, it now stands for us to consider how an evil has become out of the eternal good, which nevertheless had no beginning toward evil within the good: from whence darkness, pain, and affliction arise, and then from whence a brilliance or light arises within that darkness.

2. For we cannot say that the eternal light or the eternal darkness is "created," for then they would exist within time and within a contained beginning, which is not so; for they are also present in the birthing—though not in the wisdom or the birthing of the word of the **Godhead**—but they take their origin in the *desire* <note>original: "begeerte"; in this context, a magnetic, drawing force that pulls spirit into form</note> of the speaking word.

3. For in the eternally speaking word, which is beyond all nature or beginning, being solely the Divine understanding or sound, there is as yet neither darkness nor light, nor anything thick or thin, nor joy nor sorrow, nor any perceptibility or experience; but it is purely nothing other than a power of the understanding in a single quality <term>qual|A technical term (related to the German *Qual* and *Quelle*) referring to the fundamental "source-property" or "working drive" of a thing. It suggests both the source of a thing's nature and the tension or "torment" required for it to manifest.</term>, will, and dominion; there is for the same neither friend nor foe, for it is the sole good, and nothing else.

4. Since then the same eternal good cannot be an unperceivable being (for then it would not be manifest to itself), it leads itself into itself, into a delight <note>original: "lust"; a joyful inclination or pure will toward manifestation</note> toward its own contemplation or seeing what it is. In this delight stands **Wisdom** <note>Often personified as "Sophia" in mystical literature, the mirror in which God perceives his own potential.</note>; and when the delight thus sees itself—what it is—it then leads itself into a *desire* to experience what it is: namely, toward a sensation of smell, taste, colors, powers, and virtues; and no sensation could arise in the free Spiritual delight if it did not lead itself into a desire (just as if into a hunger).

This process is described as the "Verbum Fiat" or the creative Word.</meta>

5. For the nothing hungers after the something, and the hunger is the desire: namely, the first **Word Be** <note>original: "verbum fiat"</note>, or making; for the desire has nothing that it could make or grasp: it grasps only itself, and impresses itself—that is, it **coagulates** <term>coagulates|In mystical philosophy, this refers to the process of spirit or thought condensing into a more solid, perceptible form.</term> itself, it pulls itself into itself, and grasps itself, and leads itself from the **abyss** <term>abyss|The *Ungrund*, the bottomless, non-existent void before God manifests.</term> into the ground, and overshadows itself through the magnetic pulling; so that the nothing becomes full, and yet remains like a nothing. It is but a property, namely, a darkness which is the eternal origin of darkness; for where a property exists, there something already is, and that same something is not like the nothing; it gives off darkness, unless it be filled with something else—namely, a radiance—in which case it becomes light, yet in its property it remains a darkness.

6. In this **coagulation** <note>original: "coagulatie"</note>—that is, the compression or impression, desire or hunger (however I might give it to be understood)—we are now to understand two things with this **compaction** <note>original: "Compactie"</note> or drawing together: firstly, the **free longing** <note>original: "vrye lust"; refers to a divine delight or will that is not yet bound by material desire</note>, which is the wisdom, power, and virtue of the colors; and secondly, the desire of the free longing within itself. For the free longing, being the wisdom, is no property, but is free of all **inclination** <note>original: "aanneigelijkheid"; the tendency to lean toward or be affected by something</note>, and it is one with God; but the desire is a property. But now the desire arises out of the longing; therefore the desire also grasps the free longing in the compaction of the grasping, and leads it into experience and perceptibility as well.

7. And you must understand us well and rightly at this place: the desire arises out of the will toward the free longing, and leads itself out through the free longing, and into a desire; for the desire is the property of the Father, and the free longing being the wisdom, the property of the Son. Though God, who is a spirit, is not named Father or Son here in this place until the revelation through the fire into the light—there He is named Father and Son; but I set this forth for fundamental understanding, for the sake of nature’s birth, so that one may understand which Person in the **Godhead** <term>Godhead|The essential nature of God, often distinguished from the individual persons of the Trinity in mystical thought.</term> is attributed to nature, and which person is attributed to the power in nature.

### 8. *The Center of eternal nature: how the will of the abyss leads itself into nature and form.*

The desire out of the eternal will of the abyss is the first form, and it is the **Fiat** <note>original: "Fiat"; the Latin command "Let there be"</note>, or the "it created," and the power of the free longing is God, who carries the "it created," and both together are named **Word Be** <note>original: "Verbum Fiat"</note>—that is, the eternal word, which creates there where nothing is, and is the origin of nature and of all beings.

♄ **Saturn.** 9. The first property of the **desire** <note>original: "begeerte"; here refers to the first movement of the divine will to manifest itself</note> is harsh, severe, impressing, grasping itself, overshadowing itself, and it firstly creates the great darkness of the **abyss** <term>abyss|The *Ungrund*, the bottomless void before God's self-revelation.</term>; secondly, it makes itself substantial—according to spiritual nature—quite raw, hard, and firm, which is to say dense, or closed, or massive, and coarse; and it is a cause of the cold, and of all sharpness; also of all that which is called **being** <note>original: "wezen"; referring to material or essential existence</note>, and it is the beginning of **perceptibility** <term>perceptibility|original: "bevindelikheyd"; the state where the divine can be felt, found, or experienced as something distinct.</term>, in which the **free longing** <note>original: "vrye lust"; the pure, unconditioned divine will</note> finds itself and introduces itself into contemplation. Yet the desire, in itself, leads itself through this into pain and torment, but the free longing only accepts the perceptibility.

☿ **Mercury.** 10. The second form or property is the pulling-in of the desire; the same is a **sting** <note>original: "prikkel"; a sharp, stimulating impulse</note>, a stirring or moving: for every desire is pulling-in, and it is the beginning of moving, stirring, and of life, and the true origin of the **Mercurial life** <note>original: "Mercurialisghe leven"; in alchemy and mysticism, Mercury represents the principle of motion, fluidity, and communication</note>, and of the painful torment: for here arises the first enmity between the harshness, or hardness, and between the sting or movement; for the desire makes hard and firm, and shuts in just as the cold shuts in water: thus the harshness is a simple cold; and the sting, being the pulling-in, is then born through the pressing-in.

11. It is here like **Father and Son**: the Father wants to be still and hard, and the sting—that is his Son—pulls within the Father and creates unrest; the Father, being harshness, cannot tolerate this, and pulls the desire much more vehemently toward himself, in order to thus hold the disobedient Son fast and shut him in; through this, the Son only becomes stronger in the sting. And this same is the true ground and cause of the perceptibility which is in the free longing of the eternal beginning, of the moving of the powers, colors, and virtues, and of the kingdom of Divine joy: and in the dark desire, the same is the origin of enmity, pain, and torment, and the eternal origin of the **wrath of God** <note>original: "toorn Gods"</note>, and of all unrest and adversity.

♂ **Mars.** 12. The third property is the anxiety, torment, or the vexing, which the first two properties create when the sting—being the motion in the hardness, that is, in that impression—moves itself through raging and breaks the hardness; so arises, in the breaking of the hard, the first sensitivity, and that is the beginning of the **Essences** <term>Essences|original: "Essentien"; the fundamental spiritual "substances" or qualities that make up all created things.</term>; for (1) it is the **separability** <note>original: "scheydelikheid"</note>, through which, in the free longing, in the word of the powers, each power becomes feeling in itself and distinct; it is the origin of distinctness, (2) so that the powers each become manifest in themselves, as well as being the origin of the senses and the mind.

### Chapter 3. How out of the eternal good an evil has arisen.

13. For the eternal mind is the all-present power of the Godhead; yet the senses arise through nature along with the movement in the distinguishing of the powers, wherein every power finds and feels itself. It is also the origin of taste and smell; for when the perceptibility <term>perceptibility|original: "bevindelikheyd"; the state where divine forces become tangible or sensible to one another.</term> of the powers in their distinctiveness continually enters from one into the other, they then feel, taste, smell, hear, and see one another. And here arises the joy of life, which could not exist in the stillness of the power of God, in the freedom <note>original: "vryheyd"; refers to the "Ungrund" or the absolute liberty of the divine before manifestation.</note>. Therefore, the Divine understanding leads itself into spiritual properties so that it may manifest itself and be a working life.

14. But now we must consider the anguish in its birthing and its own property; for just as there is a mind in the freedom, in the word of the power of God—being an understanding—so the first will likewise leads itself into the desire, into the desire of the darkness, toward a mind. This mind is the anguish-torment <note>original: "angst-quaal"; "Angst" in Böhmean thought refers to a "narrowness" or "constriction" (from the Latin *angustus*) that characterizes the first stage of creation.</note>, being a sulfurous torment; and here it is understood as nothing other than Spirit.

15. The anguish-torment is understood as follows: the harsh <note>original: "wrange"; also meaning astringent or bitter.</note> desire grasps itself and pulls itself into itself, making itself full, hard, and raw. Thus, the pulling is an enemy of the hardness; the hardness is holding, and the pulling is fleeing; the one wants into itself, and the other wants out of itself. Yet, since they cannot yield or separate from one another, they become within each other like a turning wheel: the one wants to go up over itself, the other under itself.

16. For the hardness gives being and weight, and the sting <note>original: "prikkel"; a sharp, stimulating impulse or goad.</note> gives spirit and the fleeing life; the same turns with one another into itself and out of itself, and yet it can go nowhere. That which the desire—being the Magnet—makes hard, the pulling breaks apart again; and it is in itself the greatest unrest, like a raging madness, and it is in itself a terrible anguish. Yet, at this point, no true feeling is yet understood until the stage of the fire is reached; and we give the true knower of nature <note>original: "natuurkender"; one who understands the hidden spiritual laws of the physical world.</note> here to understand what such a thing is or signifies: let him reflect, and he shall find it in his natural knowledge.

17. The anguish makes the **sulfur-spirit** <note>original: "swavel-geest"</note>, and the sting makes the **Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurium"</note>, being the master-builder of nature. He is the life of nature. And the harsh desire makes the sharp **salt-spirit** <note>original: "zout-geest"</note>. And yet these three are all nothing other than a single thing, but they divide themselves into three forms, which are named: **Sulfur, Mercury, Salt** <note>original: "Sulphur, Mercurius, Sal"; these are the *tria prima*, the three primary alchemical principles representing the soul, spirit, and body of all things.</note>. These three properties impress the free longing into themselves, so that it also creates a material essence, the same—

24. 25. 26. And in this shock, the kindling of the fire occurs; for the harsh, rigorous darkness, which is a coldness, is startled by the light and by the great meekness of the free desire, and becomes within itself a shock of death, where the fierceness and the cold property retreat into themselves and close themselves up as if in death; for the dark mind becomes substantial in the shock, it gathers itself into itself, like a selfhood, like a great fear of the light, or like an enmity toward the light; and this is the true origin of the dark world—namely, of the abyss, into which the Devils have been cast, which we call Hell.

# CHAPTER 4.
## *Of the two eternal principles, namely of God's love and wrath, of the darkness and the light. Very necessary for the reader to contemplate.*

<margin>1.</margin> In this shock, or kindling of the fire, two kingdoms separate, and yet they are but a single one; however, they divide themselves in their <term>essence|original: "effents"; the underlying substance or "being" of a thing</term>, <term>woe|original: "quaal"; a term Böhme uses to mean both a "quality" and a "source of pain" or "torment"</term>, and will. They also become invisible to one another; the one does not comprehend the other in its own woe, and yet they are from a single origin: they also hang together, and the one would be a nothing without the other, and yet they both take their woe from a single origin. Understand it as follows.

2. Whenever the shock, or the lightning, arises, it is a single point, and makes, in a flash, a Triangle Δ, or a Cross +, and this is the true significance of the Character ♃ <note>The astrological symbol for Jupiter. In Böhme’s system, Jupiter represents the "Light-Fire," the source of life and joy, as opposed to the "Dark-Fire" of Saturn.</note>; the same is first the sharpness of all things, and the revealed God in Trinity: the Triangle points to the hidden God, being the word, or the Divine understanding, which in its eternal, beginningless birth is threefold, and yet but one in its revelation: in the fire- or light-world this trinity reveals itself in the birth—not that there is any place where such a figure is standing, no; but the entire birth is así: wherever the Divine fire reveals itself in something, there it makes a Triangle Δ in its kindling, which is well worth noting for the children of men, how life also kindles itself in a Triangle: the same signifies the Holy Trinity: and since the light of life was in the word of the Deity, which was breathed into man (as John Chapter 1 says) but was <note>original: "verblikkert"; literally "flashed away" or "eclipsed." It refers to the divine light being lost or extinguished in man after the Fall.</note> eclipsed from God in Paradise, so it had to be born again at the † Cross.

7. Here it is not to be understood that God takes a beginning in such a manner, but it is the eternal beginning of the manifested God; how the Divine understanding with power reveals itself in distinction, and introduces itself into the kingdoms, which is an eternal birthing; we speak here only of how the invisible God introduces himself into experience and reveals himself.

8. But now, with the kindling of the fire, we are to understand a twofold fire, a twofold spirit, and a twofold being: namely, a love-fire in the free desire, which becomes substantial through the impression or longing; and in the fire, spirit and being separate, and yet they are in one another, just as the spirit and the body are one. And as the spirit is now, so also is its being; and just as in the impression of the free desire there is a holy, sweet being and a holy, sweet spirit, so also there is in the dark impression a wrung, severe, raw, and bitter being and spirit; as the being is, so also is the mind of the understanding and the will within that being.

9. Although the eternal is like the spiritual in contrast to the temporal, yet the true spirit is still much more subtle than that which it makes into a substance in its grasp; for the true, understanding spirit first proceeds out from the substance, which before the substance was nothing else but a will, and did not manifest itself: for the will introduces itself into substance and being for this reason, so that it may be manifest to itself.

10. Now we must consider the divisibility within the fire; for when the fire ignites, there is the fire-lightning or the terror of *salnitris* <note>original: "salnitris"; in Böhme’s alchemy, this refers to the explosive 'nitre' or spiritual force that triggers the manifestation of nature.</note>, in which all powers spread out from one another and enter into division. There, the single eternal power of God reveals itself and divides into distinctiveness and into properties, both spiritually and substantially, as can be seen in this world. There, the manifold salts arise, which entered into such materials during creation; in eternity, this was nothing other than a spiritual being, but with the beginning of time, it became coarse and hard.

11. From this eternal root also arise the manifold spirits, both good and evil, as well as the manifold constellations, along with the four Elements and everything that lives and moves. Yet we must understand the division within itself as follows: when the lightning rises, the separation goes out from the fire. The terror of the fire is consuming; it seizes the captured being—both that which is in the <term>free desire|original: "vrye luft"; typically "vrye lust," referring to the unconditioned will of God</term> and that which is in the harshness—and consumes it instantaneously. For here in the fire, the eternal will, which has no ground <note>This refers to the *Unground*, the absolute, undifferentiated state of God before creation.</note>, becomes revealed; before this will, no being can stand; it devours everything into its Nothingness.

12. And here is the origin of eternal death, or of consumability, and in this very consuming lies the highest <term>Arcanum|original: "Arcanum"; a secret or hidden mystery of the divine workshop</term>, or mystery: for from this consumability, the true essential spirit and understanding go forth and make another beginning. For the first beginning belongs to God, who leads Himself from the "unground" into "ground" for His own contemplation; but this beginning, which goes out again from the consuming, is a spiritual beginning, and it yields three worlds. First, the dark fire-world, in heat and cold, an entire harshness without being; the second world is the spiritual, light, or <term>Angelic world|original: "Engelsche wereld"; often confused with "English," but here referring to the realm of Angels</term>; and the third world took its beginning with the start of time. When God moved both inward worlds, He then birthed and created this outward visible world out of them, in the form of a time.

13. But now, the division in the fire of consumability is to be understood thus: the powers that were made substantial through the first impression <note>The "impression" is the contraction or compression of the divine will into matter.</note> are led into spirituality within the fire. Namely, first, a spiritual <term>Mysterium|original: "Mysterium"; the hidden spiritual essence of a thing</term> goes forth from the free desire; this is according to the Godhead—that is, according to the eternal understanding, spiritually—and it is the Angelic life and light, as well as the true human life, and of everything that resembles it. For these are the powers of God; therefore, the Angels bear the great name of God within them, as do the true humans who possess the Divine power.

3. # Of the 5 Senses. Chapter 5.

5. The Divine kingdom of joy in the Heaven of God—namely, in the revealed God in His spoken or * breathed-out being <note>original: "uytgegaademt wesen"</note> (howsoever I might give the same to be understood)—stands in the desire of love; that is, in the power that reveals itself through the fire in the light. For the fire gives to the gentle, free desire *Essence* <note>original: "Essents"; the spiritual substance or "being" of a thing</note> and source-quality <term>source-quality|original: "quaal"; a term used by Böhme to describe both a "source-spring" and a "tormenting" driving force</term>, so that the same becomes distinct and moving, and that it becomes a kingdom of joy.

6. Likewise, we are to understand the darkness in the same way; that which is a desiring love in the light, wherein everything rejoices, is an enmity in the darkness. For the fire in the darkness is cold and hot, as well as bitter, harsh, and stinging; the properties are altogether rough and conflicting. They do not seek the "One" <note>the unified, peaceful state of God</note>, but rather the elevation of their own power. For the greater their exaltation and ignition is, the greater is their power, and the greater the joy becomes in the light.

7. That which is good and Holy in the light of power, is anxious and conflicting in the darkness. The darkness is the great enmity of the light, and is yet the cause that the light becomes revealed; for if there were no black, then the white could not be revealed to itself, and if there were no sorrow, then joy would also not be revealed to itself.

8. Thus joy exalts itself in itself, so that it is not like sorrow; and sorrow exalts itself in itself, so that it is a power and strength of the fire and of the light, from which pride and self-will arise. This is so that the dark fire-power, *Essence*, and moving source-quality might give to the light: which moved King Lucifer to exalt himself in the root of the fire, in order to rule over fire and light, and therefore he was cast out from the light into the darkness, and the light also withdrew itself from him.

9. Therefore understand us well in this place, what Hell and the dark world—or the wrath of God—is, of which the Holy Scripture says that there is a Hell, which is a cavern of despair of all good. It is not to be understood as a separate physical place; but it is the first ground of the eternal nature. The place is between the kingdom of God and the kingdom of this world, and it causes its own <term>principle|original: "principium"</term> to dwell within itself; it has neither place nor location, and is everywhere, yet only [revealed] to itself.

## Of the essence of Corporeality; the seventh property of Nature. ☾ Moon and ♄ Saturn, end and beginning.

<margin>1.</margin>
We recognize that God in His own Being is not a "being" <note>in the sense of a tangible substance</note>, but only the sheer power or the understanding toward Being; namely, an ungrounded eternal will, in which everything lies, and which is itself everything, and yet only a single "One," but which desires to reveal itself, and to lead itself into a spiritual Being, which occurs through the fire, in the love-desire, in the power of the light.

<margin>2.</margin>

# Chapter 6. Of the Essence of Corporeality.
<note>original: *D*; this letter indicates the "signature," a mark used by early modern printers to keep pages in the correct order for binding.</note>

### *Fourth form: fire, spirit, intellect, desire.*

17. Fire is the cause of true spiritual life, for it is there that the holy powers of free delight are liberated from harsh sorrow. This is because fire consumes—within its subtle essence <note>original: *Essents*; the underlying substance of a thing</note>—the dark nature of the impression <term>impression: the spiritual force of contraction or "drawing inward" that creates density</term> and carries that same nature out of itself into the light as spiritual power.

### *The fifth form: light, love.*

18. The holy, spiritual love-desire—in which the holy will of God has sharpened itself within the strict impression and has manifested through the fire with the power of omnipotence—now leads itself through the fire and out into the light. Thus, it has entered into the powers, the life, the movement, and the desire; it is here that the holy birth and the kingdom of joy of God's great love exist and are made manifest.

### *The sixth form: resonance, sound, word.*

19. The sixth form is the resonance of the Divine word, arising from the Divine powers. This resonance forms itself within the love-desire and enters into all powers as a sounding word. Therein lies the revelation of the Divine kingdom of joy, standing within the free delight of the wisdom of God.

### *The seventh form: Essence, Dwelling.*

20. The seventh form is the formed essence <term>essence: here meaning a tangible or "corporeal" spiritual substance</term> of the powers, being a single revelation of those powers. What the first six forms are in the spirit, the seventh is in the comprehensible essence; namely, a dwelling for all the others, much like a body for the spirit. Within this body the spirit works and plays with itself. It also serves as food for the fire, from which the fire draws the essences for its consumption and in which it burns. This seventh form is the kingdom of the glory of God. These seven are named as follows:

21. The seven spirits of God, or powers of nature; how they show and manifest themselves in love and wrath, in the Heavenly and the Hellish, as well as in the kingdom of this world.

| Form | Hellish / Heavenly Qualities | World / Earthly Realm Qualities |
|----------|---------------------------|------------------------------|
| 1. Harshness, Desire. | Hard, Cold, Greed. | Hardness, Cold, Stones, Bones, Salt. |

22. Gentle reader, understand the meaning rightly and well: it is not to be understood as if the seven properties were divided, one placed next to the other, or one existing before the other. No, all seven are nothing else but a single unity, and none of them is the first, second, or last—for the last is again the first. Just as the first introduces itself into a spiritual being, so too the last introduces itself into a bodily being; the last is the body of the first. We must speak as if in "piece-work" <note>original: *stuk-werk*; meaning describing things in fragments or steps</note> so that it can be written down and presented to the senses for the reader to contemplate. They are altogether nothing other than the revelation of God, according to love and wrath, according to eternity and time.

23. But this is well worth noting: that every property is also substantial <note>original: *wesentlik*; having the nature of an actual substance or essence</note>. In the kingdom of Heaven, this same essence is among one another like a single being, and it is a *Mystery* <note>original: *Mysterium*; in this context, a hidden creative source or "womb" from which things manifest</note> from which heavenly growths sprout out of the property of each individual power. It is just as the earth is a *Mystery* of all trees and herbs, as well as of the grass and the worms; and as the four elements are a *Mystery* of all that has life; and as the stars are a *Mystery* of all activity in the living and the growing.

24. Every property is substantial for itself, and it also contains within its essence the essence of the other six forms. It makes the essences of the other forms substantial within its own essence, just as we see in the earth and stones—and especially in metals. There, often in a single *Compaction* <note>original: *Compactie*; a dense compression of matter</note>, all seven metals lie within one another, and yet only one single property is the highest, which coagulates <term>coagulates: the process of a liquid or spiritual force thickening into a solid form</term> and holds all the others captive within itself. One is usually more manifest than the others, according to which property is strongest in a thing. This is also to be understood in growing things; in a herb or a piece of wood, there is often that which is harsh or sour, bitter, anxious, or sulfurous, fiery, sweetish, and insipid or watery.

# Chapter 7. Of the Holy Trinity.
## D 2
<meta>catchword: 6. But</meta>

...the fire, there in the ignition in the terror, the separation goes forth; but the powers of both in the internal and external world, these are altogether understood in the light or love-fire, that is, in the love-desire.

2. For its first ground is the eternal word, being the single unity in which everything lies; the second ground is the free delight of the word, being the wisdom, where all the colors of the single power are manifest in the will of the Godhead; the third ground is the love-desire, where the free delight—with its colors and virtues of the powers—has sharpened itself through nature, and through the ignition of the fire, has entered into a spiritual dominion, which introduces itself into an eternal kingdom of joy within the light and the powers.

3. The fourth ground is the oily <note>original: *olyfschen*; referring to the "oleosum" or the spiritual oil/fuel that allows the light of God to burn without the consuming "wrath" of fire</note>, in which the free delight in the fiery love-desire takes hold of itself in gentleness—that is, in its own form—and also takes hold of the fire’s and light’s brilliance and *Essences* <note>original: *Essents*; the spiritual substances or "beingness" of a thing</note>, and introduces them into the first being: which power, of fire and light, in the gentleness of the free delight, in the oily property, is the true and Holy *Tincture* <note>original: *Tinctuur*; in alchemical and mystical thought, a spiritual force that can transform or "color" a substance into a higher state</note>.

4. The fifth ground is the watery one, resulting from the mortification <note>original: *dooding*; the process of "dying" to one state to be reborn in another</note> in the fire, where the first spiritual being in the harsh, severe dark desire was consumed in the fire; thus now, from the consumability of the fire, a spiritual being goes forth—this is the oily ground—and a watery being goes forth out of the deathliness, which takes away the fire-spirit’s wrath, so that it cannot ignite itself in its wrathful property within the oily ground. Thus the fire must burn through death, and be nothing other than a light, otherwise the oily ground would be set ablaze; thus the fire, in its consumability, had to give birth to the water, which is its death, and yet it must also have it again for its life, otherwise neither fire nor light could exist. And so the same is an eternal birthing, consuming, and taking back; a consuming and yet an eternal giving, and there is neither beginning nor end.

5. In this way we now understand what God and his essence may be: we Christians say that God is threefold, yet one in essence; but that which is commonly said—that God is threefold in Persons—that is understood very strangely by the ignorant, and even by some scholars; for God is no Person, except only in Christ; but he is the eternal birthing power, and the kingdom, together with all being; everything takes its origin from him.

# Of the Holy Trinity. Chapter 7.

6. But what is said of God—that he is Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—is entirely correct; only it must be explained, otherwise the unenlightened mind does not understand it: the Father is primarily the will of the <term>Unground<note>original: *ongronds*; referring to the *Ungrund*, the primal void or absolute mystery of God before any nature or beginning</note>; he is, beyond all nature or beginning, the will toward something, who takes hold of himself in a delight for his own revelation.

7. And the delight belongs to the will, or is the Father’s conceived power, and it is his Son, heart, and dwelling place; it is the first eternal beginning within the will, and is therefore called a Son, because he takes an eternal beginning within the will through the will’s own self-conception.

8. Now the will speaks itself out from itself through this conceiving, like a <insert>breathing out<note>original German: *Aushauchen*</note></insert> or a revelation; and this same outgoing of the will in the speaking or breathing is the Spirit of the Godhead, or the third Person, just as the ancients have established.

9. And that which is spoken is the Wisdom—namely, the power of the colors and virtues of the will, which he eternally conceives into a <term>Center<note>original: *Centrum*</note></term> or heart as his dwelling; and from that conception—that is, from his eternal form—he speaks it forth again eternally, and also eternally conceives it back into the Center of his heart.

10. Thus the conceiving of the will—that is, of the Father—is from eternity to eternity; he conceives his speaking word from eternity to eternity, and speaks it from eternity to eternity: the speaking is the mouth of the revelation of the will; and the outgoing of the speaking or birthing is the Spirit of the formed word; and that which is spoken is the power, color, and virtue of the Godhead, being the Wisdom.

11. Here one cannot say with any firm foundation that God is three Persons, but rather that he is threefold in his eternal begetting; he begets himself in threefoldness, and in this eternal begetting there is nevertheless only one single being and begetting to be understood: neither Father, nor Son, nor Spirit, but the one eternal life or Good.

12. The Trinity is first rightly understood in his eternal revelation—namely, where he reveals himself through eternal nature, through the fire into the light.

13. There, one understands three properties in a single being: the Father is understood with the fire-world; and the Son with the love-desire in the light—that is, with the light-world, or with the great gentleness within the fire; and the Holy Spirit with the moving life in the <term>Tincture<note>original: *Tinctuur*; a spiritual essence that transforms or "colors" reality, often associated with the life-force or the soul's illumination</note></term>, in the oily and in the watery life and dominion, which exists in the fire and in the light.

### Chapter 8. On the Creation of the Angels.

26. Just as the body and soul are a single unit, and yet one is not the other; or as fire and water, or air and earth, are from a single origin and yet one is not the other; they are nevertheless bound to one another, and the one would be a nothing without the other—so too must we understand the Divine being and the Divine power.

27. The power in the light is the love-fire of God, and the power in the darkness is the wrath-fire of God. And yet it is but a single fire, though it divides itself into two <term>principles</term> <note>original: *principien*; referring to the two fundamental realms of light/love and darkness/wrath</note>, so that the one may become manifest in the other. For the flame of wrath is the revelation of the great love; in the darkness, the light becomes known, for otherwise it would not be manifest to itself.

28. Thus we are to understand that the evil and good Angels dwell near one another, and yet there is between them the greatest, unmeasurable distance. For Heaven is in Hell, and Hell is in Heaven, and yet the one is not manifest to the other. Even if the Devil traveled many hundreds of thousands of miles and wished to invade Heaven to see it, he would still be nowhere but in Hell and would not see it. Likewise, the Angels do not see the darkness, for their sight is purely the light of the Divine power; and the sight of the Devil is purely the darkness of God's wrath. The same is to be understood regarding holy and, conversely, godless people: therefore, when we lost the Divine sight in Adam—where Adam saw out of Divine power—Christ said: you must be born anew, otherwise you cannot see the kingdom of God.

29. We must understand the Creation of the Angels as coming from the spirit-fire, where the will of the <term>Unground</term> <note>original: *ongronds*; the bottomless, eternal void or abyss from which all existence originates in this mystical philosophy</note> introduces itself into a "ground" <note>a foundation or manifest state</note>, and through the fiery birth, the <term>eternally speaking word</term> <note>original Latin: *verbo fiat*; literally "let there be word," the creative command of God</note>, or life, is revealed. This occurs with the first <term>principle</term>, where the spiritual government is made manifest through the fire-birth. In this spiritual fire all the Angels arise—namely, from the qualities leading toward the fire-<term>source-quality</term> <note>original: *vuur-quaal*; a technical term describing the laboring tension or "anguish" of the elemental source of life</note>. For out of the fire itself nothing can be created, because it is not a "being" <note>meaning a tangible substance</note>, but out of the qualities belonging to the fire, a creature can be grasped in the "desire"—that is, in the *creative word*—and be brought into a creaturely form and characteristic.

30. Therefore, the Angels are many and manifold, and also in many distinct offices. # THE 9th CHAPTER.

->On the fall of Lucifer with his Legions.<-

<margin>1.</margin> Although natural reason <note>original: *eygen vernuft*; the human intellect when operating without divine illumination</note> might wish to rebuke us here and say that we were not present when this happened, we say here that we were truly present there in a **magical manner**, according to the law of eternity, and saw such things; but I, as the person I am, did not see it, for I was not yet a creature; but we have seen it in the *Essence* <term>Essence</term> <note>original: *Essents*; a term used by the author to describe the fundamental spiritual substance of the soul or reality</note> of the soul (which God breathed into Adam).

2. Since God now dwells in this same *Essence*, and has dwelt there from eternity, and reveals Himself in His **Mirror**, and looks back through the Soulish *Essence* to the beginning of all beings; why then should reason rebuke me for that to which it is blind? I want reason to be warned, that it should for once look into the **Mirror of understanding** and consider what it is, and cease from the building of the frantic **Babel** <note>In this context, Babel refers to the "confusion" of human-made religious systems and intellectual pride</note>; the time shall come.

3. The fall of Lucifer did not happen out of the intent or the preordination of God: in the **wrath of God**—that is, according to the property of the dark world—it was well known how it could or would happen, but in the holiness of God—that is, in the light—no such desire is manifest in such a property; otherwise the holy God would have to have a devilish or hellish grim desire in His love, which is completely not the case: yet in the *Center* <term>Center</term> <note>original: *Centrum*; the core point of spiritual manifestation where life and nature originate</note> of the eternal nature, that is, in the form leading to the fire, there, in the dark impression, such a property does indeed exist.

4. And every good Angel has the *Center* within itself, and is always manifest to a degree in the *Center* in its creaturely property; which property is the greatest in the creature, and according to it is also its office and dominion.

10. You say: what caused this within himself? Answer: his great beauty. ### Concerning the Creation of Heaven and the outward World.

1. When reason <note>original: *vernuft*; the human capacity for logical and sensory understanding</note> looks upon creation, it appears very wondrous to the same: how God created the Stars and the four Elements; especially when it considers the earth, along with the hard Stones, and the very rough and severe essence; and when it sees how great rocky cliffs are created there, which in part can be used for nothing, and are nothing but an obstacle for the creatures of this world to use; then it thinks: from what could such a compaction <note>The process of spiritual forces becoming solid, physical matter</note> have arisen, in so many kinds of forms and properties? For there are many kinds of stones, many kinds of metals, and many kinds of earth, from which also many kinds of trees and herbs grow.

2. When reason observes this now, it finds nothing, except that it recognizes that there must be a hidden power and might, which is unfathomable and unsearchable, which has created all things in such a way, there

### Of the Creation of the Heavens, etc. Chapter 10.

...there reason lets the matter rest, and thus runs to and fro among created things, just as a bird flies in the air. It looks upon such things as a cow looks at a new stable door <note>A traditional idiom meaning to look at something with total incomprehension or blankness</note>, and it never considers what it itself may be. It seldom comes so far as to recognize how man is an image formed out of all these beings; it runs about like cattle that have no understanding, desiring nothing else than to fill themselves and to give birth. And whenever it reaches its highest point and wishes to investigate something, it searches in the outward playwork of the stars, or else for a mere representation of outward nature. In short, it does not want to learn to know its creator, and if it should happen that a man comes so far as to learn to know Him, reason calls that man a fool, forbids him the noble knowledge of God, even reckons such knowledge to him as a sin, and mocks him for it.

3. Such beast-men <note>original: *vech-menschen*; literally "cattle-humans," referring to people driven by animal instincts rather than spiritual intellect</note> have we become after the fall of Adam; so that we do not even consider that we are created in the image of God, and were gifted with the true natural understanding according to both the eternal and temporal nature. We should remember to strive with great earnestness to regain what we have lost, since we still possess that same original soul in which the true understanding lies, if only we would work for it—so that that same lost light, which is still offered to us through grace, might shine in us again.

4. Therefore there shall be no excuse on the great day of the Lord, when God shall judge the hidden things of man; because we have not wanted to learn to know Him, nor obey His voice, which daily knocks at and within us. We have not surrendered ourselves to Him so that our understanding might have been opened. There a stern judgment shall pass over those who let themselves be called "Lord and Master" and yet do not know nor walk the way of God—and furthermore forbid those who wish to know it and walk it.

<margin>Exhalation <note>original German: *Aushauchen*</note></margin>
5. The creation of the outward world is a revelation of the inward Spiritual Mystery <term>Mysterium (Mystery): In this context, a hidden spiritual reality or divine plan that is not yet visible</term>, being the center <note>original: *centrum*</note> of the eternal nature with the Holy Element. And she <note>Nature or the World</note> was born through the movement of the inward, like a <gloss>breathing out</gloss>, through the eternal speaking word, which has spoken the essence out from the inward Spiritual world. And though the same during the speaking was not yet a physical essence, but like a vapor or smoke compared to the inward—coming from both the property of the dark world and of the light world—therefore the outward essence of this world is both evil and good.

Secondly, we must consider from where such a grimness originated, which has compacted and introduced the powers of the properties into such a wild nature, as we see in the earth and stones.

7. For we must not think at all that in Heaven—that is, in the spiritual world—anything of the sort exists; these things are nothing other than the properties of possibility in the spiritual world. However, these are not manifest in such wild properties there, but are as if swallowed up, just as the light swallows the darkness; and yet the darkness truly dwells in the light, and [the darkness] nevertheless does not comprehend [the light].

8. This gives us even greater cause for reflection: that when man could not endure in the spiritual **Mystery** <note>original: *Mysterium*</note> of the Paradisiacal property, God cursed that same compaction (which is the earth) and ordained an earnest judgment to separate the good from the evil once more within the compaction of the earth. Thus, the good had to remain within the curse—namely, in death. Whoever does not see this is truly blind. Why would God have wanted to curse His good being, if something had not entered into it that was contrary to the good? Or has God become at odds with Himself? (As human reason might say). For in Moses it is written: *And God looked upon everything He had made, and behold, it was very good.*

9. ### II. Mercury.

19. Secondly, I find—according to the second form and property of the dark nature and worldly essence in the compaction <note>original: *compactie*; the process by which spiritual forces solidify into physical matter</note> of metals and stones—a bitter, stinging, raging being, which is a poison. ### III. Sulfur.

20. Thirdly, I find the third property, being the anguish, which is the Sulfur-torment <note>original: *Swavel-queel*; a term describing the agonizing tension or "source-point" where different forces struggle together</note>, in which the divisions of the properties—being the Essences—reside.

### IV. Saltpeter.

21. This same shock is the origin of the saltpeter, arising out of the sulfurous, watery, and earthy properties; for it is the awakener of death (that is, within the deadly property) and the first origin of life within the fire. The property of the dark world grips into the fire up to this point, but it can go no further.

### V. Oil.

22. Fifthly, we find in the compaction of metals and stones an oil that is sweeter than any sugar can be, provided it can be separated from the other properties. This is the first Heavenly holy being, which has taken its origin from the free air. Thus it is whiter than anything in nature can be, yet because of the fire, it remains a crimson red, which changes the light into yellow, then toward red and white, because of the earthy property and the power of the Sun.

23. For there Lady Venus has laid her treasure chest; it is the Virgin with her beautiful crown.

# Chapter 10: Of the Creation of the Heavens, etc.

34. The stars signify the Spirit, and the earth the body; before the Creation, in the eternal birthing, everything existed within one another, yet in no <term>coagulation</term> <note>original: *coagulatie*; the process of spiritual essence thickening into solid matter</note> or creaturely form, but rather in a powerful, wrestling play of love, without such a material essence.

35. But in the movement of the word, when the <term>word "let it be"</term> <note>original: *verbum fiat*; the creative command from Genesis</note> was ignited, it divided itself through that ignition into the <term>Salnitric flash</term> <note>original: *Salnitriſchen*; a term used by theosophers like Jacob Böhme to describe a sudden, explosive spiritual tension or "lightning" that births nature</note> of the fire, each property into itself. And such was seized and thus coagulated by the awakened, harsh <term>impression</term> <note>original: *impreſſie*; the first stage of nature where the divine will "contracts" or "presses" itself into being</note> (which is called the *fiat* or "let it be," being the first form of nature). Thus, every property was captured in its own essence—the subtle in its essence, and likewise the coarse—all according to the degrees of the eternal birthing of nature, from one thing unto infinity.

36. Through the stars, both good and evil are made manifest, for the fierce fiery power of eternal nature, as well as the power of the Holy Spiritual world, is manifest in them, like a <gloss>breathed-forth</gloss> <note>original Dutch: *uytgeſproken weſen*; the author provides a German gloss at the bottom of the page: *Ausgehauchtes*, meaning "that which is exhaled or breathed out."</note> being. Therefore, there are many dark stars, which we do not all see together, and many light ones, which we do see.

The element is neither hot nor cold, neither dry nor wet; it is the movement and life of the inward Heaven, being the true Angelic life, according to the Creature. It is the first Divine revelation through nature out of the fire; when the properties of the eternal nature work within it, it is then named *Paradise*.

### Of the Creation of the Heavens, etc. Chapter 10

51. The Spirit-water is living, and that which is exhaled <note>The author distinguishes between the living divine essence and the "exhaled" or manifested world which appears "dead" by comparison.</note> is mute, or insensible and without understanding; and compared to the living, it is as if dead. Of this, Moses says: God has separated it from the water above the firmament.

52. The firmament is another <term>principle</term> <note>original: *principium*; a foundational source or beginning of a specific state of being</note>, that is, another beginning of motion. The water above the firmament is the Spiritual essence, in which the Spirit of God rules and works; for Moses also says: the Spirit of God hovered upon the water. For the spiritual element hovers within the four physical elements, and within that spiritual element, the Spirit of God hovers upon the Spirit-water—the one exists within the other.

53. The Heaven where God dwells is the holy Element; and the firmament, or the abyss between God and the four Elements, is death. For the inward Heaven has an entirely different birth—that is, a different life—than the outward, four-elemental world. They are indeed within one another, yet one does not comprehend the other, just as Tin and Silver do not truly mix. For each comes from a different principle, and even though they may appear similar and seem closely related, they are like the inward and outward waters compared to one another. In this way, they must be understood: for the inward <term>Venus</term> <note>In Böhme’s mysticism, Venus represents the desire for love and beauty; here, he distinguishes between its pure divine form and its corrupted material expression.</note> and the outward Venus are stepsisters. They come from one Father, yet they have two Mothers, where the one is a Virgin and the other is a * ravished woman <note>original: *verkrachte*; the text suggests a loss of purity in the material world. A marginal note suggests the word *geswachte*, meaning "enfeebled."</note>. Therefore, they remain distinct until the judgment of God, who shall wipe away her shame through fire.

54. Moses writes: God created the Heaven out of the midst of the water. This is entirely correct; the stars are an outward water-spirit—that is, the powers of the outward water—and the material water is the body of those powers in which they operate. Thus, in the stars, there is the fiery, the airy, and also the earthly <term>quality</term> <note>original: *quaal*; likely referring to the *Qual* or "source-spirit," the driving force or characteristic of a substance</note>; the same is found in the material water. The upper is the life and the government of the lower; it kindles the lower, whereby the lower becomes mobile and active. The lower is the body, or the "wife" of the upper; the upper also lies within the lower, though as if powerless.

55. And the upper would be just as powerless if it were not kindled by the Sun. The Sun is the heart of all outward powers, and it is the open point up to the <term>tenth number</term> <note>A reference to Pythagorean or Kabbalistic numerology, where ten represents the return to unity and the completion of a cycle of manifestation.</note>. If we were not so blind, and did not despise everything that our "cow-eyes" <note>A derogatory term for physical, materialistic sight that cannot see spiritual reality.</note> cannot see, it would be only right that this should be revealed;

# CHAPTER 11.
## *Of the Mystery of the Creation.*

<margin>1.</margin> The reason of the external man says: how is it that God has not revealed the Creation of the world to men, since it is the greatest and most principal work, upon which everything depends? Why have *Moses* <note>original: *Moyses*</note> and the Children of God written so little about it?

2. Yes, dear reason, smell in your own bosom—what do you smell? Behold your mind—what does it lust after? Much likely after the Devil’s sorcery; if the Devil had not known this foundation, he would perhaps still be an Angel; had he not seen the *Magical birth* <note>The process by which the divine will brings forth spiritual and material substance.</note> in his high exalted light, he would not have desired to be his own Lord and Maker in the being.

3. Why does God cover His Children, who receive His Spirit of knowledge in this time, with the Cross, and cast them into sorrow, and into the filth of vanity? Truly, it is so that they should play the *Have Mercy* <term>original: *Miserere*; a reference to the penitential Psalm 51, meaning they should live in a state of constant humility and repentance</term>, and remain in humility, and should not play in the light of nature in this time; otherwise, if they became aware of what *Divine Magic* <term>original: *Magia Divina*; the holy power of creating through the Word or the Spirit</term> is, they might also receive a desire to [follow] the Devil...

6. And that same thing was the cause of Lucifer’s fall: that he wanted to be a God of nature and live in the [state of] change. This was also the very idolatry of the Heathens; because they understood the Magical birth, they fell from the One <note>The singular, unified source of God.</note> into the Magical birth of nature, and chose for themselves Idols out of the powers of nature.

7. Therefore, the Creation has remained so dark, and God has covered His children—in whom the true light has shone—with sorrows, so that they would not become manifest to themselves. For Adam also imagined after the same desire, to know and taste Magic <note>original: *Magiam*</note>, and wished to be like God. So God allowed him to fill his Heavenly image with the vanity of nature, making it quite dark and earthly, just as Lucifer did with the center <note>original: *centrum*</note> of nature, where he made a Devil out of an Angel.

8. Therefore I wish to have warned the reader of this: that he use Magic <note>original: *Magiam*</note> rightly, namely, in a right faith and in true humility before God; and that he does not stir up the great turmoil <term>original: *turbam magnam*; a term often used in Theosophical texts to describe the awakening of God's wrath or chaotic forces within nature</term> in a magical way, unless it serves the glory of God and the well-being of mankind.

### Ch. 12. Of the 1st and 2nd and 3rd day of Creation. ###

Here the light shone in the power, which now had been awakened anew in the darkness, which the Prince of Wrath <note>Referring to Lucifer, who embodies the "wrathful" aspect of nature in this mystical system.</note> could not comprehend, nor was it of any use to him, for it was the light of nature; it is of no service to him.

15. And Moses says: God separated the light from the darkness. This is to be understood as follows: the darkness remained in the wrathful property, not only in the earth, but in the entire space; however, in the essence of light, the light of nature rose from Heaven—namely out of the fifth <term>essence</term> <note>original: *essentie*. Also known as the "quintessence," it was believed to be the pure, celestial substance that makes up the stars and planets, distinct from the four earthly elements.</note>, out of which the stars were created—which essence is in the earth and above the earth everywhere.

16. Thus the darkness remained in the property of wrath, in the essence of the earth, and also in the entire <gloss>depth of the text</gloss> <note>original: *Text tieffe*. 17. Thus, in the first movement of the <term>Word: Let there be</term> <note>original: *Verbum fiat*. The earth was contained with the *Word: Let there be* and created on the planetary wheel; and thus we are to understand the creation of the first day with the separation, namely the separation of light and darkness, and with the expulsion of the Prince Lucifer.

18. The first day now carried itself, with the revealed word, through the other five days until the day of rest, where the beginning enters again into the end, and the end back into the beginning. For the first movement of the word, where the light of nature ignited itself in the essence, that is the joy of creation, which has opened itself with the other days through all the properties of nature, where one may call every property a "Heaven." For it has and brings its own particular working with it into the others, and every day has a property moved and revealed; therein a particular working has become manifest.

## Of the Second Day. ##

19 The second day we call *Monday*; and this is because the Moon rules the first hour of the day. It may well be that the ancient sages understood something of this in the light of nature <note>The "light of nature" is a term used by Christian mystics and alchemists to describe an innate, divinely-given understanding of the natural world.</note>, which they kept hidden, depicting it much more through figures and symbols than by explaining it directly. That they certainly understood this is evident in the names of the seven planets, for they gave them names according to the seven properties of nature. These properties agree so perfectly with nature and the creation that it seems to me they partly understood the true foundation of creation. This is because the names of the planets arise so precisely out of the language of nature <note>original: *natuur spraak*. This refers to the "Signatura Rerum," the idea that the true names of things reveal their inner essence.</note>. However, the reason this was not clearly brought to light—as was mentioned previously—is because of false *Magic* <term>Magia</term> <note>original: *Magia*. In this context, it refers to a spiritual or creative power that can be used for good or corrupted into "magic tricks."</note>. ## CHAPTER 13.
### Of the Creation of the fourth day.

1. On the fourth day, *Mercurius* <note>In this system, Mercury represents the principle of movement, communication, and the "spirit" that connects different realms.</note> has the first hour of the day, which creates the sensing life; here one understands the ground of the revelation of the internal nature into the outward, most properly. For on the fourth day the *Sun* and the *Stars* were created; these same are the true *Mercurial* life. Here the property of fire has opened itself in the *Sulphur-source* <note>original: *Swavel quel*. In alchemy, Sulphur represents the active, combustible soul-energy.</note> through the water, and the fifth essence <note>The "quintessence" or highest element that permeates all nature.</note> has become manifest through the light of nature, being an oil of fire and of water out of the *Sulphur*, which is a *Mercurial Salt-nitre* <note>original: *Salniter*. A mystical explosive force representing the flash of life.</note>, an igniting *Mercury*, a living sensing one.

2. In the third form of nature there is an unfeeling life within the *Sulphur* and *Mercury*, but in the fourth there is a sensing life. For in the fire the properties become painful, and in the oily principle <note>original: *olyfsche*. Refers to the soothing, balm-like quality of the soul that balances the "fire."</note> the same become soft and joyful; thus now the movement in the oily principle is sensing the painfulness <note>The author suggests that "feeling" or "consciousness" arises from the tension between the harsh fire of existence and the soothing "oil" of life.</note>.

3. Here one now understands quite thoroughly how the separation in the fire of eternal nature has revealed itself in visible beings of the outward world, with a formal nature. For in the ignition of the fire in the *salt-nitrous shock* <note>original: *Salnitrischen schrik*. The sudden, violent flash that brings forth life or light from darkness.</note>, two beings separate themselves: namely a watery one from the consumability in the fire, where the fire consumes the raw torment of the impression within itself; then from that consumability there goes out a great softness, which has died-away to the fire and is unfeeling, and gives the water-source.

4. Secondly, the fire-source <note>original: *vuur-quel*.</note> also separates itself—namely the properties belonging to the fire-source (which now, with the ignition of the fire, have become painful and sensing)—into its own *Principle* <note>original: *Principium*. A fundamental starting point or realm of existence.</note>. This fire-source was not able to exist if it did not swallow the water back into itself again, from which it strengthens itself; from this the *salt-nitrous shock* then also arises, where the fury <note>original: *grim*. The harsh, wrathful aspect of nature.</note> is terrified before the being of the meekness of the water, from which sensing, as well as the luster of the fire, arises.

### Of the fourth day of Creation. Chapter 13.

5. For that which is swallowed by the fire from the water is resolved into a **Spiritual oil**, in which the fire shines; and from that oil comes the air, being the floating **Spirit of the fire**, which has become movable within the fire.

6. The air is nothing other than the movable life, where the **speaking word** <note>The "speaking word" refers to the divine creative command that continues to resonate through nature.</note> carries itself out through nature, through the powers of nature, through the fire in the oil of the nature of light in the water-source; it is the life of the fire, yet it has "died" to the fire <note>Meaning it has moved beyond the destructive heat of the fire into a new state.</note>, and yet it becomes manifest in the fire; it is the life of nature according to the property of gentleness.

7. Thus, with the ignition of the fire, we are to understand four properties in the light of the fire (which is the light of nature): namely, a **fiery**, an **airy**, and an **oily** one—in which the light is manifest—and a **watery** one. These all arise originally from the first desire toward nature, while the free air introduces itself into a desire and into nature; and they all carry themselves out through the fire into a movable life. And yet, that life is not an intelligent life, but nothing other than properties toward the true life: the intelligent life is the * **breathed-out word** <note>original: *Ausgehallete*. 8. This **Salnitric** and **Sulphuric** property was brought forth from the third day of work—that is, out of the terror of the fire—and from that the fourth movement arose, being the **Mercurial** <note>The "Mercurial" principle represents movement, communication, and the spirit that animates the physical stars.</note>, which the *fiat* seized, impressed into itself, and made visible. These same are the **stars**, which are nothing other than the properties of the powers of nature. That which nature is within itself in a tiny spark, the entire firmament of stars is in its circle; and what nature is in its secrecy and hiddenness, the firmament is in a publicly working being, to be understood as follows.

This refers to the divine command in Genesis that brings the universe into being.</note>, and spoke with the holy eternal, speaking word, through the *let it be* <note>original Latin: *fiat*</note> that same life into forms according to the properties of the constellations <term>constellations: In this mystical context, the Dutch *gesternte* refers not just to stars in the sky, but to the "astral" or spiritual influences that govern the characteristics of all physical matter.</term>, in Spiritual bodies, in which the *let it be*, or the desire, drew the Elements to itself, being a body according to the outward essence.

3. In this same third constellation of properties, grass, herbs, and trees also stand, and yet they also make use of the ignition from the upper regions, through which they are qualified differently.

3. And we see how every genus has a Spirit and a body according to the degree of its star; for it is understood that from a single constellation many kinds of genera come. This is caused because every constellation again has its own degrees within itself; for in every constellation lies everything that all stars are, though in distinct degrees in their manifestation. Therefore the properties in every constellation are manifold, and so also from every constellation manifold genera have gone forth. The Spirit of every genus is from the stars, but all the genera must use the four Elements, for they arise from the source-fountain <note>original: *quell-bron*</note> from which all stars arise.

There they then change back into one in the fire, and proceed out of the fire as a single essence again, namely in an oily property, in which they stand at the bond of the highest desire of love; for their light shines in the oil. And just as the fire-world desires the light-world, and the light-world the fire-world—being Father and Son—so we are to understand the two genders in the same way.

This indicates that all which they worked and revealed, out of the wonders of eternal wisdom, would enter again into the **One**, that is, into the rest, which is the seventh property, being a dwelling of the active life. 4. 5. That is, a living, ingenious, and understanding image, according to the revelation of this revealed property.

## THE 16th CHAPTER.

### *Of the distinction between the Heavenly and the Earthly Human.*

<margin>1.</margin> **I**f we consider the image of God—that which God created in Paradise for the eternal, unbreakable life—we cannot in any way say of the coarse, fleshly image that the earthly, coarse property is the "image of God" which can possess the Holy world. For it is not of such essence <note>original: "Essents"</note> and being of which Christ speaks in John 6: *the flesh is of no use, the spirit is the life*; likewise, *flesh and blood shall not inherit the Kingdom of Heaven*. And yet, the true body lies within this animalistic, coarse property just like gold in a coarse stone.

<margin>2.</margin> Everything about man that is earthly is animalistic and perishable, and is not "man"—even though God did indeed create an outward body for man out of the Clay <note>original: "Limo" — Latin *limus*, the "slime" or "dust" of the earth from Genesis</note> of the earth. Nevertheless, this is not to be understood by us as it currently exists; for the true human body, according to the inward world, is a spiritual Sulfur, a spiritual Mercury, and a spiritual Salt <term>Sulfur, Mercury, and Salt: the "Tria Prima," representing the soul's energy, the spirit's mediation, and the physical/substantial form</term>. Every property of the soul has something bodily or essential about itself.

<margin>3.</margin> God created such a body, just as the soul was in its essence <note>original: "Essents"</note>—that is, in the spoken word of the understanding—and breathed the soul into it for the purpose of understanding. To that end, the outward Sulphurous body is also in no way the coarse animal which passes away and does not re-

<margin>5.</margin> All properties of the internal Holy body, together with those of the external, were in the first man directed in an equal Harmony; none of them lived in their own self-desire, but they all together gave their desire into the soul, in which the Divine light was manifest, just as in the Holy Heaven. The light shone through all properties, and it created in all the properties an equal temperance; all properties gave their desire into the light, namely into the revealed sweetness of God, which permeated through all properties. In this permeation, they were all together tinctured <note>original: "getingeert" — an alchemical term meaning to be imbued with a specific quality or transformed by a "tincture"</note> with the sweet love, so that between them there was nothing else but sheer good taste and a desire for love.

<margin>6.</margin> The internal Holy corporeality of the pure Element pressed through those four elements, and held the *Limum* of the earth <note>original: "Limum der aerden" — Latin for the "slime" or "clay" of the earth from which Adam was formed in Genesis</note> (being the external **Sulphurous** body) as if enclosed within itself \*; and while it was truly there, yet it was in such a manner as darkness dwells in the light, and yet its darkness cannot become manifest because of the light; but if the light is extinguished, then the darkness is manifest.

<margin>7.</margin> Thus the internal [man] held the external man captive within himself and permeated the same, just as a fire glows through iron so that one thinks it is entirely fire; but when the fire is extinguished, then the black, dark iron becomes manifest.

<margin>8.</margin> Thus also was the first man, when he stood in Paradise in fine fixity, on earth just as time is before God, and God is in time, and neither is the other, and yet they are not separately divided. Just as time is a play before God, so also was the external life of man a play before the Holy internal man, who was the true image of God.
