## Chapter 16. Of the distinction between the Heavenly and the Earthly Human.

9. The external spirit and the external body were, for the internal, like a miracle of the Divine revelation according to the fiery dark world and the light world; they were a mirror of the great omnipotence and omniscience of God: and the internal was given to him as a ruler.

10. Just as God plays with the time of the external world for Himself, so the internal Divine human was meant to play with the external human in the revealed wonders of God in this world. He was to open the Divine wisdom to all creatures, each according to its own property, as well as in the earth, in stones, and in metals, within which a twofold being also lies—namely, one from the origin of the dark fire-world, and one from the origin of the Holy light-world.

11. All this was given to him as a play; he had the knowledge of all the *tinctures* <term>Tinctures: In the mystical philosophy of Jacob Böhme, a "tincture" is a spiritualizing life-force or "inner quality" that can transform or "color" matter with its own nature</term>, and everything was under him. He ruled in Heaven and earth, and in all Elements, as well as in all the stars. This was because the Divine power was manifest within him; neither heat nor cold pressed upon him, just as a *tincture* permeates a body [Corpus] and preserves it from sickness, and as the warmth of the Sun preserves the body from cold. Thus also the highest *tincture* of the Divine fire and light—being the Holy power of the internal Spiritual body—permeated through the external body of flesh and blood. It took all external Elemental properties, as well as the *Limum* <term>Limum: Latin for "slime" or "clay," referring to the "dust of the ground" from Genesis from which man was formed</term> of the earth, into its preservation and protection.

12. For in the body [Corpus] of the internal and external Human, there was a single temperance <note>In this context, "temperance" refers to a state of perfect balance or harmony between conflicting forces</note>; therefore, nothing outside the body was able to disturb or seize this harmony. Just as gold persists in the fire, and as a tincture permeates everything and yields to nothing, so also the human was subject to nothing, except solely to the one God, who dwelt through him and was manifest in him with the power of the Holy Being. He was an image and likeness of God, in which the spirit of God dwelt.

13. Reason <note>original: "Vernuft," referring to the limited intellectual capacity of the human mind which often fails to grasp spiritual truths</note> will understand us very poorly and say that we speak of two different humans, but I say no; I speak only of a single one, who is a likeness of God—that is, of the revealed God, according to the spoken, formed word of the Divine power of the Divine understanding.

19. Now, when Moses says: God rested on the seventh day from all His works, and sanctified the seventh day for rest, this has an excellently high meaning. Yet it is also childlike; if we were still in Paradise and lived in the Sabbath, we would understand it as follows.

For the seventh day has been from eternity outside of all time, for it is the formed word of the divine understanding. # CHAPTER 17.
## On Paradise.

1. Moses says that when God had created man, He planted a garden in Eden and placed man within it, to cultivate and to preserve it. In the garden, He caused all kinds of fruits to grow that were delightful to look upon and good to eat; and He planted the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil in the middle.

2. Here, a veil lies before Moses’ face <note>A reference to Exodus 34, where Moses veiled his face because it shone too brightly for the Israelites. Böhme uses this as a metaphor for the "hidden" or "veiled" spiritual meaning of the Bible that remains invisible to the unspiritual.</note>, because he has a clarified face, so that sinful Israel cannot look him in the eye. For the man of vanity <note>The "man of vanity" refers to the fallen human who is focused only on temporary, worldly things.</note> is not worthy to know what Paradise is; and even though the same is given to us to understand according to the hidden man <note>The "hidden" or "inward" man is the spiritual soul or the spark of God within a person.</note>, nevertheless, through this description, we shall remain hidden from the animals <note>By "animals," Böhme refers to people who live only by their physical instincts and lacks spiritual rebirth.</note>, but will be sufficiently understood by our own.

3. The garden in Eden was a place on earth where man was tested, and Paradise was in Heaven; yet it was also within the garden of Eden. For just as Adam—before his Eve and before his sleep <note>Böhme believed Adam was originally a singular, spiritual being; the "sleep" was a step toward his fall into physical division and mortality.</note>—existed in Heaven according to the internal man and on earth according to the external man; and just as the internal holy man permeated the external, like a fire makes an iron glow through and through, so too did the Heavenly power from the pure Element <note>The "pure Element" is Böhme’s term for the spiritual substance of the Heavenly world, distinct from the four physical elements (earth, air, fire, water).</note> permeate the four elements. It flourished through the earth and bore fruits; these were both Heavenly and earthly, but were qualified <note>A technical term meaning the fruits were filled with the properties or "qualities" of the divine.</note> by the Divine power. The vanity within the fruit was held as if half-swallowed, just as the day hides the night and holds it captive within itself so that it is not recognized.

4. Paradise was nothing other than the property of the seventh day. The Heavenly essence of the second principle <note>original: "principium"; This refers to the World of Light or God’s love, the second of Böhme’s three fundamental layers of reality.</note> lies locked within the earth; the curse of God has hidden it. In the beginning of the world, this Heavenly essence flourished through the earthly essence, just as eternity is within time, and just as the Divine power is through all things and yet is neither grasped nor understood by earthly things in their own selfhood.

6. Every creature brings its clothing <note>meaning its skin, fur, or natural covering</note> with it from the mother’s body; but man comes miserably, naked and bare, in the highest poverty and powerlessness, and is capable of nothing. At his arrival into this world, he is the very poorest and most wretchedly forsaken creature among all kinds, unable to help himself at all. This sufficiently shows us that he was not created by God in this misery, but in his perfection—just like all other creatures. This perfection was squandered by the very first man through false desire. Afterward, God shaped him in his sleep into a natural life as Man and Woman, according to the property of all earthly creatures, in the outward **Let it be** <note>original: *fiat*</note>, and attached to him the **maggot-sack** <term>maggot-sack: (Dutch: *madensak*) A blunt term used by the author to describe the human stomach and intestines, symbolizing the transition from a spiritual body to a mortal, decaying one.</term> with the animal members for reproduction. Because of this, the poor soul is still ashamed today, because it must carry an animal form upon its body.

7. In Adam were two fixed and steady beings: namely, the spiritual body of the love-essence of the inner Heaven, which was the Temple of God; and the outward body, being the **Extract** <note>original: *Limus*; literally "slime" or "clay," referring to the refined spiritual substance of the earth used to create Adam's body.</note> of the earth, which was the clothing and the dwelling-house of the inner spiritual body. This was in no way manifest according to the vanity of the earth, for it was an extract of the good part of the earth, which shall be separated from the vanity of the curse and the corruption of the Devil in the earth during the Last Judgment.

8. These same two beings, namely the inner Heavenly and the outer Heavenly, were bound into one another and contained in one **Body** <note>original: *Corpus*</note>. In the same was the high Holy **Tincture** of the divine fire and light, being the great joyful love-desire that ignited the essence. Thus, those two beings entirely **ardently** <margin>Ardent</margin> desired one another in love-desire and loved themselves; the internal loved the external, being its manifestation and experience, and the external loved the internal, being its greatest sweetness and joy, its noble pearl and most beloved consort. And yet they were not two bodies, but a single one, though of two kinds of **Essences** <term>Essence: (Dutch: *Essens*) The inner spiritual substance or "being" of a person.</term>: namely, an internal Heavenly Holy one, and one from the essence of time, which were **joined** <margin>Married</margin> together in an eternal being.

10. Understand that if Adam had stood firm in the trial, the magical birth would have occurred in this way: not through a specific exit from Adam’s body as is the case today, but just as the Sun shines through water and does not tear it, so the spiritual body—namely, the birth—would have gone out. In that exit, it would have become **Substantial** without effort or distress; it would have occurred on earth in great joy and well-being. Just as both seeds, the man’s and the woman’s, receive a joyful aspect in their * union, so too would the magical pregnancy and birth have been: a virginal image, entirely perfect like the first.

11. This later had to occur through anguish, pain, woe, and distress, once Adam’s **Matrix of Venus** <term>Matrix of Venus: (Latin: *Veneris Matrix*) A term for the creative, feminine principle of desire and manifestation that the author believes resided within the original, non-gendered Adam.</term> was taken from him and formed into a Woman, just as God said to Eve,

> I will add much to your pains when you become pregnant, and with pain shall you now bear children, and your will shall be subject to your husband;

Why? Because she had sprouted from the will of the man. Eve was half of Adam—specifically that part in which Adam was meant to love and impregnate himself. That same part was taken from him in sleep when he did not withstand the trial, and it was formed into a wife. Therefore, Adam said when he saw her: "She shall be called **Woman-man** <note>original Dutch: *manninne*, a feminine version of the word 'man,' emphasizing that she was derived from the male body</note>, because she was taken from the man."

12. Humans would have gone naked on earth, for the heavenly quality penetrated the external, and that was his clothing. He stood in great beauty, joy, and delight, in a childlike frame of mind. He would have eaten and drunk in a magical fashion—not into the body as happens now, but in the mouth, for there was the separation; for such was the nature of the Paradisiacal fruit.

# Chapter 18, Of the Paradisiacal Rule.

13. It was all made for his delight; in him there was no sleep, for the night was to him as the day, because he saw with **transfigured eyes** in his own light. The internal man—namely, the internal eye—saw through the external, just as we shall have no need for the Sun in the world to come, for there we see within the **Divine seeing**. In the light of his own nature, neither heat nor cold would have troubled him, nor would any winter have been made manifest on earth, for in Paradise there was a constant, equal temperance.

14. The **Tincture** <term>Tincture: In Böhmean thought, the spiritual life-force or "quintessence" that gives quality and beauty to matter.</term> of the earth would have been their play; they would have had all things for their play until the time that God would have changed the external world. No fear nor terror would have been in them, nor any Law governing anything or leading to anything, for all things would have been free to them. Adam would have been their great Prince, and they would have lived in the world and yet also in Heaven, dwelling in both worlds at once; Paradise would have been spread throughout the whole world.

15. But since **Divine Providence** well knew that Adam would not endure—because the earth had been corrupted by its former prince <note>A reference to Lucifer, who in this theology was the original ruler of the earthly realm before his rebellion.</note>—and because the **wrath of God** <note>original: *grimmigheyt Gods*; refers to the harsh, contracting quality of divine energy when separated from love.</note> had been stirred and had captured the essence in a harsh impression, God created all kinds of fruits and animals. He also created all kinds of medicines for the future sicknesses of men, and all kinds of food, so that man might have nourishment and clothing in this world.

16. For He had decided to send another Prince, through whom He would deliver man from his sickness and death, and to purify and sweep the earth through the fire of God, and lead it back into the Holy state, just as it was when Lucifer was an Angel, before he entered into such a [corrupt] creation.

17. And Adam was created in nothing else but the divine image, which was to be eternal; and even though it was known within the wrath of God that man would fall, yet the **Regenerator** was also known in God’s love. To this Regenerator, this **Hierarchy** <note>original: *Hierarchia*; the cosmic order or sacred government of the world.</note> would be given as a princely possession in Lucifer’s place.

18. But so that the fall should not proceed from God's decree, God created man perfect and placed him in Paradise, and there ordained him, and forbade him the false lust, which the devil—through the **Slime of the earth** <note>original Latin: *Limum terrae*</note>—awakened in Adam’s external body with his false imagination and hunger-desire.

19. And Adam stood in temptation in Paradise for forty days before the creation of Eve, before God made the woman out of him; had he stood firm, God would have thus confirmed him for all eternity.

But that I write of forty days, contrary to the custom of other writers <note>original: *Scribenten*; refers to biblical commentators or theologians of the time.</note>, for this we have knowledge and cause, not only by opinion, but from other knowledge, of which we shall show you examples; namely, with Moses on Mount Sinai, when God gave him the law, it occurred in forty days, and Israel was tested to see if they would remain in obedience to God; but as they made a Calf and an Idol and fell away from God, so Moses had to break the first tables of the law. This same thing points to the first Adam in the Divine law, who fell away from it, and so that same law was broken for him, and he fell into the breaking of his body, just as Moses broke the tables, and just as God gave another writing on a sphere <term>sphere: original *kogel*. In this mystical context, it refers to a central point or a "globe" of divine substance, often used to describe the "center" of the heart or the tablets of the heart.</term> to Moses.

21. 22. The second figure of Adam in Paradise is the forty years in the wilderness, where Israel was tested in the law with the Heavenly Manna, to see if they would be obedient to God, so that the wrath would not consume so many of them.

26. For these forty days, Adam stood in his innocence during the trial, to see if he would and could persist in possessing Lucifer’s throne as a hierarch <note>original: *Hirarcha*; a high-ranking spiritual ruler</note> and Prince of God; but since God recognized that it would not happen, He resolved—through His deepest love—to move within this Adamic angelic image of the internal holy man (who shimmered within Adam) and to bear him anew. 28. Here he was tempted in soul and in body, pulled by all three principles, as each wanted to bring forth its wonders through him.

29. It was not that the principles in Adam stood in unequal measure or weight; they were in him in equal balance. However, they were not so outside of him. Furthermore, the devil was working within the wrath of God in the first principle through his false desire, and he continually led his imagination <note>original: *imaginatie*; the spiritual power to form an internal image or "longing."</note> into the soul and into the external flesh—namely, into the clay-matter <note>original: *Limum*; referring to the "dust of the ground" from which man was formed.</note> of the earth. He worked in the first principle (that is, in the fiery property of the soul, in eternal nature) from which the first principle in the soul was moved to mirror itself in the devil's imagination. Specifically, this was in the magical birth: to contemplate what was evil and good, and how it tasted and existed in the inequality of the essences <note>original: *Essents*; the fundamental spiritual "flavors" or qualities of being.</note>, from which a lust arose in the soul.

30. 32. 33. And Adam did not eat of it with his mouth; he ate of it only with his imagination or desire. Through this, the heavenly tincture <term>tincture: the spiritual radiance or "life-essence" that gives a being its divine quality</term>—which stood in a fiery love—faded away <note>original: *verblikte*; literally "flickered" or "paled"</note>; and the earthly properties in the character of the outward soul woke up, by which the heavenly image was darkened.

34. At that moment, the Magic Birth was at an end. Even though Adam stood in Paradise, it was of no use to him; for through his imagination, or his hunger for good and evil, the outward man within him woke up and took rule. There, the beautiful image of Adam fell into impotence <note>original: *onmagt*; a state of spiritual swoon or powerlessness</note> and drew toward the rest of its workings; for the heavenly tincture was captured in the earthly desire. The outward desire impressed its essence from the vanity into the form <note>original: *fig*; likely an abbreviation for *figura* or "form"</note>, by which the man was darkened and lost his bright eyes and constant vision—meaning the eyes from the Divine Essence <note>original: *Essents*</note>, through which he had previously seen.

35. So Moses now says: "God has spoken: it is not good that this man should be alone; we will make him a helper to be with him." # THE 19th CHAPTER.
## *Of the building of the Woman; how man was ordained to the outward natural life.*

And Moses says: God let a deep sleep fall upon the man, and he fell asleep, and He took a rib from his side, and built the woman from it, and closed the place with flesh; Moses says that the woman is made from a rib, from Adam's side. Who can understand this without the light of God? But here Moses places the veil of his clarity <note>A reference to the "Veil of Moses," a theological concept suggesting that the literal stories of the Bible hide deeper, mystical truths from those who are not spiritually ready.</note> before the eyes, because of the unworthiness of the animalistic man.

2. For we find that the woman was conceived and formed in the *fiat* <term>fiat: the creative "let it be" or the formative power of God's will</term> out of Adam's essence, out of body and soul; but the rib signifies the breaking of Adam—namely, that the same body must and would break. For in the place of that same rib, the *Spear of Longinus* <note>original: *Lance van Longenus*; refers to the Roman soldier who pierced Jesus' side on the Cross</note> had to enter afterward at the *Cross* of *Christ*, and tincture <term>tincture: to spiritually transform or "re-color" a substance through divine influence</term> and heal the breach in the wrath of God with Heavenly blood.

3. When Adam now stood in his hunger for earthliness, he imprinted into his beautiful image the vanity of evil and good through his magical or magnetic power. Through this, the Heavenly image—of the essence of the angelic world—faded away, just as if one introduced a different matter into a bright light, from which the light itself becomes dark and finally is completely extinguished. It happened to Adam in the same way, for he led his will and desire away from God into "selfhood" <note>original: *selfheyd*; the state of being focused on the ego rather than the divine</note> and vanity, and broke himself off from God, namely from the Divine *Harmony*.

4. There he immediately sank down into the powerlessness of sleep—that is, into an incapacity which signifies death. For the image of God is unchangeable and does not sleep; in that which is eternal, there is no time. But with sleep, "time" became manifest in man, for he fell asleep to the angelic world and woke up to the outward <note>physical/material</note> world.

### Cap. 20. and the destruction of man.

9. Now the question is: why did the devil deceive Eve specifically through the serpent, and not through something else? Could he not have done so in his own form? Why did he speak to Eve specifically through the serpent, and why did the serpent lean against the tree to persuade Eve against God’s commandment?

10. Here Moses again places a veil <note>original: "dexel"; literally a "lid" or "cover," referring to the use of allegorical language that hides deeper spiritual truths from the uninitiated</note> before his clear eyes, for he describes the history quite correctly; yet how can one who is unenlightened understand it? For he speaks of the serpent, saying that Eve spoke with the serpent and was deceived by it, though a serpent cannot speak, nor is it anything other than an animal without divine understanding. It could not have known the image of God within itself, much less understood the heavenly powers or the prohibition.

11. But hear what Moses says: the serpent was more cunning than all the animals of the field that the Lord God had made. Here the question is first: from where did its cunning come, such that the devil wanted to speak and deceive Eve specifically through its cunning? Herein lies the *Mystery*.

12. When God, according to his spoken word, moved in the *Word "Let there be"* <note>original: "verbum fiat"; the divine command of creation from Genesis</note> toward both internal worlds—that is, toward God’s love and his wrath, toward the eternal nature of darkness and the eternal nature and power of light—then all properties, both evil and good, compacted themselves. For the *fiat* <note>the creative "let it be" power</note> was in all properties: in those belonging to the *center* <note>original: "centrum"; the core of nature where the divine fire resides</note> as well as in those where the divine power was manifest in holiness, just as the unlocking was in every point. Because there was a desire for the revelation of the great *Mystery* of all beings, the *fiat* (being the first form of nature) took an essence or *clay* <note>original: "Limum"; the "dust" or "slime" of the earth used in creation</note> from the earth, as well as from above the earth in every magical constellation, according to the degrees of separation. And so, in that same essence, a Spirit was formed according to that same degree or magical constellation; and the *fiat* figured a body exactly as that Spirit was.

13. Since Prince Lucifer sat in divine splendor like a *Hierarch* <note>original: "Hierarcha"; a high-ranking angelic prince</note>, and since he wanted to rule in divine power over and in everything with the power of fire, and since he despised love and humility and entered with his false desire into the essence of the spoken word, into the *fiat*, like a juggler <note>original: "googelaar"; here meaning a false creator or a deceiver who mimics God's power for selfish ends</note> who also wanted to form and create, he infected that same essence. This happened specifically according to the property of the dark world (which also entered into the *fiat* during the *coagulation* <note>the process of spiritual essence becoming solid matter</note>, that is, into an essence where good and evil were suspended together). For he (meaning the devil) desired the greatest cunning from the *center* of nature, like a fallen juggler, and he wanted to rule in the revealed *magic* <note>original: "magia"; the creative, shaping power of the will</note> within the *fiat*.

This does not mean she had entirely taken the essence of the dark world into her own essence; no. But as God said to her, "You shall die"—that is, die to the heavenly kingdom, or fade away. For the Kingdom of Heaven does not contain any true death within itself; only, when the light of the divine principle <note>The fundamental source of life or "First Principle" in Boehme's cosmology</note> is extinguished, then the very being from which it burned and shone becomes mute, as if dead, without feeling or understanding, like a nothing. It is like when a candle burns in a dark place and lights up an entire room; if it is extinguished, it leaves no trace behind, and its power vanishes into nothing—just as God made all things out of nothing.

28. This is not to be understood as if the heavenly being <term>ens</term> <note>Latin for "being" or "essence"</note> of man had become a nothing; it remained within man, but in his life, it became as if it were nothing. For it stood hidden in God and was incomprehensible to man without life. In God, it does not die, but in human life, the holy being <note>original: "ens"</note> faded away.

# THE 22ND CHAPTER.
## Of the origin of actual sins, and of the awakening of the wrath of God in the human property <term>property</term> <note>original: "eygenschap," a central term in Boehmian mysticism referring to the specific quality, nature, or inherent characteristic that defines a being or state of existence.</note>.

1. Scripture says that God has made all things through his word, and without the same nothing is made of that which is made (John 1). From his outspoken word, which became substantial in the **"word let-it-be"** <note>original Latin: "verbum fiat," referring to the creative command "Let there be" in Genesis.</note>, all things have proceeded into forms: first into an *essence* <term>essence</term> <note>original: "ens," a philosophical term for a fundamental being or entity before it takes physical shape.</note>, or a desire for a specific property, and from that same property into a compaction of *Sulfur*, *Mercury*, and *Salt* <note>These are the three alchemical principles (the *tria prima*). In this context, they represent spiritual forces: Sulfur as the fire/will, Mercury as the movement/word, and Salt as the physical substance or "body."</note>; namely, into a formed nature. And from that same *essence* in the formed nature, the word became a creaturely life, and it carries itself out from the compaction of *Sulfur*, *Mercury*, and *Salt*—out from the *body* <note>original Latin: "corpus."</note>—that is, it reveals itself in a resonant being <note>original: "luydbaar wefen," suggesting that the physical world is a "sounding out" or audible manifestation of God's internal thought.</note>, for which purpose God created nature and the creature.

2. Thus every creature has a *center* within itself for its own "out-speaking," or the sound of the formed word, both of the eternal and of the temporal, the irrational animals as well as man; for the first *essence* was spoken out from the sound of God, through Wisdom, from the center toward the fire and light, and was grasped in the **"let-it-be"** <note>original: "fiat."</note> and entered into a compaction.

3. That same *essence* is from the eternal, but the compaction of the four Elements is from time; thus in every thing an eternal [property] lies hidden in time, whether in the living or the non-living, in the *Elements* and creatures, in things that grow and things that stand still. In every one is the first *essence*, from which the form of the compaction (which arose from time) originates, being an eternal word speaking from the eternal. Through Wisdom, it is spoken from the being of the Spiritual world into a time; that is, into a formed being according to the Spiritual *essence*, which *essence* can be destroyed by no *Element* or by anything at all.

4. And although the Elemental compaction of the *body* <note>original Latin: "corpus."</note> perishes and becomes nothing—because it had a temporal beginning—(which body the *essence* has drawn to itself, that is, has breathed out <note>original German: *Ausgehaucht*.</note> from itself like an external degree), nevertheless the first *essence* cannot perish, just as one then sees that all things return again into their first mother from which they arose and proceeded; namely, into the four *Elements*.

6. Thus we now see today with great misery how it goes with us: that even if we wish to speak (though the intelligent word may take hold in the innermost *essence* and wish to reveal the truth), the awakened vanity in the earthly *mud* of the body immediately takes hold and *interacts* within its own property. Consequently, the word of human understanding speaks out from itself <gloss>projects or babbles out</gloss> <note>original Dutch/German: "Ausballet."</note> lies, evil, falsehood, and sharp-witted frivolity. When the spoken word is a false word from a false *essence*, it is infected by the Devil and sealed for destruction; it is also taken into the *Mystery* <term>mystery</term> <note>original: "Mysterium," here referring to the hidden source or dimension of the dark world.</note> of wrath, which is the property of the dark world. From that source every thing arises, and it is the same with its *essence*.

8. They form their swearing and cursing, along with all **frivolous talk** <margin>Extravagant talk.</margin> that occurs there in the serpent's essence, and they sow into the wrath of God. In contrast, all the children of God—to whom this is a serious matter—form their words in the holy essence, especially in prayer. When the free will of the soul takes hold of itself in the Holy essence—which was opened through the humanity of Christ—it forms the true, substantial word of God within itself, so that it becomes a **substance** <note>original: "substantie"; a spiritual reality or "matter."</note>.

51. Therefore Paul says: *The Spirit of God helps us mightily before God, according to His good pleasure,* for the Spirit of God is formed in the desire for the Holy Word. He is taken hold of, and this "taking hold" is what Christ meant when He said: *He would give us His flesh for food and His blood for drink.*

52. The soul's will takes hold of the **essence** <term>ens</term> of Christ, and in Christ’s essence is the Word of Christ which became man. This same Word takes hold of the soul's desire, or the **vessel** <note>original: "fat"; likely meaning the container or form of the soul.</note> within its (in Adam, tarnished) holy essence. Here Adam stands in Christ, and he becomes Christ according to the Heavenly **essence** and according to the Divine Word; and from this essence of Christ, Divine knowledge proceeds from the Word of God.

53. In such a way, the children of God are temples of the Holy Spirit who dwells within them, and thus they speak God’s word. Outside of this, there is no true knowing or willing, but only fables and **Babel** <note>original: "babel"; referring to the Tower of Babel, signifying spiritual confusion or the "jumble" of human religious systems.</note>, a confusion of the crafty serpent.

### On the origin of actual sins. Chapter 22.

54. Therefore Christ calls the Pharisees a generation of vipers and a brood of snakes, even though they were the High Priests; for he knew them in their **Essence** <term>Essens</term> <note>The inner, fundamental nature or "being" of a person.</note>, seeing that they had formed their will in the **being** <term>ens</term> <note>original: "ens"; a Latin term for "being" or "essence" used frequently in 17th-century philosophy.</note> of the serpent. They carried the words of Moses in their mouths, and therein they mixed the **being** of the serpent—as still happens today with many, where the "Man-Devil" carries God's word on his tongue, yet only uses it to hide the **being** of the serpent. He introduces the **being** of the devil into the literal word, from which "Babel," the mother of all spiritual harlotry, is born: a mere quarreling over words, where the **Being** of the Devil and the serpent runs against the Divine **being** in the formed Divine word.

55. Yet it must happen this way, so that the formed and understood word may be sharpened and practiced in the children of God, and the truth may be exalted. Dear brothers, Adam and Eve bequeathed such a state to us, and that is the reason why the body must die and completely perish, and go back into its first **being**; for the **being** of the serpent must be entirely removed; it cannot inherit the kingdom of God.

56. 61. ->How God called Adam and his Eve again. Chapter 23.<-

# CHAPTER 23.

### How God called Adam and his Eve again after they had entered into sin and vanity, and had awakened in the serpent's essence <term>ens</term> <note>original: "ens"; a term used in mystical philosophy to describe the fundamental "being" or "spiritual substance" of a thing.</note>, and how He imposed on them the order of this troublesome world and ordained the serpent-treader <note>A reference to the "seed of the woman" in Genesis 3:15, traditionally interpreted as Christ, who would crush or "tread" the head of the serpent.</note> as a help.

1. When Adam and Eve had eaten from the tree of knowledge of good and evil, and had become monstrous <note>Meaning they lost their original divine form and took on a "monstrous" or corrupted earthly shape.</note> because of the serpent, Moses writes of it thus: Their eyes were opened, and they became aware that they were naked, and they sewed fig leaves together and made themselves aprons. There, the soul recognized the monstrous image and felt ashamed, because in its tender body such a coarse animal had awakened—with coarse flesh and hard bones, and a bestial maggot-sack <note>original: "maden sak"; a vivid Baroque term for the mortal, decaying physical body, often used by the mystic Jacob Böhme.</note> of vanity. And they wanted to hide the same from the eyes of God, and because of their shame, they hid behind the trees, so greatly did they shame themselves for the deformity of the beast; for the animal essence <term>ens</term> had swallowed the heavenly one and exalted itself to the highest place, which they had not known before; therefore, they did not know what to do out of shame.

2. The serpent’s cunning did not want to cover the shame here, but rather revealed it all the more, and accused them as apostates and unfaithful ones; for the wrath of God awakened within them and placed them there before Him for strict judgment, to swallow them up into the dark world, just as happened to Lucifer.

3. And here is the place where the earth trembled at the death of Christ, and the rocks were rent asunder; here, the wrath of God enclosed the holy essence <term>ens</term> of heavenly humanity within death—which Christ enclosed again <note>Meaning He "locked it back up" or overcame it.</note> when He broke death upon the cross, for which the grimness <note>The fierce quality of divine wrath or judgment.</note> in the curse of the earth and in the rocky cliffs trembled.

4. And here was the heavy state before the wrath of God, in which state Christ in the garden—when He prayed and was to overcome this wrath—sweated bloody sweat, when He said: "Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me; but if it be not possible unless I drink it, then let Your will be done."

<meta>This page continues the theological explanation of the Fall and Redemption. ->How God called Adam and his Eve again. Chapter 23.<-

5. This fierce wrath, which had awakened in the essence <term>ens</term> <note>original: "effents" (essence/ens); a term used in mystical philosophy to describe the fundamental spiritual substance or "being" of a person.</note> of Adam, had to be drunk by Christ in His holy heavenly essence on the cross, and transformed with great love into divine joy. The drink of gall and vinegar—a mixed drink given to Him by the Jews—was an outward sign of what was occurring inwardly within Christ's humanity.

6. For the outward image of man also had to be delivered from wrath and death, and rise again from the earth; therefore, the outward humanity of Christ, belonging to the kingdom of this world, also had to drink from this cup which God the Father, in His wrath, had poured out for Adam. Christ had to drink it to the dregs and turn that wrath into love. Therefore Christ said: "If it be possible, let this cup pass from me" <note>A reference to the prayer of Jesus in the Garden of Gethsemane (Matthew 26:39).</note>; but it was not possible to overcome the wrath unless the sweet name of Jesus drank it in and changed it into joy. Consequently, Christ says: "Father, your will be done, and not the will of my humanity."

7. God's will was meant to be done in Adam as well, but through the serpent's cunning, he elevated his own will to the highest place. This same self-will <term>selfheid</term> <note>A term denoting egoism or the independent will of the creature separated from God.</note> the humanity of Christ now had to surrender to the wrath of God on the Cross to be devoured. For the fiery property of the soul entered into the earthly realm with lust, and from that same virginity—through the attachment of all three principles <note>The three principles are typically the dark world (fire/wrath), the light world (love/spirit), and the outward world (nature/matter).</note>—the woman was made. And the woman made herself monstrous toward the serpent and corrupted the virginal matrix; through her lust, she introduced a beastly <note>original: "vehiſche"; referring to the animalistic or brutish nature of the fallen human body.</note>, monstrous, and serpent-like matrix into it, infected with the devil's will and desire.

37. Now, this Holy virginal matrix in Eve was captured by the monstrous property, and the image within her faded <note>original: "verblikte"; meaning the heavenly luster or "being" grew pale or lost its divine brilliance.</note> from the heavenly *ens*. And into this very same heavenly *ens*—understand this as the true virginal seed of chastity, discipline, and purity, which in Eve was captured by the monstrous serpent and the fleshly whore-desire—the Word of God promised itself with the Holy, highly-honored name *Jesus*. It promised that it would again introduce living heavenly *ens* into this imprisoned, faded *ens*, and would crush the head of the serpent's *ens* (which is the whore-monster), kill its desire, and cast away the whore-image. It would overwhelm the ignited wrath of God in this virginal center <note>original: "centrum"; the spiritual point of origin within a person.</note> with the highest love of God, and completely kill and do away with the monster. This is what God meant when He said: *the seed of the woman shall crush the serpent's head.*

38. Understand this rightly: the virginal seed of Eve, through the Word of God, in the name and in the sweet power of *Jesus*, would do this. The seed contained within the covenant of God, from which the virginal child was born—like the dew from the dawn—would accomplish it.

39. For it is not the child born from the blood of man or woman that would inherit the kingdom of heaven, but that which comes from the virginal *ens* in the sign of the covenant, from the promised Word of God. The child of the man and the woman is a monster, and it must die and perish in the earth. But the virginal *ens*, which lies hidden within this monster, is the true seed from which the children of Christ are born, even in this present time. For the life of this child is the true faith and the great divine desire.

40. This same virginal child lives in the children of Christ, in the spirit and in the flesh of Christ, in a spiritual body; but on the outside, it is covered by the monster, the child of the whore and the serpent. There is no human being who does not carry this outward serpent-child upon themselves.

And just as the <term>Artist</term> <note>original: "konstenaar"; likely referring to an Alchemist or God as the Master Craftsman</note> brings forth beautiful gold out of the earth, so too the human gold lies buried in the earth, awaiting the <term>Artist</term> for the resurrection.

### On the Curse of the Earth, Chapter 24

6. This same property shall be tested in the fire of God, whether it has impressed into itself a fixed, enduring property of the Divine <term>ens</term>, or a hellish property; all of this shall be tested in the fire of God. And just as the <term>ens</term> is within each body, such a fire shall also ignite itself within that same <term>ens</term>.

7. And just as the <term>quicksilver</term> <note>original: "Quiksilver"; mercury, which evaporates when heated</note> evaporates in the fire, so too shall all the godless, devilish work of the serpent—which was impressed from the dark world and the devil's desire—[evaporate].

8. It is like a glowing wick that labors toward the fire; or like the precious gold enclosed within a coarse stone or within lead, awaiting the <term>artist</term> <note>original: "konstenaar"; here referring to the Alchemist or God as the Great Physician who refines the soul</note> to release it; so also shall be the resurrection of the human body from the earth.

9. Thus we now understand the body of sickness, and also its Physician; for when the heavenly <term>ens</term> grew dim and was captured by the earthly, like gold in lead, then the outward <term>constellations</term> <note>original: "gesternte"; the "stars" or astral influences that govern the physical world and the lower mind</note> awoke in the body. And just as the outward constellations now break the <term>ens</term> of one another and transmute it into another, all according to the power of the greatest; so also the human mind (which is likewise a magical constellation) is governed by this, as is the body. It is thereby led into strange desires and lusts, from which it becomes sick and tormented, and where one introduced <term>ens</term>—whether through food, thought, or worry—torments and weakens the other.

10. This is evident in how man torments and sickens himself most of all in the "star-mind" through desire, even plaguing himself for that which he cannot obtain—that which is not revealed in his "constellation" and which his constellation cannot grasp or receive. Because of this, the false, introduced desire of the foreign "constellation" plagues itself and torments itself day and night; from this, great greed arises, so that man desires something of such a kind and introduces it into his constellation.

### Ch. 24. And of the body of sickness, how it arose. 155

...introduces, which is a harmful poison and plague to him; he can create nothing fixed or lasting through foreign material within himself that can endure for eternity.

11. All that the soul's own constellation <note>original: "gefternte"; in Böhme's thought, this refers to the internal "astral" or spiritual configuration of a person’s life</note> (being the true constellation of life) impresses upon itself from the foreign constellation is false and a contradiction. From this arises enmity—that is, the great envy in nature—because the human mind wants to rule over the foreign <term>ens</term> <note>original: "ens"; the essential spiritual substance or "being" of a person</note>. If it cannot achieve this, that same foreign, introduced <term>ens</term> burns within him in a spiritual way, like a poisonous, hungry, envious fire that begrudges another what it wishes to possess itself.

12. And though it may happen that it can attract or possess [this foreign power] through the cunning of the serpent, it still has no fundamental seat in its true constellation of life, for the soul is not receptive to such a thing. Instead, the false desire sets it above itself as a king and boasts of it as its own God, who has usurped foreign power and sits upon foreign violence. From this arises the pride of wealth, and self-attained honor and power; and in its ground and origin, all of this arose from the devil through the <term>ens</term> of the serpent. He also, out of his own <term>ens</term> and with a free will, entered into foreign desire, through which he introduced and awakened within himself the hellish pains of sickness with a foreign <term>ens</term>, so that the constellation of his life went out of balance <note>original: "uyt de gelykheid"; literally "out of equality," meaning a loss of harmony or temperance</note> and entered into a bewitching property; so it also goes with the fallen man.

13. But now man has his healing, while the devil does not; for when Divine Providence recognized that man would not endure, He let all kinds of medicine grow for him out of the earth to resist the introduced foreign property, both of the constellation and of the elements. And to the mind, God has given His Holy Word as a healing, so that the mind might sink itself into that same Word and, through the power of the Word, continually reject the introduced foreign loathsomeness.

14. And if this does not happen, but instead the soul remains in the introduced foreign <term>ens</term> (which the devil continually introduces through the image of the serpent), then the foreign <term>ens</term> becomes a substance and surrounds the enclosed <term>ens</term> of the essence of the Heavenly world. Thus, the same Ens of the Divine property remains obscured in death <note>original: "verblikkert"; dimmed or extinguished, like a light failing to shine through a thick covering</note>...

### Of the Curse of the Earth, Ch. 24. 156

...and it cannot reach the dwelling place of God. From this follows eternal death, as can be seen in the case of Lucifer; for his divine <term>ens</term> <note>original: "ens"; the essential spiritual substance or "being" of a person</note> is also locked in the "nothing"—that is, in the greatest hiddenness—so that within his magical constellation <note>original: "geſternte"; the internal spiritual or "astral" configuration of a person’s soul</note>, in his creaturely nature, he cannot reach the dwelling place of God.

15. Therefore, it is necessary for man to sink himself entirely into the promised, indwelling Word of God, and to continually cast away the foreign, introduced essence which the devil brings into his mind (whereby he desires things that are foreign to him). He should accept nothing else but what he can obtain in virtuous truth and with an honest appearance—that which falls to him in his calling through the body’s necessity. This is brought to him by his own true constellation of life, and thus he is receptive to it; it causes him no torment or pain, provided he does not allow pride, greed, or the wrath of the serpent to enter into it.

16. And it is the greatest folly for a man to torment himself for the sake of foreign things, taking into his desire that which does nothing but harm him and ultimately banishes him from God, closing off his heavenly <term>ens</term> in both body and soul. Of what use is that which he sees outside of himself, exalting himself in a mirrored glitter <note>original: "ſpiegel glans"; referring to a false, external brilliance or vanity</note>, when he is not truly receptive to it? That which he then takes on, he turns into a temporal and eternal torment and unrest for himself.

17. God created man naked and gave him nothing in this world of which he should or may say, "this is mine." While everything is indeed his, it is held in common; for God created only one single man, and to that same individual he gave everything that was in the world. Now, all people are surely descended from that same single man; he is the trunk, and the others are his branches. They all draw strength from their trunk and bring forth fruit upon the single root. Every branch enjoys the *ens* of the tree, just as they all equally enjoy the four elements and the constellations.

18. What folly is it, then, for the branch to want to be its own tree, shooting up like a foreign growth as if its fellow-branch did not also stand in the same trunk? It is the introduced *ens* of the serpent which leads the branches on the tree of human life away from the single human life. Every branch, in a particular hunger, wants to be its own tree, under its own power and rule. For this reason, it desires the abundance of this world as its own property, so that it [himself]...

For in it you serve only the root upon which you stand: in your labor, you bear the fruit of the root, which you must leave standing free, using your office to serve your brother and help increase his sap, so that he may grow up alongside you and bear fruit.

21. In all selfhood and selfishness <note>original: "eygenheid"; the quality of being focused on the self</note>, there is a false growth. One brother must be the ¶ physician <note>original: "Artzt"</note> and refreshment of the other, and quiet his mind by introducing his will of love. There would be enough for everyone in this world if greed did not pull it into selfishness, but instead allowed one's brother to have as much as oneself, letting go of pride—which surely comes from the Devil.

22. Otherwise, with great pride and worry for the belly <note>meaning material greed or physical sustenance</note>, he runs nowhere else but to the devil in the abyss. He wishes to be noble and better than his brother: from where will he obtain such a thing? God, after all, has given only one single life to mankind, and from that one, the life of all people proceeds.

23. But for him to imagine a greater nobility within himself and to flaunt it—such is an apostasy from God and His Word. For in the Word of God was the one life of man; the Word breathed this into the created image, and this same one life is from eternity and has never had a beginning. Why then does man introduce a foreign life into it, which disturbs the one life?

# ->Concerning the Curse of the Earth, Chapter 24.<-

...therefore it must simply come to this: either that he, with his will and desire, enters again into the one and childlike life and leaves behind all that was introduced <note>The "introduced" refers to the false desires and ego-driven nature that humanity took on after the Fall.</note>; or that he remains eternally in unrest within that introduced essence.

24. If then I must leave behind everything that I have introduced to myself as my own property, and if the same is nothing other than my own harm, why do I not leave that same false desire which introduces death and this hellish torment into me? It is better, then, to break the desire now, rather than later breaking the substance with great pain; for it is a very painful process when a person, through an earnest turning back into the childlike life, must break the substance within themselves.

25. But if the free will breaks the desire and lust in the beginning, so that the lust does not become substantial <note>original: "weſentlyk"; meaning to take on a solid, essential form in the soul</note>, then already the <term>Master Physician</term> <note>original: "Medicyn Mr."; a reference to Christ as the healer of the soul</note> is born. Then there is no need for such great earnestness as must be undertaken by one who must go out from his own created abominations and leave and break the essence he has made within his mind <note>original: "gemoet"; the inner disposition or soul-center</note>. Yet it must eventually come to that, or he cannot reach the gate of eternal life which God gave to mankind; and if he does not reach that, then he also does not reach the gate of God.

26. For the "one life" must be introduced into the **nothing**, outside of all creature and essence; for it has its eternal origin from the **nothing**—that is, from the Divine understanding. When it exists in the **something**, it is in torment, unless its "something" stands directed with its desire toward the **nothing**; then it is a joy for the life of the "something," because the life of the **nothing** may dwell and work within the "something."

27. For God is like a **nothing** to the creature <note>To Böhme, God is "Nothing" not because He doesn't exist, but because He is beyond all physical "things," definitions, and limits—He is the *Ungrund* or the abyss of potential.</note>; but if the creature has introduced its desire into Him (understand: into the **nothing**), then the creature becomes something out of the **nothing**. And the **nothing** <margin>Rules/Governs</margin> and works in the "something" of the creature, and the creature in the **nothing**. In such a working, no <term>turba</term> <note>original: "turba"; Latin for "disturbance" or "uproar." In Böhme's philosophy, it is the spirit of wrath or chaos that destroys the harmony of life.</note> can arise, for it is His own love-play, which loves itself, and it stands with its life at the end of nature.

28. Thus we understand what Adam has bequeathed to us: namely, the curse and vain desire. We regard the outward man in his life as a monster of a true human life, unless the noble mind is born anew in the spirit of **Christ** <note>original: "Christi"; Latin genitive of Christ</note>; otherwise, the outward center in the mind is a serpent.

32. Thus a divine person must have enmity within himself and trample the monster (being the child of the serpent) underfoot, and continually kill it. This same seed of the serpent in man is the **Devil’s riding horse** and his fortress, wherein he can dwell within man.

# THE 25th CHAPTER.

## How God drove Adam and Eve out of Paradise and placed the Cherub before the Garden.

1. When God had cursed the serpent, as well as the earth, then the animal-man was no longer of use in Paradise, for he could no longer enjoy the fruit of Paradise. At that time, He laid upon him the labor and toil of the world, and drove him out of the Garden of Eden, and placed the Cherub with the flaming sword of judgment before it. This was so that, should the newborn Virgin's child <note>Refers to the Christ-nature or the "New Man" born within the believer</note> from the seed of the woman come again and enter into Paradise, this Angel with the flaming sword would cut off the serpent-animal <note>The corrupt, worldly nature acquired at the Fall</note> from it, and no longer let it into Paradise.

2. This Angel with the sword is the true striking Angel, who carries death and life in his sword; he has within the same the love and the wrath of God. And so, when man dies in this world, he then comes before the gate of Paradise, before this Angel; there the soul must pass through this judgment.

3. If the soul is now imprisoned in the wrath of God, it cannot pass through this judgment. However, if it is a Virgin's child, born from the seed of the woman, then it can pass through that same sword; for then the Angel cuts off the animal, which is bred from the serpent's *essence* <note>original: "ens"</note>. Thus the soul is then an Angel of God, and serves Him in His temple in Paradise, and awaits the day of judgment, which is the resurrection of the outward body; when this Angel with the flaming sword [cleanses] the earth from—

# How God Drove Adam and Eve out of Paradise, Chapter 25.

...since the good [principle] within the enclosed earth was without a heavenly creature—because its former prince had been cast out—God created Adam as another *Hierarch* <note>original: Hierarcha; a high-ranking spiritual ruler or governor</note> out of this good *essence* <note>original: ens; a philosophical term for the fundamental "being" or "substance" of a thing</note> to be a ruler of this place. From this arose the Devil's envy against humanity and all the good creatures of this world.

20. But now we must contemplate the human fall and the sword of the Cherub; for *Paul* says we were provided for in *Christ Jesus* before the foundation of the world was laid. Here, the saying of *Paul* is fitting: God knew that this very *essence* <note>original: ens</note> from which Adam was to be created already contained something of a "false-longing," a corruption introduced by the Devil's desire. Therefore, before the foundation of the world, God provided for this *clay* <note>original: limum; referring to the biblical "dust of the ground"</note> from which He intended to make man. He did so because He wanted to lead man through the judgment of the fiery sword—through death and through fire—to burn away the false longing entirely. In His highest love, in His Word, in *Jehovah*—that is, revealed from *Jehovah* through *Jesus*—He would bring about a new birth, introducing a new *clay* <note>original: limum</note> into the longing soul, and lead them together through the judgment of the fiery sword to make them entirely pure.

He also broke the sting of death which was present in the *clay* <note>original: limo</note> of the earth, from which Adam was created according to his outward humanity. This fiery sword has its awakened origin in the corruption of *Lucifer*.

### How God drove Adam and Eve out of Paradise. Chap. 25.

28. The word was a <margin>Echoing out <note>original: "Aus hall" (German); suggests a sounding forth or resonance</note></margin> sounding forth out of the spiritual fire- and light-world, from which God names himself—namely, according to the fire, a strong, jealous, and angry God, and according to the light, a merciful, dear God.

29. The Father, being the fire-world, surely begets the Son, being the light-world; because the word in the fire-world was then ignited fiercely by the movement of God toward creation—as can be seen in the <term>solidification</term> <note>original: "coagulatie"; the process of spiritual substance becoming dense, physical matter</note> of stones—if we were not blocks and had more than the understanding of a calf, how could that same fire have been brought back into the light in the same <term>harmony</term> <note>original: "concordantie"</note>? Especially the ignited essence in the solidification; there was nothing else but the love of God that had to do it.

30. But how shall a creature now, namely a fire-soul or Angel, enter into a created thing or formation if the fire-source were not especially moveable? There would remain nothing else but an equality within equality; but if it is nothing else but an equality, then it has only its own play, with and in itself, as it has been from eternity. And therefore the unchangeable God moved himself according to fire and light, and awakened the property of the fire, so that he might make for himself a play—that is, a "conceived word" out of himself—which would be a play for and in the unformed word.

31. Here we now understand that if the ignited essence from which the earth and man were created had been introduced back into the unformed word—that is, entirely into equality, into love—then no creature could have been born; for a zealous soul-spirit must be a moveable fire, as are also the Angels and everything that lives.

### Chapter 25. And the Cherub placed before the Garden.

32. Being eternal, God previously moved within His own <term>mystery</term> <note>original: "mysterium"; the hidden, spiritual source of all things</note> with the creation of the angelic thrones. However, this movement had already been ignited and poisoned by the "sigh" <note>Boehme often uses "sigh" or "groan" to describe the initial movement of selfish desire or will</note> of the <term>Hierarch</term> <note>a high-ranking angelic ruler</note> Lucifer. If God had wanted to change this movement into love before He created the earth and man, He would have had to move once again according to the property of fire if He had wished to create another Prince-Angel.

33. But because that could not be, He created the earth, and out of the earth He created man from the first movement. He breathed the fire-soul and light-soul into man from the sound of His revealed and moved Word—namely, from the first movement. For from that first movement of the Word, another Prince was to come into the created Princely throne of Lucifer and occupy that first movement.

34. And in this first movement, God established judgment. He took the sword of rule away from Lucifer within the <term>essence</term> <note>original: "ens"; the fundamental spiritual substance of a thing</note> of heaven and earth and placed it in Adam. Afterward, He introduced the highest love from God through Christ into Adam, bringing the moved Word back into a state of <term>harmony</term> <note>original: "gelykheid"; literally "likeness" or "equality," referring to the restoration of spiritual balance</note>—that is, into an eternal confirmation. He gave Adam, through Christ, the fiery sword to rule over the fallen Prince Lucifer.

35. For Adam, though he was the corrupted <term>slime</term> <note>original: "Limus"; the clay or "dust of the ground" from which man was formed</note> of the earth, would in Christ judge the Prince he once had over him, using this very same generated fire-sword. As Christ tells us, the holy shall judge the world. Understand that the ignited essence of man and the earth would judge the Prince of Lies (who had turned the truth within the holy essence into lies and corrupted it with false desire).

36. But since the essence of man was corrupted and could not achieve this, God brought the most holy essence from His highest hiddenness into the corrupted essence of man—specifically into the heavenly part. He led the outward part through the fiery sword and through death, and the inward part into an eternal harmony. Thus, human <term>reason</term> <note>original: "vernuft"</note> has its mirror here; if it is enlightened by God, it will understand us here; if not, there is no possibility of attaining this knowledge.

37. And we wish to warn the slanderer not to call this blasphemy. Let him first put away his "calf-eyes" and "animal-eyes" and look us in the face before he mocks. This subject requires a different alphabet than what reason uses; it must be born a degree deeper within the soul.

-># How God drove Adam and Eve out of Paradise, etc. Chapter 25.<-

38. Thus we can also better understand the expulsion of Adam, and why he was tempted and driven out of Paradise: because his <term>essence</term> <note>original Latin: "ens"; the fundamental spiritual substance of a being</note> was somewhat ignited by the poison of the Devil, he could not possess Paradise. Therefore, God drove him out through the sword of judgment into death and into perishability; but He gave him the word of promise of His deepest love within the essence of the being of the heavenly world as a firm covenant. In this covenant, Adam and his children had to trust and believe: that at the end of time, God would lead them back from death through the fire-sword into this embodied Word, with the introduction of the Holy essence. He would cleanly cut away the false <term>craving</term> <note>original: "sugt"; refers to a distorted spiritual longing or sighing toward earthly things</note> through the sword of judgment, and bring them in as Angels of God to take the place of the fallen Lucifer. And this is the mystery of the Angel and of the sword of Paradise.

39. This Angel bore the name of the covenant, through which God wished to reveal Jesus, the great Prince. And it is this very same Angel who afterwards performed many miracles on earth; who was with Abel, Enoch, Noah, Shem, Abraham, and Moses; who appeared to Moses in the fire-sword of the flame in the bush; who led Israel out of Egypt and went before them in a pillar of fire by night and a pillar of cloud by day; who gave them the law in the fire; and finally, through Joshua—who was a <term>type</term> <note>original: "voorbeeld"; a prophetic symbol or precursor</note> of Him who would be born from the fire-sword—led them into the land of Israel.

40. This fire-Angel turned his inward light outward and revealed himself in the person of Christ, in humanity with Christ. Being the holy oil of anointing of the deepest, hidden love, he changed the fire-sword of the Angel into a sword of love and into a holy government.

41. And that is the true Cherub, who drove the false Adam out of Paradise, and through Christ—the virgin child, born anew out of Adam in Christ—leads him back in; and it has no other ground or understanding.

8. Why did God not cast Adam away when He saw that he became evil, or turn him to nothing and create a new Adam? 9. This God did not want. 10. Love alone is named God; wrath is named His strength and power. Whatever the free will would now desire, in that same thing it would be confirmed, whether in love or in wrath.

11. For the free will was born out of the love and out of the wrath—that is, out of the fire-world and the light-world—and so it may choose a place for its active life. 12. 13. The Word which had taken on a body had the **fire-sword** <note>The flaming sword held by the Cherub guarding Eden.</note>—which is the **Cherub**—on the outside, and Jesus on the inside. He would overcome the fire-sword with love. Thus the name Jesus stood hidden in the fire-sword and was not revealed until the time that God wished to move Himself therein and reveal Him.

14. But on the other hand, the soul in its free will was manifest in the heavenly, glimmering essence—the sign of the covenant in the word of promise—into which the free will should enter.

### Chapter 26. And of Cain, the firstborn and fratricide.

Whoever seeks the kingdom of God must allow themselves to be persecuted, mocked, despised, and killed by the Cain-like church, just as Cain did to Abel.

26. For the Devil still desires to be a Prince of this world continually, in the children of the serpent; and if the Virgin-child <note>A reference to the "crushing of the serpent's head" (Genesis 3:15), often interpreted by mystics as the birth of Christ-like nature within the human soul.</note> does not become manifest in the child of the serpent—which treads on the head of the serpent—then the Devil is and remains Prince and lord in the house of the soul, just as happened to Cain.

27. Understand the ground of this rightly: in the birth of this world, two kingdoms lie open, namely the kingdom of the love of God in **Christ**, and the kingdom of the wrath of God in **Lucifer**. In all creatures these same two kingdoms are in struggle, for in the struggle lies the origin of all spirits; and in the struggle of the fire, the light becomes manifest. The fire is a cause of the light; the wrath of God is a cause for God to move once more in His deepest love, in the name of **Jesus**, and thereby blot out the wrath.

Wrath is the root of love, just as fire is the root of light; but in the free will there is understanding—it makes itself into whatever it desires.

29. Do you not see the same in the earth, that the free will has made itself into stone and metal and earth in the <term>ens: the spiritual essence or "inner being" of a thing</term> of the Word? Stones and earth are not the free will itself, but the free will has introduced itself into such an *ens*, and through its desire and movement, brought the <term>ens: the spiritual essence or "inner being" of a thing</term> into a <term>compaction: the process of making something solid or dense</term>, or <term>coagulation: the thickening or solidification of a substance</term>; and there was truly no other maker than the free will in the formed and revealed Word. ### Of Man’s Procreation in This World, Chapter 26.

31. The desire in the word was the *fiat* <note>Latin: *fiat*, meaning "let it be done"; the creative command of God</note>, which there introduced the free will into an *essence* <note>Latin: *ens*; in Böhme’s philosophy, this refers to the fundamental spiritual "substance" or "being" of a thing</note>: likewise, that same revealed word is still in all things, and it has the *fiat*, being the desire within itself; just as the free will introduces itself into every thing into a spirit, so the *fiat* forms and signifies all things: every root bears from itself a branch of its own kind: but when the branch shall be born and take its beginning in the *essence* of the root, then the *essence* forms itself into a branch, just as at that same time the root is contained in its power and free will by both the upper and lower *stars* <note>original: "gesternte"; referring to astrological and cosmic influences believed to shape a person's character at birth</note>.

32. This is also to be understood in man, just as the will is in the seed—that is, as the desire of the father and mother, and also the other influences of the stars and the Elements, as well as the Devil's frequent interventions at any given time—so also a spirit is formed in the *essence* of the seed: many times an Angel, if the parents are in a holy desire, and many times also a beast, a serpent, and an image of the Devil, both according to the *essence* of the soul and according to the outward flesh.

33. The power of the revealed word gives itself into all things, into every thing, according to the will of the thing, according to the desire in the *essence*: for the desire in the *essence* is that which the word, being the sound of life, forms, as it stands written: such as the people are, such a God they also have; with the holy you are holy, and with the perverse you are perverse, Psalm 18. All of this together is understood of the spoken word in the *fiat*, that is, in the desire of nature: and therefore God has incorporated another word from the center of His love into the image of man, so that, in the event that he has arisen from an evil quality, a free will might go out from his *Selfhood* <note>original: "Ikheid"; the ego or self-centered will that acts independently of God</note>, and die away to itself in that same Holy incorporated word; then the *fiat* bears and forms another new creature out of the *essence* of the free will.

34. In all men lies the possibility, yet the making into a child of God now belongs to the holy *fiat*, in the newly introduced word; for it does not depend on anyone’s own willing, making, running, or walking, but on God’s mercy; He has mercy on whom He will, namely only those who with their free will let their selfhood die in His grace, and give themselves over to Him: and He hardens whom He will—namely, those who, like Cain, run by themselves, and would take the kingdom of God for themselves in their own evil will, and will not let their own self-will die in its selfhood.

For without evil and good, no ground would be able to exist.

38. Yet this same being divides itself into two powerful distinctions, and such is nonetheless no actual separation, for one dwells in the other; yet the one does not grasp the other, it denies the other, for it is not the other.

The second principle, being the Kingdom of God or the Angelic world, had shimmered within the essence of the soul, and God united His single, most holy Word therein once again for the <term>rebirth <note>original: "wedergeboorte"</note></term>.

48. And this union was present in Cain's as well as in Abel's essence. However, Cain's essence was caught in the wrestling wheel—in the struggle of the three principles within the wrath—and was covered with the monster of the serpent. This was not precisely so to the point of impossibility, as if he were born unto damnation, but rather to a possibility of the will: whether he would let the "self-right" <note>the ego or self-centered nature inherited from the fallen Adam</note> in Adam sink away and live in the will of God, or whether he would live for himself. It was upon this that the election turned.

49. Now, God knows the free will and which way it has gone. If it has entered into wickedness and selfhood, then the wrath of God confirms him in his election to damnation; but if he has entered into the Word of the covenant, then God confirms him as a child of Heaven. Here it is now said: *To whom I am merciful, I am merciful, and whom I harden, I harden.* <note>A reference to Exodus 33:19 and Romans 9:15-18</note> God knows His children even in their essence, in the mother’s body. Why should He give His pearl to such a one whom He well knows will turn away from Him? 43. And after this first seed, Abel pressed forward into the holy covenant and offered his sweet blood to the Wrath for the sake of the sinful seed, so that the Wrath might let its flame sink, and allow the first birth to pass through the blood of the second.

44. The first birth became a murderer; this points to the Devil in man. But the second became a sacrifice for the first; this indicates that the "Devil-wrath" in the first Adam would be reconciled in the sacrifice of the second.

## On Human Procreation in this World, Chapter 26.

I have told you above that love and <term>wrath <note>original: "toorn"; in this context, the "wrath of God" refers to the harsh, consuming fire of divine energy before it is tempered by love</note></term> are in conflict; whichever one the <term>essence <note>original: "ens"; the fundamental being or spiritual substance</note></term> unites itself with, it is seized and confirmed by that same power. However, it is so that the will is free to move from evil into good, and from good into evil, and this is so while one lives on earth. In this way, both doors stand open to him, for the free will is not bound. For if it were bound, then no judgment could pass over him with justice. He has laws and teachings, and these are not given to him for death, but for life. If it happens that he transgresses them and persists in that transgression, then the judgment passes over him; for every judgment arises from the transgression of the commandment.

<margin>Proverbs 1</margin>
52. Now you say: "He cannot keep it; he is being pulled." Yes, rightly so; the Truth also reproaches him to his face as a faithless person who allows himself to be pulled toward evil. The law to do right stands in the light of life like a constant mirror; he sees it, and he knows well that he is a liar and walks on the Devil’s path. It shows him the way of truth, yet the free will rejects it. Then he is predestined to damnation—but in such a way that the will was free while he was in this <note>The "hut" is a common metaphor for the temporary physical body or the mortal life</note> hut. But the heavy bond of God’s wrath in the pulling of the Devil’s desire draws many of them to the damnation of death.

53. Reason says: "If man has a free will, then God is not almighty over him, to do with him what He wills." Answer: the free will is from no beginning; it is contained in nothing and formed by nothing. It is its own origin, arising from the Word of divine power, from God’s love and wrath. Within its own will, it forms for itself a center for its own seat. It births itself in the first <term>principle <note>original: "principium"; the foundational realms of spiritual existence</note></term> toward the fire and toward the light. Its true origin is in the Nothing; there the Nothing (being the Δ <note>The triangle symbol, representing the Trinity or the divine eye</note>, or as one might unfold it: A.O.V. <note>likely Alpha, Omega, and Vader (Father) or Verbum (Word)</note>) introduces itself into a delight for contemplation. This delight carries itself into a will, and the will into a desire, and the desire into an <term>essence <note>original: "wesen"; being or substance</note></term>.

54. Now, the eternal Understanding—which is God—is a judge over that essence. If the delight (which has strayed from Him) has introduced itself into an evil essence, then He judges that same essence in its principle. Into whatever distress and quality, or into whatever <term>essence <note>original: "ens"</note></term> the delight from the strayed Δ has introduced itself into a principle, therein it confirms the general, eternal free will, which is the <term>Unground <note>original: "ongrond"; the "Abyss" or "Groundless" void that precedes all created things and even God's self-manifestation</note></term> and the cause of all ground.

56. But how can such a thing judge a matter which is not its own? How could God judge the will of creatures if the same had not originated from Him? Likewise, how can a judgment pass over a thing that is bound, and is not free in its willing and doing?

57. The human and angelic will arose through the movement of the <term>Abyss <note>original: "ongronds"; the "Ungrund" or Groundless, the divine source before creation</note></term> (when the Godhead once moved itself in its contemplation and perception, and with that movement introduced itself into a beginning and into spirits). 58. Now God is before and outside all beginning, and from Him all beginning proceeds; He is also the end of all beginning. Thus stands the middle of all beginning things, between the beginning and the end, for it must enter back through the end with its beginning into that from which it originated.

59. For when a thing begins, it enters into a time; but when that same time is grasped by the end—that is, by eternity—then it is in its own eternity, from which it introduced itself into a compaction, and is thus confirmed into eternity.

60. Therefore, the free will has its own judgment for good or for evil within itself; it has its court within itself, it has God's love and wrath within itself. That which it grasps and desires, it forms within itself, and through its own desire, it forms itself solely into a center.

62. For in this way the world also has its origin: namely, in the free will of the two eternal principles, that is, from the dark fire-lust and from the divine light-fire-lust.
