### Chapter 27. Concerning the offerings of Cain and Abel.

...what kind of circumstances led God to smell the smoke <note>original: "aan het roken was," referring to God receiving the "sweet-smelling savor" of the burnt offering</note>, which was rightfully kept silent by Moses out of respect for God’s purpose. Such things were indeed not hidden from the children of the Saints, nor from Moses, but before the eyes of the people a veil hung.

3. Israel (seeing as the greater part of them were nothing but wicked children, and moreover idolatrous, as was immediately apparent from their golden calf) was not permitted to know this because of false *Magic* <note>original: "Magia"; in this context, Böhme distinguishes between divine creative power and the "false magic" or sorcery of the fallen human will</note>. We shall also write for no one but our own, and yet it shall be understandable enough: mark it as follows.

4. The free will of the soul is as thin as a "nothing," and although it is encompassed by the "something" within its body, the "something" it has grasped is nevertheless in a false, moist essence originating from sin.

5. If the free will, with its desire, intends to go toward God, it must first depart from its false "something." When it thus departs, it is naked and powerless, for it is back in the first <term>Nothing <note>The "Nothing" or "Unground" refers to the absolute, undifferentiated state of God before creation; to reach God, the soul must strip away its selfish, worldly identity</note></term>. For if it wishes to go to God, it must die to and abandon its false selfhood. When it abandons that selfhood, it is as bare as a "nothing," and thus it cannot go forth, work, or * move <note>original: "bewegen"; the footnote suggests "weben," meaning to weave, stir, or live</note>. If it wishes to prove its power, it must be within a "something" in which it can grasp and form itself.

6. We have an example of this in faith: if there is to be a faith that works, it must grasp onto something in which it can work. The free will of God has grasped the inward spiritual world and works through it; and the free will of the inward world has grasped the outward world and works through it. Likewise, the free will of the soul—which also has its origin in the <term>Unground <note>original: "ongrond"; the groundless, bottomless source of all existence from which the divine will emerges</note></term>—must grasp onto something through which it may be manifest, and with which it can † work <note>original: "werken"; the footnote suggests "wallen," meaning to boil, surge, or flow forth</note> before God.

7. Since Adam’s body was made from the *clay* <note>original: "Limo" or "limus"; refers to the primordial "slime" or "dust" of the earth</note> of the earth, and also from the *clay* of the holy Heaven—though the heavenly *clay* in Adam had become obscured <note>original: "verblikkerd"; suggests the divine substance had faded or become pale/hidden within him after the Fall</note>, in which the free will could have grasped a heavenly form to move, work, pray, and beseech before God—they set fire to the fruits of the earth. Namely, *Cain* brought from the fruits of the field, and *Abel* also brought the firstlings of his flock; these they set ablaze with fire.

# Concerning Cain’s and Abel’s Offering. Chapter 27.

...they brought offerings before God, and the free will of the soul would, through its prayer, penetrate to God. As the soul was to exit the human house of corruption and enter into God, He desired a substance in which He might work; thus, the imagination of the will took hold through the sacrifice. Then God ignited Abel’s sacrifice with the holy fire as a sign of the covenant, which in the fullness of time would again ignite within the fire of souls.

9. In this same fire, the will of Abel’s soul took hold in a holy substance. Through the desire of that captured free will, it pressed forward into the free will of God. This was not pleasing to the will of the Devil or the serpent. The serpent’s and Devil's will within Cain understood well that the sign of the covenant was opening in the holy fire through Abel’s desire and prayer.

10. He did not want to ignite Cain’s offering; thus Moses here creates a veil <note>A "veil" is Böhme’s way of saying Moses hid a deeper spiritual truth behind a simple literal description.</note> over this and says: God did not look upon Cain’s offering with grace.

11. The igniting of the outward sacrifice was a figure <note>A "figure" is a symbolic foreshadowing or a physical representation of a spiritual reality.</note> of the inward spirit. For the spirit of the soul, moving in its free will toward the *center* <note>original: "centrum"</note> of light, was ignited with the love-fire of God. Meanwhile, the imagination of the body (including its heavenly part) was ignited in the sacrifice with the fire of the holy part of the earth—which lies hidden within the curse. In this fire, the free will of the soul and the free will in the <term>essence <note>original: "ens"; a technical term in alchemy and Böhme's theology meaning the essential, spiritual "stuff" or "being" of a thing</note></term> of the heavenly part of the body took hold of a substance, and with it pressed before the holiness of God.

12. And here, for the first time, the head of the serpent was bruised. For this was the figure of the new birth out of *Christ* <note>original: "Christo"</note>; not that Abel had at that time put on Christ in the flesh, but certainly in the spirit of *the Lord* <note>original: "Jehova"</note> within the sign of the covenant. In this sign, the name *Jesus* <note>original: "Jesus"</note>—being a regenerator in God—stood hidden. In the fullness of time, He intended to move and open Himself within this sign, introducing a heavenly, holy *essence* into the faded <note>original: "verblikte"; refers to the "tarnished" or "dimmed" spiritual nature of man after the Fall</note> essence of the heavenly part, making it alive once more through the opened power of Jesus.

14. But if man introduces the desire of his faith into it, he then commits his free will to it. How this now happens is understood as follows:

15. There, a **conjunction** <note>original: *conjunctie*; a spiritual joining or union</note> occurs.

16. But now the human free will has become sinful, while the free will of God (from which the human one originated when it was first breathed into him in the beginning) is holy and pure. 17. This swallows up the ignited wrath and the vanity of the free will of man. In the "dying of death"—namely, in the fire of the wrath of God—He makes that vanity into nothing, so that the human will becomes pure before the will of God and may enter into the love-will of God. Therefore, the love-desire of God in Abel and Moses ignited the sacrifice itself, so that the love-fire and holy-fire (within the wrath-fire of eternal nature, which is the property of the Father) might swallow the **turba** <note>original: *turbam*; the "disturbance" or destructive turmoil caused by sin within the soul.</note> in the human free will of the soul.

18. 10. But since wrath had gained the government in man, yet nevertheless the maiden-child <term>Maiden-child: In this mystical context, the "virgin" or "maiden-child" refers to the pure, divine spark or the Christ-nature born within the soul of a believer.</term>, from the essence of the angelic world, out of the covenant of God, out of the shining essence <note>original: "ens"</note>, would sprout through the wrath, just as a bright light shines from the candle through the fierce fire, which takes away the power of the darkness; thus the outward body, in the children of God, had to let itself be killed and persecuted by the fierceness of God, for it was a foreign figure to the maiden-child.

11. For Abel had the awakened vanity in his outward flesh just as much as Cain; according to the outward man he was also sinful, but in the inward man the angelic world and the **Paradise-image** bloomed out again in the covenant. This was now a great enmity against each other; the inward man stepped upon the head of the serpent-monster <note>A reference to the prophecy in Genesis 3:15, where the offspring of the woman crushes the serpent's head.</note> regarding its false desire, while in contrast, the serpent-monster bit the heel of his angelic will and mocked the angelic image, just as it still happens today: as soon as the maiden-child is born in the spirit of Christ, the outward earthly body, along with the maiden-child, is persecuted, despised, and mocked by the children of Cain, and held as a strange child of the world.

12. For the serpent-monster is nothing but a fool before God, and since the noble maiden-child must nevertheless carry such a monster in the outward flesh—to which the devil still has constant access—this body is violently attacked by the devil in the wrath of God and by his children; they constantly wish to murder it, for the child of the maiden works through the outward man like a light through the fire, and reveals itself; it teaches and reproves the godless heap, which the devil cannot endure, for it is against his kingdom, just as Abel's offering was against Cain's.

13. For Cain offered in the desire of the pride of the serpent, like a hypocrite, and wished in his serpent-like desire to be a pious, godly child; but Abel humbled himself before God and entered with his desire into the mercy of God. God’s fire of love accepted his offering, and the same penetrated through the earthly offering and fire; this is also to be understood regarding the body of Abel: just as the immortal shall swallow up the mortal, in such a manner the heavenly took the earthly captive into itself.

# Chapter 28. Of Cain’s Murder of his Brother.

14. Now, that Cain murdered Abel’s outward body serves as an image showing that the outward body shall be killed in the wrath of God; the wrath must devour and kill the outward image—which grew within the wrath—so that the great eternal life may sprout forth through death.

15. Abel was a figure of Christ; the children of God's wrath must execute the judgment of God's wrath upon the children of the saints, upon their outward image (which is also earthly and animal). Just as the Pharisees (who were nothing but children of false serpents before God, as Christ calls them) had to persecute and kill the humanity of Christ, so too was Cain an image of these serpent-like, wolf-like Pharisees, and of false **mouth-Christendom** <note>Those who profess faith with their mouths but do not live it in their hearts; hypocrites.</note>.

16. Just as the false serpent-child is a monster and a fool to the angelic world, so too do the children of darkness hold the children of light for fools. For there must be a *contrary* <note>original Latin: "Contrarium"</note>, so that one may be revealed in the other. If wrath had not taken hold of humanity and devoured it, then the deepest love of God would not have been revealed in man.

17. However, love takes occasion from the wrath to overwhelm it with its own movement and revelation. This is seen in Christ, who was God’s Son and yet entered into our image (which had been awakened in wrath), so that He might be revealed with His love within the wrath, changing it into joy.

18. Christ gave our human image to His Father's wrath to be swallowed up in death, and led His life into death; but He revealed His love in that life which had swallowed up death, and led that same life out through death into love. Just like a grain of wheat sown in the earth must die in the earth, yet from that which died, a more beautiful, newer body grows. In the same way, the corrupted body of Adam had to be sacrificed to death and wrath, and out of death and wrath the body of God’s love would be revealed.

19. In Cain and Abel was the image of how things would go in the future: since Abel, in his outward part, bore the earthly image and yet in his spirit was an image of Heaven, his outward body in its corruption was nothing more than a *mask* <gloss>original Dutch "momaangesigt", referring to a disguise or a deceptive face</gloss> for the outward world. ### Chapter 28. On Cain’s Brother-Murder.

...condemn, and can bring forth such **sharp-wittedness** <note>original: "spits-vinnig," implying a biting or overly subtle cleverness used for argument</note>, who can wrap themselves in a cloak of ingenuity, and the wolf, who thereby murders and devours the flock of Christ, covering it under a purple cloak of Christ; they listen to him gladly, for the fleshly **serpent-heart** <term>serpent-heart: in mystical thought, this refers to the corrupted nature of man following the Fall, characterized by ego and guile</term> tickles itself with the same in its own wicked property; it is of the very same nature.

48. Such seed is sown by these teachers chosen by men, who desire the office only for temporal honor and pleasure; however, they are uncalled by God, and also without Divine knowledge. They do not enter through the door of Christ, but through the election of men out of favor, by their own will, running and racing; these cannot be counted as shepherds of Christ at all, for they are not born of Christ, nor chosen for His office.

49. They are nothing other than builders of the great **Babel** <note>In this context, Babel refers to the "Tower of Confusion," representing the various competing and worldly religious denominations that lack spiritual unity</note>, where the languages are confused, and men are thereby made discordant, and cause war and strife on earth; for they dispute over the empty husk, that is, over the written words and letters, and they do not have the living Word of God—in which they should teach—dwelling in them. The Spirit of Christ must itself be in the word of the teacher with living utterance; the human spirit must recognize and find Christ within itself, otherwise no one there teaches the word of Christ, but only mute words without power and spirit.

50. This now rebukes the Spirit of Christ in His children, and shows them the true way, how we must die to selfhood and the false desire for temporal pleasure and honor through the death of Christ, and be born from the Spirit of Christ into another new will and desire, out of the love of Christ, in true self-knowledge; and Christ must preach and teach out of us.

51. Cain in Babel cannot tolerate this—that one teaches that Christ Himself must be the teacher in the human spirit. They appeal to the prescribed Apostolic word and say: "when we teach the same, then the Spirit of God is poured out." Yes, quite right, I say so too—provided that the same word is taught in the spirit and in the power of Christ, then it is truly so.

52. But the Spirit of Christ in His children is not bound to any fixed form, as if He should need to speak nothing more than what stands in the Apostolic letters; just as the Spirit in the Apostles was free, and they did not all speak the same words and languages, yet they all spoke from a single Spirit and ground, each as the Spirit [gave them utterance...]

# Chapter 28. On Cain’s Fratricide.

...substance has been led, and that same substance is the great **Babylon**, where evil and good have been built into a single structure. <note>In this context, "Babylon" represents a state of spiritual confusion and the corruption of the true church by worldly interests.</note>

58. But if no explanation had been introduced regarding the Apostolic Word, and if it had not been cast into another form, the instrument would have remained pure. However, the unenlightened mind has established itself therein, and has formed and explained it according to the "fat belly" <note>An idiom for greed or self-indulgence.</note> and the worldliness of this age; thus the spirit is extinguished. It has become nothing other than an **Antichristian order** and practice; the word has been shaped and captured like the mechanism of an organ. In this way, it has been put into use: some play upon it, and others listen to the sound. Thus, nowadays, for the most part, nothing is used but such organ-players who play externally upon the organ-work and thereby create a fine piece for themselves which they enjoy hearing; but the organ-work sounds no differently than the master himself plays it.

59. 60. ## THE 29TH CHAPTER.

### *How the Adamical human tree has introduced and opened itself from its trunk into branches, shoots, and fruits, from which opening all invention and governance have arisen. The deep gateway of eternal and temporal nature, and how eternal wisdom has introduced itself.*

1. The eternal Divine understanding is a free will, not arisen from anything or through anything; it is its own seat and dwells solely within itself, uncomprehended by anything, for outside and before it there is nothing, and that same nothing is one, and it is also like a nothing to itself. It is a single will of the Unground <note>The "Unground" (Dutch: *ongrond*) is a central concept in this philosophy, referring to the "groundless" or "abyssal" nature of God that exists before any creation, desire, or differentiation.</note>, and it is neither near nor far; neither high nor low; but it is everything, and yet as a nothing: for it is in itself no visibility or perceptibility, such that it might find a likeness within itself.

2. Its "finding" is its own self proceeding out of itself, for then it beholds itself in that proceeding; since that which has proceeded is its eternal joy, experience, and perception. And this same is called the Divine Wisdom, which Wisdom receives the groundless will into itself as a center of the vessel of joy—that is, into an eternal mind of understanding. This understanding forms the free will within itself into its own image—that is, into an eternally speaking, reasoning, living Word, which the free will exhales <note>original Dutch: *uyt-ademt*; glossed in the source as German *Aufzhauchet* (breathes out)</note> or speaks out from the formed wisdom of joy.

3. And this exhalation is the Spirit, or the mouth of the understanding in the formed will of wisdom, which distinguishes the speaking Word, so that the mind and the understanding of the mind become manifest. In this manifestation, the free joy, or the wisdom of the free will, is formed by the Spirit into distinctness through the speaking or sounding out <note>original Dutch: *uytſchallen*; glossed in the source as German *Aufzhallen* (resounding)</note>.

4. In this formation, the powers of the Divine properties arise, so that one can rightly say of God: He is the eternal will, understanding, mind, counsel, power, hero, and wonder, with which

...into self-observation, a child of **selfhood** <term>Selfhood (Dutch: *selfheyd*): A central concept in this philosophy referring to the state where the human will turns away from God to focus entirely on its own ego and desires</term>; which introduces itself into nature as its own government and will. This, says the spirit in Lamech, would be avenged seventy-sevenfold.

63. Before this, the understanding lay in a single sound, but now the vengeance came into it and confused it into seventy-seven parts.

64. For the human wheel of sound or understanding was turned, and the ten forms of fire opened themselves in every form of nature, in which time and eternity stand; this was seven times ten—that is seventy—and to that belongs the *center* <note>original: *centrum*; the spiritual core or origin point</note> with its unchangeable seven forms of eternal nature, which together make seventy-seven.

The time is near. Hallelujah.

<header>Chapter 30. Of the Line of the Covenant.</header>

# THE 30TH CHAPTER.
## *Of the Line of the Covenant.*

<margin>1.</margin> THE Line of the Covenant is not to be understood as if the covenant applied only to that specific Line; no, the covenant concerns the eternal life which was in the Word before the times of humanity. The Line of Seth concerns only the manifestation in the flesh, in which Line the Word in the covenant wished to manifest itself outwardly in the flesh. However, the Spirit from the <term>center<note>original: *centrum*; in Böhmean theosophy, the point of origin where spiritual properties emerge</note></term> in the covenant applies to Cain’s Line as much as to Seth’s—though in Cain’s it works in the spirit, and in Seth’s in the outward mouth; that is, in the <term>formed word<note>The "formed word" refers to the Word of God as it is expressed through human language and the "teaching office" or ministry</note></term>, which is the office of teaching. For Seth had sprouted according to the Spirit from the covenant, where the Spirit moved itself within the incorporated Word in the covenant; whereas Cain was within the comprehension of the Spirit of Nature.

<margin>2.</margin> For through Cain’s Line came forth the arts, which were a wonder of Divine wisdom, contemplativeness, and form-giving—namely, of the formed word through and in nature. In Seth, the Word entered into a formal life, namely into a spiritual contemplativeness, where the Word of God contemplated itself with wisdom in a spiritual image. In Cain’s Line, it was in a naturally formed word; and both serve the wondrous deeds of God.

<margin>3.</margin> It is not as <term>Babel<note>Böhme uses "Babel" to refer to the confused and sectarian state of organized institutional churches</note></term> judges—that God, out of His own purpose, has thus predestined and chosen one portion of humanity in His wrath for damnation, and the other portion for life. Those who judge in such a way are still among the number of seventy-seven in the multiplication of the word <note>This refers back to the previous chapter's discussion of the seventy-seven languages and the fragmentation of truth</note>. For the promise was made to Adam before Cain was even conceived; the covenant rested in Adam and in Eve with grace. But the Spirit of Sanctification and of rebirth through Christ applied only to the <term>seed of the woman<note>A reference to Genesis 3:15, interpreted here as the spiritual potential within humanity</note></term>; that is, to the enclosed seed of the kingdom of Heaven, in the <term>tincture of light<note>original: *tinctuur des ligts*; a spiritual essence or quality that illuminates and transforms</note></term>, in the <term>Venus Matrix<note>The "Venus Matrix" represents the feminine, creative principle of love and desire from which spiritual life is birthed</note></term>. In this, Adam—when he was both Man and Woman—would have reproduced himself in his own desire and love; which, because it was not possible, was taken from Adam and made into a woman.

<margin>4.</margin> But when the Woman became earthly, then the Heavenly part of this Matrix was enclosed in death until the Heavenly birth; into which Matrix the Word of God incorporated itself again with the covenant, in order to

Böhme uses it to describe the spiritual substance that makes up the soul.</note></term>. Through that same newly quickened Heavenly essence—namely through the "seed of the woman" from the Heavenly part—the Word crushes the head of the serpent's introduced desire. This occurs within the **wrath** <note>original: *grimmigheyt*; this refers to the harsh, fiery quality of nature when it is separated from God’s light and love.</note> of nature, which is the anger present in both Cain’s and Seth’s lineage.

6. That many of them nevertheless remain in death and despise the voice is the fault of **free will**, which allowed itself to be held by the Devil in the wrath of God, and still allows itself to be held today, because the Cain-like will loves nature and **selfhood** <note>original: *selfheyt*; the state of being focused on the individual "I" or ego rather than on God's unity.</note> too much.

7. For if the free will of the soul wishes to grasp the Word in the covenant, it must die away to its natural selfhood and its own self-will. It must be surrendered, along with that self-will, into the covenant, so that it follows the Word and the Spirit in the covenant with its desire, just as the Spirit leads it.

8. And Cain does not wish to do this gladly; he wants to be his own master. In his free will, he fashions his desire into a **Monster** and an evil beast, which does not conform to the first image of the **formed life** in the Word of God. Concerning this very beast, the words of Christ apply where He says:
> Unless you turn back and become like children <note>original: *’t en sy dan dat gy omkeerd, en word gelyk de kinderen*; a reference to Matthew 18:3.</note> (that is, that you exit from the will of the self-born beast and enter again into the form of the first life), otherwise you shall not see the kingdom of God.
Likewise:
> You must be born anew out of the water of the essence of the Heavenly world, and out of the same Holy Spirit from the covenant, otherwise you cannot behold God.

9. This same evil beast of the ungodly form is predestined to damnation, but the covenant is in Life. If the free will enters into the covenant, then Christ rises from the covenant into life in His humanity; then the **strange beast** dies in the death of Christ, and the will forms itself again into the first image, just as God created it. And this applies not only to Seth, but to the life of Adam—that is, to the single life of humanity which was in the Word of God. It presses from one upon all, just as all the branches exist in a single tree.

27. **Enoch**, in his own language <note>The author is likely referring to a mystical or "Adamic" etymology rather than literal Hebrew, though the name Enoch/Henoch is traditionally associated with "dedication" or "initiation."</note>, means as much as an exhaled breath of the **Divine longing**; which, by exhaling, has thus contemplated itself in time, within a form. The power of this speaking draws the formed breath back into itself again, only giving off its sound, like a voice of the will of God. It signifies, firstly, a branch from the **line of the covenant**—that is, from the inward **priestly office** out of the Holy Divine longing of the wisdom of God from **Jehovah**. The spirit wished to grasp the deepest love in **Jehovah**, in a name called **Jesus**, within the Word. Meanwhile, it played with that name in the time of the "figure" <note>The "figure" refers to the symbolic era of the Old Testament before the physical incarnation of Christ.</note> within the holy wisdom, in the line of the covenant, as if with an inwardly hidden holy kingdom which he wished to reveal in the fullness of time.

28. Secondly, it points to the power of the formed word—that is, the person or the body <note>original: "corpus"</note> from the earthly <term>limo</term> <note>From the Latin *limus*, meaning mud or clay, referring to the "dust of the earth" from which man was formed in Genesis.</note> of the heavenly part of the earth. It suggests that this same body should be captured in the holy word and snatched away <note>A reference to Enoch being "taken" by God so that he did not see death (Genesis 5:24).</note> from this earthliness, just as light takes away the darkness and swallows it into itself. In this way, the good part of true humanity, in **Adam's** first image, would be snatched by the Word out of the earthliness and rise from the earth, which Enoch’s removal from this world indicates.

29. Thirdly, it signifies the Prophet, being the voice of the Divine longing, who proclaimed the kingdom of **Christ**, and also the kingdom of wonders, and how things would fare in the future. For the prophetic voice revealed itself again from the "assumption" <note>His being taken up into heaven.</note> and pointed out from the essence of the spirit—namely, from the most spiritual kingdom (the human angelic kingdom) through the spirit of the souls. It then pointed from the bodily kingdom—that is, from the <unclear>nature</unclear> of wonders, from the clay of the earth, and from the stars—how the outward kingdom of man would in the future rise up in the essence of this world, and what would happen therein. The inward, holy, omniscient spirit points this out through the outward—that is, through the wonders of the "womb" of the outward being, namely through the spirit of the outward world—showing how it would go with the human kingdom on earth. For the inward spirit contemplated itself through the formed wisdom of God and viewed itself in the formed spirit of wonders: this is what the name of **Enoch** points out to us.

32. **Moses** points in the lines, at every degree, only to a single person whom he also places in the line through which the spirit of wonders passes; after that **Moses** says: *and he lived for such a time, and begat sons and daughters*, of whom he speaks no further. By this, he intends to indicate the spirit of revelation of the wonders of God in each line. Their age, which the spirit sets down, indicates the times: how long each one's rule <note>original: "regiment"; referring to a period of dominion or spiritual governance.</note>—both the worldly and the spiritual—would stand in its grasp. That is to say, how long each arising **Monarchy** of the worldly dominion would last, as well as the spiritual **Monarchy**.

33. And these same **Monarchies** of wonders were presented immediately from the first branches, from the beginning of the **human tree**; namely, in each line in the seven numbers from **Adam**, through **Cain** up to **Lamech**, and in the other line from **Adam** to **Jared**. By these numbers and names, the spirit particularly points in each line to seven outgoing properties of the tree, and the power of the wonders: how the powers of the wonders would thereafter introduce themselves into rules, and how one figure would arise out of the other, and how one would break the other, and from that breaking set up another form, just as has happened in the spiritual and worldly rule. For the worldly is always understood alongside the spiritual; for the outward formed word, in the rule of nature, always places its form beside and according to the spiritual formation. Therefore, take sharp heed here.

-># Of the Line of the Covenant. Chapter 30.<-

34. Seven times are determined from the **tree of life** in the **word of power** <note>original: "woord van de kragt"; this refers to the creative speech of God that sustains existence.</note>. The first time proceeds from the pure life of **Adam**; for before the creature was made, life was in the **Word**, where it was introduced purely into the image. This lasted until the **Fall**. From that same pure life, an internal sprout sprang forth; this was **Abel**. However, because the **Fall** clung to him externally, that same pure life was led through death into the holy world. This points to the **kingdom of Christ**, who would lead us back into the pure life through death.

35. The second time begins with **Seth**; for **Moses** says: *Adam was a hundred and thirty years old, and begat a son who was like his own image, and called him Seth.* Understand this: he was an image just as **Adam** was after the **Fall**, and he was in the **spiritual line of wonders** <note>original: "geestelyke wonder-linie"; in this mystical tradition, this refers to a lineage of individuals through whom God reveals divine mysteries.</note>. Parallel to this, **Cain** was in a worldly, natural line of wonders, for both kingdoms progress together. **Seth’s** time lasted until the **Great Flood**, and it held the supreme rule until the **Flood**.

36. The third time begins with **Enoch** during the time of **Seth**, and it carries itself through like a spiritual preaching or acknowledgment of God during **Seth’s** era, like a hidden kingdom. It lasts until **Abraham**, to whom the **covenant of Christ** in the flesh was confirmed.

37. The fourth time begins with **Kenan**; this is the spiritual form with prayer and spiritual offering, wherein the **Word** forms itself in **wisdom**. It carries itself through the times of **Seth** and **Enoch**, and reveals itself with **Moses**, just as **Enoch’s** time first revealed itself with **Abraham** through the promise in the **covenant**. This time of **Kenan** lasts in its revelation and dominion under **Moses** until **Christ** in the flesh.

38. The fifth time begins with **Mahalaleel**, and this is the grasping of the **angelic form** <note>original: "Engelsche form"; referring to the restored, spiritual state of humanity that resembles the nature of angels.</note>, being the new rebirth from the **covenant**. This proceeds hiddenly through the preaching of **Enoch**, and under **Seth** and **Kenan** in the word of the promises, through all three times. It reveals itself with the fulfillment of the **covenant** in the humanity of **Christ**. There, the true **Mahalaleel** and **angelic image**, which was extinguished in **Adam**, became manifest again in the humanity of **Christ**.

39. The sixth time begins with **Jared**; this is the **spiritual priesthood** <note>original: "geestelyk Priesterdom"</note> under the external [order]. While **Seth**, **Enoch**, **Kenan**, and **Mahalaleel** were external in their ordering in their respective times—namely the preaching of **Enoch** concerning God, His essence, and His will; as well as the preaching of **Abraham** regarding the **covenant** and **circumcision**; and also **Moses** with the **Book of the Law**—under all of these, the internal priest **Jared** went hiddenly...

->Of the wonderful line from Enoch.<-

1. Moses writes, Enoch begot Methuselah; this name in the **nature-language** <note>original: "natuurfpraak." # Chapter 31. Of the Wonderful Line from Enoch.

2. ...so the Divine Spirit spoke here as well: the human essence is Lamech; that is to say, the damage is too great, it hovers above <note>The author is using a mystical etymology where "Lamech" is associated with the Dutch word "lam" (lame) or "schade" (damage/injury), suggesting the broken state of humanity.</note>; although the strong breath of God went out from Methuselah through the prophetic sound, nevertheless the essence formed itself in the reproduction of the corrupt nature in Lamech. This is seen in the "two wills," just as Moses says that the first Lamech in the line of Cain took two wives, namely Adah and Zillah; and so it would be no different here in this lineage.

3. Thus Moses now says: *and Lamech begat Noah*: with this name the spirit goes out from the damage of Lamech, even unto the end of time, and brings the end into the beginning; for Noah, in the **nature-language** <note>original: "natuurspraak." A concept in Böhme’s thought where the sounds of a name reveal the inner essence or "signature" of the being.</note>, signifies "end and beginning." Thus the spirit finds the holy word at the end, which had incorporated itself into the covenant, and says: *this one shall comfort us in our toil and labor on earth, which the Lord has cursed.*

4. For the consolation of humanity was to come from the beginning and the end; for in the beginning is and was the Word of God, which is the beginning of all things; and in the end is also the Word of God; the same is the consolation of all things, that the creature shall be delivered from vanity. The spirit looked toward that and said: *this one* (meaning the Word, which desired to manifest itself in humanity) *shall comfort us in our toil on earth, which the Lord has cursed*: for Noah himself could not comfort humanity, as he preached to them punishment and destruction, but the One who was in the beginning and in the end, He comforted humanity in their toil on earth, which they experienced under the curse and wrath of God.

5. ### Concerning the Wonder-Line from *Enoch*: Chapter 31.

Human reason will say: "Did He not know beforehand what would happen? How can He repent of His own will, which He is Himself?"

18. Here one must enter into the <term>center<note>In the author's mystical theology, the "center" refers to the core of divine being where the internal movement of the Godhead begins.</note></term>: in God there is no repentance; nothing can repent Him. But there is a repentance in His outspoken, formed word. For the formed word repents in the Devils, that from an <term>essence<note>original: "ens." This refers to the fundamental spiritual substance or being of a thing.</note></term> of light, they have become a being of darkness. It repents the Devil that he did not remain an angel. Likewise, it eternally repents the godless man that the divine essence stood in the formed word, and he changed the power of the word into evil. Thus there is a repentance in the formed word, in nature, across all generations, because the property of grimness rules in the curse of wrath in the formed, spoken word. The essence of love from the word repents that the devil and wrath rule within it and destroy so much.

Chap. 32. Of the covenant between God and Noah.

# THE 32nd CHAPTER.
->Of the covenant between God and Noah.<-

1. God spoke to Noah, "with you I will establish a covenant, and you shall go into the Ark with your sons and your sons’ wives." We have a great and remarkable example in Noah and his children; the covenant was made with Noah because his spirit was a manifestation of the **formed word** <term>formed word: the expression of God’s eternal speech as it takes shape within a created being or the natural world</term> in him, in the beginning and in the end of time. And the beginning and the end was the **eternal word**, which had betrothed itself into the covenant; in this covenant the soul of Noah, being the formed word of eternal nature, found grace and received the confirmation of the covenant of grace.

2. Just as his name in the **language of nature** <term>language of nature: the mystical belief that the sounds of words correspond to the inner essence or "signature" of the things they name</term> is properly understood to mean a contemplation of the beginning and the end; in that same beginning and end—namely, in the eternally speaking word of the Father, which desired to open itself again in human life—grace stood turned toward Noah, so that God confirmed the covenant with him.

3. And we have an excellent example in the three sons of Noah, which is worthy of mention: they were in three kinds of lines from the stem of Adam in their own properties, just as three kinds of peoples have arisen from them. Yet God still flowed all three of them, together with their wives, into the covenant of grace and commanded them to go into the Ark in the **second Monarchy** <term>second Monarchy: a term used by the author to describe the historical-spiritual age of the world beginning after the Flood</term>, and He did not cast out the fleshly Ham.

4. This is first to be highly considered: how a door of grace stands open to all people, and that God has not predestined any election in nature, but that election arises out of the free will, when the same will turns itself from the good into the evil.

5. Secondly, this is a bridge or image of the **three principles** <term>three principles: a cornerstone of the author's philosophy, referring to the dark/fire world (wrath), the light world (love), and the external/visible world</term>. Namely, Shem represents the spiritual light-world in the covenant; and Japheth represents the fire-world, who would be a housemate of the light-world and a mirror of the great joy in the light-world; and Ham is a figure of the **earthly slime** <note>original: "limus"</note> <term>limus: the "dust" or "clay" of the earth from which man was formed, representing the physical, mortal, and sometimes corrupted material of the world</term> of the earth, to which the curse and the wrath of God cling. God took all three of these with Noah into the covenant and led them into the Ark.

This does not mean the creature was righteous and without evil in itself, but rather it refers to the One who opened Himself out of the covenant within Noah at this time—the One who repented for the evil of this time and brought His repentance into the love and mercy of God. Thus, He introduced the righteousness of mercy into that repentance and revealed the repenting Spirit within the **ens** <term>ens: a Latin term for "essence" or "being," referring here to the spiritual substance or potential within a person</term> of the covenant in the creature. Thus, Noah was righteous before God at this time, for the covenant moved within him; the Spirit says clearly, *at this time*; within this lies the righteousness.

14. This "time" is the movement of the covenant which made Noah righteous, for it was the time when Noah received his life in his mother's body. ### Chapter 33. and God's covenant with Noah and all Creatures.

...shall not inherit the kingdom of God; God recognizes the kingdom of nature as His ordinance, and He has given it into the power of man, so that through it he might separate the evil from the good, and choose for himself a judge over the wickedness of false desire and lust; for He said: "Whoever sheds man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed again"; that is to say, through the ordinance of nature; not to avenge oneself through one's own violence, but through the ordinance of nature, through the law of God, which is itself the avenger; for God says: "I will require <note>original: "wreken"; to avenge or demand an accounting for</note> the blood of your lives, and I will require it of every beast"; by this He means the ordinance of His law, and those who carry out the duties of that office.

16. This is not to be understood as meaning that a Prince or Lord has the power to shed blood outside the law of God; if he does so, then the law of God also condemns him to death. In this matter, there is no power over a man's blood simply because one is a King or Prince; for they are nothing other than officials <note>original: "amptlieden"; stewards or officers of a specific duty</note> over the ordinance of Divine law; and they must not go further than the Divine command. They indeed have the law of nature in their service, as its ministers, yet only according to justice and truth, and not through their own desire; for God created man in His own image; the kingdom of nature, in its official capacities, has no power to kill that same Divine image, but the office extends only over the outward image of nature in the ordinance of God.

17. Therefore, if an official of nature takes the life of a righteous man, the nature within God’s judgment ordains that such a person is held until the day of separation. Where will the Tyrants remain now, who turn the truth into a lie, and shamefully condemn the children of God for the sake of Divine knowledge and their confession of faith? They also stir up war and destruction over land and people; all of these belong in the <term>Great Turmoil</term> <note>original: "turba magna"; a term used by Boehme to describe a state of chaotic disruption, wrath, or the "source of anger" within nature</note> to the judgment of God, for they wield the sword of the <term>Great Turmoil</term> in their own self-indulgent lust; unless the spirit of God commands them to do so, in which case they must do it by virtue of their office; just as Israel did with the Heathen.

18. Everything that sheds blood out of its own lust, in order to increase its own power, without urgent necessity or the command of God, is ruled and driven to it by the grim wrath of God, and finally returns home to that same kingdom.

...shall not inherit the kingdom of God; God acknowledges the kingdom of nature as His ordinance, and He has given it into the power of man, so that through it he might separate the evil from the good, and choose himself as a judge over the wickedness of false desire and lust; for He said: whosoever sheds man’s blood, by man shall his blood be shed again; namely, through the ordinance of nature; not to avenge oneself by one's own violence, but through the ordinance of nature, through the law of God, which is the avenger; for God says: I will avenge the blood of your body, and I will avenge it on all animals; this He understands through the ordinance of His law, and through the executors of its office <note>The "office" refers to the legal and social roles—like judges or rulers—appointed to maintain order.</note>.

Such is not to be understood as if a Prince or Lord has the power to shed blood outside the law of God; if he does so, then the law of God also condemns him to death; there is no power here over the blood of man, though he be King or Prince; for they are nothing other than officials over the ordinance of the Divine law; and must not go further without Divine command; they indeed have the law of nature in their service, as ministers of the same, yet only according to justice and truth, and not through their own desire; for God created man in His image; over that same Divine image <note>Here, the author distinguishes between the soul (the "Divine image") and the physical body (the "external image").</note>, the kingdom of nature in its offices has no power to kill, but the office only applies to the external image of nature in God’s ordinance.

17. Therefore, if an official of nature takes the life of a righteous man, the nature in God's judgment ordains such a one who does this until the day of separation: where will the Tyrants remain now, who turn truth into lies, and shamefully condemn the children of God for the sake of Divine knowledge and confession, also bringing war and destruction upon land and people? All these belong in the *turba magna* <note>original: "turba magna"; Latin for "the great turmoil." It refers to the state of spiritual chaos and wrath where nature is out of balance with God’s light.</note> to the judgment of God, for they carry the sword of the turmoil in their own self-indulgence; unless the spirit of God commands them to do so, then they must do the same by virtue of their office; just as Israel did with the Heathen.

18. All that which, out of own self-indulgence, to increase its power, sheds blood without urgent necessity or the command of God; the same is ruled and driven thereto by the fierce wrath of God, and finally falls home to that same kingdom <note>meaning the kingdom of wrath or the "turba magna".</note>.

12. <note>The numbering in the original text jumps from 18 to 12.</note> Every soldier is a rod of the wrath of God, wherewith He thus punishes and devours men through His wrath, and belongs not at all to the order of nature; but in the desire in the *turba magna* <note>the great turmoil</note>.

22. 23. The wisdom of God desires no war, but the wrath of God according to the nature of the dark world desires such, and leads the same into the vanity and wickedness of men.

24. If we lived among one another as children of God, we would need no war; but by our warring we testify that we are nothing other than children of this world, and that we fight and war for a foreign inheritance—something we must surely leave behind—and we serve therein the wrath of God, like obedient servants; for no warrior, so long as he remains such, shall inherit the kingdom of God, but only a new-born child from the spirit of God, who leaves this world behind.

### Chapter 33. and the Covenant of God with Noah and all Creatures.

->Kk 3<-

26. This covenant with men is an image of the three principles of the Divine being, that is, of the essence of all essences; for the rainbow is a sign of this covenant which God remembers and beholds entirely inwardly: that man was created into one [being] out of three principles, and that he must live in all three. He [God] beholds the inability and great danger of man, and set before Himself this sign of the covenant as a prefiguration, so that His wrath <note>original: *grimmigheyd*, referring to the fierce, burning quality of divine anger</note> would not be stirred up to destroy the life of all.

27. The rainbow has the color of all the three *principles* <note>original: *principien*</note>; namely, the color of the first *principle* is red and dark brown, which signifies the dark fire-world, being the first *principle*, the kingdom of the wrath of God. The color of the second *principle* is white and yellow; this points to the Majestic color, being an image of the holy world, God’s love. The color of the third *principle* is green and blue: blue from the Chaos, and green from the water or saltpeter <note>original: *ſalpeter*; in Böhme’s alchemy, this refers to a spiritual-material explosive force within nature</note>, where in the terror of the fire, the sulfur <note>original: *ſulpher*</note> and the mercury <note>original: *Mercurius*</note> separate; thus it gives distinct colors, which point us to the inward spiritual worlds that stand hidden within the four elements.

28. This bow is a figure of the last judgment: how the inward spiritual worlds shall manifest themselves again and swallow the four-elemental world into themselves.

29. And it is the sign of grace of the covenant, which sign in the covenant points to the judge of the world, being Christ, who at the end of days shall appear in all the three principles. Namely, after the sign of the fire, as a severe Judge over the *turba* <term>turba: the "disturber," a destructive spiritual force that breaks down forms and executes judgment</term> and over all that shall be found therein, He shall manifest the judgment of the fire and ignite the *turba*, so that the first *principle* shall appear in its fiery property; for all things belonging to the essence of this world must be tested in the fire of the first *principle*, which is the center of eternal nature; there, the *turba* of all beings shall be swallowed up.

30. And after the sign of the light, He shall appear in the midst of the fire like a lovely face to all the Saints, and preserve His own in love and meekness before the flame of the fire.

31. And after the kingdom of the external nature of this world, He shall appear in His assumed humanity; and the external *mystery* <note>original: *myſterium*</note> of the four elements—namely, according to the sulfur, mercury, and salt <note>original: *ſulphur*, *Mercurius*, and *Sal*; the three fundamental alchemical properties Böhme uses to describe the makeup of all reality</note>, according to all properties of the wonders of the spoken, formed word, according to light and darkness—all shall become manifest before Him.

### Of the beginning of the second Monarchy, Cap. 33.

32. The rainbow is an image and a figure here, for it is a counter-image, or a reflection of the Sun; it reveals what kind of property exists in the depth. The Sun casts its luster into the four elements against the Chaos <note>In Böhme’s thought, "Chaos" refers to the unmanifested potential or the "hidden ground" from which all matter arises</note>; through this, the Chaos reveals itself, from which the four elements proceed according to the principles with their respective colors. It points to the hidden ground of the four elements, being the hidden world and also the mystery of humanity. For in this hiddenness of creation, God placed His covenant: that He would no longer destroy His image with water, and that the springs of the depths in the Chaos would no longer open as they did during the Great Flood and at the creation of the world.

33. The rainbow is an opening of the Chaos in nature, and—if the Sun stands in a favorable aspect <note>referring to astrological positioning and its influence on earthly matter</note>—it can produce a wonderful birth within the elements. In growing and living things, it can even cause a living, creaturely being to be born in the depths: namely, according to the property and power of the Sun, as it finds a specific stellar property within the elements. This can be for evil or for good—often manifesting as worms, flies, locusts, and the like, but also as a good life, depending on how Saturn and Mercury are ignited in their desire.

34. For if the Chaos opens itself, the harsh Saturnine property <note>the quality of contraction, coldness, and solidification</note> draws toward itself as if with a hunger and desire. It captures the property of the Chaos wherein the hidden powers lie, and coagulates them. Then Mercury <note>the quality of movement, sound, and life-force</note> immediately becomes alive within the sulfur <note>the flammable, soulful essence of matter</note>, for the Sun ignites the fiery Mars in its property, which makes Mercury mobile. Saturn captures this into a body—that is, a tangible being. The saltpeter <note>the explosive, "divine-nitre" or vital salt of nature</note> cannot unite with Mars; therefore, it leads to a separation and movement. Yet they cannot escape Saturn, who is the *command* <note>original: *fiat*; the creative word 'let there be'</note> of the external world; thus, it becomes a flying life, according to that specific constellation and property.

35. If the Sun is in a good aspect, then Saturn—meaning the Saturnine property—can capture a "dew-water" from the rainbow into itself, which afterwards falls upon the water. Certain fish swallow this and coagulate it within them, from which precious pearls can be produced.

36. For the Paradisiacal property also unfolds itself within the Chaos, provided it is not hindered by evil aspects; though the "all-too-wise" master <note>a sarcastic reference to scholars who rely only on rationalism or external observation</note> does not dare believe this—those who treat the ground of nature as if it were...

### Chapter 33. and God's covenant with Noah and all Creatures.

36. For I have no need of calves <note>a contemporary idiom for those who are spiritually dull or foolish</note> to understand my writings, but rather good, clear, enlightened eyes; for all others, these writings are entirely mute, no matter how wise those people may think they are.

37. 38. And the rainbow is primarily presented to man as a sign of grace, so that he may see himself in a true, open mirror of what he is. For in the rainbow, the sign of good and evil is made manifest, being an image of the center of nature from which evil and good arise, over which the Son of Man was appointed by God as a judge.

39. For the image of Noah’s Ark is also in the rainbow—would that we were not so blind! In the same way, the Trinity of the Godhead is pictured there: for the red color signifies the Father, the yellow and white the Son, and the blue the Spirit.

40. And God placed Himself in a figure according to His revelation in that same sign of the Covenant, so that we might flee to His grace, accept His Covenant, and constantly remember His future revelation, when He shall reveal the spiritual world once again; just as He placed a likeness for us there in the rainbow so that we might see what is hidden within it, and how we continually stand before Him.

4. 5. 6. The Spirit from this property mocked its own being in the *center* <note>original: "centrum"</note> of nature; he looked at himself in the shame of his father from which he had arisen, as if in a mirror of his selfhood. Thus that same spirit immediately went forth, being a life of vanity, and revealed what he was: namely, a mockery of Heaven.

### Cap. 34. How Noah cursed his son Ham. 267

7. Which the spirit from the image of God, in the formed word of the good essence <note>original: "ens"; the inner spiritual substance or being</note> in Noah, recognized; and in him, it awakened the center <note>original: "centrum"</note> of the fire of the souls in wrath, and cursed this spirit of vanity, so that it should not inherit the Kingdom of Heaven. The mocking-spirit shall not inherit the kingdom of God, but be cut off from the image of God—that is, from the outward image of the formed creature.

8. For that same property, from which shame arose, is in itself good; but in Adam’s imagineering <term>imagineering: the process by which Adam’s desire or imagination shaped his physical and spiritual form</term> toward the animal property, it became monstrous, bestial, and foreign to the image of God; therefore, this strange shape and form shall not remain eternally.

9. The mockery arose from the strange shape; the Devil crept into the figure of Ham’s strange spirit and mocked the heavenly womb, because the same had become a monster in the image of God; therefore, Noah's spirit cursed the false mocking-spirit.

10. It is not to be understood that Ham was cursed in his soul, or in the spirit of his soul; but rather according to the mocking figure of the mocking-spirit, which manifested itself out of the monster. Yet he (namely, the earthly image from the mud <note>original: "limo"; the clay or slime of the earth from which man was formed</note> of the earth) had to hide himself in the image of God with his own will, and be nothing other than a servant or a working-instrument of the image of God, out of the holy essence <note>original: "ens"</note>. The earthly spirit must not rule, but the heavenly one—namely, the soul with its spirit. The monster (that is, its spirit) should not be manifest; but because the free will awakened the monstrous spirit, which was nothing other than a mocker of the mystery in the Covenant, Noah cursed the same, and he would be a servant to his brothers.

11. For he said: Blessed be the God of Shem, and let Canaan be his servant; God enlarge Japheth, and let him dwell in the tents of Shem. The God of Shem was the one who had incorporated himself with the Covenant in the seed of the woman; his figure was Shem in the spirit. And Japheth was the figure of the poor soul that lay imprisoned in the monster; this same Japhetic or soulful property God would allow to dwell in the tents of Shem, and expand in Shem's figure.

12. But the figure of Ham, according to the monstrous spirit, would not be in the government of life in the rebirth <term>rebirth: the spiritual regeneration or "wedergeboorte" through which man returns to God</term>, but only as a servant, or like a working-instrument without its own will or its own life of selfhood; it would be used as a help and servant of the spiritual kingdom. On earth, it is like the night, which is hidden in the day and yet is truly there; and it is nevertheless as if it were not there, being the servant of the day for its work and power.

14. For Shem’s figure passed into the Covenant through Abraham and Israel, where the word of the Covenant was manifest and audible. Japheth’s figure proceeded into nature—specifically through the wisdom of nature within the kingdom of nature—from which the Gentiles <note>original: "Heydenen"; the non-Jewish nations who sought God through natural philosophy or reason</note> arose, who looked toward the light of nature. Shem’s line, however, looked toward the light within the Covenant. Thus Japheth—that is, the poor captive soul which is the eternal nature—dwelled in the tents of Shem; that is, under the Covenant. For the light of nature dwells within the light of grace and is a member of the household of the light of grace, being the light of God—namely, a formed or contained essence of the uncontained light of God.

15. From this arose the Sodomitic and truly bestial people, who esteemed neither the light of nature nor the light of grace within the Covenant.

16. This points to the external part of the souls belonging to the Spirit of this world. In the spiritual world, during rebirth, this must become a formed and contained will which, according to the manner of its own Spirit, cannot or does not desire to rule. Instead, it acts as a servant and minister to the creaturely soul and to the spirit of God within the Holy image of the light. This is not manifest in any independent understanding or in selfhood <note>original: "selfsheyd"; the state of being focused on one's own ego or separate identity</note>, but is hidden like the night within the day, and yet it truly exists.

17. For the animalistic soul shall not inherit the kingdom of light; even though it shall and must be present within it, it nevertheless holds no governance. Just as a tool is silent before its master—yet it remains the master's tool with which he makes whatever he wills—the animalistic soul in the rebirth is to be understood in the same way.

18. But this same will desires to have the supreme governance during the time of the four Elements; for it has introduced itself into a private ownership and into a figurative life of selfhood. Therefore, God has cursed it and condemned it to death, so that it must die away from this selfhood.

But it is to be lamented that this hunter hunts, slaughters, and eats the tame <term>animal-men<note>Humans living according to their physical instincts rather than divine spirit.</note></term> who do not belong to his hunt. Yet what shall be said, or with what shall the children of God excuse themselves and free themselves before God from this hunter? For every person carries the marks of the hunter’s hands on their external self, over which the hunter of nature has power. The internal spiritual man must simply leave his external animal under the hunter, for his external animal is also evil.

38. Under Ham’s lineage, the Spirit through Moses sets forth twenty-nine names that arose from Ham. This points to twenty-nine properties from the <term>third principle<note>original: "derde principium"; in this theology, the third principle is the visible, material world created from the interaction of light and darkness.</note></term>—that is, from the Spirit of the external world—showing how the <term>formed word<note>The divine "Speech" of God manifested in the shapes and varieties of the natural world.</note></term> would reveal itself through external nature, both in tongues and in the properties of nature. From these, the regimes and the ordering of lands have arisen. Although every property in turn has its own birth—just as a branch on a tree bears other sprouts—nevertheless, the Spirit through Moses points to the main root and properties under these names: what kind of peoples would arise from them, and how they would find their change and their end. All of this lies hidden within their names.

39. Thus Ham has twenty-nine names among his children, and he is the thirtieth. Twenty-nine is the number of his named children and grandchildren; within that lies the number of the end of Ham’s regime. His total number is thirty. Of this, the Prophet says that this Ham will sell the righteous one for thirty pieces of silver and give the same for a <term>Potter’s Field<note>original: "Pottebakkers Akker"; an allusion to the field bought with the blood money of Judas (Matthew 27:7), signifying the earthly and the transitory.</note></term>. Just as a pot is esteemed by its master, so is the fleshly "Ham-man" esteemed by God; he takes his thirtieth number, which he should have brought into the kingdom of God, and gives it for an earthly vessel, which compares to the field, and therein sells the righteous one. The righteous one lies hidden under the thirtieth number in the word of power. Thus the righteous one separates himself under the thirtieth number—through the dying of Ham’s flesh—from the twenty-ninth number of these properties which exalted themselves to the highest in Ham. For in the thirtieth year, the righteous one separated himself into his <term>office<note>original: "Ampt"; referring to the beginning of Christ’s public ministry at age 30.</note></term>, being Christ, and in the thirtieth number lies this same mystery. For our purposes here, this is enough to understand, and it is merely pointed out.

# How the human tree [spreads] through the children of Noah, Chapter 35.

40. Shem has twenty-six names in his line of expansion, and he is the twenty-seventh. The Spirit through Moses speaks very cryptically here; he is a father of all the children of Eber, and Eber fathered two sons; one was named Peleg, and the other Joktan; and this was because the world was divided in his time. Whenever the Spirit through Moses speaks of external history, he is simultaneously looking through it toward the <term>Line of Christ<note>The specific genealogical path leading to the birth of Jesus, viewed here as a spiritual current through history.</note></term>. For he says, Shem is a father of all the children of Eber; and although Eber is only in the third degree after Shem, nonetheless the Spirit watches so closely for the word in the <term>covenant<note>original: "verbond"; the sacred agreement and spiritual connection between God and humanity.</note></term>, observing where that same word opens itself into a specific Line.

41. For in the <term>formation of the word<note>The process by which the divine "Speech" of God takes shape in the physical and spiritual world.</note></term>, Eber signifies a sound, or a revelation of the word from the <term>Center<note>In this mystical context, the "Center" is the divine source from which all life and light originate.</note></term>, and he says further: he fathered Peleg, and named him so because of the "division." The Spirit does not merely look at the external division of the lands, but much more at the Line in which the sign of the covenant stood. For in Eber, the sign opened itself in the word—namely, in the "sound"—and passed through the seed to Peleg. There, the Lines of Adam and Christ separated within the two brothers, just as occurred later with the children of Abraham and Isaac, with Isaac and Ishmael, and with Jacob and Esau. So it was also here with Peleg and Joktan: outwardly the world was divided, and inwardly the Kingdom of Christ and the kingdom of the world were divided. This is not to be understood as if Joktan did not remain within the covenant; rather, the Spirit looks at the movement of the "seed," observing in which Line the sign was moving, where the word wished to move again within the <term>shining humanity<note>original: "verblikkerde menscheid"; a reference to the divine light reflecting or "flashing" through human nature.</note></term> of the <term>Heavenly essence<note>original: "Hemelsche ens"; the pure, spiritual substance of the divine realm.</note></term>, and reveal itself within mankind.

42. The names of the children and grandchildren of Shem are individual pointers to the properties from the "wonder-line" of the prophetic spirit of Enoch, where those same properties led themselves out from the trunk into branches; yet here they sprout forth.

43. But of Peleg, he says no more than that he fathered one son when he was 30 years old, whom he gave a name, namely, Reu. Pointing to the Line of Christ, in which the sign stood, the Spirit points there only to a single person: for through one single individual, the covenant would be opened. For the Spirit looked with that one individual toward the kingdom...

### Of Abraham and His Seed, etc. Chapter 37.

So too is the lineage of Christ—in the same trunk of the promised word within the covenant—grown from branch to branch, even to the height of the sprouts, until its proper maturity; until the power of the tree (that is, the word in the covenant) has opened itself with the glorious, beautiful blossom.

2. From which blossom, in turn, the holy image of God has grown in flesh and blood—namely, in a holy body. One sees its branches and sprouts so very beautiful that the soul rejoices greatly at the sight of them, and rightfully desires to grow out upon these branches and sprouts, to the great praise of God, in our <term>Angelic tree<note>A mystical concept representing the spiritual community of believers or the restored state of humanity in Christ, often contrasted with the "tree of the knowledge of good and evil."</note></term> of the <term>Hierarchy of Christ<note>original: *Hierarchia Christi*</note></term> of the Holy Paradise.

3. God made a covenant with Adam after his fall, when He poured that **heavenly <term>ens<note>From the Latin for "being" or "essence"; in this context, it refers to the spiritual substance or "soul-matter" of the human being.</note></term>** into him, [promising] that He would make him alive again and give him new birth. This covenant was the root in the dimmed *ens*; it grew in this lineage of Adam, from Seth and his children and descendants, up to Noah, in one trunk of the tree; and with Noah, God renewed the covenant.

4. For the undivided <term>sensual tongue<note>The "sensual tongue" refers to the original, unified language of humanity before the Tower of Babel, which was believed to perfectly express the inner essence of things through the sound and spirit of the letters.</note></term>, in which the spirits of the letters ruled in a single harmony, lasted until the Deluge, so that all men spoke in a single tongue, in which the Spirit of God hovered from the five vowels, being the Divine understanding.

5. But after they had introduced the image and the beast of vanity into the sensual tongues, and fornicated with the **Harlot of selfhood**, God complained of them, that they no longer wished to let themselves be ruled by His Spirit, and said He regretted that He had made man.

8. 9. In this way, the spirit of nature's formed word also claimed them, and one intellect moved the other: namely, the human intellect in its desire moved the intellect in the soul of the external world. # Of Abraham and his Seed, etc. Chapter 37.

...of the covenant is the **oracle** <note>original: *oraculum*; the divine voice or prophetic utterance</note>, being the Divine voice, made manifest in Abraham; therefore the spirit of the Lord commanded him to depart from his fatherland, from his kindred, for from kinship—that is, from his own blood—the voice of Divine revelation with the Messiah or Christ would not come, but from God. Yet within him lay the **vessel** <margin>vessels <note>original German: *Gefäße*</note></margin>, being the **essence** <note>original: *Ens*; Böhme uses this term to describe the inner spiritual substance or "being" of a person</note>, in which the Divine voice wished to reveal itself; and therefore, because a foreign seed was to be introduced into his own seed, namely a heavenly **essence** <note>original: *ens*; see John 3</note>, He commanded him to go out from his lineage.

22. For the power for Divine revelation did not reside in man's **essence** <note>original: *ens*</note>, but in God's; yet the **essence** of man had to be joined to it, so that Adam's heavenly obscured **essence** might become living in the living **essence** of Christ, and arise from death in Christ. Therefore God spoke to Abram: "Go out into a land that I will show you." Here the spirit indicates that in his fatherland—that is, in the earthly man—he would not behold God, but in the land which the Lord would show him in his seed, which was a foreign seed from the Divine **essence** <note>original: *ens*</note>. In that same foreign seed, He wanted to bless and sanctify his own seed—that is, to **tincture** <note>original: *tingeren*; to transform or infuse with spiritual quality, like an alchemist's dye</note> it with the Divine **tincture** <note>original: *tincture*; the spiritual life-force that enlivens and purifies nature</note> of the ninth number in the **Holy Ternary** <note>original: *in ternario Sancto*; the manifestation of the Trinity within the spiritual world</note> with the **tincture** of the holy spiritual world.

23. For thus the spirit spoke to Abraham: "Go out from your fatherland, and from your kindred, and out of your father’s house, into a land that I will show you, and I will make you into a great nation, and will bless you; and make you a great name, you shall be a blessing, I will bless those who bless you, and curse those who curse you, and in you shall all the families of the earth be blessed." God spoke, wishing to make him a great name, and to bless all those who would bless him, and curse those who would curse him. This great name that He wished to make for him in his seed was not to be understood only in the kingdom of this world; for Abraham was nothing else on earth but a stranger, and had to wander from one place to another, and possessed no principality nor kingdom, like the great names of the heathens arising from the **sensual** <note>original: *Sensualische*; relating to the physical senses and the outward, fragmented language of the fallen world</note> compacted tongue. ### Of Abraham and his seed, etc. Chapter 37. ###

...has, neither time nor place nor possession; but through all and in all is from eternity, into eternity, and has revealed itself only in humanity, just as a fire glows through iron and changes it entirely into fire, while the iron yet remains iron; so is it also to be understood of the human being, or humanity, whom Mary bore as a single being out of her essence and out of God’s essence.

40. She has borne the humanity, and God the Father has from eternity born the Word, which revealed itself in the humanity and filled the humanity, just as a fire glows through iron, and as the Sun shines through water or glass.

41. She did indeed bear the Heavenly body, yet not out of the power of her **ens** <term>ens: a term used by theosophers like Jacob Böhme to describe the essential "spiritual substance" or soul-matter of a person</term> or seed, but out of the power of the **ens** that was revealed in her seed; namely, the essence of eternity revealed itself through time, and yet time could not take the essence of eternity into its own power. Rather, the essence of eternity took the essence of time upon itself, just as the inward Heaven and the inward world brought forth and took upon itself the outward Heaven and the outward world; thus also eternity has taken upon itself the essence that had breathed itself into Adam—which died or faded away—in the seed of Mary (<insert>meaning in her own human seed</insert>).

42. # CHAPTER 39.

->*How God appeared to Abraham in a vision, and confirmed the covenant with him in his seed, and how Abraham's faith laid hold of the covenant, which was counted to him as righteousness, and how God commanded him to sacrifice, what is to be understood thereby.*<-

->Genesis Chapter 15.<-

1. Moses says: it happened after these occurrences that the word of the Lord came to Abraham in a vision, and spoke, "Fear not, Abraham, I am your shield and very great reward." Whereupon Abraham said: "Lord, Lord, what will you give me? I go hence without children, and my house-steward has a son, this Eliezer of Damascus." And Abraham spoke further: "To me you have given no seed, and see, this son of my household shall be my heir." And behold, the Lord spoke to him: "He shall not be your heir, but he who shall come from your own body, he shall be your heir." And He commanded him to go out, and spoke: "Look toward Heaven and count the stars, if you can count them." And He spoke to him: "So shall your seed be." Abraham believed the Lord, and He counted the same to him as righteousness.

2. In this part lies the root of the Christian faith: for God said to Abraham that He was his shield and reward; He wanted to give him the seed from his loins. God wanted to be Abraham's reward and give him a Son from within himself, whose seed should be as the stars in the Heavens, which are innumerable. Not the son of his household was to be his heir—not the seed of the animal-like man <note>The "animal-like man" refers to the fallen, earthly nature of humanity that is driven by fleshly instincts rather than the spirit of God.</note>, full of snakes, etc. <note>original: "ens," likely an abbreviation for "enzovoorts" (etc.) in this instance</note>—but God’s reward, God’s **essence** <term>essence: the original text uses the Latin "ens," a technical term in mystical philosophy referring to a spiritual substance or the fundamental "being" that makes up a soul or divine entity</term>. He wanted to give him his reward in his seed, namely, into the powers of his loins, and that would become a seed like the stars in the Heavens. He looked upon the seed in the covenant, namely upon the eternal kingdom, which would be like the stars in the Heavens, so pure, clean, and innumerable; and this same thing Abraham believed, and that was counted to him as righteousness.

# CHAPTER 39.
### And of the covenant confirmed with him in his seed.

3. To believe, in this context, means this: that he grasped *the word*, and he received it into his desire—that is, into the human *essence* <term>ens: a Latin term used here to describe the fundamental spiritual "being" or "substance" of a person</term>. The sign in the covenant, in the formed, compacted word—namely in Abraham's nature and quality—took on the speaking word of God, which is the promise. These two formed themselves into one, and in this "one," Abraham's faith was justified. For God credited to Abraham the word—which he took into the desire of his faith—as righteousness, as a possession and justification.

4. For this internal word justified the creaturely word, which is the spoken, created word. Understand this as that which has formed itself in the human quality and has entered into a creaturely form—that is, into an image composed of three principles <note>In the author's philosophy, the "three principles" usually refer to the dark world (fire/wrath), the light world (love/majesty), and the outward world (nature/matter)</note>. In this image, the self-will—through desire and lust, combined with the quality of the dark world (which is the fire and wrath of God)—has elevated itself to the highest position and introduced itself into an earthly coarseness. Into this coarse image, the Devil, through the serpent’s "fine essence" <note>original: "fijn ens"</note>, introduced his own will and desire.

5. To this same *essence* and compacted word, and to this created image, the living, eternal, speaking Holy Word came to help, from the quality of light and Divine love, and became its reward. It took into itself the natural word and power of Abraham; and that same internal word of God, grasped in the desire, justified the corrupted word of Abraham. It became his righteousness, which broke the wrath and frustrated the Devil’s desire and will. Understand that this occurred within the human *essence*—that is, in the formed word.

6. For there is no faith without the word, and without the power of God. Thus Abraham now took God's word, power, and promise into himself, into his *essence*, and grasped it into a substance of his spirit. That was the faith of justification: that the word of God and the will and desire of man entered into one spiritual substance. Thus God credited to Abraham that same internalized or "spoken-in" grasped word as righteousness—that is, as a possession. This is the ground and the root of faith: that he grasped the promise of God in his desire as his own possession and did not let it go in doubt. Just as Jacob did, who grasped the word of the promise within himself and said, "I will not leave you, unless you bless me" <note>A reference to Genesis 32:26</note>; and he wrestled the entire night with the word of power until he overcame, so that the promised word gave itself to him as a possession—that is, as a blessing or a great reward—just as it did here with Abraham.

We do not mean the coarse earthly man, full of the *essence* of the serpent, who shall not inherit the kingdom of God (John 6), but the true man, whom God created in his image.
