With this we do not judge nor condemn worldly dominions and ordinances, but we point out the ground of all mystery: dominion arises from the kingdom of nature, and may well enter into the kingdom of God, provided that it exercises its power like a servant-maid in the kingdom of nature, and not like a god of its own self who does what he pleases; provided that they acknowledge themselves to be God's **officials** in his kingdom of nature, and do not transgress the order of nature, nor set themselves higher than the office of nature ordains for them, making themselves into **idols**. Of these God says to Abraham: *This people whom they must serve, I will judge.*

# CHAPTER 40.

### Concerning the History and completely marvelous representation of the Spirit of God with Hagar, the Maidservant of Sarah, and her Son Ishmael; concerning his expulsion from the inheritance and concerning the inheritance of Isaac.

->Genesis Ch. XVI.<-

1. Whoever wishes to read the history of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and to understand it rightly—what the Spirit of God points to therein—must not view it merely as a bare history <note>original: *Historie*. In this context, the author warns against reading the Bible as a simple record of past events, suggesting instead that it contains deep, hidden spiritual truths.</note>, under which nothing more than a narrative exists. The entire kingdom of Christ, alongside the kingdom of nature, is depicted therein. It portrays not only the work of human redemption but also who, what, or how one shall inherit the Kingdom of God. It is not as the Jews boast, that they alone are the people of God; no, it is something entirely different. God does not look upon a single lineage, but upon the stem or root of the tree.

2. In two brothers, namely in Isaac and Ishmael, the two kingdoms are prefigured: in Ishmael the **kingdom of nature**, and in Isaac the **kingdom of grace**; so it is also in Esau and in Jacob. For from Abraham two lines now went forth, being those of Japheth and Shem <note>While Japheth and Shem are sons of Noah, the author here links their spiritual lineages to the descendants of Abraham to show how different "types" of humanity emerge.</note>. Ishmael was the first, just as Japheth was among the children of Noah, and likewise Cain among the children of Adam. This points to the **kingdom of nature**, which has its origin in the "property of the father" <term>property of the father: In this mystical theology, the "Father" represents the raw, fiery power of nature and justice, while the "Son" represents the light of grace and love.</term> and must always be first if a creature is to be born at all.

3. After that, the **kingdom of grace** first arrives, which takes possession of nature; just as a fire must first exist if there is to be a light. The fire gives birth to the light, and the light makes the fire manifest within itself; it takes the fire, which is nature, into itself and dwells in the fire.

4. Similarly, we are to understand the two properties of humanity, namely in two principles according to **fire and light**; that is, according to the Father's and the Son's properties—according to **wrath** and **love**, which are both in a single being.

5. But since the human will has subjected itself to the kingdom of nature, the kingdom of nature now also represented the properties of the highest God in the human image; firstly in

6. Those two images were established there: namely, in Ishmael, the poor, weak, evil, and corrupted Adam, who had fallen away from the will of God; and in Isaac, the image of Christ, who had come to help poor corrupted Adam, and to lead his fallen will into death and into a state of dying, to refine it again in the fire of God, and to give it a new birth in the fire of love, back into the first, single will of God—where the Father and Son, though existing in the fierce fire of wrath and in the fire of love and light, are but one single will and essence.

7. For with the movement of the Divine attribute, when God moved nature and created creatures, the two attributes—love and wrath—separated within nature. This was so that through struggle and opposing wills, the mystery of God (being the invisible spiritual world) would become manifest and enter into a wrestling game <note>The author uses the concept of a "wrestling game" or "counter-play" to describe how spiritual growth and divine revelation require the friction of opposing forces.</note>.

8. For if there were but one single will, then all beings would do but one single thing. But in the conflicting will, each thing raises itself within itself toward its own victory and exaltation; and in this struggle stands all life and growth. Through this, the Divine wisdom is made manifest and takes on a form for contemplation and for a realm of joy; for in victory there is joy. But a single, unconflicted will is not manifest to itself, for in it there is neither evil nor good, neither joy nor sorrow. And even if it were so, yet the one—being the single will—must first introduce itself into a counter-play within itself, so that it may reveal itself.

9. Thus we must also understand it here with Isaac and Ishmael: because Christ was to be born from the seed of Abraham, the corrupted man (whom Christ would help) also had to be born from this same seed of Abraham.

10. For Christ, being the word and the will of God, took upon himself—into his holy Heavenly <term>ens</term> <note>ens: A philosophical term meaning "being" or "essence." In this mystical context, it refers to the underlying spiritual substance of a person.</note>—man’s apostate <term>ens</term> and will. He led these himself into the death of selfhood, even into the root from which the fallen human will had originated at the beginning of the creation of man; that is, into the fierceness of the eternal—

17. Within Ishmael was the self-willed, apostate natural will, which he had inherited from his mother Hagar and from Abraham’s natural Adamic will; this will was a mocker of the new rebirth.

18. This false spirit was a mocker within Ishmael, and of him God said: *drive out the son of the maidservant, who is the mocker; for the mocking spirit and will shall not inherit with the free—that is, with the singular will of God.*

It is a kingdom of grace and not a kingdom of inheritance from a human lineage, but God gave it out of grace to Abraham in his seed.

## Of the Seal of the covenant of the circumcision of the Foreskin and of Baptism.

1. When God had made the covenant with Abram, and blessed him, and had made him a Father of many nations, who through him—that is, through Abram’s blessing—should be blessed in the covenant, He gave him the seal of the covenant, being the sign and the figure upon whose <term>being</term> <note>original: "ens"; Böhme uses this Latin term to describe the essential, spiritual substance or "soul-stuff" of a person.</note> the blessing was directed. He showed him in this figure what would inherit and possess the eternal blessing: namely, not the coarse, earthly fleshy man, who is conceived and born in the lust of the flesh, from the carnal lust of man and woman, and who in Adam turned toward the animal and fleshy property of the divided essence of the interwoven life. The covenant and the blessing were not directed toward this [fleshy man], but toward the formed <term>being</term> <note>original: "ens"</note> of the word, out of the <term>slime</term> <note>original: "limo"; referring to the *Limbus* or the "dust of the earth" mentioned in Genesis, interpreted here as a refined, heavenly substance.</note> of the earth, out of the property of the Heavenly world; not upon the introduced <term>being</term> <note>original: "ens"</note> of the serpent, out of the essence and property of the dark world, but upon the soul and upon its right body, which was created for it in Adam.

2. And one sees here in circumcision an image: that the fleshy mingling of man and woman is an abomination to the holiness of God, which is nevertheless tolerated under Divine patience, because it cannot now be otherwise with man, and because he has lost the magical birth of Paradise. For God set forth the figure here, in circumcision, that everything which was male must allow itself to be circumcised at this member of the propagation of the male seed. Since man sows his own will, out of the property of nature, into his seed, God established the figure there, with the cutting off of both the earthly seed and also of the member and will: for the spirit in the covenant would cut off this figure in the inward spiritual man through the death of Christ, together with this fleshy will and desire.

3. For the fleshy, coarse, earthly seed of the man, or of the woman, would not attract the covenant and the blessing, as Christ also said: but that which is born not of the will of man, nor of the flesh, but of God. 33. 34. For in the fire-baptism of the Jews, the Spirit baptized only without water; but among Christians, the Spirit baptizes through water. Jewish women could indeed take on the Spirit in the fire-baptism of the man; but since that same fiery Word has now become flesh, they must now rightly take on Christ in the flesh as well, and be baptized. For their heavenly dimmed Virginity must also take on Christ's introduced Heavenly Virginity within them, so that they may become a true masculine virgin in Christ's spirit and being.

35. Now reason asks further: why then did the children—namely the boys—have to be circumcised only on the eighth day? Why not earlier or later? For that which is the rest and the true life of the six properties, God also included in the <term>compaction</term> <note>original: "compactie"; the densification or structural forming of creation.</note> of the creation.

37. So the eighth day came to his aid out of pure grace, and gave itself back into his seven working days; that is, into the seven properties of his own being. 38. 39. And from this arose the commandment for the Jews that they must also outwardly sanctify and rest on the **Saturday**, being the **Sabbath**; thereby pointing to the inward, Holy, eternal Sabbath, in which the spirit of God works in humans and in all creatures, in each according to its property; for all that is created rests in him.

40. And therefore He commanded the boys to be circumcised on the eighth day—that is, in Himself—for He is Himself that same eighth day who circumcises. For before **Christ’s** humanity, the process proceeded in the form of nature; but now that **Christ** has fulfilled the nature of man and has entered into the seven days of man's property, the eighth day—namely **Christ**—is now within the seven days. Now, one may baptize children on any day.

# THE 42ND CHAPTER.

## *Of the three men who appeared to Abraham in the oak grove of Mamre (what this figure represents), who went to Sodom and set the cities of the children of Ham on fire from the Lord.*

->*Genesis 18.*<-

1. Firstly, because Abraham [at first] was only named Abram, God appeared to him in a vision as a single being. And once he had sealed the covenant with circumcision, He called him Abraham, which means "a multitude of nations" <note>original: "eenen hoop volkeren"; a reference to the Hebrew etymology of Abraham's name provided in Genesis 17:5.</note>: a breathed-out, public people of God, into whom God had breathed Himself, or revealed Himself. And He appeared to him thereafter in the revelation of the Holy Trinity—namely, in three men who were nothing other than a single one. Therein, the revelation of the Holy Trinity in the Godhead was presented in the image of man, showing how the entire trinity of the Godhead now wished to reveal itself in humanity through this covenant, so that one would see the Holy Trinity of the Godhead in the flesh.

2. And this points to the great humility in the Godhead, that is in Christ: how Christ would dwell with men and allow Himself to be fed by men, just as He came to Abraham in these three men and let His feet be washed, and also ate and drank. This indicates that one must feed the poor Christ—who is poor in this world—in His members and children (who shall also be nothing other than poor, despised people). Whatever one does for them, one has done for the three men; that is, for Christ and the Holy Godhead in humanity.

### Of the three men who appeared to Abraham Chapter 42.

26. And when God—now with Abraham, in the *heavenly <term>ens</term>* <note>original: "ens"; a Latin term meaning "being" or "essence." In this mystical context, it refers to the spiritual substance of the soul or the divine spark.</note> (which He wished to reveal and introduce into the seed of the woman, as also the heavenly *ens* into the *ens* of the covenant, with the opening of the living word)—had delighted Himself and played before him, and had fed Himself in the *ens*, namely in the power of Abraham's praise, to wit: in his humility, God then asked after Sarah, whom He well knew; but Sarah did not know that He was the Lord in such a form. So He spoke to Abraham: where is your wife Sarah? That is to say, she was not yet in this play; until she received the *ens* of Abraham’s faith, then this play was awakened in her, which is why she laughed at this; for she did not know the mystery, which now revealed itself only in the spirit of Abraham, where the *ens* of faith lay; and he spoke, she is in the hut, that is: she is in the human hut, covered with the earthly hut; so that she does not see who is with me. <note>The "hut" or "tabernacle" is a common metaphor for the physical, mortal body that veils the spirit.</note>

27. And the Lord spoke; I shall come to you again, behold, then Sarah your wife shall have a son; that is to say: I shall come to you again with the movement of your seed, when Sarah shall become pregnant, so I shall dissolve her in her enclosed seed and come into your seed; that is, to move, for "to come" is called to go, to move; when God comes, He moves the person, and comes or goes in and with the person.

28. But where He says, *as I live*, the same is spoken in an *essential* <note>original: "essentialische"</note> manner, for God told him how He wished to come, not before him as He did this time; but *so*, that is, just as the appearance and power of the Sun enters into a fruit, so it does not step beside the fruit when it comes, but *so*, that is, it penetrates *essentially* <note>original: "essentialiter"</note> with the *so*. For *so* means as much as "I will look into"; "as I live" is not to be understood as if He said, "if I am still alive"; but He wished to live in the *so*, He wished to come *essentially* in the *so*, and not figuratively as He did this time.

29. For when God comes, He comes in no other way than *so*, that is, like a sunshine into the fruit: in the <term>language of nature</term> <note>original: "natuurspraak"; a mystical concept referring to the original, universal language that expresses the true essence of things.</note> one understands this *essentially* very beautifully; for when God speaks of His own coming, He speaks in no other way than *essentially*, in the manner of the uncompacted *essensual* tongue.

30. And Sarah laughed at this; she thought that she should now still bear a son from the desire of Abraham, from human cohabitation in the lust of the flesh, therefore she said: shall I, now that I and my Lord are old, still practice pleasure? The spirit of the animal world mocked its youth, that it was already weak, and should now still become lustful, and thought it would be a game that you could do such a thing, as if one said to an old person: you shall become young again, and receive such a desire and lust once more.

### Chapter 42. In the Oak Grove of Mamre.

just as when you were young; nature would laugh at that and think, "Yes, could this really be true?" where half-doubt and half-hope were mingled together. So it went for Sarah too, for the spirit of the world does not understand the mysteries of God; before God, it is nothing other than an animal. And when the spirit of the world heard that it would happen in such a way, it thought: "I shall be the master-builder; yes, if only I could, I would gladly do so," and it laughed at itself, thinking it would become young again.

31. The natural man understands as much about God as an animal does; when it sees hay, it thinks, "there is something to eat," but if it does not see it, it hopes out of habit. But Sarah had hoped until she had become 90 years old, and it seemed a wonder to her that God would do something to her beyond the natural course and custom, and she imagined the matter in the manner of human <term>lust</term> <note>The Dutch "wellust" here refers to physical, carnal pleasure or the biological drive of procreation.</note>.

32. But the Lord spoke: why does Sarah laugh at that? And she feared and said, "I did not laugh." But the Lord spoke: "It is not so; you did laugh; should anything be impossible for the Lord?" Here stands the image of Eve, when she had turned her curiosity in her own lust toward the forbidden tree; and when God asked her afterward why she had done such a thing, she also denied her own lust and laid it upon the serpent.

33. Since God had now played here with Abraham concerning the <term>new birth</term> <note>The "new birth" (nieuwe geboorte) or regeneration is the central mystical process of the soul returning to God.</note>, He also played here with Sarah regarding the lust of Eve—which was to be killed by this "seed of the woman" as if it were a lie. For this reason, Sarah had to speak a lie here—that she had not laughed—because Eve had lied. Thus, God set before Himself the lie of Eve: how He wished to put the same to shame through the eternal truth and drive it back; just as He did to Sarah, driving the lie back into her so that she had to be ashamed.

34. And you must understand here that God has presented the entire process: how He wished to give new birth to the true man whom He created, how the same would come to pass, and how He wished to burn the <term>ens</term> <note>original: "ens"; refers to the essential spiritual substance or "being" of a thing.</note> of the serpent in the eternal fire, and how He wished to make the lie of the poor soul a mockery upon the cross and kill it; for we see this entirely clearly here in the image.

35. After God had presented the process of the new birth, these three men went toward Sodom, and wished to burn <term>Ham</term> <note>In this mystical tradition, Noah's son Ham represents the "fleshly" or "dark" property of man that must be purified or judged.</note>—that is, the evil, fleshly property of Ham—with fire from the Lord. This also occurred, so that one clearly sees how the judgment of God begins at the house of Israel, and how Christ has been established as a judge over the *ens* and the will of the Devil, who would burn the Devil's essence with fire, just as this following figure indicates.

# CHAPTER 43.

->*Concerning the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah, and how God revealed the same to Abraham beforehand.*<-

->*Genesis 18 and 19.*<-

1. AND the Lord spoke to Abraham (after he had blessed Abraham and said that he should command his children to walk in the way of the Lord, and how he wished to bless them likewise, as has been explained here previously): behold, there is a cry reaching to Sodom and Gomorrah; it is great, and their sins are very heavy. Therefore I will descend and see whether they have done everything according to the cry that has come before me or not, so that I may know it. And the men turned their faces and went toward Sodom. God spoke: how can I hide from Abraham what I am doing, since he shall become a great nation? And he pointed out to him there what he intended to do.

2. The <term>unilluminated intellect</term> <note>The original Dutch uses "onverligte vernuft," referring to human reason that lacks spiritual or divine insight.</note> looks upon these <term>figures</term> <note>Historical or biblical events seen as symbolic patterns of spiritual truths.</note> with wonder—that God said he would descend and see whether the same cry were true or not. For the intellect thinks: "is he then <term>measurable</term> <note>original: "afmetelijk," meaning finite or limited by dimensions</note> or only existing up there? Does he not know everything beforehand?"—especially since the Scripture says of him: "Am I not he who fulfills all things?" Likewise: "Heaven is my throne and the earth is my footstool." How then should he descend, like a measurable being that is separated by time and place?

3. Even more incomprehensible to that same reason is the "cry" that has risen up to him. For this reason, <term>creaturely reason</term> <note>The logical mind of a created being, which is limited compared to the Creator.</note> thinks: God dwells only above the stars, in a Heaven alone, and he looks down here just as the radiance of the Sun looks and shines from its body upon the earth. This is as far as the intellect has come; it knows nothing more of what God is or where God is. It does not know that he is all being, and dwells through all beings, and possesses no place, nor requires any space or room for his dwelling. It does not know that he—insofar as he is named God—is not a "being" in the physical sense, but is relative to being like a "nothing," even though he is nonetheless through everything and gives himself into being by working within it, just as the power of the Sun works upon the fruit—yet not from the outside inward, but working from the inside outward toward its own revelation, along with the creature and its life. The nature and the creature are his revelation; if the [intellect] understood this rightly, it would have no need to ask further here.

4. Now understand the contents as follows: God dwells in himself, both

according to love and according to wrath, each property sees only into itself, and is not manifest in the other with its own property; just as you have an analogy here in the day and night, namely in light and darkness: the light dwells in the darkness and does not see it, and likewise the darkness does not see the light. And just as the light, in its great gentleness, dwells in the fire, yet does not take on the distress and pain of the fire, but remains only good, without a sensory life of the fire—even though it arises through the consuming of the fire, namely through the dying of the substance—understand also the being of God in this way.

5. The love-eye of God does not see <term>essentially</term> <note>original: "essentialiter"</note> into the evil, turned-away soul, nor into the Devil; but his wrath-eye sees into it. That is, God sees into the Devil and into the false soul according to the fierce property of wrath or fire.

6. Therefore God said that a cry had come before him. By this he meant his manifested word—that is, the voice in the divine revealed <term>ens</term> <note>From the Latin for 'being' or 'essence'; refers to the fundamental spiritual substance or the "being" of a thing in its potential state.</note> of these three men. It had come before the *ens* and before the hearing, which had now presented itself in three persons within the promised *ens* to mankind, toward the humanity of Christ.

7. For to this word, or hearing, the judgment over all devils and godless people had been given; for this was the moving hearing through which God the Father heard within humanity, and through which he wished to separate the evil from the good.

8. So this same hearing—being the hearing that wished to reveal itself in humanity in the person of Christ—had heard within itself the voice of the Sodomites, that is, of the children of Ham, namely according to the property of wrath. And it brought this same hearing before the infinite hearing in the <term>first principle</term> <note>original: "eerste principium." In this mystical theology, the "first principle" refers to the dark, fiery source of nature, while the second is the light of God.</note>, that is, in the origin of nature and the creature. For the Sodomites—understand the children of the flesh—all live together in the hearing of this world, which is the spoken, formed word in the figure of the Deity, where evil and good are manifest together in a single being.

9. Now understand this thoroughly: the <term>angelic world</term> <note>original: "Engelsche wereld." In 17th-century Dutch, "Engelsch" can mean "English," but here it refers to "Engelen" (Angels).</note> is called "above," and the formed external world is called "below"—spoken in the same way as when one lights a fire: the light is above, and the substance is below. When one speaks of God’s "above," one means "inward"; for that which is inward, outside of the substance, is "above." For outside of the substance, everything is "above" and there is no "below"; that which is below the substance is also "above."

10. So the cry of the Sodomites had come before that which is "above," that

but they had all turned away together, except for his brother's son <note>referring to Lot, the nephew of Abraham</note>, who was a stranger among this people; God led him out beforehand, before He kindled the wrath.

22. The spirit of Moses speaks here in a very veiled manner, as does the spirit in Ezra, who wrote down these histories in the spirit of God after they had been lost among the children of Israel <note>According to Jewish and early Christian tradition, the priest Ezra was said to have miraculously reconstructed the books of the Law after they were destroyed during the Babylonian exile</note>, and one sees clearly how the spirit looks so closely at the figure of Abraham and points out what is to be understood by it.

23. For at the appearance to Abraham, he speaks of 3 men, and here he speaks of 2 Angels who went to Sodom and destroyed those cities; showing that the person of Christ is the third, who did not go along, for here only two went, being God’s truth and God’s justice—that is, judgment and truth. The judgment remained in Sodom, and the truth led Lot out of there.

24. And when these both came to Sodom toward evening (when their time was up and the day had passed), Lot sat at the gate, and when he saw them, he stood up to meet them, and bowed with his face to the ground and said: "See, my lords, please turn into the house of your servant and stay the night, and let your feet be washed; then you may rise early tomorrow and go your way." But they said, "No; we will spend the night in the street." Then he urged them greatly, and they turned in to him and came into his house; and he prepared a meal for them and baked unleavened cakes, and they ate.

25. When one wishes to show this in its true understanding, it is explained thus: the cry of the Sodomites was the curse that Noah placed upon Ham when he cursed him because of his unchaste and fleshly eyes and desire. That same cursed fleshly spirit had propagated and raised itself in the malicious, completely earthly and serpentine property <note>In this mystical context, "serpentine" refers to the corrupted nature inherited from the Fall of Adam and the influence of the Serpent</note> in the flesh and in the soul of these children of Ham, so that it had established itself in a kingly government, under which they lived more as flesh than as truly human.

26. This cry of the cursed serpentine <term>ens</term> <note>From the Latin for 'being' or 'essence'; refers here to the fundamental spiritual substance or the corrupted "being" of the Sodomites</note> which had grown up in the wrath, was now manifest and audible in its mother (understand: in the wrath of God, in the property of the dark world), and it had awakened the judgment over and within itself. So God now sent a judgment over the serpentine *ens*; this was the time of the hidden and now opened seal of Enoch (as has been indicated here before regarding the seven lines), where its mystery was at an end, and now, like a sound of his preaching, became manifest in the word of power, both in love and in wrath.

27. Namely, in Abraham in love, where the formed word—which they began to preach in Enoch's time <note>According to tradition, the era of Enoch marked the beginning of public worship and the formal "preaching" of the Word</note>—now revealed itself in the formed, grown essence (or being) in Abraham, along with the promised and holy seed of faith. And in the children of wickedness, who were of the cursed nature of Ham, the property of wrath revealed itself here, from the preaching of Enoch, where he threatened with the judgment and punishment of God; this same wrath had also grown up in the children of wickedness and had become a substance <note>In this mystical context, "substance" refers to a spiritual reality that has taken solid form in a person's character or nature</note>.

28. And when this seal of Enoch now opened, signifying that his mystery was at an end and was now to be revealed according to love and wrath, every property presented its being there for Divine contemplation. All that the word had wrought in the essence <note>original: "ens," a philosophical term for the fundamental being or "thing-ness" of a creature</note> of love under the sound of Enoch, as well as the sound of the threat of God’s wrath: now the beings of both properties opened themselves and presented themselves in the trial for the judgment of God’s righteousness. Thus it stood there in judgment: namely, in Abraham [was] Christ, in the judgment of Enoch’s preaching of repentance; and in the threat of Enoch's punishment, there stood in judgment, in the children of the curse, in Ham, the earnest judgment of God—namely, Prince Lucifer, for the execution in the wrath of God, being a servant of the house of darkness.

29. For God said to the people of Israel at Mount Sinai: *I shall visit and punish the iniquity of the parents upon the children, even unto the third and fourth generation* <note>A reference to Exodus 20:5</note>; which is to be seen here in Ham, the son of Noah; here the curse of Noah first came into judgment.

30. And here two Angels—that is, in the strength and power of judgment—were found in the place of Christ, since Christ was not yet in the flesh, nor yet in His office <note>The "office" of Christ refers to His role as Mediator and Savior</note>; for the office of Christ remained standing before the Lord in Abraham, and he prayed for the apostate people in Sodom and Gomorrah.

31. But when they were tested before the Lord in the judgment—that is, in the office of Christ’s love with Abraham—to see if there might still be people in Sodom who were receptive to the office of Christ in love, and none were found, then the office of Christ remained behind in Abraham and did not go along to Sodom. But the office of Divine righteousness and truth went in the form of two Angels to Sodom, and looked deep within their very essence and being, testing that same thing in themselves; as can be seen: as soon as these two Angels came into the city, its property <note>the inherent spiritual quality or "nature" of the city</note> opened itself, and it wanted to have these men out there among them.

32. For these two Angels had awakened or moved their property, and presented the same before the Lord to contemplate what was in them; so they found that they were nothing other than bestial, unchaste murderers; this they placed in judgment, as they now had to be judged according to their essences <note>original: "effents," likely a variant of "essences," referring to the fundamental spiritual nature of a person</note>.

33. But that the Spirit in Moses points out that Lot sat at the gate and recognized these Angels, and invited them to come in to him, and wished to wash their feet and baked cakes, and that they ate, and at first refused to enter to him: this is a great hidden mystery. For it was the Spirit of truth and righteousness; Lot recognized him, for he went movably into the essences <note>original: "effents"</note>, and first pressed into Lot with the trial <note>original: "proba," a Latin term for a test or proof of quality</note>; and when he bowed himself to the earth before the Lord and humbled himself, he was tested and found righteous within himself.

34. But the truth first refused to go into his house with righteousness—that is, with the judgment—and wished to remain in the street; for it was known of Lot’s wife, who, when she was tested and the judgment pressed through her, was denied temporal life. For she remained standing in the judgment like a **First Matter** <note>original: "Prima Materia"</note>, being a **Sulphur** and **Mercury** <note>original: "Sulphur, Mercurius." In the author's mystical chemistry, these represent the fundamental energetic building blocks of the physical world</note>, that is, a compressed matter of the judgment, being a change into the first being from which the body was created.

35. Yet not immediately before the execution of this judgment, but when Lot went out of Sodom with her and the judgment began, the judgment within her drew her back again, as is seen in the judgment, and caught her; for she was caught in the trial.

36. A commandment was then still given to her not to look back; thus she might have overcome, provided she had immediately entered into repentance and broken the evil earthly will, and fallen at the feet of the Lord with Lot; and that was the reason why the two angels refused to enter to Lot.

37. And with Lot’s wife, the earthly matrix <term>Matrix: a source-structure or "womb" of nature that gives form to matter</term> was indicated, which shall not go through the judgment, even though she must help work and bring forth the fruit like an instrument; nevertheless, in her outward form, she is not chosen for the kingdom of Heaven. For this same [matrix] was attached to Eve in Adam’s fall, during the sleep, and shall remain in the judgment and be changed back into her first matter from which she was created; not to damnation in the abyss, but into the **Mysterium** <note>original: "Mysterium," referring to the Great Mystery or the underlying spiritual potential of the universe</note>,

38. Understand the figure <note>the symbolic spiritual representation</note> further in the inward sense: Lot baked cakes of unleavened dough and prepared a meal for them, so that they ate; but now, the Angels do not use such food, but they were only formed Angels in an angelic form; for Abraham and also Lot called them "the Lord," for it was God's judgment and truth.

39. This eating was performed in the same manner as the offerings of *Abraham* and *Moses*, as was related previously; for the desire of the will grasped itself therein into a substance. God eats only the word of the will, but the food is consumed by the outward Spirit in which it is worked.

40. For the desire of Lot's faith was the food of God from these men, but with the meal which Lot gave them out of a good will of love, Lot's will grasped itself into a substance; so that he was preserved according to the outward earthly life and according to the inward will of faith in this judgment.

41. For these Angels ate of Lot's food, as if they ate of his body and spirit, which was included therein, to be understood in the same way as in the offerings; as has been sufficiently explained before regarding the offerings of Cain and Abel. For the unleavened cakes were the "incorporation" <note>original: "invatting," the catching or taking hold of spirit into matter</note>, as is seen throughout the books of Moses, and such points to the body of *Christ*, into which God's imagination entered—namely, as a prototype—and yet it grasped itself only in faith.

42. Furthermore, the Spirit speaks through Moses: and before those men lay down, the people of the city of Sodom arrived and surrounded the house, both young and old, all the people from every quarter, and they demanded Lot and spoke to him: "Where are the men who came to you this night? Bring them out to us, that we may know them."

43. For Lot had told them of the punishment that God would let fall upon them; regarding this they said: "You are a stranger, and you want to rule over us? Whenever God has sent messengers to them who have rebuked them, the <term>Antichristian Whore</term> <note>A common Reformation-era term for the corrupt institutional church, which the author views as opposing the true spirit of Christ.</note> has cried out: "Run, run! For what the Lord speaks through his children, she will not hear, but she wants people to regard only as holy that which she speaks out of the serpent's essence.

as Sodom and Gomorrah; if it happens that she sees these two angels of Abraham—that is, from Christ—coming to her, into her Sodom and Gomorrah, and exposing her shame, then she also rouses the whole city with a murderous cry, so that all people, young and old, run toward them, thinking that some wondrous beast has arrived.

### Of the Destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah, Ch. 43. ###

54. To understand this internal figure in the spirit and what Moses indicates by it, the following applies: judgment begins at the house of God, just as it does here with Lot. The children of God must first be placed in judgment and tested, to see whether there are still children of God in any place who might stay the wrath, so that the punishment might be delayed. Therefore, the spirit places the children of God within the wickedness of that city or land and tests them, to see if they find that wickedness acceptable: just as can be seen here.

55. Lot had to place his two daughters into the judgment with his offer; he wanted to give them to the unchaste people as a test. For his saying so was ordered by the spirit, which brought the two daughters of Lot into the judgment and the trial, into their essence <term>essence</term><note>In the mystical tradition of this author, "essence" (essents) refers to the fundamental spiritual nature of a person, beyond their physical body.</note>, and thereby pointed out the shame of the City—how they were nothing other than unchaste whore-beasts.

56. For it was not spoken out of Lot's own intention that he wanted to let his two daughters be violated, but the spirit set forth its figures <note>The author argues that Lot’s offer of his daughters was a symbolic spiritual "test" directed by God, rather than a literal moral choice by Lot himself.</note>.

57. And you must know for certain that the first book of Moses is written entirely from the spirit's indications of what each history signifies in the figure. Whoever wants to read these histories and understand them rightly must imprint the old and new man <note>The "old man" refers to the fallen state of humanity (Adam), while the "new man" refers to the redeemed state through Christ.</note> in his mind and set Christ and Adam against one another; then he can understand everything. Without this, he understands nothing of it but a simple story for children, which is nevertheless so rich in mysteries that no human, from his cradle to his greatest age, could fully express them, even if he had already received the understanding for it in his childhood. And we show such things only according to our gifts; although we have understood the meaning through the gifts of God, one cannot express it all, as it would also be incomprehensible to the world.

And He shows them through His messenger the light and the way of justice, and lets them walk for a time in the offered light, until they become weary of it and consider it merely a common thing and a history <note>To hold something as a "history" means to treat the spiritual truth as a mere dead narrative or an old story rather than a living reality.</note>, and once again become a Sodom.

### Chapter 44. The Terrible Destruction of that Entire Region.

20. And one sees how the children of God can often hold back God's great punishments, and what power is in them, so that even the wrath of God cannot act and is, as it were, powerless where they are still present; likewise, they are also a power against hell and against the devil. For such a thing is true faith: that it can restrain and master God Himself in His wrath.

21. Therefore the Lord said to Lot: "I can do nothing unless you go out," and He also spared the little town called *Bella* or *Zoar*—which is an "averter of wrath" for Lot's sake. For when he arrived there, the *Turba* <term>Turba: a term used in mystical theology to describe the "disturbance" or the raging of divine wrath that destroys established forms</term> had to be quenched, just as the name expresses in the uncompacted *sensual tongue* <note>original: "ſenſualiſche tonge"; this refers to the "Language of Nature," a mystical concept where the sound of a word reveals the true essence of the thing named</note>.

22. Then the Lord rained sulfur and fire from the Lord, from Heaven down upon Sodom and Gomorrah, and overturned the cities, the entire region, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and whatever grew upon the field; and his wife looked back, and became a pillar of salt.

23. This is now the figure <note>the symbolic or spiritual representation</note> of the kingdom of Christ, which had opened itself to Abraham in love—how He would hold judgment over the world, and how power was given to Him by God to destroy the devil’s kingdom on earth and give all the ungodly over to the wrath of God to be devoured. For when He had revealed Himself to Abraham and confirmed the covenant of righteousness, He sent these two Angels—being God’s truth and judgment—to Sodom to destroy the children of Ham <note>original: "Chams"; descendants of Ham were historically viewed in this tradition as representing the worldly or apostate nature</note>, being evil, apostate, half-devilish men, so that the kingdom of the devil might be diminished and not grow so large upon the earth and hinder His kingdom.

24. The internal figure is as follows: Moses says it rained sulfur and fire from the Lord, from Heaven. This was not the same hellish internal fire which shall purge the "threshing floor" <note>the world</note> at the end of days, otherwise the four elements would have been transformed; it was but a figure of what is to come. The origin of the sulfur and fire was born in the *Turba magna* <term>Great Turba: the massive outpouring of divine wrath within the natural world</term>, namely born in the third *Principium* <term>Third Principle: the physical world of time and the four elements</term>; it was nothing else but a sword of vengeance. The internal fire devours earth and stones and all the elements, but this was only a fire as it births itself in a thunderclap within the *Turba magna*, in an *egest* <note>original: "egeſt"; a discharge or something cast out</note> which the stars cast out. This serves as a material for it; even though it is not a tangible substance, it is nonetheless a spiritual being in which the *Mercurius* <term>Mercury: the active, animating spirit or "workman" in nature</term> ignites itself in the *Salniter* <term>Salniter: saltpeter; used here to represent the combustible or explosive quality of the divine wrath in nature</term>—that is, in the terror of fire—where the terror then takes hold in a substance or essence, which is sulfur.

## How Lot went out of Sodom, and concerning Chapter 44.

25. For the three—being **sulfur**, **mercury**, and the sharpness of **salt**—are a single thing in their origin while they are still a spirit. But when Mercury—being the sound of the formed word in the *beginning* <note>original: "principium"</note>, namely in its first origin—is moved by a counter-glance, it becomes terrified within itself. That is, the movement stirs the origin of heat and cold, which is the origin of the first *principle* <note>original: "principium"</note> according to the cold and hot fire. This is the start of the conflict and of the terror, from which the flash of fire, or the *saltpeter-like shock* <term>Saltpeter-shock: a term used by mystics like Jacob Böhme to describe a sudden, explosive ignition of spiritual or natural forces, similar to the ignition of gunpowder</term>, arises. There, the three first things—namely heat, cold, and sound—each press and enter into their own being through this shock: the heat into sulfur, the cold into the nature of salt, and **Mercury** into the watery nature. Yet they are not entirely separated, and each possesses the nature of the others, but each becomes fixed according to a single property.

26. Thus we are to understand the sulfurous fire here: the fierceness of the first *principle* <note>original: "principium"</note>, being the wrath of God according to eternal nature, illuminated the outward nature in the third *principle* <note>original: "principium"</note> with a flash called the *great disturbance* <term>turba magna: a term for the raging of divine wrath that breaks down established forms</term>. This was a *disturbance* <note>original: "turba"</note> in the soul of the outward world, in the spirit of nature, from which the outward nature ignited itself, and the three first principles took hold of themselves in one being: namely, in sulfur, salt, and in a mercurial, poisonous water. The shock or flash of fire ignited within this and pressed itself in, and thus it blazed over Sodom and Gomorrah and rained over the entire region and destroyed everything. This is what is meant by: "The Lord let sulfur and fire rain from the Lord, out of Heaven."

27. This matter of sulfur and fire did not come from the inward Heaven; rather, the fierceness came from the inward into the outward, so that the outward—within the power of the inward and out of the properties of the inward—took hold of itself and ignited. It is a true image of the inward dark world; if that same nature moves, it is spiritually characterized as what God calls His fierceness and wrath, and a consuming fire. For if the inward spiritual dark world were to move, the outward world with the four elements would immediately be spirit-swallowed in that same fire, which shall happen at the end of days.

28. And we have a figure <note>a symbolic or representative image</note> of this in Lot's wife, who became a pillar of salt because the three first principles had moved. For after she looked back into the *disturbance* <note>original: "turbam"</note>, she was seized by the salt-spirit in its *compression* <term>impression/compression: the process by which a spiritual quality "hardens" or takes material form</term>. This indicates that this same property was most prevalent in her—that is, in her desire and greed—in which she was also caught during the investigation of the angel.

### Chapter 45. How God Led Abraham So Wondrously. 11

Just as his wife Sarah was taken from him twice, yet she was most wondrously protected and preserved by God; namely from Pharaoh in Egypt, and from Abimelech, King in Gerar, and on both occasions protected by God.

2. And that Abraham now, being the stem and the beginning of the embodied <term>Ens of faith</term> <note>original: "gevat-te Ens des geloofs"; in this mystical context, 'Ens' refers to the essential spiritual substance or being of faith that takes form in the world.</note>, in which Christ is understood, thus had to wander from one place to another, and could have no permanent place on earth, and moreover faced fear and temptation; the same is the true example of Christendom on earth, how it should not be bound to any fixed place; not to one people alone, whom God would have specifically chosen for that purpose, but that Christ with His **Gospel** <note>original: "Euangelio"</note> of the kingdom of God has been given to all nations.

3. And how He, with His Knowledge, would wander from one people to another, and nowhere have an everlasting place with one people, but among all nations with His children on earth, being nothing other than a guest or stranger: and how one would constantly attempt to destroy Christendom among the nations and bring it to shame, just as they wished to bring Sarah, Abraham's wife, to shame.

4. 5. At that point, He would depart from them with the understanding and the spirit, to another people who would also be nothing other than fleshly, and would regard and look upon Christ externally as a pure human, just as Pharaoh and this King Abimelech looked upon Abraham and his Sarah, and wished to mingle fleshly with Sarah because of her beauty; which was an indication that they would indeed embrace Christ in the flesh, yet only in a **superficial manner** <note>original: "veeksen aart"; refers to a fickle, external, or hollow nature as opposed to spiritual reality.</note>, and not in power and spirit.

6. They do this so that they might climb into heaven by their own will and power, so that one does not need to enter through the death of the old, evil man, but that one might slip in quite elegantly with the "selfhood" of the evil man; or, like externally adopted children, cover themselves with the purple cloak of *Christ*, even though the will of selfhood cannot come to God.

11. Those same nations, who remained only under the name of *Christ* but in their hearts were nothing other than heathens, have always been judged and driven out by such heathen nations. This has been proven in *Asia* and *Egypt*, also *Greece* and others; how God stripped the cloak of *Christ* from them—being lip-hypocrites and mockers of *Christ*—and gave them a darkened heart and understanding of the kingdom of *Christ*, and took the candlestick away from them <note>A reference to Revelation 2:5, where God threatens to remove the "candlestick" (the light of the church) from those who have fallen away.</note>, so that they no longer dared to say, "We are Christians and belong to *Christ*," but instead fathered *Turks* and *Barbarian* nations from the wild tree of *Nature*.

Thus Nature stands in the corrupt Wilderness in the vanity of death, encompassed by sin, and must now labor and bring forth, yet finds herself quite powerless—namely, regarding the internal Spiritual will from **Christ**—as if entirely cast out. In herself, she is like the fools despised by the world, and cast out everywhere from her own will. She hopes and doubts—that is, she hopes for improvement, or that she might at last be delivered from the mockery and restored to the honor of her selfhood—but her water-well is also dried up, and the wrath of God appears before her eyes. She is a mockery to every Man; everything she looks upon decries her as a fool, because the power has been taken from her, so that she must leave the beauty, wealth, and honor of the world, and everything that can temporally exalt her—and she would still gladly have the same, yet is drawn away from it by the internal man in the Spirit of **Christ**, and is decried in this temporal life as unrighteous and damnable.

15. The man thinks this is an injustice, since that same word was born from his body and originated from his mind.

<margin>Genesis 21.</margin>

It shows us how we must constantly stand in trials <note>original: "aanvegtinge"; refers to spiritual assaults or testing of one's faith.</note>, in danger, and in adversity, and how God so wonderfully delivers His children. This is what happened to *Abimelech* when he was inflamed with false desire for *Sarah*; God so terrified his conscience that he went to *Abraham* and humbled himself before him, making a covenant with him along with great gifts. So it also goes with all the children of *Christ*: when they endure trials patiently and remain steadfast in faith, all their enemies must finally be ashamed and retreat, as is seen in this figure.

He shows how *Christ* would offer our soul and humanity back to His *Father*, how He, as a sacrifice, would be cast into the fire of God’s wrath, and how the selfhood and the own-will of the human soul must die away <note>original: "affterven"; a mystical term for the mortification or "dying off" of the ego.</note> in the fierceness of God, and then still with the Divine oneness

[God’s holy] will <note>Completing the sentence from the previous page: "how we poor children of Eve should and must [go into the] holy will of God..."</note>, to penetrate through death and wrath, and to break and mock the death that held humanity captive. And so, to lead the human soul back to God His Father, into the single, eternal Divine will, and to surrender again the kingdom He had given Him in humanity, so that thereafter and for eternity God alone may be all in all. In this way, the creature should no longer have its own will or life, but be nothing other than an instrument of the Divine voice, sounding in Divine harmony, and the entire human tree might be but one in all its shoots and branches.

2. The Spirit presents this figure quite clearly in *Moses* until the end of all his writings, and plays with the internal figure—which shall remain eternally—under the guise of the external figure. Therefore, I will also present this figure of the testing of *Abraham* with his son *Isaac* in its spiritual meaning, explaining what is to be understood by it. For although the scholars have pointed out that God tested *Abraham* to see if he would remain steadfast in faith, it nonetheless has a much deeper meaning. God knows beforehand what man will do; furthermore, without His grace, man cannot withstand temptation <note>original: "verſoekinge"; can also be translated as "trial" or "testing."</note>, as can be seen with *Abraham* when he denied his wife before King *Abimelech* when he traveled to *Gerar*.

3. Here, *Abraham* was represented as *Adam*, and his son *Isaac* was represented as the humanity of *Christ*. The voice that spoke to *Abraham* is the voice of God the Father. These three stand here as figures for the process of the work of human redemption: how *Abraham* (that is, *Adam*) would offer up his image in *Isaac* (that is, in *Christ*) to the voice of God in the fire of God, so that humanity might be tested in the fire of God.

Here, through *Isaac*, the Spirit looks toward *Christ*. For in *Isaac* lay the covenant and the *essence* <term>original: "Ens"; a philosophical and mystical term referring to the core being or spiritual substance of a thing.</term> of *Abraham’s* faith, from which *Christ* was to come. Thus the voice of God spoke to *Adam* in *Abraham*: "Take your son, whom you love, and offer him as a burnt offering on that mountain I shall show you." This signifies that the Jodes <note>original: "Joden"; the Jewish people.</note>, being *Adam's* children, would offer *Christ* as a burnt offering. That is, the Divine essence <note>original: "Ens"</note> would enter into the essence of *Adam*, and the children of *Adam* would together offer it to God in the fire of God. 5. Thus says the Spirit in *Moses*: "your son whom you love," that is, your own will, which has introduced itself into self-love. This own-will must be sacrificed to God, so that in the fire of God it may leave behind self-love and entirely surrender its selfhood, no longer willing or living for itself, but for God. In this devouring by the fire of wrath, the love-*Being* <note>original: "Ens"</note> in the word of faith would be grasped by the Divine power—the right man, created in *Adam*—and be preserved in the consuming fire. Just as silver and gold on the refining-cup <term>refining-cup: a "fineertest," a vessel used by goldsmiths to separate precious metals from impurities through intense heat</term>, where the copper and all other impurities smoke away while the gold and silver alone withstand the fire, so also the assumed human selfhood, along with the assumed *Being* <note>original: "Ens"</note> of the serpent and the beast, and everything that cannot withstand the Divine fire, would be consumed in the sacrifice. This was done so that we, in the person of *Christ*, might again have a complete, pure access and an open fountain of grace. Thus *Christ* would sacrifice our human will and selfhood to His Father and give it back to Him, just as on Mount *Moriah*—that is, in His death and dying—where He would die to human selfhood for all and in all. Just as when the trunk of the tree dies, all its branches also die within it; and just as when the tree is renewed, it also introduces its new power back into its branches. While this is not possible for external nature, it is indeed possible in God, as can be seen in the dry staff of *Aaron*, which had died to its sap and life, and yet in one night turned green and bore beautiful almonds.

7. So God now said, "upon a mountain that I shall show you." That is to say, it should not happen according to *Abraham's* will, nor should such a thing happen in us according to our own will—that we should want to prescribe for ourselves where and how we wish to sacrifice ourselves to the Father in *Christ*, as *Babel* <note>In this context, "Babel" refers to the "confused" or institutional church that relies on outward rituals rather than internal transformation.</note> does. No, it must be on the mountain—that is, in that place, in that quality, and in that death just as the Lord sends it to us. We must only be obedient with *Abraham* and be willing to surrender ourselves therein when He wishes to sacrifice us to Himself. We should not scourge, strike, or plague ourselves, but only sink into Him with our will, and wait until the Lord shows us the place where and how He wishes to sacrifice our selfhood. We must—

### Chapter 48. *The Offering of Christ, represented in His suffering and death.* 35

...surrender to Him alone our whole heart and will, with body and soul, and further entrust to Him what He wishes to do with us; where He wishes to sacrifice us in the body into the image of Jesus Christ; and when the Lord calls us to an offering, through his cross, or wishes to sacrifice us to temporal death, then we must say with Abraham: "Here I am, Lord; do that which You will."

8. And Abraham rose up early in the morning, and saddled his donkey, and took with him two servants and his son Isaac; and split wood for the burnt offering, and set out, and went to the place of which God had told him.

->*This figure/symbol is understood as follows.*<-

When the voice of God calls us, we must go immediately with Abraham; for "early" is to be understood as when the voice breaks through like a dawn, when God calls within us; that thoughts occur to the person: "you must do penance and turn back"—that is when it is "early." Thus he must immediately and with force saddle his donkey—being the animalistic man <note>The author uses the donkey as a metaphor for the physical, animal-like nature of human beings which must be "saddled" or disciplined</note>—even if it cries out, "Wait, tomorrow is time enough." Nevertheless, it must happen immediately, in the first glimpse of the will towards God; for it is the hind <note>original: "hinde"; a female deer. This likely refers to Psalm 22, often titled "The Hind of the Dawn" in mystical traditions, representing the suffering Christ</note> that is hunted early, as the Prophetic Spirit indicates; for early, with the voice of God, Christ would saddle this donkey and bring it to the offering.

9. And the two servants whom Abraham took with him indicate the soul of the first *Principle* <term>Principle: translated from the Latin "Principium," a term used by 17th-century mystics to describe the fundamental layers of reality, specifically the dark/fire source and the external/physical world</term>, and the soul of this world, being the outward spirit of the external life. These must go with Isaac—that is, with Christ—in the old Abraham (who is Adam) to the offering of God. And Abraham—that is, the man Adam in his children—must himself split the wood on which the offering is to be burned. That is: when he recognizes Christ, he splits the hearts of the ungodly, who hasten with him to death and to the offering of God. For Adam had split the love and the wrath of God in his humanity <note>Meaning that Adam's fall divided the unified experience of God into perceived "wrath" and "love"</note>; so now Abraham also had to split the wood for the offering; for Christ would also split death and life from each other, and allow Himself to be sacrificed in the wrath of God upon that same split wood of death and life.

10. And on the third day Abraham lifted up his eyes and saw the place from afar. Here the Spirit points to Adam's sleep, when he fell asleep in the Angelic World; and on the third day after his falling asleep—now that the woman <note>referring to Eve</note> was made from him and the fall had occurred—he saw Christ, being the place of God in the covenant, from afar. Likewise, it is enclosed within this the resurrection of Christ on the third day, where He [saw] His place, where He would and should [bring] the men...

### How God Tested Abraham, and the Symbolism of Chapter 48.

...to God his Father, offering and surrendering, which he saw from afar, being the final judgment and the last sacrifice; it also indicates that Abraham foresaw in the Spirit the sacrifice of Christ from afar, as if it were coming, more than two thousand years in the future. And when the Spirit says: "Abraham lifted up his eyes on the third day and saw the place," it means nothing else than that Christ, on the third day, raised our human eyes from the grave and from death back into God; and because this was still far off in Abraham's time, the Spirit plays, as it were, with this figure <note>A "figure" in this context is a prophetic symbol or type that foreshadows a future spiritual reality.</note> regarding the future.

11. And Abraham spoke to the two servants whom he took with him: "Stay here with the donkey; I and the boy will go over there, and when we have worshipped, we will return to you."

->This figure is understood inwardly as follows.<-

The two servants with the donkey were to stay there and not go along on this journey to the sacrifice; only Abraham and Isaac were to perform it. That is, we poor children of Eve must remain here in this world with our internal and external soul—namely, with the first and third *Principium* <term>The "Principles" are a concept in Behmenist theology: the first is the dark fire-world, and the third is the external material world.</term> of our lives—along with the donkey, which is the external body. But Christ in Isaac, and Abraham in Adam, had to go to the sacrifice; that is, Christ stood in Abraham’s person (representing Adam) and also in his own Heavenly humanity; they alone would go and offer the sacrifice of his body to the fire of the Father's wrath, and worship God his Father for us. Therefore he said he wanted to go there; that is, when he would sacrifice his life, he wanted to go to God and worship before God for us.

12. This also points to his Ascension <note>original: "Hemelvaard"</note> according to his humanity. When he had completed the sacrifice, he went there and worshipped in our assumed humanity, in God his Father; that is, in our assumed soul, in Divine power and property, he prays for and helps our weakness and ignorance in and before God. Therefore Abraham said, "We will go there and worship," meaning we, God and man; "and when we have worshipped, we will return to you." That means we, poor children of Eve, must meanwhile wait with the donkey <note>The author consistently uses the "donkey" to represent the physical, animalistic nature of humans which cannot enter the highest spiritual states.</note> until the time of his sacrifice and prayer is over; then he will return to us when we have finished the course of this external, donkey-like life.

13. And this indicates that from that place where he has ascended, when the time of his sacrifice in prayer is finished, he will certainly come back to us and, with his creaturely humanity, dwell visibly among us, just as the two angels said to the men of Israel when he ascended to Heaven.

### Chapter 48. The Sacrifice of Christ, represented in his suffering and death.

33. And the Angel of the Lord called Abraham a second time from Heaven, and spoke: "I have sworn by myself," says the Lord, "because you have done this, and have not spared your only son, that I will bless and multiply your seed like the stars in the Heaven, and the sand on the shore of the Sea; and your seed shall possess the gates of your enemies, and through your seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed; because you have obeyed my voice." Thus Abraham returned again to his servants, and they rose up and traveled together to Beersheba, and lived there. This very thing is the **seal of faith**; when a person surrenders themselves entirely to God, then God swears an oath within the human nature <note>original: "menscheid"</note>, by Himself, that He desires to bless that person. This means that the essences <note>original: "essentien" — the fundamental spiritual qualities or "building blocks" of a person's life</note> of their life shall henceforth expand in His power, and grow into a great tree of Divine Essences in the Wisdom. The fruit and knowledge of this tree would be infinite and innumerable; just as He swore to Abraham that from his body, or the essence of his life, many nations would arise. It also shows how the essence of his life would possess the gates of his enemies—namely, of the devil and of death—just as He here prophesies of Christ and His Christendom: how they would destroy the devil's kingdom and break his gates within man. Such is the power of faith in the children of God.

34. For as soon as the judgment over the earthly man is held within the penitent person—so that the soul rejects the will of the evil flesh (which is the will of the **animal soul** <term>animalise ziele: the lower, instinctual part of human nature driven by earthly desires rather than spiritual light</term>) and places it in judgment unto the damnation of death, surrendering itself entirely to God—then God swears this oath in the soul through Christ Jesus. He appoints the soul as a prince over the enemies—namely over the bold Devils—acting as their judge, so that the soul receives the power to drive them away.

35. After this history, Moses recounts how the blessing of Abraham expanded, and points to his brother Nahor; how Milcah bore him eight sons, from whom great nations arose, namely the Syrians. These had not sprouted from the **Ens of faith** <term>Ens: a Latin term used in mysticism to mean the "inner essence" or "spiritual substance" of a thing</term> as Abraham had—that is, in the **Line of Christ**—but rather from the natural Adam. Nevertheless, the blessing of Abraham extended over them as well. For the History is depicted so perfectly that one can see how God chose not only the natural Line of Christ from Abraham and Isaac, but also the Line of Nature in the Adamic tree. He wished to lead that line as well, revealing Himself to them, so that those who would become believers in God might be grafted into the Line of Christ. These are the ones who would be receptive to the Divine *Ens* in the voice of the Lord, and whose will would turn toward God.

# How God tested Abraham, and the figure of Chapter 48.

36. As is seen again in this figure, God has not rejected the **kingdom of Nature** within man, but desires to redeem it in Christ out of its anguish and conflicting will. A person must remain standing within the kingdom of Nature, just as Abraham—after he had performed this sacrifice—returned to **Beersheba** with his son and two servants and lived there. Under this, the Spirit points through Moses that when Abraham had performed his role in the **figure of Christ** <note>A "figure" is a symbolic representation or prophetic "type" that foreshadows a later spiritual reality.</note> before the Lord, he returned to his natural occupation—namely, working within the essence of this world. This was at Beersheba, which signifies the "toils" into which Adam had led us. There, a child of God must work within God through the breaking of Nature—that is, in Beersheba—through teaching and prayer, and also labor with their hands in Nature to sustain the outward man. They are to work the wonders of the outward world into the <term>formed word</term> <note>original: "geformeerde woord" — the idea that human actions and speech "give form" to God’s creative power in the physical realm</note>, and through figures, help reveal and shape them for the contemplation of the **wisdom of God**.

37. This also shows that a child of God, while existing in the essence of this world, is not every day or hour in the operation of the **spiritual figure**—where his spirit is able to see and recognize the same—but also exists in the natural state. There, the Spirit of God works alongside him in the works of Nature, and reveals itself in him in a different quality. This is seen in Abraham and all the Saints: that God reveals Himself to them now in the **figure of Christ**, and then again in the cross and toil, in the temptation and adversity of the nature of the **corrupt Adam**, so that they lived in weakness and failings just like all the children of Adam.

38. and we must not view or consider this figure of Abraham, in everything that the Spirit has written through Moses and **Ezra**, as anything other than an example of Christ and Adam; that is, of the **Kingdom of Christ** and the **Kingdom of Nature**. It shows how God has presented the figure of Christ and His Christendom to Himself, and how He desired to redeem man from his great toil.

It shows how man must be tested and refined, and this is the most important part: how man must surrender himself to God in faith and total trust, keeping himself still to let God work within him. He must learn to subdue his own Nature and lead it to God, so that in all things it desires to be God's instrument and servant, and wills to work nothing else but that which leads to the Divine revelation, in the wonders

### Chapter 49. And of Abraham’s ancestral burial. 49

First, he presents through Isaac the figure of Christ with his sacrifice and death; and immediately thereafter, he also presents here man's own death and dying. He shows where man must die—namely, in his city of Hebron <note>Hebron is interpreted here mystically as the place where the "human selfhood" or ego is surrendered to God.</note>, away from his human selfhood—and where he must be buried: namely, in the double cave. This cave represents the kingdom of God and the kingdom of this world. It is called a double cave because it contains two kinds of dwellings, that is, a concept of two kinds of life in two principles from which man originated. However, if a person is buried in the will of his own selfhood, in the desire of the serpent, he does not understand this double cave. Even if he were within it, he would live in nothing other than the fallen **essences** <note>original: "essents"; refers to the fundamental spiritual qualities of a person's being</note> in the property of the Devil; that is, in the introduced serpent-**Ens** <term>Ens: a term from Latin meaning "being" or "essence," used here to describe the corrupted spiritual substance introduced by the fall of man</term>, in the quality of the dark world, which is manifest and in command within the selfhood of the serpent-being.

14. In this figure, the most important point that the Spirit of Moses points out is the twofold life: how this world is a twofold life and being. He indicates this through the double cave where Abraham wished to have his burial. He is showing that his twofold humanity—namely, the one from the Divine **Ens** <note>original: "Ens"</note> out of eternity and the Heavenly Spiritual being, and the other from time out of the being of this world—would be buried in an eternal burial. There, the being of the twofold body would lie within its original mother, leaving the "own will" in this eternal grave in death, so that only the Spirit of God might live, rule, and will in the Spirit of the Creature—that is, in the soul—and so that the life of man is nothing other than His working instrument, with which He does how and what He wills.

15. For it had to be so, in order that the human will might be brought back into the single will of the Deity and eternity. For in the beginning, when God breathed the soul into the flesh, it had been in the eternal living Word: **John 1** <note>A reference to "In the beginning was the Word."</note>. And the Spirit of God had formed it into an image of the Deity; that is, into a creaturely soul. This soul had turned itself away from the single eternal Word of God into a selfhood, in order to be manifest in evil and in good, and to rule in inequality.

16. This inequality had to be buried again in equality—that is, in the being from which the soul and body had arisen. Specifically, every being of the "property" <note>The term "property" here refers to the specific character or spiritual quality of a thing.</note> must return to its Mother. This mother is a double cave: namely, the internal Spiritual and Divine kingdom, and the external visible, experiential, comprehensible kingdom of the outer world. It was there that Abraham wished to have his burial.

# How Abraham sends out his servant, Chapter 50.

17. For the outward Kingdom remains eternal, because it is out of the eternal, as a model or visible image of the inward Spiritual Kingdom; however, the governance by the stars and the four Elements does not remain eternal in such a particularity, but only a single Element, in which the four are understood, yet in equal concordance, in equal weight, in a single will of Love, where the ascending, surging power of the divided figure—the four Elements—no longer governs, but rather the soft, still humility, in a lovely, pleasant whispering <note>The author likely refers to the "still small voice" or "gentle breeze" in which God appeared to Elijah in 1 Kings 19:12.</note>.

18. The compacted property of the Word in the soul of the outward World—that is, in the particularity of the third **principle** <note>original: "principium"; in the author's mystical system, the "third principle" refers to the visible, material world</note>—comes to an end; the outward Spirit of the World is changed into the inward, so that the inward governs and leads everything through the outward. This occurs when the great movement of the ignited power of the dark World ceases and is led into its governance—wherein the Devil is an incoming prince, directing everything toward separability—so that the properties of the three **principles** <note>original: "principien"</note> each become creaturely within themselves. To this end, eternity has introduced itself into a **fiat** <note>original: "fiat"; a Latin term meaning "let it be," referring to the creative command or the desire for manifestation</note>, or a desire for the formation of being; this being the **Great Mystery** <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum"</note>, which has introduced itself so that one thing may be made manifest in the other: evil in the good, and good in the evil, and every thing may receive its possession.

# Chapter 50. To take a Wife for his Son Isaac. 51

...whole written histories of the first book of Moses, as if with a comedy <note>The author uses "comedy" in the classical sense: a narrative that begins in conflict or darkness but ends in joy and restoration.</note>, and point consistently, beneath the outward histories of the outward man, to the spiritual figure of the spiritual, eternal man in the kingdom of Christ.

2. The servant had to swear an oath to Abraham to take a wife for his son from his own tribe and lineage. Why did Abraham impose an oath upon him, since the servant surely had to obey his master without an oath, and Isaac would not have taken a wife without his father's will? But the Spirit of Moses looks at the internal figure <note>The "internal figure" refers to the symbolic or mystical meaning hidden within the literal biblical story.</note>. Isaac stands here as the figure of Christ; Abraham’s servant stands as the figure of Nature; and the Canaanites stand as the figure of the introduced **essence** <note>original: "Ens"; a philosophical term referring to the fundamental being or "stuff" of a thing</note> of the snake, from which the apostate, self-centered will of human selfishness had arisen—that is, in the figure of the animalistic man who shall not inherit the Kingdom of God. These three the Spirit of Moses has set before himself, and points beneath them to the true man who shall exist eternally.

->The internal figure is as follows:<-

3. Abraham called his servant, who governed his entire house. Abraham signifies here God the Father, and the servant through whom he governs signifies Nature—Nature in her power and might. This servant had to swear here in God—that is, to sink himself and bind himself **essentially** <note>original: "essentialiter"; meaning in his very being or essence</note>—so that he would not add or join a wife (that is, a **generative source** <note>original: "Matrix"; here used to mean the source or womb of life and characteristics</note>) from the Canaanites—namely, from the snake's **essence** <note>original: "Ens"</note>—to Isaac (that is, the Christians, being God's children) for the propagation of the snake’s **essence** <note>original: "Ens"</note>. This is so that they would not draw the poison of the property of the dark world (being the Canaanite property) into themselves and introduce it to the children of Christ as a wife—that is, in the **tincture of Venus** <note>original: "Veneris tinctura"; in the author's alchemical language, this refers to the refined essence of desire, love, and the power of generation</note>, which is the true feminine **generative source** <note>original: "Matrix"</note> in men and women—but rather that they would add the **essence** <note>original: "Ens"</note> of Christ to the true Adamic man whom God created in His image, being the true human **essences** <note>original: "Effents"</note> from the first original tree, from the first root—namely, from Abraham's tribe, which represents Adam. This is the true Isaac in the children of Christ.

4. This is understood as follows: Adam introduced the **essence** <note>original: "Ens"</note> of the snake and the Devil into our flesh and soul, which Nature has taken into soul and body, and a self-turned will was born therein, which is disobedient to God.

5. But because God had now reintroduced His holy **essence** <note>original: "Ens"</note> of His holy Word into Isaac—which Abraham had grasped in the desire of faith, and established in Isaac as a new sprout from the corrupted tree of the human property, born of the Spirit of Christ...
