# CHAPTER 51.

## How Abraham took another wife, with whom he yet fathered six sons, to whom he gave gifts, and all his goods he gave to his son Isaac, but the others he sent away from him during his lifetime; and how he died; what is to be understood by this.

->Gen. 25.<-

<margin>1.</margin>
Moses says: Abraham took another wife, who was named Keturah; she bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah, from whom six lineages arose. With Sarah, Abraham fathered only one son, of whom the entire history speaks; but with Keturah he fathered six sons, of whom nothing remarkable is told, except for their lineage.

->This is understood inwardly as follows.<-

Abraham had to first become old with his Sarah before he fathered Isaac, indicating that Christ would be revealed in the flesh in the old age of the world <note>The "old age of the world" refers to the theological idea that Christ arrived in the final era of human history</note>.

2. Isaac was fathered out of Abraham’s Nature, and out of the **Essence** <term>Essence: the original Latin "Ens" refers to the fundamental spiritual substance or "being" that underlies physical reality</term> of faith; he was conceived from an old **womb** <term>Womb: original Latin "matrix", used here to mean the creative vessel or formative principle of nature</term>, which was by then almost dead according to human nature, so that God’s **Essence** might have the preeminence. But when Sarah died, Abraham took Keturah and quickly fathered six sons with her. *Keturah* expresses, in her name, the **Center of Nature** <note>The "Center of Nature" is a concept in mystical philosophy representing the driving forces or properties that constitute material existence</note>; when one forms the sensual, uncompacted Spirits of the Letters in this word *Kethura*, then one understands that Keturah is a formed **Womb** of **Nature**. This indicates that Abraham, after he had fathered the image of **Christ** <note>original: "Christi"</note> in the **Essence** of faith, would now father his own image according to Adam’s Nature, out of the six properties of the natural life of the Spirit, and establish his own natural image there as well, for which he also required such a vessel.

3. Sarah had to bear only one son; indicating that the Kingdom of men is given to only **one**, and that they all together under this one...

### Chapter 25. With whom he also fathered six sons.

24. Thus, in Abraham, the **figure** <note>original: *figuure*. In this context, a "figure" or "type" is a person or event in the Old Testament that foreshadows something in the New Testament.</note> of the kingdom of Christ was presented through his son Isaac. But when Christ came in the flesh, God did away with the figure and took from the outward children of Isaac the external goods of the land of Canaan. This demonstrated that the holy land of Canaan has now been revealed, where the children of Isaac should take up the true promised inheritance in Christ—no longer the figure, but the **essence** of this figure, which is the state of perfection. They must now leave behind the external goods along with the figure and put on Christ in the flesh.

25. But as for the fact that the Jews—being Isaac’s and Abraham’s children, that is, the children within the figure of Christ—did not all turn to Christ when He revealed Himself in the flesh, the meaning is this: God gave them the **law of nature**. In that law, the external rule of nature is understood outwardly, while inwardly Christ is understood, being the covenant and the promised gift of God in Paradise. The law of nature was to become Christ's "housemate." The true man under the law of nature was meant to live in reason, yet bring his own nature into Christ’s house. For this reason, the figure of the law had to remain with certain children of Abraham—that is, with certain Jews—to show that the law is a companion to Christ.

26. Understand that human nature shall remain; it is not entirely rejected by God so that a completely foreign, new man would arise out of the old. Rather, the new man arises out of Adam’s nature and property, combined with God’s nature and property in Christ. Thus, the man is an <term>Adam-Christ</term> and Christ is a <term>Christ-Adam</term>—a **man-God** and a **God-man**. This is why the figure remained with the Jews, and why they were not all converted to Christ: so that nature might keep its figure and its right. For nature had to surrender its children under the law—which is the figure of Christ—to God the Father in Christ. Nevertheless, their figure shall be tested in the fire of God, so that it may be known who was a true child of the natural law within the figure of Christ, and whether they were born in the Spirit within the law from the figure of Christ or not.

The law of God has enclosed such a person within the figure of Christ and shall lead them into the fulfillment of that figure.

He who has been a true Jew, and has put on Abraham’s faith in the law, has put on the <term>Being of Christ: *Ens Christi*, referring to the spiritual essence or substance of Christ.</term> which Abraham received; which Essence of faith has fulfilled the humanity of Christ, and he is hidden to himself as to what he is; for he works in the office of nature in the law of God, which Christ has taken into Himself and fulfilled: thus he serves God in the office of nature, and the office of nature serves Christ; for it has become Christ’s property.

29. For to Him is given all power in Heaven and on earth <note>original: "Mat: 28:" referencing Matthew 28:18.</note>, under which power the office of nature in the law also exists; for God, in the Spirit of Christ, is Himself the one who gave the law and the office of nature to do right—along with the figure of the Kingdom of Christ with the Essence of faith—to Abraham and Moses; and He is also Himself the one who fulfills the faith and the law.

30. Thus, the Jew works in his faith in the Officer <note>or "Governor"</note> Christ, that is, in the law, by which Christ rules in nature, and he has put on Christ in the covenant and in the Essence of faith in the figure of Christ, which Christ has fulfilled.

31. And the Christian, who knows Christ in the flesh, works in his faith in the flesh of Christ, and has the law of nature as God’s Officer to do right in his faith; for Christ reigns with the law of God, which He fulfilled and made into a servant in His children, and He kills the law of sin through the fulfillment of His love, in His blood and death—both in those who live under the governance of His law, and also in those who live in the governance of His victory, namely the Christians.

32. For the faith which, in the law, penetrates to God in the figure within the covenant, penetrates into the Essence of Abraham’s faith (from which Christ was born) to God; but he who penetrates to God in the fulfillment, penetrates into the humanity of Christ—that is, into His whole process of suffering, death, and resurrection—to God.

33. A Christian is Christ in the internal humanity, and a Jew is Christ in the figure and in the Officer of His law, namely according to nature; but now, Adam in his nature and Christ in the divine nature have become a single person, only a single tree; who is it now that judges here?

# Chapter 51. With whom he also fathered six sons.

...for it is not those who hear the law who are righteous before God, but those who do the law shall be justified; for when the Gentiles <note>The Dutch *heydenen* literally means "heathens," but here refers to the non-Jewish nations as described in the New Testament.</note>, who do not have the law, nonetheless do by nature the things contained in the law, these—even though they do not have the works of the law—do the works of the law by nature, and so they are a law unto themselves. By this, they demonstrate that the works of the law are written in their hearts, as their consciences convict them, along with the thoughts that accuse or excuse one another; and this is named as follows:

35. If the Gentiles reach Christ, they reach the Law of Nature <note>The inherent moral sense or natural conscience God placed in all humanity.</note> to do right; for Christ is the beginning and the fulfillment of the law. But the Jews have the law; whoever then transgresses and sins—whether it be the Jew under the Law of Nature, or the Gentile who confesses Christ under the Law of Fulfillment—each shall be judged according to his own law: namely, the Jew in the law of God the Father in Christ, and the Christian in the law of the Gospel, which is the law of fulfillment.

36. And here there is no regard for names, such that one might say, "I am a Jew," and another, "I am a Christian." The name makes no difference in being a child of God; rather, it is the Spirit in the heart to do right and to obey God. They all come into grace under the obedience of Christ to God—both the Jew and the Christian.

37. For outside of Christ there is neither law nor Gospel; Christ is the righteousness that counts before God within the law. Likewise, man has no God outside of Christ; whether he walks according to the law or the Gospel, if he walks in the desire to obey God, then he walks in the law of fulfillment. For Christ is the only obedience that counts before God, both in the law and the Gospel. All people who surrender themselves to the obedience of God are accepted into the obedience of Christ—that is, into the fulfillment of obedience—be they Jew, Christian, or even the Gentile who possesses neither law nor Gospel.

38. For if the Gentile desires to obey the one God, even if he does not recognize Him according to His essence or His revelation, yet still presses into the obedience of God, then he is a law unto himself. He testifies through his works that God has written His law within him, which He has fulfilled in His Son, as Paul says <note>A reference to the Apostle Paul’s arguments in the Book of Romans, Chapter 2, regarding the salvation of those who have not heard the Mosaic Law.</note>; for he who knows the law and the Gospel knows them as a gift from the Giver who granted him that knowledge. But he who does not know them, yet nonetheless desires the power of the law and the Gospel—in such a person, God knows in Christ what he wills.

39. For grace lies not only in knowing—that someone knows of the grace of Christ—but in the penetrating into grace and into God's mercy in such a way: one person penetrates into the mercy of God through the law, another through the Gospel, and a third without knowledge or awareness of the Gospel, having none of it, but instead clinging to the grace of God. To this last person, grace is granted through the merits of Christ without his own knowing.

40. Just as a branch on a tree does not know from where the trunk provides it with sap and strength, yet it leans solely toward the power of the root and draws the sap into itself through its own desire; so likewise many an ignorant person leans toward his eternal Mother <note>Original: *eeuwige Moeder*. In Böhme’s theology, this often refers to the Divine Sophia or the "Matrix" of divine nature from which humanity originally came before the Fall.</note>, out of which he arose with Adam, and in his ignorance he enters again into the gift of grace which God granted to Adam in his fall. For the covenant and the grace are inherited from Adam by all, just as sin inherited from one to all. Whoever desires the grace of the only God receives it in Christ, who is grace itself.

41. The Jews will not believe in the outward humanity of Christ and they deny it; but the Christians believe it, yet they defile it with an ungodly way of life. Thus, one is the same as the other before God, except for the children of faith among both Jews and Christians, whose stained garments are washed in the blood of Christ.

42. By this we do not confirm the unbelief of the Jews and Heathens <note>original: *Heydenen*. Used here to refer to those outside the Abrahamic faiths.</note>, as if they should remain in their blindness—for the time of their visitation has been born, so that they shall become seeing—but through this we uncover the false Anti-Christ among the Jews and Christians, in that each person boasts of his name and condemns the other: the Jew in the law, the Christian in the Gospel, and the Heathen in his superstition.

43. Everyone wants to be God’s child through their own knowledge <note>original: *wetenſchap*. In this 17th-century context, this refers to intellectual "head-knowledge" or formal doctrine rather than modern physical science.</note>, and yet disobedience and unbelief are just as great in one people as in the other. For even if I hold it to be true that Christ was born, died for me, and rose from the dead, that does not make me a child of God. The Devil knows such things as well, yet it does him no good. I must put on Christ in the faith-desire <term>faith-desire: *geloofs-begeerte*, a central concept for Böhme where faith is not a mental belief but an active, hungry longing of the soul for God</term>, and I must enter into his incarnation <note>original: *menſchwerding*</note>, suffering, and death, and rise in him, and put on the obedience of Christ; then, and not before, am I a Christian.

44. Judging and condemning without God’s command is nothing other than the Anti-Christ among both Jews and Christians. Without the mercy of God, no one comes to sonship; we must all together enter through the mercy of God—the Jew and the Christian, the knowing and the unknowing; for us must...

45. But how shall such a person love, who despises his Brother for the sake of knowledge <note>Original: *wetenschap*. In this context, Böhme refers to academic or dogmatic knowledge as opposed to spiritual wisdom.</note>, especially since God loved us when we knew nothing of His love? If a person does not have the love of God within them—with which God loved us when we did not yet know Him—why does anyone boast so much of their divine sonship? If anyone is a child of God, they also possess the free love of God with which God loves all things; if they do not have it, they are not yet receptive to that sonship. Now, if someone despises and condemns his Brother who does not yet possess such knowledge, how can such a person boast of the Love of God, with which God loved His enemies in Christ, and for which Christ prayed for His enemies?

46. O you false, cold love of nominal Christendom! <note>Original: *naam Christenheid*. 47. All your wrangling is nothing other than the mocker Ishmael, who mocks Christ in His members. ## CHAPTER 52.

->*The History of Isaac; also how Esau and Jacob were born,*<-
->*and what occurred therein, and what is to be understood by it.*<-

->Genesis 25.<-

1. Moses says: after the death of Abraham, God blessed his son Isaac, and he lived by the well of the living and seeing <note>original: "de bron des levenden en zienden"; a reference to the Hebrew *Beer-lahai-roi* (Genesis 25:11).</note>. Human reason <term>vernuft|The author distinguishes between "vernuft" (the worldly, logical intellect) and spiritual revelation.</term> understands this outwardly as a place where Isaac lived; but the Spirit looks upon the figure of the condition of life: how human nature and the creature lived by the wellspring of the Divine Essence <term>Ens|A Latin term used in alchemy and philosophy to denote the essential "being" or "substance" of a thing.</term> in the covenant which Abraham received in faith. As Isaac’s soul lived by the wellspring of the Holy Trinity, in which the soul received its light and recognized the will of God, from which wellspring the highest love of the Godhead revealed itself to the soul; from which wellspring thereafter, in the fullness of time, the holy Name of Jesus revealed itself out of Jehovah, and married the soul as a Bride.

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of Genesis 25, focusing on Isaac’s dwelling at the well of "the living and seeing One" (Beer-lahai-roi). It interprets this location not just as a geographical place, but as a spiritual state where the soul encounters the divine essence.</meta>

### The History of Isaac, Chapter 5.

2. The soul of Isaac lived by this well of the living and seeing <note>Original: *bron des levenden en zienden*, referring to the well Beer-lahai-roi mentioned in Genesis 25:11, meaning "Well of the Living One who sees me."</note> until that same fountain-spring later poured itself out and opened into the soul within the humanity of Christ; so the soul lived thereafter in the well-spring when it was exalted, in the person of Christ, to the right hand of God. Thus the well-spring of God flowed out through the soul, where it received Divine power, being a prince of God or like an imaged God, or a formed word of the voice of God—through which voice God became audible and manifest.

3. So also our soul, when it leaves the earthly will of the adopted selfhood and takes hold of the <term>Ens</term> <note>Latin: Being or essence; the fundamental substance of spiritual reality.</note> of Christ in the covenant and turns itself toward God, also dwells by the well of the living and seeing—that is, by the eye of God, which He has revealed again in humanity through Christ. In this time of the earthly hut <note>A metaphor for the physical body.</note>, our soul does not dwell in the well-spring of God in such a way that it encompasses the well within its selfhood; rather, it is as when the sun shines through glass: the glass does not become a Sun, yet it dwells in the luster and power of the Sun and allows the sun to shine and work through it. So it is with the soul in this time.

4. But this is just as the sun gives its <term>tincture</term> <note>A mystical or alchemical term for the spiritual life-force that penetrates and transforms nature.</note> into the metallic <term>Ens</term>, and the metallic <term>Ens</term> gives its desire into the <term>tincture</term> of the sun, so that from these both the beautiful Gold is born; so is it to be understood with the soul and the well-spring of God. The Godhead dwells through the soul, yet the soul does not encompass it according to its creaturely capacity; rather, the eye or light of God, with the holy love-<term>tincture</term> of the luster of the light, gives itself into the desire of the soul.

5. For the desire of the soul is the <term>fiat</term> <note>Latin: "Let it be"; the creative command of God that brings things into being.</note>, which takes the power of the holy love-<term>tincture</term> into itself and makes it into a being, so that from the Divine <term>tincture</term>, from the desire of the love-well, from the fountain of the living and seeing, and from the faith-desire of the soul, a single being is formed.

6. Understand this as a Spiritual being; and that same Spiritual being is the inward new man, being a new house or dwelling for the soul, in which it lives according to the inward Heavenly world. The name of this being is called <term>Sophia</term> <note>Greek: Wisdom; representing the divine mirror or the bride of the soul.</note>, being the Bride of Christ; the humanity of Christ, in which the noble Star of Jacob, from the precious Name of Jesus, is a shining light through which the soul sees and recognizes God.

7. The soul is not transmuted into the Godhead—namely, into the fountain of the living and seeing—for the soul is the eternal and temporal nature. Yet the Godhead is not nature, but the will toward nature, and it reveals itself through the soul’s nature, just as fire reveals itself through iron: there one looks upon the iron as pure fire, and yet it retains its nature.

# How Esau despised his birthright. Chapter [53]

11. For this is the very figure <note>The author uses "figure" to mean a symbolic pattern or spiritual allegory</note> of how God the Father gives His Nature and His soul to His Son **Christ**, entirely into the Being of Love <note>original: "liefde-Ens"</note> and into His own spirit, where the fiery justice of love becomes subject to the light. It happens exactly the same way in our new birth: the soul also hungers for this righteousness <note>original: "geregte," a wordplay in Dutch meaning both "a prepared dish/stew" and "justice/righteousness"</note>, but if she wishes to taste it, she must first give up her birthright. She must swear to God today—that is, for all eternity—to abandon her natural right. This appears ridiculous to the outward understanding—namely, to the children of earthly lust. When a person gives up honor, goods, and even their temporal life for this righteousness, they call such a person a fool, just as **Esau** is seen here.

12. In this figure, there is a twofold understanding. Internally, it is the figure of **Christ** and **Adam**, as was told above; externally, it is the figure of the earthly man, and how he runs so carelessly and sells and gives away the Kingdom of Heaven for the filling of his belly and the lust of his will. The poor soul, in her essence <note>original: "essents"</note>, indeed hungers for this "red dish" <note>referring to the lentil stew as a symbol of divine life</note>, but earthly cleverness perceives nothing other than a lentil stew for the hungry belly; this is also how **Esau** is to be understood.

13. **Esau’s** soul longed for the Heavenly Being <note>original: "Ens"</note> of **Jacob**, but the earthly part of him longed for the external soul and intended nothing more than earthly power. The right <unclear>of</unclear> nature had become so entirely earthly in him that he neither understood nor valued the eternal, but said: "What use is the birthright to me, since I must die?" He sat himself down, ate and drank earthly food instead of the Heavenly.

14. And **Moses** says that when he had eaten and drunk, he went <unclear>away</unclear> from there; that is, he filled his belly with the lentil stew and sold to him <note>Jacob</note> his natural right, and walked away with the earthly man from the Divine enjoyment.

->The internal figure is as follows:<-

15. **Abraham** received, in the desire of his faith, the Divine Being <note>original: "Ens"</note>; in this was the stem and the root of **Israel**, but he was not yet **Israel**. For the Kingdom of corrupted Nature and the Kingdom of Grace (being the received Being <note>original: "Ens"</note> of faith) were not yet unified in him. It is just as when a grain of <unclear>corn</unclear> is sown in the earth: the grain does not yet have a root upon <unclear>which</unclear> the stalk and the fruit must grow. However, the power of the grain draws the essences <unclear>of the earth</unclear> into itself, and from these both—namely, from the grain and from the power <unclear>of the</unclear> earth—the root of the stalk grows, and above it, eventually, the manifold <unclear>fruit.</unclear>

16. This is also to be understood here: the divine Holy Being <note>original: "Ens"</note> is not of <unclear>Nature</unclear>, but the soul is of Nature. Now, if the Divine Being is to be made manifest, <unclear>it must</unclear> happen through a natural essence, wherein the invisible becomes a visible being.

### Chapter 53. *And sold for a pottage of lentils.*

17. The *Ens* <term>Ens: A philosophical and alchemical term meaning "essence" or "fundamental being."</term> of the Divine faith, which **Abraham** received, was of an invisible spiritual quality. It desired to introduce itself, through human Nature, into a visible, substantial, creaturely, and natural being, in order to become an active life. There, the natural *Ens* of the Holy Light and the *Ens* of the soul (which is of a fiery nature) worked and bore fruit in a single being. For **Adam’s** Nature had departed from the Holy *Ens*, which had become tarnished within her; and here was the ground of reunion once again. Just as it is with grain in a field—where the power in the grain mixes with the *Ens* of the earth, and thereafter leaves its husk, where the *Ens* of the earth and the *Ens* of the grain are transformed into a single *Ens*—so it is also to be understood here.

18. **Abraham** received the *Ens* of divine faith, in which his justification consisted, yet his life-nature had not yet grasped it for its own power. For the Divine being does not surrender itself to the "own-power" of Nature; it does indeed give itself into the essence <note>original: "effens," likely meaning the smooth or receptive part of the nature</note> of Nature, but the Divine desire does not surrender itself to Nature in her own will, allowing Nature to hold the supreme Command. We have a likeness of this in the Grain that is sown.

19. Earthly nature cannot make another Grain by its own power, even if it draws the *Ens* of the Grain into itself; it bears nothing other than a stalk, in which stalk the *Ens* of the Grain grows out and introduces itself into a blossom, and again into a Grain. To this process, the earthly Nature with its *Ens* must be merely a servant.

20. And just as the earthly Nature of the soil always shows its child visibly in its growth first, while the *Ens* of the Grain hides within it, so it is also to be understood here with **Abraham**. **Adam’s** Nature showed itself from **Abraham** first with its fruit, with **Ishmael**; but the Divine *Ens* was still hidden within him in his Nature, and grew out with **Isaac**. And in **Isaac**, the Adam-nature and the Heavenly-nature grew out again alongside one another, although in a single seed.

21. Yet, just as the *Ens* of the earth in the stalk and the *Ens* of the grain in the internal ground grow up in and with one another, and yet each brings forth its own fruit—namely, the earth the stalk and the dwelling-place of the Grain, and the Grain the blossom and the fruit—and nonetheless one cannot come into being without the other, so it is also to be understood here.

22. **Abraham** was the field in which God sowed His Grain. **Ishmael** was the root, being the first birth; **Isaac** was the fruit, which grew from the seed of God—understand: from the *ens* of grace—and **Ishmael** from the *ens* of Nature, from the property of the Father. ### How Esau Despised His Birthright, Chapter 27. A

22. Nature submitted to this; thus each established his figure there: **Ishmael** as the Kingdom of Nature, and **Isaac** as the Kingdom of Grace. **Isaac** was now the branch that grew out of the field of faith—specifically, in the Line of Christ <note>original: *Linea Christi*</note>—and from him came **Jacob**, namely the expanding branch in a tree with many branches and sprouts.

23. It is not to be understood that **Jacob** sprang entirely from the Kingdom of Grace; for the Kingdom of Nature, in which **Ishmael** and **Esau** stood, was also his creaturely ground. However, the Essence <term>Ens: The spiritual essence or fundamental being of a person or thing.</term> of faith had entered into it, tinged <note>An alchemical term meaning to permeate, color, or transform the inner quality of a substance.</note> Nature, and carried its power—being the Line of God’s Covenant—into the highest part of Nature.

24. Just as a blossom from a stalk has a much more subtle quality than the stalk and the root, and just as the fruit and new seed come first from the blossom—namely, from the subtle essence—so also in **Jacob** there came forth the blossom of the Kingdom of **Israel**. This was no longer in separation, as is understood with **Ishmael** and **Isaac**, but both kingdoms together: namely, the Kingdom of Nature and the Kingdom of Grace. They were no longer separate figures for each kingdom, but combined in the image of the new rebirth. This shows how God had submitted Himself again to man—specifically, into the Kingdom of Nature—and how through His power the false essence of the serpent, which had been sown by the Devil, would be broken and killed within the Kingdom of Nature.

25. And therefore God called **Jacob**, **Israel**, being a greening tree with many sprouts and branches; or, as it is understood in the grasp of the word in the high tongue <note>A reference to a mystical or primordial language believed to reveal the true nature of things.</note>, a "Greening of Paradise." There, the (I) <note>The letter 'I' here represents the divine unity or the name of Jesus (Iesu).</note> has entered the root as a new Center and pushes out through the root; by this, one understands the Word of the Covenant in the name of **JESUS**. For (I) is the character of the One <note>original: *unum*; the indivisible unity of God.</note>—that is, of the eternal One in the divine light—which **Adam** lost when he went out from the (I) (that is, from the single will of God) into selfhood and into the multiplicity of properties in the discordant Harmony <note>original: *ongelyke Concordantie*; a state where the natural elements are out of balance.</note>, to test and taste good and evil in the five senses.

26. This (I) led itself out of grace back into the divided and separated properties of the Adamic human tree, and grew out through it along with the Adamic tree. From this arose the name **Israel**, signifying a great multitude of such branches, which all grew and branched out together in the new tincture. In these, the Essence of corrupt Nature also grew at the same time—just as the power of the sun and the earth work and grow together in the fruit of the tree. They stand in constant struggle with one another until the fruit is seasoned, and a new kernel is born and ripe for a new fruit. Then the tree leaves the fruit and sows the new kernel for another little tree.

27. Thus the struggle began over the sovereignty and the kingdom. The *ens* of Christ established itself as the highest part in Jacob and trod the *ens* of the serpent in Esau upon the head; simultaneously, the serpent there bit Christ in the heel <note>A reference to the prophecy in Genesis 3:15 regarding the seed of the woman and the serpent.</note>, and from this it came that those two children struck one another within the mother's body.

And just as *Isaac* in this blessing set *Jacob* as a Lord over his brothers of the Natural property <term>property: "eygenſchap," a technical term in mysticism referring to the inherent qualities or "signature" of a being</term>; so had God established the new birth in the blessing of **Christ** also as a Lord over the **Adamic Nature** in flesh and blood. This ensures that the new man, born from the blessing of God, should rule over all the members of his Natural Body, and that they should be subject to the new man.

34. And just as *Isaac* placed a curse therein—that he who cursed *Jacob* would be cursed, and he who blessed him would also be blessed—so also had God placed the curse upon the corrupt **Adamic kingdom**. All those who are not found within the blessing of **Christ** must eternally remain in the curse of God; but whoever would bring his mind and will into this *Jacob*—that is, the **Christ-blessing**—the same shall be eternally in the blessing.

35. Further, we see in this image how it goes with the children of God; for when *Isaac* had blessed *Jacob*, then *Esau* came with his venison, whereat his Father *Isaac* was terrified and spoke: "How, who are you?" He was startled because he had unknowingly blessed *Jacob*. This is an image of how the **Adamic man** understands nothing at all of the ways of God; how God often leads him so wonderfully according to the inward ground <note>original: "inwendigen grond"; a mystical term for the deepest, most spiritual part of the human soul where God dwells.</note> that even though he is led upon the path of God, he yet looks more at the outward...

### ->Chapter 55. How *Isaac* unknowingly blessed *Jacob*.<-

[...you shall] serve and it shall come to pass that you also shall be a lord and shake his yoke from your neck. <note>The text here completes the biblical prophecy from Genesis 27:40 regarding Esau's relationship to Jacob.</note>

41. And this indicates the kind of governance under which the outward **Natural man** is led, driven, and nourished, and what his desire and actions are: namely, that in his mind he is nothing other than a robber, a murderer, and an evil beast, who desires to draw everything to himself through violence and killing.

42. For *Isaac* does not say: you *must* sustain yourself by the sword; rather, he says: you *shall do it*. That is to say, the fierceness of God <note>original: "grimmigheid Gods," a term referring to the wrathful or stern aspect of divine nature that governs the fallen world</note> in the kingdom of corrupt Nature, combined with the will of the devil, shall move you to seize the fatness of the earth for yourself. You shall be ruled and driven from above by the constellations <note>original: "gesternte," referring to the astrological influences that the author believes govern the physical body and "natural" impulses</note>, and in your natural strength, you shall drive away the children of God who rule in the power of God. This is what it means to "shake the yoke from your neck": whenever the **Holy Spirit** in the children of God rebukes the "Esauites" for their tyranny, they murder and kill them, thereby ripping the sword of the Holy Spirit from their own necks, just as *Isaac* said: "you *shall* do it."

43. Just as *Esau* did this immediately and sought to kill *Jacob*—so that *Jacob*, bearing the blessing of God, had to flee from him—*Esau* had already shaken the burden of the Holy Spirit from his neck. This sign or prophecy from the Patriarch *Isaac* is a figure <note>A "figure" or "type" is a historical person or event seen as a symbolic preview of a later spiritual reality.</note> of how the **Esauites** and tyrants, being the fleshly brothers of the **Christians**, would live among them. Though born of the same parentage and shared ancestry, like *Esau* and *Jacob*, they would nevertheless persecute their brothers with the sword and plagues. They would still present themselves as Christians and desire God’s blessing, just as *Esau* stood and wept for the blessing; yet he did not care for the Kingdom of God, but only desired to be a lord on earth over his brothers and other men, and to have wealth and a full belly.

44. This *Esau*, in his blessing, is a true figure of the **Antichrist**, who approaches God with his lips and enters into an outward, deceptive service of **Christ** as if he were doing it for God. He stands and shows off with hypocrisy, acting with great devotion so that he may be honored by men and so that his god <term>Maosim<gloss>A Hebrew term from Daniel 11:38, often interpreted by mystical writers as a "god of forces" or "god of fortresses," representing worldly power, riches, and institutional pride.</gloss></term> may grow fat. He also weeps out of malice when people will not do what he wants, or when he cannot obtain the "blessing of the belly" as much as his god *Maosim* desires. Whoever challenges him or speaks of the true blessing of God, he wishes to kill; he cannot endure a servant of **Christ** beneath him.

<meta>This page continues the interpretation of Isaac’s prophecy to Esau. The previous page discussed how the "Natural Man" (represented by Esau) is driven by earthly desires and astral influences, often reacting violently toward the "Spiritual Man" (represented by Jacob).</meta>

### ->How *Isaac* unknowingly blessed *Jacob*. Chapter 55.<-

45. Human reason assumes that because *Isaac* said to *Esau*: "you shall support yourself with your sword," God had commanded him to do so. Reason relies on this interpretation, but the truth is different; God does not desire war. Rather, it is the kingdom of Nature—existing within the **Wrath of God** <note>original: "Toorn Gods," referring to the harsh, judgmental, or "dark" aspect of divine power that governs the fallen material world</note>—that desires it. He who is born solely from the kingdom of Nature lives according to that same nature.

46. Therefore, *Isaac* said: "you shall do it," as if he were saying: you shall serve the **Wrath of God** through your own wrath, and you shall be a lord in the kingdom of Nature in this world. This is how the powerful earthly empires establish themselves through force and might; they do so through the kingdom of Nature in its "fierceness" <note>original: "grimmigheid," a term often used by theosophical writers to describe the raw, unrefined energy of the physical world</note>.

47. And we see further how *Esau*, for the sake of the blessing, was angry with his brother *Jacob*, even though he was not capable of receiving it according to the kingdom of Nature. This shows how the true **children of Christ**, for the sake of this spiritual blessing, are hated, persecuted, and killed by the "children in the kingdom of Nature." The reason is this: the **kingdom of Grace** must rule over the kingdom of Nature, and at the end of days, it shall break the kingdom of Nature and transform it into its own power. Therefore, there is a constant struggle between these two kingdoms.

48. For in this time, the **children of Christ** must live—according to the outward man—within the kingdom of corrupt human Nature; that is, in the kingdom of the **Esauites**. Yet, according to the Spirit, they are nothing more than foreign guests there. As *Christ* said: "my kingdom is not of this world." For this reason, the children of this world are angry with them and persecute them, just as *Esau* persecuted his brother *Jacob*.

49. For wherever the **kingdom of Christ** begins to flourish <note>literally "to turn green" (groenen), a metaphor for spiritual growth and vitality</note>, the kingdom of the devil immediately begins to rage. This happens because the kingdom of Christ intends to—and shall—strip him of his power and his princely throne. This is the source of the battle between the children of *Jacob* and *Esau* in this world.

50. For as soon as *Jacob* received the blessing, *Esau* resolved in his mind to murder *Jacob*. This is a "figure" <note>a symbolic representation or "type" that foreshadows a future spiritual reality</note> of *Christ*: it shows how the **Wrath of God** would murder him in this blessing, within his humble humanity <note>original: "onfeaangename Menfchheid," referring to Christ's state of lowliness or "unpleasantness" in the eyes of the world during his incarnation</note> according to the kingdom of Nature. It also shows how the **children of Christ** would be murdered within the **Wrath of God** according to this natural kingdom, and how they would shed their blood in this "Murderous Spirit" <note>term: <term>Moord-Geeft</term> (the spirit of violence and destruction inherent in the fallen world)</note> so that the **Wrath of God** might be extinguished and transformed into love.

1. When *Jacob* had received the blessing, he had to wander away from his father’s house, from father and mother, and flee before the wrath of *Esau*. This is a figure of **Christ** <note>original: "figure Christi," a typological interpretation where Old Testament events are seen as prefiguring the life of Jesus</note>: how He, after having taken on our humanity and fasted <note>original: "gefaft," likely referring to Christ’s trials or the "fixing" of His nature during His earthly ministry</note> within it, would flee with our humanity out of its Adam-like father’s house <note>the state of fallen nature inherited from Adam</note>, back into the first Paradisiacal house.

2. At once the devil and the world become angry with them, so that they must immediately set out upon the pilgrim-path of **Christ** and live in misery and oppression under the world’s servile yoke. For God leads them immediately, with their senses and minds, out of the house of their father—that is, out of the desires of flesh and blood—so that they think nothing of the world’s pleasures and flee from them, just as *Jacob* fled from his father’s house.

3. We also have a beautiful example here in *Jacob*: how he left his father’s house, as well as father and mother, for the sake of the blessing, and loved God more than all temporal goods, gladly leaving everything to *Esau* so that he might only be the blessed of God.

36. 37. > Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me;
whereupon the Gate of God immediately appeared to him and comforted his humanity, just as it did here to Jacob, when he had to flee from his father’s house in sadness.

### How Jacob journeyed to Laban. Chapter 57

...my *Bridegroom*, then *God* the *Father* commands him to be led into his own house, just as *Rachel* did here for *Jacob*, and told her *Father* who this *Jacob* was and what he intended; so too *Christ* shows his *Father* what the intention of the poor, tested soul is when it comes to him.

7. Then the most beloved and beautiful *Sophia* <note>The personification of Divine Wisdom, often viewed in this tradition as the soul's true spiritual bride.</note> is promised to them and set before their eyes, for which they feel great joy.

8. But when it happens that the soul thinks it shall take this *Bride* into its arms and have complete joy with her, then the other *sister*—namely *Leah*, that is, the *cross of Christ*—is laid there instead. The beautiful *Sophia* hides herself, and the soul must first take the *cross of Christ* as a spouse; and for another seven years for *Rachel*—that is, the *noble Sophia*—it must tend the sheep **of Christ** <note>original: "Chriſti"</note> before he receives her as a spouse.

9. But *God* the *Father* gives to the soul in its place the other *sister*, being the faint-heartedness <note>original: "blodigheid"; a state of humble trembling or spiritual timidity.</note> of the heart, so that the soul during this time might not play in the rose garden, but live in sadness, so that it may be tested and humbled, and continually tend the little sheep **of Christ** <note>original: "Chriſti"</note>, and in such a marriage not give itself over to lust or pride, as *Lucifer* did.

10. And even if it happens that this *noble Rachel* or *Sophia* is given in marriage to this soul—as happens to the steadfast children **of Christ** <note>original: "Chriſti"</note>, so that the soul holds this great wedding of joy with this *Bride*, which is understood only by those who have been a guest at such a wedding—the *noble Sophia* afterward behaves as if she were barren. The joy of the wedding passes, and the soul feels as if the love of this bride were taken away.

11. Meanwhile, *Leah* breaks forth under the *cross of Christ* and brings fruit; that is to say, when the soul receives the *Spirit of Christ*, then the great joy of this union begins, of which *Christ* spoke.

### Chapter 57. How Jacob came to Laban.

He then stands in our poor and simple form, in our innermost ground, and hides his great sweetness—which the soul tasted in the union—and covers her with his cross. Thus, the poor soul must meanwhile take the weak-eyed <note>original: "bloode", meaning timid or weak-sighted, referring to Leah's description in Genesis.</note> Leah, who represents patience, and work with her to produce fruit in the vineyard of Christ <note>original: "Chriſti"</note>.

In the same way, the noble **Sophia** <note>The personification of Divine Wisdom, often viewed in this tradition as the soul's true spiritual bride.</note> also says to the soul: "Produce divine fruits in my love-desire, or I shall depart from you," even though the soul cannot do such a thing by its own power.

15. Then she surely gives birth to the true Joseph—being a humble, chaste, and disciplined soul—who afterward becomes a prince over the Egyptian house of flesh and blood. In this house Pharaoh lives, who is the animal spirit; over this spirit, this Joseph is set as a ruler and governor. He becomes a ruler of the intellect <term>vernuft: the human capacity for logic and reason, which the author argues must be governed by the divine Spirit</term> and governs it with Joseph—that is, with God’s Spirit.

16. This is thus a part of the spiritual figure of Jacob, in which the Spirit plays with the future kingdom of Christ; just as He now, in the present, plays along with the fulfillment in the children of Christ, and continues to lead them in this way.

17. But we see here especially in this figure the ways of God: how the mind of God is very different from that of man. God hides Himself in that which man loves; for that which is simple and despised by the world pleases Him well—those who cling to Him alone and fear Him.

# How *Jacob* came to *Laban*. Chap. 57.

18. *Jacob* loved the beautiful *Rachel* and desired her, but the *linea* <term>lineage or spiritual line</term> of the covenant, through which *Christ* <note>original: "Chriftus"</note> was to be born, did not wish to push through *Rachel*, but through *Leah*. Furthermore, *Rachel* could not become pregnant until *Leah* had birthed the root or *linea* of the Royal Priesthood and Princely lineage, namely *Levi* and *Judah*.

19. For out of *Levi* came the Priesthood, and out of *Judah* the Scepter of the Kingdom, and the Prince *Christ* according to his humanity. This indicates that *Christ* wished to be revealed and born only in such people, and carries out His Priesthood of the Holy Spirit in those who depart from self-love and fleshly lust, and who are weak <note>original: "bloode", meaning simple, timid, or lowly in the eyes of the world</note>, plain, and despised by the world. These are the ones who consider themselves unworthy of such honor and do not claim these Divine workings as their own property or show them off, as the bold *Pharisees* did and still do.

20. For this *Leah* only desired to bear children for *Jacob* so that she might become pleasing to him, since she was otherwise despised for her weakness <note>original: "bloodigheid", referring here to her low status or the "weakness" of her eyes mentioned in Genesis</note>. Likewise, the true children of God desire to walk in the ways of God with divine power, through teaching and a simple life, for the sole purpose of pleasing God and serving Him.

21. For first *Leah* bore *Reuben*, who defiled his father’s marriage bed, showing that this root still sprang from human lust.

He would not dwell in their churches with the honor of His victory, nor allow His honor to be bound to houses made of stone, where men perform a beautiful, shining appearance, yet have nothing but murderous, arrogant hearts within, and with the "murdering sword of *Levi*" <note>A metaphor for using religious authority or harsh words to condemn others</note> kill and despise one another with words.

27. But in the soul of man, where one thanks and praises the Lord in great humility—just as *Leah* did when she gave birth to *Judah* in the lineage of *Christ*—there He wishes to dwell. They love and honor nothing but themselves, and thus bestow upon their "devised office" the honor that belongs only to God and to the love of one's neighbor in great humility.

1. <margin>Gen. 30.</margin> In this history, we see primarily how it fares for the children of God in this world, how they must live in nothing but crosses <note>The "cross" refers to spiritual trials or the suffering inherent in earthly life.</note> and adversity, just as Jacob did with his wives: for when Rachel saw that she was barren, she envied her sister Leah, showing that man's self-love does not seek the glory of God, but only itself, just as Rachel envied Leah because she had a name <note>Meaning status or a reputation for being favored.</note> that God had blessed her, and said to Jacob, "Provide children for me also; if not, I shall die."

2. There we see then how the ways of God are entirely hidden from human reason <note>Original: "vernuft," referring to the intellect's inability to grasp divine mysteries.</note>, even though they stand in the figure of Divine wonders; just as Rachel here represents the Adamic self-nature <note>The "Adamic nature" refers to the fallen, ego-driven state of humanity.</note>. This same nature desired the power of life from Jacob, out of the blessing of God, and if she did not obtain it, she would have to die; which the spirit of zeal in her desire well demonstrates, according to her inner ground <note>The "inner ground" (inwendigen grond) is a mystical term for the deepest center of the soul where God resides.</note> in the covenant of God. Yet her reason did not understand this, but desired only children so that she might be delivered from reproach. But her inner ground stood hidden, and longed to manifest itself through human nature into the human essence <note>Original: "essents," a technical term in mystical philosophy for the fundamental substance or "being" of a thing.</note>; therefore, the inner ground in the covenant of grace indicated through her own Adamic essence that if that same inner ground was not made manifest through the human essence...

...became, she would have to die eternally; therefore human reason <note>Original: *vernuft*. In this mystical context, it refers to the clever but spiritually blind intellect that relies on self-will rather than divine grace.</note> spoke: give me children, or I die. Outwardly, this appears to be a contrary will and dejection, but the Spirit of God has indicated His holy figures beneath it.

3. And so we see in these two sisters, who were daughters of God's covenant in the promise, how the serpent's poison in the wrath of God <note>Original: *grimmigheid Gods*. This refers to the "fierceness" or harsh quality of nature that exists apart from God's light.</note> has set itself so vehemently in flesh and blood against the line of Christ <note>Original: *linea Christi*.</note> within the covenant. This worldly nature continually despises that line and, in the clever human property of self-will, exalts itself and climbs high like a proud Lucifer, desiring to hold the rule.

4. Just as Rachel here despised her sister because she was outwardly more beautiful than Leah—while Leah was simple and plain <note>Original: *blode*. While biblical translations often say "weak-eyed," the author here emphasizes her lack of worldly charm or sharpness.</note> before the world, and Rachel possessed the spirit of the world in her intellect and elegance—so the Adamic nature ruled in Rachel over the revealed blessing of the covenant in Leah. This indicates that the line of Christ would be revealed in a lowly, simple, and despised form in such people in this world.

5. Such people are regarded only as foolish and timid by those of the clever intellect and by the splendor and beauty of the world. They may indeed walk through such mockery and contempt, sowing with tears, but in their inner ground, in the line of Christ, they would bear fruit and finally harvest with joy. This shows that the kingdom of Christ is not of this world; it must be cast into the wrath of God and into scorn and death in this world. By such a casting-in, it fulfills the wrath of God with love and meekness, growing green <note>Original: *voortgroenen*. A favorite term of the author to describe spiritual life blooming out of the "winter" of suffering.</note> with love through the wrath and death. It makes the proud Lucifer of human self-will and fleshly lust into a mockery and nothingness—a fleeting life that cannot overpower divine humility.

6. This humility <note>Original: *demoedigheid*.</note> grows green amidst all mockery; it breaks through death and the wrath of God, turning death into life and stripping hell of its victory. It transforms the sting of the serpent's false essence with sweet love, as we see here with Leah. Even though she was envied by her sister—that is, by the clever reason—nevertheless the line of Christ in the covenant grew green within her amidst all mockery. It made her fruitful and Rachel barren, until Rachel gave her maidservant to her husband as a wife. This indicates the Adamic line—the servant's line <note>Original: *knegts linea*.</note>—which comes to the marriage of the line of Christ in the kingdom of Christ in the manner of a servant.

### Ch. 58. And he begat 12 sons and one daughter.

7. For Adam squandered the <term>line</term> <note>Original: *linea*. In this mystical context, it refers to the spiritual "thread" or lineage of divine grace that leads from the beginning of time to the birth of Christ.</note>; the right of Nature in the kingdom of God was lost in Adam and now returns in the manner of a servant, just like the handmaids of Jacob’s wives. There we see that Rachel—representing the right of one's own Nature—could bring forth no fruit or work until the line of servitude, under the yoke of the Adamic Nature and of self-love, first became fruitful. This indicates that human Nature must submit itself to service under the <term>Line of Christ</term> <note>Original: *linea Christi*.</note> if it wishes to be wedded to that Line and established as an heir of God.

8. Only then does the kingdom of Nature first sprout within the Kingdom of God and become fruitful in blessing, just as Rachel first became fertile after her handmaid had given birth. This shows that Rachel also had to be a "handmaid" for the covenant of God and for the Line of Christ, and that within her, the Line of Christ must also be her Lord. Thus, she comes to the marriage of the Line of Christ in the manner of a handmaid, for she did not possess the Line of Christ in her own power or by right of Nature, but rather as a gift of grace which exists in another <term>principle</term> <note>Original: *principium*. This refers to a fundamental source or a different realm of existence (the divine vs. the earthly).</note>.

9. And it is shown here how the Line of Christ is not propagated by any human power of one's own, but rather how it forces its way into its own branches. No "high names" of men or noble lineages are regarded; instead, it presses just as readily upon the most wretched in the world—those who are nothing more than servants and maids—as it does upon the high-born.

10. We have a powerful example of this in Jacob, who had to be a servant for twenty years, living as a laborer until the twelve tribes of Israel were begotten through him. This indicates that a Christian must be born under the serving yoke of the corrupt, self-ruling, and self-willed Adamic Nature. But if he is to be born out of the Line of Christ, then the one "bearing" him <note>The author uses "baarder" (one who gives birth) to describe the spiritual process of bringing forth a new, holy nature within the self.</note> must give themselves over as a servant of God. In the kingdom of Nature, they must be only as a minister of God who serves his Lord therein, abandoning all temporal things in his heart and regarding nothing as his own.

11. Just as Jacob begat the tribes under such servitude, it shows that they would be "foreign guests" in this world, serving God their Lord within the kingdom of Nature. He himself would give them their reward, so that they might enter with great goods out of this world into the kingdom of Christ—that is, into their original Adamic, Paradise fatherland. This is mirrored in how Jacob, through his service, acquired the goods of his father-in-law with a great blessing.

He desires to take his fruits with him—which are the children, brothers, and sisters, and all the children of this birth. He develops a great longing for it, just as Jacob did for his Father’s house. But the Lord says to him: "Stay and serve me here still, and tend my sheep; name the wages I shall give you"—that is: "Ask of me, and I shall give it to you," just as *Christ* said: "Whatever you shall ask of the Father in my name, he will give to you."

53. This Jacob thus sinks into patience <note>original: "lydsaamheid" - implying a state of humble endurance or long-suffering</note> and tends the sheep of *Christ*, hoping for the eternal reward that follows him. For in Joseph—that is, in *Christ*—the reward is first given to him, just as Joseph became Jacob's reward in the external kingdom, and sustained him along with his house during the animal time <note>A reference to the famine in Egypt, which the author interprets as the spiritual hunger of the fallen world.</note>; this points toward *Christ*, who wants to sustain us in himself eternally, and lead us home with him into his Father’s house, just as Joseph led his Father and children into his Lord’s land.

46. 47. In *Rachel* we now see self-love in the kingdom of Nature, where both tinctures, male and female, unite in conjunction according to the kingdom of Nature in self-love, just as *Jacob* [loved] his *Rachel* according to the kingdom of Nature—according to the tincture of self-desired love—and likewise *Rachel* loved *Jacob*. Therefore these tinctures of self-Natural love had to remain closed for so long, and bring forth no life, until the Lord remembered *Rachel* and heard her, as the text in *Moses* <note>The Book of Genesis.</note> says; that is, until the Lord moved the tincture of the kingdom of Nature with his blessing. Only then did she bear a Prince in the kingdom of Nature, being *Joseph*, in whom we see—by his great discipline and fear of God—that the blessing of God moved the tincture of the kingdom of Nature which lay enclosed in the seed, and revealed the covenant of grace therein.

48. 49. Through *Leah*, *Christ* was represented according to his Heavenly hidden humanity, showing how the essence of the heavenly world would hide itself in our humanity, under the yoke of the Wrath of God, and how *Christ* had to appear in a servant-like and despised form.

# CHAPTER 59.

## *How Jacob departed from Laban, what this figure signifies, and what is to be understood by it.*

->Genesis 31<-

1. IN this Chapter, for the most part, the external history is presented, beneath which the Spirit has His hidden <term>figure<note>In this mystical tradition, a "figure" is a symbolic archetype where historical events mirror the internal spiritual development of a believer.</note></term> with which He plays; for the Text says: and the words of Laban’s children came before Jacob, saying that Jacob has taken all of our Father’s goods for himself, and has brought about such wealth from our Father’s goods; and Jacob looked upon the face of Laban, and behold, it was not toward him as it was yesterday and the day before.

2. This is a figure prefigured in the Spirit of Christ: when the Spirit of Christ has drawn the kingdom of human Nature in man to itself, then the envy of the serpent wakes up in the <term>fieriness of Nature<note>original: "grimmigheid der Nature"; this refers to the harsh, "dark" quality of nature that exists when it is not tempered by divine light and love.</note></term>, in flesh and blood, because it understands and feels that the power of Nature in man is being withdrawn from it, and it becomes an enemy in the power of Nature against the Spirit of Christ.

3. Then begins the warring will in man, so that the poor soul is everywhere constricted, because she becomes aware that she dwells among foreign goods, and that the devil is her neighbor, and still generally has an access to her own Nature, and is her enemy; because she, in the Spirit of Christ, has withdrawn from him the kingdom of Nature—that is, his land or seat that he once held. Thus, the mortal Nature in <term>God’s Wrath<note>original: "Gods Toorn"; for mystics like Jacob Boehme, the "Wrath" is the fundamental fire of existence that becomes "Hell" when separated from God's light, or "Heaven" when unified with it.</note></term>, with its desire, then behaves strangely and unkindly toward the poor soul, just as one sees that she loses her lustful earthly inheritance; the right to which Laban's children point out, where reason sees how she loses temporal honor and lust, and all her Natural rights are withdrawn from her, just as Jacob withdrew Laban's goods through his cunning.

4. Then God speaks to the soul, just as He did here to Jacob: "Depart again into your Fatherland to your kindred, I shall be with you." That is, the poor soul should depart again into her first Fatherland—namely, into the Eternal Word from which she came; in that same Word, God blesses her, and therein can—

### How Jacob departed from Laban. Chapter 31. ###

...mortify the external humanity, yet he rose again from the dead, and carried his acquired goods into his fatherland.

9. In this chapter, the Spirit of Moses sets forth a wonderful figure <note>The author uses "figure" to mean a "type" or a prophetic symbol—an event in the Old Testament that foreshadows a spiritual reality in the New Testament.</note> that is well worth noting, as he points to something hidden beneath it. For he says that when Jacob fled from Laban, Rachel stole her father’s gods. He further says that Jacob "stole the heart" <note>original: "stal... het herte". A Dutch idiom meaning to act without someone's knowledge or to deceive them by silence.</note> of Laban the Syrian, because he did not tell him that he was fleeing. We see further how Laban, when he reached Jacob, so vehemently searched for the gods and ransacked all of Jacob’s household goods because of them. We also see in this text how Rachel must have loved these same gods very much, as she sat upon them and hid them so that her father could not get them back.

10. In these words, an external figure is presented to us of how it would go with Israel in the future. For these gods were not heathen idols according to the Moloch <note>An ancient Ammonite god, often associated with the stars or planetary influences in mystical traditions.</note> of the stars, such as the heathens had; rather, as one reads, they made images of their deceased as a memorial. These images later became idols among the heathens. It may well have been such images of his deceased friends that Laban was unwilling to lose, since through them he remembered his dear ancestors and friends.

11. Yet the true figure, by which the Spirit points to the future, is this: first, that Israel would not always cling to God with their whole heart, but they would always carry these gods of fleshly self-love with them. They would love themselves and their own images—the lineages of human highness—more than God, just as indeed came to pass.

12. This departure of Jacob primarily points to the exodus of Israel out of Egypt into the promised land, where they also took their fleshly gods with them. Afterward, they served their own gods—namely, human highness—and abandoned their God. They looked toward their Mammon <note>A term from the New Testament referring to wealth or material greed personified as a false god.</note> and desired to have kings among them according to the custom of the heathens, abandoning their true King who had led them out of Egypt.

13. Secondly, it points to how Christ, in whose figure Jacob stood, would take this "Rachel" in our flesh and blood unto himself. This Rachel represents the idolatrous will of the soul, which in Adam had turned away from God and had seized upon and possessed images and gods. Just as Rachel did, Christ took the turned-away will of the soul with its adopted gods and im—

14. Then **Jacob** spoke to his household and to all who were with him: "Put away the foreign gods that are among you, and purify yourselves, and change your clothes, and let us go up to **Bethel**, so that I may make an Altar there to the God who heard me in the time of my misery, who was with me on the way that I traveled," etc.

He would purify our hearts (which are the wild souls) and change our clothes (that is, our flesh and blood), just as the text of **Genesis 35** clearly indicates to us. It pertains entirely to how **Christ** would offer us to God on that same Altar of his **New Testament**—he who appeared to us again in his covenant of grace during our sorrow and our misery after the Fall.

16. For the Word became man and took **Laban’s** daughters (**Laban** being the earthly **Adam**) and led them away by divine craft <term>divine craft: original "Goddelijke lift" (list), referring to a holy deception or "pious trick" by which God rescues the soul from the powers of darkness</term> out of **Adam’s** house and into God’s house. At this place, it is called "stolen" because the children of **Adam** are thus "stolen" away from the kingdom of the **Wrath of God**—that is, they are carried away by divine craft.

17. For the **Wrath of God** had possessed humanity by natural right <term>natural right: original "Natuur-regt," the idea that, following the Fall, human nature legally belongs to the realm of judgment or "wrath" until redeemed</term>; but **Christ** came and betrothed himself to humanity, and stole them away from the **Wrath of God** along with the idols, and offered them up to God on his Altar (which he himself is), and laid aside the images of human self-love, and purified our clothes before God, so that we might serve him at this Altar.

18. This is what is actually understood by the gods of **Rachel**: the figure indeed represents the external history, but the **Spirit of God** has his figure there

Why do you not observe the custom of the churches, in which the kingdom of Christ stands in joy, with the sound of organs and pipes? Why do you steal away from us in secret and walk a different path than our ordinances and institutions?" For this reason, they become their enemies, persecuting them and hunting them down with damnation and contempt, as if they were wicked or perjured children who had robbed them of their gods and refused to honor their beautiful outward appearance as God. This is just as Laban pursued Jacob and scolded him for not having maintained his display of pomp beforehand and for not notifying him that he wished to depart.

20. A derogatory term for religious rules focused on material gain or carnal traditions rather than spiritual truth.</note>; and whoever wishes to enter into God in another way, and to flee from this house of bondage other than through her order, that person she damns and claims they cannot come to God.

21. But Jacob could certainly come to his father without Laban’s pomp; and even though Laban scolded him and called his way wrong, it was nevertheless right before God, for God had commanded it of him. And Laban could not hold him back; so too the children of Christ—when the Spirit of Christ within them commands them to flee out of Babel—cannot be held back at all. Nor does it harm them in the least, no matter how much the world scolds, despises, mocks, and calls them fools, heretics, and Enthusiasts for it.

22. Indeed, the Most High rebukes Laban, telling him that he shall speak only kindly to Jacob; that is, the slanders of Babel over the children of Christ...

When they secretly flee from the same and leave the house of idols, the children of the Kingdom of Nature scold the children of Christ as fugitives and oath-breakers, as heretics and novices, as *Enthusiasts* <note>original: *Enthusiasten*; a 17th-century derogatory term for those who claimed direct divine inspiration outside of church authority</note> and whatever other such names there are, and say to them: "When you wished to depart from the way of the ungodly into another life, why did you not say so to our high priests, so that they might have led you there with their ceremonies—namely with confessions, sacraments, and intercessions? Why do you not observe the custom of the churches, in which the kingdom of Christ stands in joy, with the sound of organs and pipes? Why do you remove yourself secretly from us and go a different way than our ordinances and institutions prescribe?" And for this reason, they become their enemies, persecuting them and chasing after them with condemnation and contempt, just like wicked or perjured children who had robbed them of their gods and would not honor their beautiful appearance as gods—just as Laban pursued Jacob and scolded him for not maintaining his pomp before him and for not announcing that he wished to depart.

20. Likewise, **Babylon** <note>original: *Babel*; signifying the "City of Confusion" or the worldly, institutionalized church systems</note> only wants the children of Christ to enter into God through her pomp and "belly-order" <note>original: *buyk-order*; a critical term for religious rules served for physical comfort or clerical greed</note>; and whoever else wishes to enter into God and flee from this house of bondage by any order other than hers, the same she condemns, claiming they cannot come to God.

21. But Jacob could indeed come to his father without Laban’s pomp; and even though Laban scolded him and called his way unjust, it was nevertheless right before God. For God had commanded him so, and Laban could not hold him back. Likewise, the children of Christ—when the Spirit of Christ within them commands them to flee out of Babylon—cannot be held back. Nor does it harm them at all, no matter how much the world scolds them for it, and despises, laughs at, mocks, and brands them as heretics and Enthusiasts.

22. The Most High indeed rebukes Laban, telling him that he shall speak nothing but kindly to Jacob; that is, the slanders of Babylon over the children of Christ

25. For as soon as Christ is born in a person, so that the mind departs from the Adamic house of bondage and from imagery, the angels of God are appointed to them as companions.

### Chapter 60: How Esau met Jacob.

Jacob sends word to you: I have been staying with Laban until now, and I have oxen, donkeys, sheep, menservants, and maidservants; and I have sent to tell this to you, my Lord, so that I might find grace in your eyes. The messengers returned to Jacob and said: We came to your brother Esau, and he is also coming to meet you with 400 men. Then Jacob was greatly afraid and became distressed; he divided the people who were with him, and the sheep, the oxen, and the camels, into two camps <note>original: "heyren," referring to hosts or companies</note>, and said: If Esau comes to the one camp and attacks it, then the remaining one shall escape.

2. This entire chapter stands powerfully as a **figure of Christ** <term>figure: a prophetic type or symbolic representation where an Old Testament event foreshadows the life of Jesus</term>; for when the Word had become human, and now wished to depart from this world and possess his eternal place again with our humanity, this "Host of War" met him in the Kingdom of Nature, within the **Wrath of God**.

3. For the kingdom of nature, being the natural Adam, was the firstborn Esau, who became angry with Jacob—that is, with Christ—over the blessing and the heavenly inheritance, namely, over eternal life; this was because the natural state had to die and lose its rights. In this kingdom, the Wrath of God had obtained the government. This same Wrath of God came to meet Christ when he now wished to bring his earned goods into his eternal fatherland—that is, into the **Love of God**—just as Esau met Jacob in the image of this figure. Before this army, that is, before the Wrath of God, Christ was as terrified as Jacob was before the wrath of Esau, as can be seen at the **Mount of Olives** <note>A reference to Jesus’ agony in the Garden of Gethsemane before his arrest</note>.

4. And just as Jacob, fearing Esau’s grimness, divided his flock into two parts so that if Esau struck one camp, the other might escape; so also the humanity of Christ was divided into two essences <term>essences: the fundamental natures or substances of a being</term>, namely into a *heavenly* one (of which he said in John 3, that it had come from Heaven and was in Heaven) and into an *earthly* one, made from our flesh and blood. If the Wrath of God struck the one part—being our humanity—with death, the Heavenly part would nevertheless escape the wrath, penetrate through death, and therein make our humanity alive. For the messengers whom Jacob sent to Esau are nothing other than the **prayer of Christ**, which he sent through the Wrath of God into His love (that is, into His mercy), so that our humanity might find grace before God.

5. For just as Jacob had Esau told that he had been away with Laban for a long time until now, and that he had servants, maids, camels, and other cattle with him, and that he hoped to find grace with all of these before his Lord Esau; so also Christ said to his Father regarding our assumed human-

38. 40. And precisely this must be pointed out: how it happened with Jacob and all the children of God in this sunshine, and how it still happens. This "creaturely imagery" lies so firmly in our mind's own deviated will that we can nowhere understand what God is—namely, that he is the abyss of all Nature and the Creature itself, being the Eternal ONE, who dwells in nothing but himself alone, and has no form or anything else.

When one teaches and speaks of the eternal God, it has happened until now that they have led us into mere images regarding His essential will—as if the one God willed "this" or "that." Yet He Himself is the single Will toward the Creature and Nature; the entire creation lies solely in the formation of His breathed-out Word and Will. The distinctness of that single Will is understood through its expression and its engagement with Nature.

42. If only Lucifer’s pride could be torn from the hearts and eyes of these same masters, then the face of God would soon be seen. But the Babylonian wrath <note>A reference to the Tower of Babel; here it signifies the confusion and pride of intellectual systems that try to "climb" to God through human logic.</note>—in which men wish to climb and ascend in their own opinions to a God locked away in a "particular heaven"—holds back true recognition and understanding. Thus, we constantly ask: *What is God’s name? Where is God? What does God want?* Furthermore, they claim He wills both good and evil, from which they construct a heap of decrees regarding God's purpose, just as a prince makes laws in his land. They have about as much understanding of God and His will as a clay pot understands its potter.

43. It is a pity that we are led so blindly and that the truth is withheld from us in images. For if the Divine power becomes manifest and active in its radiance within the internal ground of the soul, so that a person desires to leave the godless path and surrender themselves to God, then the entire Triune God <note>The Trinity: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.</note> is present in the life and the will of the soul. The Heaven in which God dwells is then opened within the soul; and right there in the soul is the place where the Father begets His Son, and where the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son.

44. For God requires no measurable place for Himself; He also dwells in the abyss of godless souls. However, according to His love, He is not perceptible to them; but according to His wrath, He is manifest and perceptible within the souls of the godless.

45. For the eternal speaking of the Word (in its relationship to Nature and Creature) becomes imaged according to the will of the soul. Of this the Scripture says: *With the holy you are holy, and with the perverse you are perverse* <note>Original: "by den Heiligen zyt gy heylig, en by den verkeerden zyt gy verkeert," a reference to Psalm 18:25-26.</note>; likewise, whatever kind of people they are, such a God they shall also have.

46. For in the thrones of the Holy Angels, God is manifest in His love; and in the thrones of the devils, He is manifest in His fierceness—namely, according to darkness and torment. And yet He is only one single God, and not two. According to the nature of the torment, He wills torment, and...

Through this, the kingdom of Nature in its wonders is nevertheless revealed and brought into figurative wonders.

# THE 61st CHAPTER

### The wonderfully beautiful figure of how Jacob and Esau come together, and how all sorrow and ill will were changed into great joy and mercy, and what is to be understood by this.

->Genesis 33<-

<margin>1.</margin> Blind reason <note>In this context, "reason" refers to human intellect attempting to understand divine mysteries without spiritual enlightenment.</note> may open its eyes better in this text than it has done until now, and better contemplate the figure of Jacob and Esau, and learn to rightly understand the decree concerning Jacob and Esau; where the scripture says: *Jacob have I loved and Esau have I hated*; when the children still lay in the Mother's body, and had done neither good nor evil, so that the purpose of God might stand <note>This refers to Romans 9:11-13, discussing divine election and the sovereignty of God's will.</note>.

<margin>2.</margin> Here one must rightly look upon the purpose of God—what the Spirit of God means by this. For Esau stood in the image of the corrupted Adam, and Jacob in the image of Christ, who had come to help poor Adam. Therefore, the two brothers had to come from a single seed, pointing to the fact that God would become man, and that the seed of God (being His word) and the seed of Adam (in his own nature) would become manifest and become man in a single person. It shows that the seed of God would overcome the corrupted seed of Adam with the greatest Divine love, and extinguish the Father's Wrath in the soul with love. The Divine love would give itself entirely into the wrath of the soul, so that the grace and mercy of God in love would penetrate through the wrath and also change the wrath into mercy. This is just as Jacob here, with his gift and great humility, gave himself over to his brother Esau and changed the wrath he bore against Jacob (on account of the natural right of the firstborn and the blessing) into great mercy, so that Esau fell upon his neck and wept in great mercy, and changed his wrath into love; just as Christ [changed] the Wrath of His Father with His great love and humility,

### Chapter 61. How Jacob and Esau come together.

When the **Wrath of God** held mankind captive in darkness, they were not recognized as God’s Holy image within that Wrath; but when, in the suffering of **Christ**, love broke through humanity and through the wrath—so that the wrath was transformed—then the one God looked upon them again in His image. 44. Now, if the Creature is to work with God, its will must enter into God; then God works with and through the Creature, for the entire creation—heavenly, hellish, and earthly—is nothing else but the working word; the word itself is everything.

### How Jacob and Esau come together. Chapter 6

48. For if evil were not recognized, then peace would not be made manifest; but when joy is revealed, then the eternal word is spoken in that joy. To this end, the word has introduced itself into a creature along with Nature.

Whoever sees and understands this rightly has no need for further questioning; for he sees that he lives and is in God, and he surrenders himself to God, so that God may know, will, and speak through him what and how He wills. 50. But as long as Lucifer has the reign in man, the creature strives for the highest place and wants to be its own God. God hated Esau <note>A reference to Romans 9:13: "Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated."</note> in the corrupt nature, even in Esau’s own nature, for Esau was the image of the fall itself. 54.
