At that time, their Paradisiacal image, which is not made manifest in this age, shall put on the essence of its faith from the spirit of Christ, through the bestowed grace of God which extends from the One to all. For that same grafted grace, being the "in-spoken word" <note>Dutch: *ingesproken woord*; the divine spark or seed of grace planted in the soul at the Fall</note>, also resides in them and is hungry for the substance of Christ.

76. But since their essence exists in the Word outside of this place in Christ—where Christ Himself fulfills their faith toward God—so too shall their substantial faith, in the grafted word of God within the Paradise-image, put on Christ in His revelation, and with it, the whole human being.

77. For the Scripture says: "By grace you have been saved, and that not of yourselves," not through your own knowing, but through God’s mercy. It does not depend on knowing—as if knowing could "take" Christ—but it depends on the giving; that is, on grace. This grace gives Christ to the ignorant through their faith in God, just as it gives Him to the knowing through their desire. For both, it happens by grace.

78. For Adam departed from the only God into a selfhood, into ignorance, and led us all together with him into that same ignorance. However, grace came back from that same only God and offers itself to all the ignorant, the Heathens as well as the Jews.

79. But the Fathers under the Figure, namely the Jews, had no greater share in grace than those to whom the image had not been revealed. For the prototype looked toward Christ. The Jews, through their faith and prayer, pressed through the prototype into the only grace that was in God, which God bestowed upon Adam and his children. But the Heathens, who did not have the Law, nevertheless believed without the circumcision in the only promised grace of God, and they pressed into that grace without the aid of the prototype.

80. For the ability was given to one people as much as the other; no people could achieve this of themselves, but grace took the will for the ability <note>Dutch: *nam den wil voor het konnen*; a phrase suggesting God accepts the sincere intent of the heart even when the person lacks the capacity to fulfill the law or understand the doctrine</note>, and gave them an equal power—the Jews as well as the faithful Heathens. # How the Sons of Jacob, due to the famine, Chapter 70. #

unbelief, and the refusal of the will, was the damnation of both the Jews and the Heathens, in that they kept their will within their **selfhood** <note>Dutch: *selfheid*; the state of being ego-centered or focused on the self rather than surrendering to the divine</note> and stubbornness, and went whoring after other gods. Thus, circumcision and sacrifices were not salvation for the Jews, but rather the grace which presented itself in such a **Figure** <note>Dutch: *Figuur*; a symbolic representation or "type" that points toward a future spiritual reality</note> until the incarnation of Christ; at that point, grace wished to fulfill the Figure, and the future fulfillment was their salvation.

81. It is the same currently: Christians have the Figure of grace under the Gospel in its fulfillment. They cannot take this fulfillment through their own power, but the fulfillment of grace offers itself to them. If they are willing to surrender themselves into it, then a "mouth" <note>An allegorical term for the capacity to receive or "taste" spiritual nourishment</note> is given to them within grace.

82. But the others direct their will toward the grace of God—which is the very same grace given to Christians, and nothing else—yet they do not know the **substantial** <term>substantial (wesentlyk): possessing a real, spiritual essence or "body" rather than being merely an abstract idea</term> grace in the image of fulfillment. Nevertheless, grace takes their will and their desire into itself, and grace possesses a "mouth" for that desire which is hidden from the **creature** <note>the individual human being in their created, earthly nature</note> until the day of the revelation of Jesus Christ.

83. Therefore, there is no difference between them other than the substantial movement within the **Paradisiacal image** <note>the original, uncorrupted state of humanity intended by God</note>, wherein the Paradisiacal image has not yet "put on" Christ in essence, as is the case with true Christians and their faith. And yet, it is substantially present in the grace of God in Christ—though not as the human's own property, but in God, who fulfills all things and dwells through all things. Thus, this same substantial grace is near to and within the believing Jews and Turks, yet it remains ungrasped by their creaturely self.

84. They have Christ within them, but they do not grasp Him unless their will enters into the substantial grace of Christ; only then does Christ reveal Himself in their creaturely being, just as He does in Christians. However, for the believing Jews and other peoples, the grace in Christ is "laid away" <note>reserved or stored up</note>; for it hovers through them, and their will toward God is within it, and walks within it.

85. A **title-Christian** <note>Dutch: *titel-Chriſten*; someone who is Christian in name only, without an inward spiritual life</note> without a divine will is further from God than a believing Jew, Turk, or Heathen—or whoever it may be—who places their trust in God and surrenders their will to Him. Such a person is much closer, and they shall condemn the title-Christian, for the latter boasts of knowledge and comforts themselves with grace, yet remains outside of grace, dwelling only in their evil will, and desires to carry their rogueishness into the grace of God.

86. You will say: "The foreign nations are not baptized in Christ, so they are not children of the covenant of grace." **Response:** <note>Original: *℞*, the Latin symbol for *Responsum*</note> If circumcision alone had been salvation, then Baptism would be as well; for one is like the other. But God required a Jew who was circumcised inwardly in the heart; circumcision was nothing other than the image of how Christ intended to cut away sin.

# Chapter 70. Journeying to Egypt again to Joseph. #

...that which Christ has fulfilled; so also the spirit of Christ baptizes with this covenant into the Paradisiacal image, into the engrafted grace, and strikes a spark.

87. But he requires an **essence** <term>essence (ens): a philosophical and theological term referring to the inner "being" or spiritual substance of a thing</term> of faith; that the "in-baptizing" is receptive, which comes from the parents, and through the earnest prayer of those who are performing the work; otherwise, the covenant is despised, and it is no circumcision of the heart and the Spirit. For the power with which the Holy Spirit baptizes does not reside with men, but in God. Whoever despises His covenant and does not practice it with earnestness and a circumcised heart, he baptizes them in His wrath—just as **Paul** <note>original: "Paulus"; referring to the apostle Paul in 1 Corinthians 11:29</note> says of the Supper of Christ, that the godless receive it to their own judgment.

88. A godless preacher has no power to baptize with the Holy Spirit; he has nothing other than the water, and he himself is not receptive to the office. Rather, it is the **essence** <note>original: "Ens"</note> of the child and of the believing parents—and those who promote the work—whose earnestness and prayer reach out through the desire of their faith to offer the covenant to the one being baptized.

89. But for the godless baptizer, there is no more use than the **baptismal basin** which holds the water; thus he carries nothing other than the water and the **ceremonies**, which even a **Turk** <note>In the 17th century, "Turk" was often used as a general term for a Muslim or anyone outside the Christian faith</note> could do without faith.

90. But a stranger, who does not have baptism and knows nothing of it, is circumcised in his heart through his faith, and the Holy Spirit baptizes him in the desire of his faith, and baptizes him upon the revelation of Jesus Christ, whereby his faith shall put on the **substantial** <term>substantial (wesentlyk): having a real, spiritual body or essence rather than being merely an abstract thought</term> covenant in grace.

91. O **Babel**! <note>Babel: A common term in this period for the "fallen" or corrupt institutional church, likened to the confusion of the Tower of Babel</note> How blind you are! How your clergy have placed themselves in the stead of Christ! Yet they do not all serve Christ, but themselves, for fleshly honor. O **Babel**, turn back! The door is open, otherwise you shall be spat out; the time is born when you shall be placed in the Light and tested, then you shall stand in shame before all peoples.

92. The Spirit of God has a further powerful **Figure** <note>Figure (Figuur): A symbolic representation or "type" from the Old Testament that foreshadows a spiritual truth in the New Testament</note> in this text: in that Joseph had his brothers sit across from him according to the order of their birth, and had five times more served to his brother Benjamin than to the others. This **prefigures** <note>original: "praefigureert"</note> for us, firstly, the distinction in the Kingdom of Christ—how they shall be unequal in the **rebirth** <note>original: "wedergeboorte"</note>, just as Paul says: they shall surpass one another in clarity, like the **Sun**, **Moon**, and **Stars**.

93. For there, he who has been a King, Prince, Lord, Noble, or scholar shall count for nothing; rather, he who has the greatest power within himself—he who shall have reached grace in the name of **Jesus** <note>original: "Iesu"</note> in the most pure way through the struggle of his penance—he shall be the greatest there. For this order only shows us how they shall be unequal in Divine highness—namely, in power—just as the Angels surpass one another in power and beauty.

### How Joseph had the sacks of his brothers filled. Chapter 71 ###

94. But the fact that five times more food was set before Benjamin points, in the Figure <note>original: "Figure"; a theological term for a symbolic person or event that foreshadows a future spiritual reality</note>, to the inward man; for Benjamin stands in that same Figure because he is Joseph’s brother. Since Joseph stands here in the Figure of Christ, it belongs to this same inward man to eat of the food of his Brother Christ, namely from His five wounds; this is what the precious Figure indicates here for those who have the eyes to see it.

95. But where the Spirit says they drank and all became drunk <note>referring to Genesis 43:34</note>, it indicates that in the Kingdom of Christ there is a universal enjoyment and joy, and that therein is no distinction; rather, they shall all together rejoice in one single God. For their drunkenness here indicates eternal joy, where we shall be as if intoxicated by such power; then the inward man shall drink and eat from the sweet grace that became manifest in the five wounds of Christ. He shall enter into the fiery soul with this grace, which—within the essences <term>essences (essentien): the fundamental spiritual substance or inner nature of the soul</term> of her fire and in this sweetness—shall awaken the triumph of the Divine Kingdom of joy. Thus the Noble Bride shall embrace her Bridegroom, which is the soul.

# Chapter 71. And laying the money with the cup in Benjamin's sack. 279

2. In this *Figure* <note>original: "Figure"; a theological term for an Old Testament event or person that serves as a symbolic preview of Christ or the Christian life</note> there now stands a follower of Christ <note>original: "een Christi"</note>, when he has become truly earnest in the image of the trial, on the pilgrim’s path of Christ in this world, showing how God now exercises and refines him; for this is the process on the pilgrim’s path of Christ, how God and the world set themselves against the creaturely ingenuity <term>creaturely ingenuity (creaturelyke vernuft): human cleverness or intellect that relies on its own power rather than divine guidance</term> of man. For in this image we see how God, when a man becomes truly earnest in his repentance, fills his sacks—being the mind and the conscience in the quality of life—with His grace, and lays in them the cup of salvation; being the true silver cup; that is the cup of Christ, from which He drank in His suffering, placed at the top in the sack of filled-in grace, from which a Christian must also drink, and follow Christ in His humiliation.

3. For the cup of Joseph from which he drank, and through which he prophesied, is in this *Figure* nothing other than the cup of Christ from His Testament <note>referring to the Last Supper and the New Covenant</note> before His suffering, from which He drank with His disciples, and thereby prophesied of His eternal kingdom, that whoever should drink from this cup, he should prophesy with Him regarding eternal life.

4. Yet this *Figure* points to the great earnestness of how this cup would be poured out for the children of God; what kind of wine it is that they must drink from it; for first Joseph sends his steward after them, and has it said to them that they had stolen the cup from him, and shows himself angry toward them, even though they were innocent. In the same way, when a Christian’s sack is filled with this food, the cup of Christ is placed alongside it: it attacks the Wrath of God in human nature, in his soul and in the mortal body, and says to the Conscience: "you do not have this cup by right, out of natural law; you have stolen it from God’s House, grace and power." In this, the Kingdom of Heaven suffers violence <note>a reference to Matthew 11:12, suggesting that spiritual grace is seized through intense spiritual struggle rather than inherited by nature</note>, and you have done violence, and drawn this Cup to yourself in your sack; you do not have grace as a natural right, yet you wish to walk along this path in peace with this Cup.

5. But no, it does not help you; if you wish to take the grace of Christ with you, then you must also take His suffering, death, mockery, persecution, and misery upon yourself, and continually allow yourself to be scolded in the world as a false person, and be regarded as a rogue by Pharisaic hypocrisy, as one who has stolen their cup and taken it into his power, because he will no longer kneel down before the great Babylonian Whore <note>original: "Babilonische Hoere"; a biblical image from the Book of Revelation, often used by historical writers to represent a corrupt or false church system</note> (who has poured out a Cup full of Hypocrisy and blasphemy) and drink from her Cup. Therefore she scolds him as a rogue who has stolen the Cup and power from her, and hunts him down, and wants to kill him, condemns him to temporal and eternal death, and scolds him without ceasing as a faithless one who has stolen the cup.

# How *Joseph* had his Brothers’ sacks filled, Ch. 7

This is the very same as saying that a true Christian must always be contradicted; even their own household members, in flesh and blood, must be their enemies, so that the planted Little Pearl-Tree <term>Little Pearl-Tree (Perelboomken): a mystical metaphor for the "seed" of divine life or the soul's spiritual rebirth that must be shaken by trials to grow</term> may be moved and produce fruit.

### Ch. 71. On placing the goods with the Cup in Benjamin’s sack.

*Christ* <note>original: "Christus"</note> [leads] the soul back out of the sack of essential grace—that is, with His flesh of the essential wisdom of God—and thus the one unites with the other for an everlasting operation.

12. And we see here how the godless must also serve God in His workings of grace, for they are His storm-wind; and their cursing and slandering of the children of God are the heat and the cold with which God stirs His Pearl Tree <note>A common mystical metaphor for the "new man" or the spiritual seed of Christ growing within the believer's soul.</note> in His children, so that it hungers for heavenly sap, draws it in, and grows. This is what *Christ* meant when He said that He had come to the earth to stir up strife; for the kingdom of *Christ* is a struggle against hell and the devil. *Christ* fights unceasingly in His children and members against Satan for the sake of the kingdom.

13. For in the earthly man still lies the "ground of the serpent," being a dwelling of Satan in which he resists the kingdom of *Christ*. Thus, the kingdom of *Christ* in grace resists the kingdom of Satan with the Cup of *Christ*, and this struggle continues throughout as long as the earthly body lasts.

14. For in this way the Wrath of God works within love, so that love—being the eternal *one* and *good*—might become distinguishable, experiential, and sensible. For in the struggle and opposition, the *Unground* <term>Unground: (Dutch: *ongrond*) a term used by mystics like Jacob Böhme to describe the absolute, groundless abyss or "nothingness" from which God and all existence originate.</term>, being the eternal *one* which is outside of Nature and the Creature, reveals itself.

15. And for this reason, God has introduced Himself—with His Holy Word of power—into Nature and the Creature, as well as into pain and torment, into light and darkness, so that the eternal power of His Word, in wisdom, might become distinguishable and experiential through His spoken word, so that there might be a knowledge [of it].

16. For without this, the knowledge of the eternal *one* would not be manifest; there would also be no joy, and even if it existed, it would not be manifest to itself. Thus, it reveals itself through introduction into Nature by the distinction of speaking, where the speaking introduces itself into properties, and the properties into opposition. Thus, through opposition, the eternal Good—which also leads itself into distinction within the word of speaking—becomes distinguishable, creaturely, and figurative.

17. Otherwise, if evil were not useful in this opposition, God—being the eternal and only Good—would not tolerate it but would bring it to nothing. However, it serves to reveal the glory of God and the Kingdom of Joy, and it is a tool of God with which He makes His Goodness figurative, so that the Good may be recognized; for if there were no evil, the Good would not be known.

### Ch. 71. *And placing the goods with the Cup in Benjamin’s sack.*

Christ [leads] the soul back out of the sack of substantial grace—that is, with His flesh of the substantial wisdom of God—and thus the one joins with the other in an everlasting operation.

12. And we see here how the wicked must also serve God in His working of grace; for he is His storm-wind. His cursing and slandering of the children of God is the heat and the cold with which God moves His pearl-tree <note>A metaphor for the growing soul or the "new man" within a believer, which requires the "winds" of trial to grow strong.</note> in His children, so that it hungers for heavenly sap, draws it into itself, and grows. And this is what Christ said: that He had come to earth to stir up strife; for the kingdom of Christ is a struggle against hell and the devil. Christ struggles without ceasing in His children and members against Satan for the kingdom.

13. For in the earthly man there still lies the ground of the serpent, being a dwelling of Satan, in which he resists the kingdom of Christ. Thus, the kingdom of Christ in grace, with the Cup of Christ, resists the kingdom of Satan; and this struggle remains throughout, as long as the earthly body lasts.

14. For thus the Wrath of God works in love, so that love—being the eternal "one" and the good—may become distinct, perceptible, and felt. For in the struggle and opposition, the "unground" <term>Unground: A term for the primal, fathomless depth of the Divine before any creation or distinction existed.</term>—which is the eternal one, existing outside of Nature and Creature—becomes manifest to itself.

15. And for this reason, God has introduced Himself with His Holy Word into the powers of Nature and Creature, as well as into pain and torment, into light and darkness, so that the eternal power of His Word, in wisdom, might become distinct and perceptible through His spoken word, so that there might be a "knowing" <note>The author argues that without contrast (light/dark, joy/pain), conscious knowledge of God’s goodness would be impossible.</note>.

16. For without this, the knowledge of the eternal *one* would not be manifest, and there would also be no joy; and even if it were there, it would not be manifest to itself. Thus, it manifests itself by entering into Nature through the distinctness of "speaking"—where the speaking introduces itself into properties, and the properties into opposition. Thus, through opposition, the eternal good (which also carries itself into distinctness through the word of speaking) becomes distinct, creaturely, and image-like.

17. Otherwise, if the evil in the opposition were not useful, then God—being the eternal and only good—would not tolerate it but would bring it to nothing. However, it serves for the manifestation of the glory of God and the Kingdom of Joy; it is a tool of God with which He makes His good into an image, so that the good may be recognized. For if there were no evil, the good would not be known.

<meta>This page continues the spiritual commentary on the story of Joseph, specifically focusing on the metaphysical relationship between God’s "Wrath" and His "Love," and how the soul must move from self-will to a state of humble "nothingness" to be filled by the Divine.</meta>

# How Joseph had the sacks of his brothers filled. Chapter 7.

18. If there were no wrath-fire, then there could be no light-fire either, and eternal love would be hidden from itself, for there would be nothing that could be loved; thus the love of God has a cause to love; for it loves the forsakenness, being the weakness, so that the same might also become great. <note>In this mystical framework, "wrath" is the necessary friction or energy that allows the "light" of love to become visible and felt. Without opposition, love would remain an unmanifested void.</note>

19. For the love of God only comes to the aid of the weak, the humble, and the forsaken, and not to that which moves in the power of fire—not the power of selfhood <term>Selfhood: The state of being driven by one's own ego or "own-will" rather than God's will.</term>, but rather the lack of power and the state of being forsaken. In all that is lowly, disregarded, humble, and forsaken, love works and dwells.

20. For love, in its own property, is nothing else but Divine humility, arising from the ground of the "only One." Love seeks and desires nothing but the "only One" alone; for it is itself the *One*, being the eternal nothingness; and yet it is through all things and in all things. But to the "selfness" of the own-will, love is a nothing.

21. Therefore, all that wills in its own power is regarded as foolishness and evil before the love of God—even if it seems useful—through which the "willing-nothing" manifests itself. Yet to this "willing-nothing," such self-driven power is nothing but a Fantasy <note>original: "Phantasie"</note>; being a game of self-driving and self-tormenting.

22. For that which wills nothing except that from which it proceeded has no torment within itself; for it does not belong to itself, but belongs only to the one from whom it came. It stands at the service of the Maker who made it; He can let it be a "something" or a "nothing." Thus, it is one single thing with the eternal One, for it does not torment itself, it does not love itself, and it does not feel itself in its own-will—for it has no own-will—but is surrendered to the Whole.

23. Just as we see that the four elements <note>The classic elements: Earth, Air, Fire, and Water.</note> exist within themselves in such a manner: there are four, and yet only one; for the four stand in a single ground, and that same ground is neither heat nor cold, nor moisture nor dryness. It is the single Element, an imperceptible life. However, it would not be manifest to itself in this way; therefore God moved it and breathed it out from Himself, and unfolded it so that it might be worthy of itself again, and stand in constant struggle, so that the One might be manifest in the Many.

24. Yet in this, one does not destroy the other so that it ceases to be or becomes a nothing; rather, that which is overcome stands still before that which has overcome it—the heat before the cold, and the cold before the heat. There is no "own-possessing" nor "own-willing," but one element wills the other so that the other may be made manifest. And as it becomes manifest, it gives itself over to the strongest movement, and thus there is a struggle, and yet the greatest love among them.

<summary>The author explains that Divine love requires "weakness" and "nothingness" in the soul to operate, using the balance of the four elements as an analogy for how opposites (like heat and cold, or wrath and love) work together to make God's glory manifest.</summary>

This is the greatest foolishness that nature has ever brought forth, and yet it is the instrument through which the highest wisdom is made manifest.

34. Yet, if the animal-like will in the flesh could be entirely broken and killed, then the curse would cease; then no Creature could be an enemy against him anymore.

35. But since that cannot be, man must stand in the struggle. He must allow much outward evil to desire within him, and also allow much evil to will out of himself into that which is outside of him. Thus, he stands in the struggle between the evil and the good, and in the evil and in the good, and lives in the struggle of the Elements and also in the struggle of his own will, which God gave him.

36. This divine willing kills his natural willing, as it were, and through man as God’s instrument, it rebukes the "children of Wrath" <note>original: "kinderen des Toorns" — a biblical reference to those living in a state of sin or separation from God, governed by ego and anger.</note> to their faces.

### Chapter 71. *And putting the money with the Cup in Benjamin’s sack.*

"The money that we found at the top of our sacks, we have brought back to you from the land of Canaan; how then should we have stolen silver or gold from your Lord’s house? With whomever among your servants it is found, let him die, and moreover, we shall also be my Lord’s servants." He spoke: "Let it be as you have said; he with whom it is found shall be my servant, but the others shall be free."

38. Whether God rebukes the soul through plagues in nature, or frequently by hiding His grace, or through the wicked world—setting the soul there as unrighteous—the conscience always wants to justify itself, as if an injustice were being done to it.

39. For once it has turned toward grace and broken away from the godless path, it thinks that no evil should happen to it anymore. It feels God is obligated to protect it, and that the world treats it unfairly when it labels the soul as false. It feels it should no longer be subject to plagues and punishments, and it claims piety and righteousness for itself. In doing so, it "steals" God’s fine Grace and counts it as its own property, as if it were no longer guilty of sin.

40. It even presumes much before the World; when the world still attributes sin and wickedness to it, the soul claims that if it were truly guilty, it would accept death or the like. This is just as Joseph's brothers did, who knew nothing of the [staged] theft; but they did not understand that all their iniquity—specifically their "theft" of Joseph when they stole him from his Father and sold him—was manifest before Joseph’s eyes, just like the money in the sacks of gifts. Joseph knew and recognized their thievery, which is why he allowed them to be labeled as thieves, hunted them down like thieves, and brought them back to face justice.

41. Yet, in place of their thievery and the sins they had committed, by which they had forfeited their lives, Joseph had his fine silver Cup placed in their sacks along with the gifts, and allowed them to be accused of a theft they would not admit to.

<meta>This page continues the spiritual interpretation of the Joseph narrative, specifically focusing on the legal and mystical implications of the silver cup found in Benjamin's sack. It transitions from the believer's external innocence to their internal participation in the "Process of Christ" and the reality of inherited sin.</meta>

### Cap. 71. And the placing of the goods with the cup in Benjamin’s sack. 287

...denounces him as false and unrighteous, and condemns him to the damnation of temporal and eternal death. Even if he is not guilty before the world, nor toward the world, he is nevertheless bound to carry the mockery, suffering, and death of Christ after Him as a Christian. He is bound to take upon himself the entire **Process of Christ** <note>The "Process of Christ" is a central theme in this text, referring to the internal spiritual journey where a believer re-lives the pattern of Jesus’s life, especially His suffering and death, to achieve spiritual rebirth.</note>, to follow Christ therein, and to suffer all things in Christ. He must fully put on Christ in His shame, contempt, suffering, and death, and carry His cross and mockery after Him, so that he may enter into the Kingdom of Christ as a member of the Body of Christ that has suffered with Him, and has daily died to his actual sins in the death of Christ, away from the <term>Wrath of God</term> <note>In the author's mystical theology, the "Wrath of God" (Gods Toorn) is the fire of divine justice that must be transformed into love through the sacrifice of Christ.</note>.

49. For all sins, wickedness, and untruth that are wrongly laid upon him by the world—of which he is not outwardly guilty in his actions—he suffers these in the **Process of Christ** as a Christian. In this way, he drinks from the **Cross-Cup of Christ**, who suffered innocently for his sins.

50. For even if he has not become guilty of these specific acts in his own life, he is nevertheless guilty of them through **inherited sin** <note>original: "aangeërfde sonden"</note>. He has inherited them in the very seed from which he originated; they lie in his foundation. Before God, in the **Process of Christ**, he cannot excuse himself; he is guilty of all **Adamic sins** <note>Referring to the "Original Sin" inherited by all humanity from the biblical Adam.</note>.

51. Yet, this is his comfort: that God reveals these sins through the "children of His Wrath" <note>This likely refers to worldly or wicked people who persecute the believer.</note> in this world. In this way, like a curse, He fastens them to the Cross of Christ through these children of His Wrath. Through such a revelation, these sins are drowned within him in the blood and death of Christ. This happens because he remains still before God, just as Christ did before His Father, and allows himself to be accused of the sins he did not commit but only inherited. Thus, they are taken from him and given over to the Wrath of God in His judgment, so that the Wrath may judge them.

52. For in such a figure <note>A "figure" or "type" is a person or event in the Old Testament seen as prefiguring something in the New Testament.</note>, Joseph also reconciled his righteous wrath against his brothers. They were all guilty toward him, yet he did not demand their debt. Instead, he only accused them regarding the Cup; for he had already forgiven them all their debt. Only regarding the Cup would he not hold them guiltless, even though by legal right they were not guilty of it; rather, he had placed it among their gifts and thus made them "guilty" of it.

53. In the same way, God has also given us His grace out of pure love. Since we were already guilty of eternal judgment, He nonetheless placed Christ—along with grace, His suffering and death, and His **Cross-Cup**—into our sack of life. He does not hold us guiltless regarding this Cup; we are all together "guilty" of it, and we do not possess this Cup by natural right, but it has been placed within us.

### Chapter 72. How Joseph revealed himself to his brothers.

...Pharaoh’s household heard it; and he spoke to his brothers: "I am Joseph; does my Father still live?" and his brothers could not answer him, so terrified were they in his presence.

->The inner Meaning <note>original: "Figure"; here referring to the spiritual "type" or symbolic foreshadowing</note> is as follows.<-

2. God gave the law to Israel and commanded them to return home to **Paradise** through it, just as the **Figure** (with the Promised Land, which they were to enter, yet for a long time could not, until Joshua led them in) stood there; this being an example of the true entry through Jesus. Under the law, they also had the Paradisiacal Covenant of Grace, as well as the Prophets, who guided them to God’s mercy.

3. Yet they could not come to rest in their first **Adamic Paradisiacal Fatherland** <note>the original state of humanity before the Fall</note> through any of these; God’s righteousness accused them without ceasing and demanded the capability and power to keep the law and the Covenant in full obedience.

4. But when it could not be that either the law or the Covenant could lead them in, the heavenly Joseph revealed himself out of the Covenant; for he could no longer restrain himself because of man’s misery. He brought his great mercy through the Covenant into the law, which mercy is indicated by Joseph's great weeping; where he could no longer restrain himself before his brothers and wept so that the Egyptians and Pharaoh's household heard it. This signifies that this weeping—being the mercy of God through Christ—would also be heard and received by the Egyptians, that is, all the **heathens** <note>original: "heydenen"; non-Jewish nations or Gentiles</note> and the peoples. This indeed happened: the weeping and mercy of Christ resounded among all nations, so that they all took it into their hearts and turned to this Joseph, who accepted them all and fulfilled the law along with the Covenant.

5. But Joseph crying out, "Let every man go out from me," when he made himself known to his brothers so that no man should stand by him—this indicates that when Jesus Christ, being the highest mercy of God, revealed himself out of the Covenant, then the law with all its ceremonies, as well as the Covenant, had to cease and pass away. Also, all of man’s ability and power, as well as all willing, walking, and running, had to depart.

6. For out of the Covenant and out of the law stepped forth the one who fulfilled the Covenant and the law. He placed himself in the stead of the Covenant and the law, between and within God and man, in the middle; being a God-man and man-God, who alone should lead **Adam** into **Paradise** and destroy sin. There, no one was to be with him; he alone willed and would reveal himself to humanity as a light (John 8 <note>original: "Joh. 8"; referencing Jesus as the Light of the World</note>) and as a new life.

8. No hypocrisy or human comfort with which one flatters <note>original: "kittelt"; literally "tickles"</note> oneself has any value before this face of Joseph. 9. The entire creaturely life must be yielded and forsaken of its own will, so that the creaturely will may be taken up again and purified. Then, God's will and man’s will become a single will. At that point, God is all in all in him, according to the inward and outward world—in each world according to its own property. That is to say: according to the eternally speaking word in the soul, and according to the **animal soul** <note>original: "animaalische ziele"; the lower or natural life-force</note> in the **spirit of the world** <note>original: "spiritus mundi"</note>, in everything acting as an instrument of God.

10. When this now occurs, the Heavenly Joseph speaks in his mercy: "I am Jesus, in you," and opens the inward eye so that the person recognizes him in a moment. He speaks friendly into the soul and says: "Does my Father still live?" That is: does the Father’s nature still live in the soul? Is there still a breath of the **Divine Life** within her?

11. Before this revelation, the **self-will** <note>original: "eygen wil"</note> of the soul is terrified, so that in its own power it can no longer say a word or speak in its **selfhood**. For in this terror, the self-centeredness of the will perishes; with this inward glance, the will of God rises up and kills the self-will of the soul. Just as Joseph’s brothers were so terrified before his face that they could not speak another word—all their power left them and they became as if struck dumb—so too shall the godless be struck dumb in the Last Judgment before the face of God. They shall be terrified unto eternal death, so that their life shall be a single agony and terror of the **evil conscience** <note>original: "quaade Conscientie"</note> which shall gnaw at them eternally.

12. But Joseph spoke to his brothers: "Come forward to me," and they stepped toward him, and he spoke: "I am Joseph your brother, whom you sold into Egypt. Now do not be distressed, and do not think that I am angry for that reason, that you sold me here; for for the sake of your lives, God has sent me ahead of you."

# How Joseph revealed himself to his brothers. Chap. 72

...jamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of garments, and to his father he sent along ten donkeys laden with goods from Egypt, and ten she-donkeys with grain, bread, and food for his father on the way; thus he let his brothers depart from him, and they went their way; and he spoke to them: do not quarrel on the way.

->The Figure is as follows.<-

27. Christ takes the provision, as well as the wagons—being the **Holy Spirit**—from the Father, which he sends to his children, just as Joseph took the wagons and gifts from Pharaoh; and he gives them food on the path of their **pilgrimage** <note>The spiritual journey of the soul through life toward God</note>, namely his Body and Blood for food and drink.

28. The change of garment that Joseph gave to each brother indicates the **Temple of Christ** <note>In mystical thought, this is the inner sanctuary of the soul where God’s presence dwells</note>, in which the soul keeps Sabbath and rests. And the five changes of garments Joseph gave to his brother Benjamin are the **five wounds of Christ** <note>The wounds in Christ’s hands, feet, and side, which the author views as spiritual places of refuge</note>, wherein the inward man rests in the love of God. But the 300 pieces of silver he gave to Benjamin are the gifts of the Word, from this great love, with which this Benjamin must trade and act, and win much for his Lord and brother, the **Heavenly Joseph** <note>A symbolic name for Jesus Christ throughout this text</note>; for one trades with money; likewise must the inward Benjamin act with his gifts of 300 pieces of silver—that is, with the gifts of Christ—which is to say, to teach and to proclaim God’s wonders; for he is Christ’s servant and fellow-helper, indeed his true brother.

29. The ten donkeys laden with goods from the land of Egypt, which Joseph sent to his father, indicate in the **Figure** <note>A prophetic symbol or type</note> the **Ten Commandments** in the nature of the law, which Joseph had laden with goods—that is, Christ had laden them with his grace—and sends them to God’s justice in the **Conscience**, where the poor nature now has food.

30. But the ten she-donkeys with grain indicate the ten forms of the **soul-like and natural fire-life** <note>A term referring to the fundamental energies and qualities of the human soul's existence, likely influenced by the philosophy of Jacob Böhme</note>, upon which Christ loads the food for the soul when it stands in his **Process** <note>The "Process of Christ" is the transformative spiritual journey of dying to the old self and being reborn</note>: the bread and the food for the way indicate the Word of God, from which the poor **Old Adam** <note>The fallen, sinful human nature</note> must eat so that he may live.

31. This Christ gives to his children and brothers on the path of their pilgrimage, when they walk home again in the process of Christ, so that they have food, and that nature—being the **old Father** <note>Referring to Jacob, representing the natural human life sustained by grace</note>—may eat; and he commanded them that they should not quarrel with one another on the way, but travel home to Paradise in love and peace.

32. O Israel! where is your peace today? It seems as if you have consumed all of Joseph’s provisions and must now suffer want, since you quarrel over this "honor of Joseph," and because of it have incited such murders; truly you have murdered your brother **Benjamin** <note>Here representing the inward, spiritual man or the spirit of love</note> along the way, therefore you stand in strife.

<summary>This page provides a mystical interpretation of the gifts Joseph sent to his family, equating the silver and garments with the spiritual gifts and wounds of Christ. The author uses these biblical elements to critique contemporary religious strife, urging a return to the "inward Benjamin" of peace and love.</summary>

37. Otherwise, if we were to teach so powerfully, we would also have to live as poorly as the Apostles of Christ and leave the world; it is not necessary, the Kingdom of Christ must now stand in prestige, in pomp, and in glory.

3. ...in the word of his speaking; which is the book of life, in which the names of the children of God are included, or written.

4. And when this person finds the same in power, he speaks back into the Word: "Here I am, Lord, make of me what you will, I stand before you." And that same internal Word of God speaks in power: "I am God, the God of your father." That is, it gives to the person in this speaking power a divine recognition <note>original: "Goddelijke erkentenis"</note>, which teaches the person to understand that God is working within him, and what God is.

5. But since the body is a dark valley, and moreover has a perverted inclination, the Word speaks into the poor soul: "Fear not when you go into *Egypt*, namely into repentance <note>original: "boete"</note>, and go out from the land of *Canaan*, that is out of the world's pleasure, falsehood, and unrighteousness." Even if they shall be hostile to you and persecute you, fear not; "I will travel with you into *Egypt*, that is into your conversion and divine obedience; I will help you work repentance, and bless you in your *Egypt*, that is in your work of repentance, and make your new birth into a great tree, which shall bring forth good fruits in the Kingdom of God." Just as he said to *Jacob*: "I will make you into a great nation in *Egypt*, and will also bring you out of there again." This means you shall not remain like one dead or separated from this world, even though you move into *Egypt* in repentance and leave the world in your mind, I will nonetheless draw you back out of the distress and sadness, and let you remain in your worldly station <note>The author argues that a spiritual life does not require abandoning one's social or professional position, only one's attachment to sin</note>, provided that station is righteous, which happens as follows.

6. When a person travels into this *Egypt*, he must leave his land—that is, all his temporal lusts of the flesh—and surrender them to God, keeping nothing more for himself, but thinking that it is not his own, that he is merely a servant of it, so that he may serve God and his fellow members therein. He should direct his heart like a traveling pilgrim who is at home nowhere in this world; he must, with *Jacob*, seat himself upon *Joseph’s*—that is, the *Holy Spirit’s* <note>original: "H: Geeſtes"</note>—wagon, wherever the Spirit desires to lead him. In this time of scarcity <note>original: "dieren tyd" — literally an "expensive time," referring to the famine in the biblical narrative</note>, God moves in and with him, and blesses him, so that he produces much divine fruit, and his name becomes very great in God's Word.

7. But for this reason God does not thrust him out of temporal possession; He leads his spirit back out from there into the activity of the work of his hands—that is, into his worldly station—so that he may serve the wonders of God, as well as himself and the members of his body—that is, his neighbor. Nothing is taken from him except unrighteousness and untruth. God now makes him, in his station, into His servant; he may well keep his cattle, his belongings, and goods, and take them with him for his necessity, just as *Jacob* did, but the false must be cast away.

# How Jacob traveled with all his children Chapter 73.

8. And when he does this, then God says: *Joseph shall lay his hand upon your eyes, that you may see*; that is, Christ shall reach with his hand of grace into your sight—which is blind to God—and lay his hand from the Divine Sun upon your eyes; thus you shall come into a state of divine contemplation <note>original: "Goddelijke beſchouwelijkheid"</note> and recognition within yourself, such that your intellect shall marvel at where such light and deep knowledge comes from.

9. Jacob came into Egypt with seventy souls, with all his children and grandchildren, of which sixty-six had come from his loins and traveled with him; for Joseph had fathered two sons in Egypt.

10. This number of sixty-six is a number of great mystery <note>original: "verborgentheid"</note>, as is also the number seventy, which is a number of the Great Babel; the number sixty-six is the number of the beast, and of the harlot <note>A reference to the Book of Revelation (13:18 and 17:5), symbolizing worldly corruption and false religious systems</note>, from which Israel and every child of God must depart.

11. This exodus of Israel is a true figure and image of the final exodus of the people of Israel—namely, of the right, true Christians—who shall also depart out of this Canaan, that is out of Babel, at the fulfillment of the number of the beast and the harlot; which signature star <term>signature star: "signaat ſterre," a concept in Boehme's philosophy suggesting an outward sign of an inner spiritual reality or a prophetic astrological marker</term> has already appeared with the wagon of Joseph.

12. For the great animalistic state <note>original: "dierte"</note> of Jacob’s time—namely, the great famine for heavenly food—is now at hand; and not only a hunger of the soul for heavenly bread, but also a very great, violent impression toward the desire for "self-interest" <note>original: "eygenheyd," the state of being focused on the self rather than God</note>, which is toward greed, usury, and pride, the likes of which have never been heard of since the beginning of the world.

13. The hunger within the wrath of God <note>original: "grimmigheid Gods"</note> for vanity, to devour the same, is so great that it currently compresses the powers of heaven, so that all provision and blessing are scattered; and the mind of man is so hungry for vanity that there is no rest at all on earth because of this desire.

14. The third principle <term>third principle: in this mystical system, the "spirit of the world" (spiritus mundi) composed of the four elements</term>, being the spirit of the world <note>original: "ſpiritus mundi"</note> of the four elements, is likewise compressed, from which all blessing is scattered, and in its place an insatiable, hungry greed has arisen; so that the beast and the harlot, together with their worshippers, are so hungry for pride, greed, envy, anger, unchastity, whoredom, and animalistic lust—and so tightly compressed in such desire—that the time is here for this beast, along with the harlot, to burst.

15. And it is then that Jacob’s spirit becomes living, and believes that Joseph is a prince in the land of Egypt; that in the conversion, there Joseph shall be revealed to his brothers. Then they must be ashamed because of their falsehood, that they suppressed Joseph and sold him into misery with lies.

### Chapter 73. The Journey to Egypt.

16. For all Israel and Egypt shall behold Joseph’s face in truth, for Israel must depart from Canaan and leave Babel at the number seventy; but the "Hunger of Babel" <note>This refers to the spiritual void or greed of the worldly system</note> says, "I first want to fill my own sack for myself, so that I may have food for the road." It does not know that Joseph has already given Israel food, as well as wagons and clothing, and that they should only take their cattle and leave their old dwellings and provisions behind.

17. The food which Israel currently gathers in Babel belongs entirely to the grim impression of God’s Wrath <note>original: "grimmige impressie van den Toorn Gods." In this mystical tradition, "impression" refers to the way spiritual forces contract or harden into material reality</note>; the Wrath shall devour it all when His fire burns. God has already, through Joseph, sent food ahead to His children; they shall have enough, provided they do not doubt on this path. Changeable garments are prepared for them there, so that they may rest from the unrest of the driver.

18. But Babel thinks: "It is still far off; Israel must serve me, I will plague her even more." But the Deluge, and the fire of Sodom, overtakes her suddenly so that there is no rescue. Whoever is awake, let them be alert, so that they do not fall asleep; for the Bridegroom passes by. The foolish virgins want to prepare their lamps afterward, but it is too late; the Hunger of Babel seizes them and devours them in its jaws.

19. Moses says further: *And he sent Judah before him to Joseph, to point the way to Goshen; and they came into the land of Goshen. Then Joseph harnessed his chariot and went up to meet his father Israel, to Goshen; and when he saw him, he fell on his neck and wept on his neck for a long time. Then Israel said to Joseph: "Now let me die, since I have seen your face, that you still live."*

->This symbolic figure is interpreted as follows:<-

20. Judah signifies the engrafted covenant of God in man, being the Divine grace in Christ; this sends Israel—that is, the whole man—on ahead to the Heavenly Joseph and unites itself with him. Thus the Heavenly Joseph leads the kingdom of Nature in man—being the old Jacob and Adam—into Goshen; that is, onto the path of repentance, into the rest of Christ, so that he arrives at the right goal. There he finds food for the hungry conscience, being the right way to salvation where true teaching and instruction are found; there Goshen is at hand, where the soul sits in plenty and grazes in the lush pasture of Christ.

21. And when the Heavenly Joseph, Christ, sees this—that the Old Jacob, that is the Adamish man, has sent his Judah to Him and follows behind—then He harnesses His wagon; that is, His workings with a powerful counter-movement <note>original: "tegen-togt"</note>, and travels to meet the Natural man; and when they [come] together

21. [...] coming, this Joseph, this Jacob-Adam, falls around his neck; that is, he seizes his [...] desire and longing, and fills it with his tears, which he had shed in his Suffering [...] and introduced into eternal joy in his victory through death.

22. With these tears of joy, he ignites the soul of the Old Jacob-Adam, so that Jacob, out of great joy, weeps long on Joseph’s neck—that is, in the joy of the tears of Christ—and mingles his inward joy with the tears of Christ. By these tears of joy, the Old Jacob-Adam is powerfully comforted, and refreshed and strengthened within himself; he finds that his heavenly Joseph still lives in him, that he has not died in the expensive time <note>original: "dieren tyd," referring to a period of famine or scarcity</note> of sin, nor has he entirely departed from him.

23. Then the natural man speaks: "Now I wish to die, and surrender all my rights and will, because I have recognized and seen my beloved son Joseph." That is: because I find that the New Man in Christ has become manifest in me, I now wish to die to my will of vanity and enter the power of His Love, just as Jacob said to Joseph.

24. Joseph spoke to his brothers and his father’s house: "I will go up and tell Pharaoh; my brothers and my father’s house have come to me from the land of Canaan. They are shepherds, for they are people who deal with livestock; they have brought their small and large cattle and everything they have. Now, when Pharaoh calls you and asks, 'What is your occupation?' you shall say: 'Your servants are people who deal with livestock from our youth until now, both we and our fathers,' so that you may dwell in the land of Goshen; for shepherds are an abomination to the Egyptians."

->The internal Figure stands as follows.<-

25. When the Heavenly Joseph, Christ, has revealed himself to the soul and the Adam-man <note>The "Adam-man" refers to the human nature inherited from Adam, which must be redeemed by Christ</note>, and they have come together and received and accepted one another, then that same powerful Word—the Spirit of Christ which has revealed itself in man—presses back into the property of the Eternal Father. This is the eternal "speaking" of the Father, who is called Pharaoh here; [it means] "I shall tell Pharaoh that my brothers, with my father’s whole house, have come to me."

26. For Pharaoh stands here as a Figure of God the Father, who is the Eternal King. Christ himself announces the word of love and grace: that his brothers—which are the properties of human life—have come to him with all their strength. That is, the Word of Christ, which came from the Father into our humanity, speaks through its power into the natural human word of life, into the eternal word of the Father, which is here called "telling the King."

### Ch. 73. Having Journeyed to Egypt. 303

27. For Christ is also the Father’s steward over humanity, just as Joseph was over Pharaoh; for in this way, the human being is made manifest in God once more, when Christ speaks into him through the Father’s word and makes it known to him. Otherwise, the human would not be able to reach God; for human life also came forth from the word of God the Father, because the Spirit of God spoke through and out of the Father’s word into the human <note>Referring to John 1: "In the beginning was the Word."</note>.

28. But after human life entered into a creaturely state and became natural, it turned away from the "Love-speaking" <note>The author's term for God's creative expression of love</note> of God and revealed itself in the "Wrath-speaking." The power of the Love-speaking was extinguished within it, this being the second *principle* <note>original Latin: "principium"; in this mystical context, it refers to the second of three foundational realms of existence, specifically the realm of light and divine love</note>, the holy birth or the working of divine powers. By its own power and might, the soul was unable to re-enter that Love-speaking so that it might speak or bring forth divine love-power again. It had broken itself off from the love of God and had entered into a natural speaking of selfhood and vanity.

29. God grieved for this and reintroduced His Love-speaking Word back into the creaturely, "imaged" word of souls and humanity. This [Word] is now this Joseph, whom God has sent ahead so that he might lead or speak the human life back into the eternal Speaking Word, and therein make it manifest before the eternal King. He introduces the human word into the Father’s own property, into the Word of God, and reconciles the fallen human word—which was in the Father’s "Wrath-speaking"—with His love. That is, He transforms the wrath in the word of human life into His tears of love, into the Divine Kingdom of joys, and reveals human life effectively in God. This is what is meant here when Joseph said:
> I shall say to Pharaoh: my brothers and my father’s whole house have come to me from the land of Canaan.

30. For Christ has become our Brother; the Word of love became human and dwells in us. He took Adam’s nature upon Himself, which is why in this figure <note>A "figure" is a symbolic representation or prophetic "shadow" of a later truth</note> He calls it His father’s house—that is, the first Adam—and He calls Adam's children His brothers. Thus the Spirit of Moses speaks quite secretly in the figure of Christ; otherwise, in this place, he would have likely said (if there were not another figure hidden beneath it): "My father has come to me."

31. He said: "from the land of Canaan," and that they are "shepherds." Thus he wished to tell Pharaoh so that they might dwell in the land of Goshen. In this figure, it signifies this: Christ points out, in the Word of His Father through His Love-speaking, that His brothers have come to Him out of the vanity of the Canaanites, out of the wild, animal-like property. He shows that from their youth onward—from the time of Adam—they have been nothing other than livestock-herders; that is, the human...

43. O World in your high stations, if only you would consider what you are in your stations before Heaven; and that you would not set your stations so high in the love of God, for they stand only in His wonders, in both evil and good.

44. Whenever God has wanted to represent a worldly station within His love, He has placed shepherds therein, or else lowly, poor, despised, and insignificant people; look at Abel, Seth, Enos, Noah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, Moses, David, likewise the Prophets, and Apostles, and all the saints through whom God has ever revealed Himself. 3. For these are the ones who shall be God’s servants in love. Christ gives counsel to these, saying: "When you come before the face of God, so that the Spirit of God proves and examines you as to what your office and work before God is, then humble yourselves and say before God: 'Your servants are nothing but shepherds, and we have come to you in the animal-like <term>dieren tyd: the state of man fallen into a bestial or purely biological existence</term> time of misery, in our great hunger, to dwell with you in the Land of God. He also frequently withdraws from them the food of grace, and lets them hunger and lament, and lets them sit in misery, and plagues them, so that they must work for him in the Divine labor in anguish, in lamentation, fear, and trembling; for the **Old Adam's Donkey** <note>The "Old Adam" refers to the fallen human nature; Böhme often calls the physical body or the stubborn ego a "donkey" that must be disciplined.</note> does not willingly go to the Divine work.

41. Therefore he is often forced, so that punishment and threat are constantly behind him, so that the spirit of Christ threatens him with hell and with the **Wrath of God** in the **Conscience** <term>Conscientie: the internal moral sense where the spiritual struggle between grace and wrath takes place</term>, just as the earthly Lords on earth also do with their subjects; who indeed stand in the Figure of Christ, but the Office is unequal.

42. Christ gathers, through the work of his children, many **Heavenly fruits** for his Father, which man shall receive back again and enjoy the same eternally; but a worldly Lord gathers, for his own honor, nothing other than money and goods in his chests, through the labor and sweat of the poor, which labor—

46. 47. 49. ...he who does that without murmuring in faithfulness, also serves his Lord Christ; for through this, God draws him away from this world, so that he places his hope in the future, and in this servitude of the hands, he gathers for himself in this **House of Sorrows** <note>original: *Huys des jammers*, a term describing the physical world or the state of suffering in mortal life</note>, with his prayer, his **Heavenly Treasure**, so that if he were in the pleasure of the flesh during this time of oppression, he would gather nothing good: therefore, for those who love God, all things must work for the best.

50. Thus one must understand the **Figure** <note>original: *Figure*, referring to a spiritual archetype or symbolic "type" prefigured in history</note> beneath the history of Joseph, although the history is described with great diligence, according to the internal **Figure**, through the inspiration of the Spirit of God, which always points more to the kingdom of Christ than to a history of a mere event.

51. For the Biblical histories are not there only to see the lives and deeds of the ancient Saints, as **Babel** <note>A term often used by mystical writers to describe the institutionalized, "confused" church that interprets scripture only literally</note> believes; no, the kingdom of Christ is depicted everywhere therein, as is the kingdom of hell: the visible **Figure** points continually to the invisible; which shall be revealed in the spiritual man.

52. 53. When the time drew near that Israel should die, he called his son Joseph and spoke to him, *if I have found grace in your sight, then lay your hand under my thigh that you may show love and faithfulness to me, and do not bury me in Egypt; but I will lie with my fathers, and you shall carry me out of the Land of Egypt, and bury me in their burial place*; he spoke, *I will do as you have said*, but he said, *then swear to me*, and he swore to him, then Israel bowed himself upon the bed's head.

54. This is now a completely secret **Figure**, and points to the **Resurrection of the Dead**, where the soul shall return to the body, and the body shall be pure and holy; for the Land of Canaan, which was also full of heathen abominations, points to the earthly **Body**, and Egypt where Pharaoh dwells and Joseph is the steward, points to the **Soul**, which dwells in God’s word, that is, with the eternal King.

55. And we see in this **Figure** very finely depicted, how the soul of Adam turned itself with desire toward the earthly Canaan of the earthly **Body**, and turned away from God; therefore the soul had to return to Egypt, in **Penance**, to Joseph, that is to Christ, and to King Pharaoh, that is to God; and there it is accepted as a child of grace as His own, so that it should want to obey God and be His servant and minister, and it must leave the earthly Canaan, being the evil **Body**, with its will and works, just as Israel had to leave Canaan.

### Chapter 74. With the five youngest Brothers of Joseph.

56. But when he was to die, he desired to have his body in the Land of Canaan, so that it should be buried there; this shows that the earthly body must be buried in its mother, the earth, and return again into its first mother. This further shows that the soul should come to its rest from Egypt—that is, from the servitude of the torment of **penance** <note>original: *boete*, referring to the process of repentance and spiritual refinement</note>—back to the body. For just as the heathens had to be driven out of Canaan when Israel moved back into it, so also must the abominations in the **inherent nature** <note>original: *eygenſchap*, a term in mystical theology for the specific qualities or "properties" that make up a person's character</note> of the body be consumed, and all false desires be killed, before the soul comes back to the body to dwell within it.

57. And it is powerfully depicted how the will of the soul, in this time, shall and must break away from the earthly Canaan—that is, from the lust of the body—and through earnest penance press back toward God. There, the soul must rightly be in Egypt like a poor, bond-servant, in much anxiety and torment; but at the end, when the body must die, the soul also wishes to leave the house of servitude—that is, the pain of penance—and desires to return to the first, pure **Adamic image** <note>The state of perfection and innocence held by Adam before the Fall</note> that God created. Just as Jacob wished to lie with his fathers, though he could just as well have lain in Egypt, his spirit stood in the **Figure** of the **restoration** <note>original: *wederbrenging*, the theological concept of all things being returned to their original divine order</note>; showing how the whole man should go back into the first image that was created by God.

58. Jacob demanded this oath from Joseph, who is the **Figure of Christ** <note>original: *Figure Chriſti*; the author views Joseph's life as a symbolic precursor to the life and work of Jesus</note>, and desired that he should lay his hand under his thigh and swear.

59. This is now the **Figure** of how **Christ** would lay His hand—that is, His power and might, being the eternal Word which is the hand that made all things—into man’s **essence** <note>original: *Effents*, likely a variant of "Essence," referring to the fundamental spiritual substance of a person</note> in body and soul. He would lay it not only therein, but also under the thigh—that is, under the power of man—and give Himself to man as a possession. Therein He would swear—that is, bind Himself—so that when man has died here to temporal death, He would lead the whole man back into the first land of inheritance where Adam dwelt in his innocence, which is **Paradise**; and bury the body and soul, by His oath, in God—that is, in the Divine rest.

60. This is what the **Figure** of Jacob points to; where the text says: **Israel** had lived a long time in Egypt and multiplied there; and when Jacob was to die, he wished to be with his fathers in the Land of Canaan after his death. ### Chapter 75. And how he placed the youngest before the eldest.

<meta>catchword: 6. And</meta>

...when he had finished his course in this world, with the **Figure** <note>original: *Figure*; a symbolic event where history mirrors a deeper spiritual reality</note> of the *Kingdom of Christ* and of His *Christendom*, his spirit once again imagined itself within the sign of the covenant. Through this sign of the covenant, he blessed his children and grandchildren and prophesied regarding the time to come; that is, he speaks from the root and points toward the branches and shoots of this tree, which God had replanted in *Paradise* after the fall and made manifest through *Abraham*. *Jacob* stood in that same trunk and pointed, through the Spirit of this tree, toward its branches and shoots, especially with the two sons of *Joseph*, both of whom he placed back into his own root, so that they should be his sons just as *Reuben* and *Simeon* were.

->This **Figure** stands as follows:<-

3. *Jacob* spoke to *Joseph*: "Almighty God appeared to me at *Luz* in the land of *Canaan* and blessed me, and spoke to me: 'Behold, I will make you grow and multiply, and will make of you a multitude of people, and will give this land to your seed after you for an inheritance forever.'" In this **Figure**, the Spirit speaks not only of the inheritance of the outward land of *Canaan*, but also of the inheritance of the *Kingdom of Christ* to be understood beneath this *Canaan*. For he says: God has given this land to him and his children as an eternal possession, which they have now for a long time neither inhabited nor held as an inheritance; therefore, in this **Figure**, the kingdom of *Christ* is understood, which shall last eternally.

4. So *Jacob* now took the two sons of *Joseph* and placed them into his root, into the inheritance of this Kingdom, and moreover into his first strength, just like *Reuben* and *Simeon* his first sons. This indicates how *Joseph’s* children—that is, the children of *Christ* in faith and in the Spirit, whose nature nonetheless came from the corrupt *Seed of Adam*—would be grafted back into the first root of the Covenant of God through faith. For *Adam* placed his branches and children with himself into the Kingdom of the **Wrath of God** <note>original: *Toorn Gods*; the harsh, punishing aspect of nature that the soul must transcend</note>, but the Covenant and grace take these *Adamic* branches and set them back into the image of God, which *Jacob* represents here through the sons of *Joseph*.

5. And *Israel* saw the sons of *Joseph* and spoke: "Whose are these?" *Joseph* answered his father: "They are my sons, whom God has given me." That is, the Covenant of Grace was a stranger to the corrupted nature and spoke: "Whose are these children of Nature in their **selfhood**?" <note>original: *selfsheid*; the ego-driven state of being separated from God</note> for they have broken themselves off from God. But *Joseph*, in the figure of the humanity of *Christ*, spoke: "They are my children, whom God has given me in the kingdom of this world," and the Covenant of Grace in *Jacob* spoke: "Bring them here to me, that I may bless them"—that is, that I may anoint them with grace. Understand that *Christ* would lead them to God so that He might bless them once again.

# How Jacob blessed the two Sons of Joseph, Chapter 48

6. And Moses says further; for the eyes of Israel had become dim with age—that is, the Nature in the property of the Father, of the **soulish creature** <note>original: *sieliſche Creatuer*; referring to the natural, psychological part of man as opposed to the purely spiritual</note>, was darkened and aged. This occurred because the **Ens** <term>Ens: a Latin term used here to mean the "essential spiritual substance" or "inner being"</term> of the souls had formed itself within time; for everything that lives in time grows old and darkens. But the covenant in Jacob does not grow old; the covenant wished to bless the sons of Joseph with the coming revelation of power in the name of **Jesus**. And Joseph, who stood in the image of the humanity of **Christ**, was to lead them to this blessing; for the humanity of **Christ** leads the children of Adam to the blessing of God, just as Joseph here leads his sons to the covenant of God in Jacob.

7. Moses says further; and he kissed and embraced them, and spoke to Joseph: "Behold, I have seen your face, which I had not thought [to see], and behold, God has let me see your seed." And Joseph took them from his lap, and bowed himself to the earth upon his face. This signifies the following in the **figure** <note>original: *figure*; a prophetic or symbolic pattern</note>: when Joseph, in the image of the humanity of **Christ**, brought his sons to his Father—that is, before the covenant of God—the covenant took them into its arms, or upon the lap of its desire, namely into God’s essence, and kissed them with the kiss of love which God wished to reveal in **Christ**. And the justice of the Father, in the word of power, spoke to the essence of the souls: "Behold, you were darkened to me, and now through the love and grace of God I have seen your face again, which I had not thought [possible]." For I thought to keep the soul in the severe power of the wrath of God, because the eye of God had turned away and departed from it; thus it was separated from God in the justice of God. But now I have seen the face of the soul again through God’s love in the grace of God, and behold, the love of God has let me see the seed of this covenant of grace.

8. And the spirit of Moses says further; and Joseph took them from his lap, and bowed to the earth before his face. That is: when the Word became man, **Christ** took the soul from the lap of the Father—that is, out of the Father’s Nature into Himself—and stepped into a creaturely nature with the assumed humanity before God the Father. And He bowed—that is, humbled Himself—with the assumed soul, being God and man in one single person, to the earth—that is, unto death. And He stepped before God’s face with our assumed soul; that is, He led the will of the soul, through the introduced power of the **Godhead** <note>original: *Godheid*</note>, back again into a yielded humility before the eye of God.

# How Jacob Blessed the Two Sons of Joseph, Ch. 75

...God's will be done in my **innermost ground** <note>term: "innermost ground" (inwendigsten grond) refers to the center of the soul where man meets God</note>; and not my **Adam-like will** <note>original: "Adamse- wil"—the fallen, selfish nature inherited from Adam</note> of the soul. It shall and must be resigned in God; the first natural right must follow behind, and Christ must lead the way, otherwise there is no salvation.

24. With this image, the Spirit of God "played" <note>The author uses "played" (speelde) to describe how God acts out spiritual truths through historical figures</note> among the children of the saints, showing how the new, engrafted kingdom of grace would exalt itself in the highest, and how the kingdom of nature would be placed behind. For when Christ arises and is born in man, then Adam must be a servant and a minister.

25. And it points out furthermore that the kingdom of nature would also be great, yet the kingdom of grace even greater. We have a parable of this in a large, many-branched tree, which through nature produces many shoots and branches, and nature is powerful within them; yet the power of the Sun is far more powerful therein. For if the Sun did not work alongside it, the tree could not grow nor bear fruit. We see clearly from this that the power of the Sun must exalt itself in the highest if the tree is to grow and its fruit is to ripen and be useful; so it is also in man.

26. Man is nature, and nature breeds him so that he comes into the form and shape of the creatures; yet the **understanding** <note>In this context, "understanding" (verstand) refers to the higher spiritual intellect or divine spark</note> must come forth in him, which governs and feeds nature. Nature indeed wants its own desires to be fulfilled, but the understanding holds dominion over nature.

27. But now, nature exists earlier than the understanding; nature goes first, but when the understanding arrives, nature must move to the back. So it is also in this **Figure** <note>term: "Figure" (Figure) is a person or event in the Bible that symbolizes a deeper spiritual reality</note>: Jacob and Joseph are to be understood as the new rebirth; that is, when the Divine understanding would again become manifest in men, then nature would follow behind.

28. Thus he blessed them that same day and spoke: "Whosoever blesses anyone in Israel, let them say; 'God make you like Ephraim and Manasseh.'" In this text, it is clear as the sun what the Spirit points to in this Figure. For Ephraim and Manasseh were placed back into the root of Jacob—that is, into the **Covenant of Grace** that God had revealed in him—and they were exchanged regarding the birthright of nature. Namely, the youngest was set before the firstborn. This must also be the blessing and the wish among the children of God: that God would set them back from the evil, Adam-like will of selfhood into the **Paradise Covenant**, and exchange them, bringing forth the kingdom of grace within them and placing it over the kingdom of nature of the first Adam-like birth. When such a thing happens in a person, then he is once again a child of God in Christ and stands within the blessing of God.

The propagation stood in a single image; just as God is a single being, so too was he [Adam] created out of that same "being of all beings" into an eternal image. For the spermatic Nature <note>The life-seed or creative essence</note> and kind was in him, the word "let it be" <note>original: "verbum fiat"</note> that had formed him into the image of God. In this image, he was the highest in the offering, and in the Kingdom; for he would have been able to offer to God, both Spiritually and Creaturely <note>In the manner of a created being</note>, just as the tree itself, without the help of another, bears its own fine branches and fruits; and casts out from itself the beautiful blossom in a lovely scent and power, with beautiful colors according to its kind; and just as God’s word has cast out and birthed him from itself; all this power also lay within him.

13. But the self-will wandered off thoughtlessly; and introduced itself into a beastly property, into false lust and desire, and climbed with beastly lust and desire into this Holy marriage-bed of God, into which lust Satan led him; being the ground of the dark world, according to the formation of the Fantasy <note>The "Phantasie" or false imagination that distorts divine reality</note>, as did the Devil with the presentation of the monstrous beastly property, and also the cunning and craftiness of the serpent, being the ground of the first principle <note>The first of the three "principles" in this philosophy, often associated with the dark, fiery root of existence</note>. Thus the self-will exalted itself therein, and was infected by it, and made his power of formation according to Soul and Body monstrous; from which the beastly imagination in Adam awoke and began.

14. Because of this, God’s Spirit—that is, the Holy word in this being of the World—withdrew from him; that is, the human self-will separated itself from the will of the word. At that moment, he became thoughtless in the Devil’s poison, and lost the Kingdom and Priesthood, being the Princely Throne, and became powerless and blind to God, and fell down into sleep, and lay in powerlessness between the Kingdom of God and the Kingdom of this World.

15. And Moses now says: *and God let him fall into a deep sleep, and made a woman from him, and brought her to him*, and gave him a beastly marriage-bed in place of a Heavenly one, in which he may now dally in his own lust.
