### How Jacob blessed all his sons Chapter 76

marriage-bed must perish and die, and Christ has entered into the midst of this marriage-bed as a redeemer of this monstrous image <note>original: "monstreuse beeld"; a term used in 17th-century mysticism to describe the distorted, beastly state of humanity after the Fall</note>, who wishes to give birth to it anew within himself.

16. The Spirit of God now also represents this powerful image through Reuben, who was Jacob's first strength; for the desire of Reuben also figured itself in this Adam-like image, and went hence and lay with his father’s concubine, playing the harlot with her in falsehood—just as the free will of the soul in Adam played the harlot with God’s concubine <note>A mystical reference to the "Sophia" or Divine Wisdom/Nature that was originally meant to be the soul's partner</note> in him with false lust, and became an adulterer against God, just as Reuben did.

17. And for this reason Adam—being the first strength of the natural man—has lost the Royal Priesthood in all men, so that the natural man in his own strength can no longer offer to God. He no longer understands anything of God’s word or Kingdom; it is foolishness to him, and he can no longer grasp it. For he stands in a poisonous, monstrous image that, in this Adam-like quality, cannot inherit the Kingdom of God and has lost the Kingdom of God; it is but a figure of this world and of Hell, a monster of the image of God. He shall no longer be the highest in the offering and the Kingdom, but Christ, in the new birth within him, has obtained the Kingdom in the offering and the government.

18. The Natural man, being the first strength, must become a servant and put off the monstrous harlot-image, and be born again: the soul through the Spirit of Christ, and the body through the *putrefaction* <term>putrefaction <note>The process of decay; in alchemy and mysticism, the necessary "rotting" of the old form so a new, purified life can emerge</note></term> of the earth, from which he shall be separated at the end of days and be formed again into the Image of God.

19. ### Chapter 76: He blessed before his end.

The Spirit has, at this same place as well as here, placed His figure <note>In this context, a "figure" refers to a symbolic representation or a prophetic type of a deeper spiritual reality.</note> beneath it, just as Jacob said how it would go with them after this time.

21. Through Reuben, the Spirit represents the Adam-like corrupted nature, showing how the first strength of man—the Priesthood and the Kingdom of God, being the Kingdom of Heaven—was squandered, and how the true marriage-bed of God was defiled and turned into a harlot’s bed. But in this figure, the Spirit of God now represents the powerful image of how that same first strength of man would still desire to keep its Priesthood and Dominion, and what sort of Priests and rulers they would be in this world, within the kingdom of their own nature.

22. For from the tribe of Levi came the Priesthood under the law, and the Spirit speaks of him here, and includes Simeon as well, who represents Worldly Dominion. He speaks of both as one, saying: "their swords are weapons of murder; let my soul not come into their counsel, and let my honor not be in their churches" <note>This is a mystical paraphrase of Genesis 49:5-6. The author uses "churches" where modern bibles often say "assembly."</note>. That is to say: the living word of God, which He calls His soul, would not be found in the dominion of this earthly world—that is, in the first natural strength of man. His holy word shall not be in their counsels, wherein they seek nothing but temporary lust and wealth; nor would it be in their churches and Priesthood, as they only practice hypocrisy with their mouths, for He says: "let my honor not be in their churches."

His church, however, is the true Image of God, originating from the essence of the Heavenly World. This image withered <note>original: "verblikte"; meaning to fade, wither, or lose luster</note> in Adam because of his murderousness—caused by the introduced poison of the serpent—and was born again in Christ. But because they wished to practice hypocrisy before God while remaining within the "monster of the serpent" <note>The "monstrous image" or "serpent-monster" refers to the distorted, beastly state of human nature after the Fall.</note>, and did not have God’s church within them, the Spirit said: "let my honor not be therein."

24. For God’s honor with Christ Jesus would not come out of the natural Adam, but out of God and His holy word. This same word would be the Holy Church of God within mankind, being the Image of the essence of the Heavenly World that died in Adam and turned green <note>i.e., flourished or came back to life</note> again in Christ. In this very image, God’s honor would appear, just as life could flourish through death. That was God’s honor; but this honor would not be held by the self-willed Adam, who became a murderer and murdered the heavenly image within himself; this honor would not appear in his murderous will.

25. In this image stands the figure clearly, which is depicted in the Apocalypse <note>original: "Apocalipsi"; the Book of Revelation</note> as the great seven-headed dragon and the Whore of Babylon riding upon it. There, the dragon and the Whore are also prefigured as one image, and it is exactly the same in this passage regarding Simeon and Levi. It points to the corrupted Adam-like strength in the monstrous image: the rule of nature in its own self-will, alongside the sectarian, hypocritical Priesthood.

# How Jacob [blessed] all his sons Chapter 7

26. The seven heads of the beast are the seven properties of nature <note>In the author's mystical system, these seven properties are the fundamental forces that create all reality, ranging from contraction and desire to light and sound.</note> from which the temperaments <note>Original: "temperature." This refers to the balance or "tuning" of the seven properties within a person.</note> have emerged; and the seven heads mean they have obtained a sevenfold will, through which life has fallen into conflict, misery, and sickness within the fragmentation. And the Harlot upon this beast is now the soul, which is defiled like a harlot and steps before God with this harlot-like image and behaves hypocritically toward Him.

27. But the will of the seven-headed beast gives its power to the Harlot—that is, the soul—so that the soul is filled with murder, pride, harlotry, and self-honor; and within this Church and murder, the honor of God does not wish to be.

28. This figure and magical indication regarding Simeon and Levi prefigure the spiritual and worldly dominion <note>The author is comparing the biblical brothers Simeon and Levi to the two great powers of human society: the State (Simeon) and the Church (Levi).</note>, both within every man himself, by which he governs himself—namely, in spiritual and natural things; and secondly, it also refers to the administration of spiritual and worldly offices—specifically in Church and State offices. Everything that rules therein through the self-centered Adam-like strength, outside of the new rebirth, carries this image within itself; it is the murder-sword with which people kill and damn one another with words.

29. All slanderous writings, where people blaspheme one another and kill with words for the sake of God-given gifts or knowledge, are these murder-swords of Simeon and Levi; likewise, all unjust judgments of the worldly courts are exactly these, and God’s honor and will are not in them.

30. For this reason, the Spirit takes them together under a single figure, because both these offices govern the Adam-like nature; they govern the world, which is the formed, spoken word of God <note>The author views the physical world as the "out-spoken" or manifested word of the Creator.</note>. To them is given the power of the kingdom of nature, but they shall give an account of this governance. For the judgment of God is placed in this figure, and in the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation.</note> the falsehood of this image is cast into the pool of fire that burns with sulfur; and it repays the beast along with the harlot for eternity, and gives the Kingdom and the power, including the Priesthood, to Christ and His children who are born from Him.

31. The Spirit of Moses says: "in their anger they murdered the Man, and in their wantonness they destroyed the Ox" <note>A reference to Genesis 49:6. In many early modern translations, "houghed an ox" was interpreted as destroying or hamstrung.</note>. The "Man" refers to the inner spiritual man, whom Adam murdered in all his children through his wrath (that is, through the first principle, being the Kingdom of God’s wrath, which Adam awakened in himself with the desire for lust), for he was the true image of God. It further points to the future of Christ, whom the Levites together with the Simeonites—being the worldly dominion, namely the Pharisees and the heathen rule—would kill; for Jacob said he would announce to them what would meet them in times to come.

32. Therefore, this figure also looks upon the Man, Christ, who was to come...

35. Especially in this present time, where men strive for nothing but the churches, and murder one another for that reason, and destroy land and people in their wantonness. For the curse breaks and scatters both their dominion and priesthood, along with their body, the outward senses, and the life; for before God it is nothing but a curse and vanity.

# How Jacob [Blessed] All His Sons, Chapter 76

26. The seven heads of the beast are the seven properties of nature which have proceeded from the **temperature** <term>balance: a term used by Böhme to describe the perfect harmony of nature’s qualities before the Fall</term>, and have acquired seven heads—that is, they have obtained a sevenfold will. Because of this, life has fallen into strife, misery, sickness, and destruction. The **Harlot** <note>A reference to the "Whore of Babylon" from the Book of Revelation, symbolizing the corrupted soul or a false church system.</note> upon this beast is now the soul, which is defiled like a harlot and stands before God with this harlot-image, acting hypocritically toward Him.

27. But the will of the seven-headed beast gives its power to the Harlot—that is, to the soul—so that the soul is filled with murder, pride, harlot-lust, and self-honor; and in this Church and murder, the honor of God will not be.

28. This Figure and magical indication in Simeon and Levi prefigure for us both the **Spiritual and Worldly Dominion**, existing within every human being themselves, by which they rule themselves—namely, in spiritual and natural things. Furthermore, it represents the administration of spiritual and worldly offices, specifically in Church and State offices. Everything that rules therein through the Adamic power, outside of the **new rebirth**, carries this image within itself, being the **murder-sword** with which people kill and damn one another with words.

29. All slanderous writings, in which people blaspheme and kill each other with words for the sake of divine gifts and knowledge, are these murder-swords of Simeon and Levi; likewise, all unjust judgments of worldly courts are the same, and God’s honor and will are not in them.

30. The Spirit groups them together under a single Figure for the very reason that both these offices rule the Adamic nature. They rule the world, which is the **formed, spoken word of God**; to them is given the power over the kingdom of nature, but they shall give an account of this reign. For God’s judgment is placed in this Figure, and in the **Apocalypse** <note>The Book of Revelation.</note>, the falsehood of this imagery is cast into the lake of fire that burns with sulfur, sealing the beast with the Harlot for eternity; and it gives the kingdom and the power, along with the priesthood, to Christ and His children who are born of Him.

31. The Spirit of Moses says: *In their anger they murdered the Man, and in their wantonness they ruined the Ox.* <note>Genesis 49:6.</note> The **Man** signifies the inner, spiritual man, whom Adam murdered in all his children through his wrath—that is, through the first **principium** <term>principle: in this context, the dark, fiery source of nature or the "wrath of God"</term>, which Adam awakened in himself through the desire of lust—this Man being the true Image of God. Furthermore, it points to the future coming of Christ, whom the Levites (along with the Simeonites, representing Worldly Dominion—namely, the Pharisees and the heathen authorities) would kill; for Jacob said he would proclaim to them what would befall them in times to come.

The Children of God must well note that the Spirit of God says in the Covenant: His soul would not be in their murderous counsel, nor His honor in their Churches; for the sake of these institutions, they murder and destroy many people who will not believe in their sects and wantonness.

35. This is especially true in this present time, where people fight for nothing but the Churches, and murder one another for that reason, destroying land and people in their wantonness. Before God, it is nothing but a curse and vanity.

# Chapter 76: How Jacob [Blessed] All His Sons

...is through the new growth; from the Covenant, the Adam-like tree shall be broken into pieces, and its works of body and senses shall be scattered, and the works of the devil shall be brought to nothing. Also, their priesthood and dominion shall be so disturbed, divided, and scattered, like chaff before the wind, when the kingdom of Christ with his priesthood shall arise. There Christ alone shall rule; then all of this itself—which Babel <note>original: "Babel"; a term used by the author to describe the confused state of worldly and institutionalized religion</note> looks upon as a stranger—comes to an end.

### IV. The Testament of Judah.

38. Judah, you are he; your brothers shall praise you; your hand shall be upon the neck of your enemies; your father’s children shall bow down before you. Judah is a young lion; you have come up high, my son, through great victory; he has knelt down and settled himself like a lion and like a lioness; who will rouse him? The scepter shall not be turned away from Judah, nor a teacher <note>original: "meester"; usually translated as "lawgiver" in biblical contexts, but here implying a master or instructor</note> from his feet, until the Hero <note>original: "held"; referring to the Messiah or Shiloh</note> comes, and the nations shall cling to him. He shall bind his foal to the vine, and the son of his donkey to the noble branches; he shall wash his garment in wine and his cloak in the blood of grapes; his eyes are redder than wine and his teeth whiter than milk.

39. In the first three sons of Jacob, the Spirit prophesies regarding the corrupted Adam and his children—how they stood before God and what their kingdom on earth would be. But here with Judah, he begins to prophesy of the Kingdom of Christ, namely of the Person and the office of Christ, and places Christ in the **fourth line**. This is a great mystery, for in the **fourth property** <term>fourth property: In the author's mystical system, this is the "Fire" or "Flash" where the dark, harsh nature of existence is transformed into the light of the spirit</term> of the birth of nature, the fire—that is, the origin of fire—is understood, from which the light takes its origin. Through this, the **Groundless Majesty** <term>ongrond Majesteyt: referring to the "Ungrund," the divine nothingness or absolute freedom that precedes all being</term> is revealed, in which the origin of Life is also understood; primarily, the soul is understood there according to its property.

40. Since this ground of the soul in Adam had fallen and was corrupted, God also placed His **Figure** <note>original: "Figure"; a symbolic or prophetic representation</note> with the new life within it. The Figure stands in this Testament of the twelve Patriarchs, showing how the beginning of Life is, and how the new birth buds forth again into the light through the corrupted fire-life. Also, all circumstances in the Testament of Judah are pointed out: how the new life in Christ would bud forth through the soul and rule over the sting of death.

41. Jacob said: "Judah, you are he; your brothers shall praise you." With this, he looks outwardly upon the Jewish Kingdom that would begin in future times, and inwardly he looks upon the Kingdom of Christ, which both Jews and heathens would receive, praising and honoring Christ as both God and man.

# Chapter 76: How Jacob Blessed [His Sons] Before His End.

42. And he says further; "for your hand shall be upon the neck of your enemies." By this, he does not mean the external enemies of the Jews, but how the hand—being the power of grace of Christ <note>original: "Christi"</note>—shall essentially <note>original: "essentialiter"; meaning through its actual being or substance</note> and effectively be upon the neck of Satan, the poison of the serpent, and the opposing will in flesh and blood; and how the "Lion" shall continually crush the head of the serpent in his children of faith.

43. Also, "your father’s children shall bow down before you." This means that before this Christ, from the tribe of Judah, all children of God shall incline themselves, bow, and worship him as a God-man and a man-God.

44. Also, "Judah is a young Lion." This signifies a roaring against the devil, a breaker of death and hell; like a wakeful, young, and fresh Lion that is strong in power.

45. Also, "you have come up high, my son, through great victory." This means that after he has triumphed over the Wrath of God, over death, sin, the devil, and hell, he has sat down as a man-God at the right hand of the power of God, and has [dominion] over all his enemies.

46. Also, "he has knelt down and settled himself like a lion and like a lioness; who will rouse him?" This means he has humbled himself so deeply with his highest love, and entered into the assumed humanity amidst the mockery and contempt of fallen man; he knelt down in the Wrath of God and allowed the natural human life to be broken, and with total patience committed his strong Lion-power into it.

47. But where the text says "like a lion and like a lioness," the "young lion" points to the Divine Word in the soul, and the "lioness" points to the name of Jesus in the most inward ground of the essence of the Heavenly world. This is the noble Lioness Sophia <note>In the mystical tradition, "Sophia" refers to Divine Wisdom, often viewed as the feminine mirror of God or the bride of the soul</note>, being the true seed of the woman of the Adamite <term>tincture of Light</term> <note>original: "tincture des Ligts"; in 17th-century mysticism, a "tincture" is a spiritual quality or life-force that gives color and character to existence</note>. This light faded in Adam, but in this Lion it became living again in the Divine power, and joined itself once more to the Lion—that is, to the soul.

48. Also, "who will rouse him [against him]?" This means, who can raise themselves against this Lion and the Heavenly Holy Lioness, who is God over and through all? Who will take the power from that which is the beginning of all power and might? Where is a hero who is able to fight where there is no higher power?

49. Also, "the scepter shall not be turned away from Judah, nor a master from his feet, until the Hero <note>original: "Held"; often used in this context to refer to the Messiah or Shiloh</note> comes, and the nations shall cling to him." But over no harlots, villains, greedy ones, usurers, unjust, unmerciful, nor proud ones—as long as they remain so—for they have nothing else around them but the Mantle of the Babylonian Harlot and do not receive this holy, washed Mantle of Christ over them. Hypocriticize as you will, you shall not obtain him unless you are first washed. Comforting words help you nothing; you must apply yourself with earnestness, so that your donkey-mare <note>Representing the animal nature of man that must be disciplined and transformed.</note> may live, and your foal be bound to the vine of Christ **in essence** <note>original: *essentialiter*; meaning the connection is not just symbolic but a literal merging of spiritual substances</note>; otherwise, you are a member of the Harlot upon the seven-headed dragon, and even if you could fly through the thrones, you would still be nothing but a child of the dragon.

62. O Babel, Babel! what have you done, that you have covered the thieves with this Mantle, while you yourself have remained nothing but a wolf beneath it.

63. Likewise, *his eyes are redder than wine, and his teeth whiter than m[ilk]*; his eyes are now the fire-flaming Love, which looks through the properties of the Father’s Wrath <note>A recurring concept in this theology where God’s "Wrath" is the raw, fiery power of existence that must be "tempered" or "enlightened" by the "Light" of the Son to become Love.</note> and through the fiery soul. Therein, the Father’s Wrath in the fiery soul has become a light-flaming fire of love; thus the **essence** <note>original: *Essents*</note> of the soul has thereby become a sweet-tasting, divine, red wine of love, where one quality in the soul’s essence tastes the other in great desire of love, and the quality of the Father’s Wrath wells up into a purely good taste.

64. And *his teeth are whiter than milk*; these white teeth are the desire of the inward spiritual man, through which the holy Word is present in the desire of these teeth. These white teeth of heavenly desire grasp, eat, and drink the body—the blood of the grapes of Christ—for this is the spiritual mouth, for which Christ has ordained his Testament <note>Referring to the Sacrament of the Eucharist or Holy Communion.</note>, so that the same should eat his flesh and drink his blood with these white teeth; the Spirit in the Covenant through Jacob shows this clearly and plainly.

65. For the Testament of Judah constantly refers to Christ, to his Person, Office, and Kingdom; for Christ would come out of Judah according to his humanity. Outwardly stands the figure of the example, and inwardly, in the spiritual figure, Christ stands clearly.

# THE 77th CHAPTER.

## *Further Explanation of the Testament of Jacob, concerning the other eight Sons, how both the Jewish Government or Kingdom on earth, and also Christendom thereunder is prefigured, and how it would go with her.*

->Genesis 49.<-

1. In the first three sons of Jacob, in the Figure <term>Figure: a symbolic representation or prophetic "type" that points to a deeper spiritual reality</term>, the Kingdom of the corrupt nature is prefigured, being the Adam-man <note>The "Adam-man" refers to humanity in its fallen state, inheriting the nature of Adam</note>; what the same is; and in Judah Christ is prefigured, who would come and bring the Adam-man into His Kingdom. But in the other eight sons of Jacob, the Figure of the worldly offices and states is now presented: how the Adam-man would conduct the supreme Government, and how also the inward Figure of the Kingdom of Christ would always stand alongside it.

2. For here it is first prefigured in the outward Figure where each tribe would have its dwelling, and what its office in Israel would be; yet alongside it stands constantly the Figure of how the outward and inward man would stand together, how the Kingdom of nature and the Kingdom of grace would dwell with one another, and how the seven properties of nature in the Wrath of God—according to the first *principium* <note>original: *principium*; the foundational source or "first principle" of existence</note>—would also develop themselves and introduce the Figure into the Divine contemplation. Let the reader pay heed to this, for we shall explain both the inward and the outward Figure.

->The Testament of Zebulun.<-

3. *Zebulun shall dwell at the haven of the sea, and at the haven of ships, and reach unto Sidon.* This is first the outward Figure: where this tribe would dwell in the Promised Land; yet the Spirit also has its inward Figure upon which it looks.

4. For Zebulun is named in the Language of Nature <term>Language of Nature: the mystical "Signatura Rerum," where the sounds of words reveal the true essence and character of the things named</term>, in the *Senfu* <note>original: *Senfu*; a mystical phonetic analysis used by the author to derive spiritual meaning from the sound of the name</note> a delight <note>original: *lust*; in this context, it refers to a holy longing or spiritual desire rather than carnal lust</note> which goes toward God, who dwells with the good. It indicates here how the Adam-man would dwell near God, and how he would have delight and refreshment from the Divine indwelling; for Jacob fathered Zebulun by Leah, who was otherwise unworthy, because she was tender-eyed and not so beautiful as

# Further explanation of the Testament of Jacob, Chapter 77

...Rachel was the one [who caused] Leah to turn her hope toward God, praying that He would bless her, so that she might become fruitful and bear children for her husband Jacob.

5. Now when she bore Zebulun, she said: God has remembered me, because I have turned my desire toward Him, and He has fulfilled the same for me; now let His will dwell with mine. She named him "Dwelling," which means "God dwells with me," and "now my husband shall also dwell with me in love." This demonstrates how the grace of God, in His mercy, would dwell with the poor, corrupted children of Adam’s flesh, and not abandon them in their misery.

6. Furthermore, this refers to the Covenant: that the children of the Covenant, in their Adam-like nature, would only be a "neighboring dwelling" <note>The author uses the term "bywoninge" (by-dwelling) to suggest that while God is present, the physical human nature and the spiritual essence remain distinct neighbors</note> in hope. This means the outward man would not attain the Kingdom of Christ, but would be a dwelling-place where Christ would live in the inward ground—that is, in the Spiritual World—while Adam exists in this temporary time; yet the two would dwell together.

7. For just as the Spirit, through the figure of Judah, had pointed to Christ in the flesh, He now shows here that our outward man would not be Christ Himself, but a dwelling of Christ. Christ would possess the inward ground, just as He said, "My Kingdom is not of this world." Therefore, the outward, mortal man must not say of himself, "I am Christ"; he is merely a dwelling of Christ. This is just as the outward world is nothing other than a dwelling for the Kingdom of Christ; for Christ is the inward Spiritual World, hidden within the outward visible world, just as the day is hidden within the night, and yet one dwells with the other.

## VI The Testament of Issachar.

8. "Issachar shall be a strong-boned donkey <note>original: *gebeenden Esel*; commonly translated in Bibles as a "strong ass"</note>, couching between the borders; and he saw the rest, that it was good, and the land, that it was pleasant; yet he bowed his shoulders to bear, and became a servant under tribute." In this Testament of Issachar, the Spirit first points to the outward figure of this Tribe and where they would live—namely, in the middle of the land in good rest—yet they would still be subject to tribute. However, this powerful figure refers to the inward ground, which is the human nature.

9. For when Leah bore Issachar, she said, "God has rewarded me because I gave my maidservant to my husband," and she named him Issachar, which means a "Divine reward" or "counter-gift." This was because she had given the mandrakes <note>original: *daim*, likely referring to *dodaim*, the Hebrew word for mandrakes</note> of her son to Rachel so that Rachel would let Jacob sleep with her that night, from which she became pregnant with this son; therefore she called him a counter-gift of God.

# Further Explanation of the Testament of Jacob, Chapter 77

...[Issachar] has been, but in the internal figure he says: the human being who is prayed for from God is indeed a gift and a reward, yet his Adam-like nature is nonetheless a **bony, lustful donkey**, who carries the Adam-like sack <note>The "sack" is a recurring metaphor in this text for the heavy burden of earthly, sinful nature and mortality</note>, but he dwells with his mind between the borders—that is, between the Kingdom of God and the kingdom of this world; his mind presses into the boundary markers of God, and the body dwells in this world.

11. Therefore, like a **bony, servant-donkey**, even if it sits in good rest and a dwelling at the borders of God, it must nevertheless carry the burden of sins and of death in the earthly sack. There is no ransoming with *Dudaim* <note>original: "Dudaim"; these are mandrakes, referring to the "love-apples" in Genesis 30 for which Rachel "bought" a night with Jacob from Leah, leading to Issachar's birth</note> for the death of the earthly human, nor does praying to God help to bring the bony donkey through to divine freedom; it must remain a donkey until Christ leads it into Himself into the eternal rest. The damage of Adam is too great; the donkey must leave the sack in the death of Christ, otherwise it is not released from it.

12. But he adds the reason why it must remain a bony donkey, for he says: *he saw that the rest is good, and the land is pleasant*—that is, that the mind would still constantly want to rest in the lust of the flesh and desire to feed the earthly lust. Therefore, the mind had to be a servant-donkey and a servant of the <term>wrath of God</term> <note>In this mystical tradition, the "wrath of God" refers to the harsh, structural forces of nature and law that govern the fallen world</note>, and thus he separates the natural, Adam-like human from the seed of the covenant, which is the person of Christ. The natural, Adam-like human in his innate nature is nothing other than this donkey with the sack, until Christ possesses His Kingdom within him. Neither covenant nor prayer helps there; Adam remains a donkey in this world until the sack is gone; only then is he called a "new child in Christ." This new child is the innermost ground in this time, but the bony donkey is the tool of the new child upon which the sack is carried, for the servitude to the wrath of God lasts as long as the sack is present.

13. > *Dan shall be a judge in his people, as another tribe in Israel. Dan shall be a serpent on the path, and an adder on the way, biting the horse in the heels, so that his rider falls backward. O Lord, I wait for your salvation:*

The Spirit says: *Dan shall be a judge in his people, just as another tribe in Israel.*

17. For the Spirit says: *he shall bite the horse in the heels, so that its Rider falls backward*, that is, he shall bite the horse—which is the office he rides upon—in the heels, which is justice. Thus justice—which is the rider of God that he ought to have carried—falls backward, so that he, as the rider of justice, may rule in the place of justice. Thereupon the rider of justice speaks in his office: "Lord, I wait for your salvation," that is, until you send the true Rider, Christ, who shall ride again over this adder and serpent.

And so she gave him her maidservant Bilhah as a wife, and Jacob lay with her; thus Bilhah became pregnant and bore Jacob a son. Then Rachel spoke: "God has judged my cause, and heard my voice, and given me a son," therefore she named him *Dan*.

### Chapter 77. Further explanation of the Testament of Jacob.

19. This is the powerful figure in the Testament of Jacob, where he prophesies so terrifyingly about *Dan*, that he would become a serpent; and in the true figure, it points to man’s own **self-will** <term>Self-will: (Dutch: *eygen wille*) the human desire to act independently of God's guidance, often described as the root of sin</term>, which will not let itself be governed and led by God, and constantly murmurs against God—just as Rachel grumbled against Jacob because things did not go as she wished, and she tormented Jacob to give her children or else she would die, which made Jacob angry.

20. Thus, the Spirit now presents the figure through Bilha, Rachel’s handmaid, whom she gave to Jacob as a wife. She bore this *Dan* <note>The name Dan means "Judge" in Hebrew</note>, who was to be a judge and an instigator of wrath and strife between Jacob and Rachel, arising from where the self-will in Rachel wanted to have children by force.

21. And this prefigures for us that the worldly office of the judge has its origin in God’s handmaid—that is, in the **kingdom of Nature** <term>Kingdom of Nature: the physical and psychological realm of existence that operates under cause and effect, distinct from the Kingdom of Grace</term>. God did not create man to be under any judicial office; rather, it was the self-murmuring, conflicting will of man—which refuses to obey God and will not be led by His Spirit—that caused *Dan* (the power to judge) to be born in the womb of Rachel, which is to say, in the freedom of Nature.

22. Therefore, in the covenant with Jacob, the Spirit passes such a harsh judgment upon it and says this *Dan*—meaning this judicial office—shall become an adder and a serpent on the path of righteousness. It shall bite the "horse" (which represents the law or the means of progress), in the heels, so that its "rider" (representing justice and the law) falls to the earth. At that point, Nature must wait for God’s salvation—that is, for the justice of Christ through love—whereupon the office of *Dan* shall then cease.

23. This would be well worth considering for you, **Babel** <note>Babel: a term used by the author to describe the "confused" institutionalized churches of his day, which he viewed as spiritually bankrupt</note>, since you boast of Christ. You should consider whether your salvation is truly within you, such that you might judge yourself, rather than needing judges to punish your unrighteousness. In this regard you are no Christian, because you are always grumbling like Rachel and seeking your own will. Therefore, the adder and serpent of *Dan* must sting you, for your own wickedness causes it, being your own self-will. Because of this, God has also placed you under the fallen rider *Dan*, so that you must live as a serf and go about like a tamed horse, stung by the serpent’s poisonous prick—which is the violence of self-appropriated ownership.

24. But the fact that the Rider, *Dan*, must fall backward indicates that this *Dan* and his office shall fall backward in the consciences of Christians when they turn to Christ and do penance. For in penance, the rule of *Dan* ceases; the Rider of God's wrath falls backward. Thus, every Christian is obligated to forgive everything from the heart when penance and the recognition of sins occur, and to cast the office of judge behind them; for the...

the judicial office is the office of sins, which separates right from wrong and always presides over falsehood; but the serpent often bites the horse in the **heels** <note>original: *verslenen*, likely a transcription error for *verzenen* (heels), referencing Genesis 49:17: "Dan shall be a serpent by the way... that biteth the horse heels"</note>, those heels being: favor, prestige, gifts, and bribes. ## VIII. The Testament of Gad.

26. **Gad**, being equipped, shall lead the troop out and lead it back again. Does this figure not prefigure exactly this: that the children of Gad would be mere troop-leaders, just as the children of Dan were not merely judges? Rather, the Spirit presents the spiritual figure which is also seen in Leah, who likewise gave her handmaid to Jacob when she ceased bearing children, wishing to hasten so as to be above Rachel. For *Gad* was born of Zilpah and was intended to get ahead of *Dan*, for she spoke boldly: "turn yourself before him, and back to me" <note>This interprets the name Gad, often translated as "a troop comes" or "good fortune"</note>. This points to **human prudence** <term>Human prudence: (Dutch: *menschelijke voorsigtigheid*) worldly cleverness or "street smarts" used to gain advantage, often contrasted with divine wisdom</term>, which is to say, the cunning and false wisdom that would bypass right and justice with all manner of trickery, exalting itself above all truth and law.

27. For *Gad* and *Dan* are both from the handmaids, and in the figure, they are like a struggle; for Rachel and Leah each wanted to be above the other, therefore their path was one of pure contrariety. This figure stands thus: whenever *Dan* wishes to judge, *Gad* comes with his cunning swiftness and thrusts him out of his office with a pretense of reason, as well as with lies and distortions. For he turns the truth backward and places his swift cunning in the place of the justice of truth; thus the judge becomes blinded by such swiftness.

28. The Spirit powerfully points this out to Israel: how they would live among one another, and how nothing other than **self-violence** with *Dan*, and **cunning** with *Gad*, would rule the world. Yet these both are only children of the handmaids and not of the free woman, and their offices shall come to an end.

He clearly points out what the government on earth would be like when following the self-will of human nature.

This also stems from the struggle between Rachel and Jacob; Rachel spoke when Bilhah her handmaid bore him: "God has judged between me and my sister, I shall prevail over her" <note>Referencing Genesis 30:8. In the mystical sense, this "prevailing" is seen as the human ego trying to outmaneuver others through intellect.</note>. In the figure, this points to the wise reasoning of Naphtali in this office of judge, who could bend and turn all matters so that the **self-will** <term>Self-will: (Dutch: *eygen wille*) the human ego acting independently of God's grace</term> would remain a judge of all things. Thus, no one could bring anything against these four rulers—the sons of the handmaids—for they would hold the government in Israel, rule the world, and win out over all men.

35. Yet all four are merely sons of the handmaids; and Sarah spoke to Abraham: "Cast out the son of the handmaid, for he shall not inherit with my son Isaac" <note>Genesis 21:10. The author uses this to distinguish between worldly authority (the handmaid's sons) and spiritual inheritance (the free woman's son).</note>. And God was pleased with this and commanded Abraham to do the same, indicating that these offices shall not inherit nor remain in the Kingdom of Christ, but shall meet their end. When Christ, being the son of the free woman, takes up His Kingdom, then all these worldly stations shall be excluded, and He alone shall rule in His children and members.

36. You wise, highly learned, and prudent of the world: behold yourselves in this mirror! Look at your wisdom, your eloquence, your favor, power, and honor, and see in what state you sit and whom you serve. Consider your "fat bread" <note>A recurring metaphor for wealth and material success gained through compromise.</note>, as well as the praise of the kings you serve; see what you do and what you intend, and how you stand in your figure before God and the Kingdom of Christ. Your eloquence counts for nothing before God, nor does your wisdom or cunning, if you do not counsel rightly and speak and do the truth. If you do not rightly guide and lead your superiors, then you are merely helping your leaders—those vipers and serpents born in the Testament of Dan—and you yourself are nothing other than the adder and serpent that bites justice and righteousness in the heel. For this, you shall receive the end and reward of the serpent in the fires of hell.

### XI The Testament of Joseph.

37. Joseph shall grow, he shall grow as if by a fountain; the daughters <note>Often interpreted as "branches" in English translations of Genesis 49:22.</note> step forward into the government. And though the archers provoke him, and fight against and persecute him, nonetheless his bow remains firm and the arms of his hands strong through the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob; from Him are the shepherds and stones of Israel <note>Genesis 49:24. A reference to God as the source of strength and the "Rock" or "Stone" of the nation.</note>. By the God of your fathers you are helped, and by the Almighty you are blessed with blessings from heaven above, with blessings of the deep that lies beneath, with blessings of the breasts and of the womb. The blessings of your father prevail more strongly than the blessings of my ancestors, reaching even to the heights of the world; they shall come upon the head of Joseph, and upon the crown of the **Nasir** <term>Nasir: From the Hebrew *Nazir*, meaning one who is "consecrated," "separated," or "crowned" above his brothers.</term> among his brothers.

### Chapter 77. Further explanation of the Testament of Jacob. 347

38. In this Testament of Joseph, the Spirit—within the Covenant—now presents through Jacob the figure of what a true **Divine ruler** is. This is a ruler in whom the Spirit of God reigns; he is not a "son of the handmaid" <note>Referring to the previous discussion where the handmaids' sons symbolized worldly, ego-driven power</note> but a son of the free woman. In his office, he serves God and his brothers; he rules out of truth and justice. He tolerates neither "ear-blowers" <note>Dutch: *oorblasers*, meaning sycophants or flatterers who whisper in a leader's ear</note> nor hypocrites. He seeks no personal gain or honor, but only the glory of God and the service of his brothers. The Spirit has excellently prefigured such a man here through Joseph.

39. For Joseph was not a usurping ruler <note>original: *ingedrongen regent*, one who forces their way into power</note>, but one truly called. This was not because of cunning or clever arguments—as if he could **turn the horse by the tail** <note>A Dutch idiom meaning to manipulate a situation or use deceptive logic to make something appear the opposite of what it is</note> and convince the simple-minded that the tail was the head. Hypocrites say of such deceptive rulers, "Yes, it is indeed the head," simply so they may eat their "fat bread" <note>A reference to worldly prosperity and courtly favors</note> at the palace. He did not sit in the judge’s office through contrived, sharp rhetoric, but through Divine understanding. If he had wished to be a hypocrite or to court favor <note>original: *boeleren*, which can imply illicit passion or compromising oneself for political gain</note>, he could have remained a ruler under Potiphar. But that was not to be; for in him stood the figure of a true **Christian**, showing how such a person should govern their life and their office, and how the good well-spring, Christ, would flow through him to judge and govern.

40. For Jacob began this testament and spoke: *Joseph shall grow; he shall grow like a fountain* <note>Referring to Genesis 49:22. While some translations say "fruitful bough," the Dutch *wassen gelijk aan eene Fontyn* emphasizes the overflowing growth of a spring</note>. This means his wisdom would grow in the power of God and well up out of him, so that he would find wise counsel. Likewise, *the daughters step forward in the government*; that is, his wise words and counsels proceed forth like a daughter in her virginal purity and virtue.

41. Furthermore, although the archers provoke him, fight against him, and persecute him, yet *his bow remains firm and the arms of his hands stay strong through the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob*. This means that although the Devil and his followers assault him and despise him—because he seeks no self-honor or profit—and shoot their arrows at him through false people who bring lies under the appearance of truth, nevertheless his wisdom remains under the Divine arm. His will for justice stands like a firm bow through the indwelling of the Mighty God.

42. Furthermore, *from him have come shepherds and stones in Israel*. This means that from him and his wisdom come other wise, just, and understanding rulers, being faithful counselors who are shepherds and pillars <note>original: *steenen*, literally "stones," here used as "foundation stones" or "pillars of society"</note> in the government alongside him. For it is said: "As the Prince is, so are his counselors." When the counselors see that the prince loves justice and is not served by hypocrisy—that only pious, truthful, and wise people carry weight with him—they also apply themselves to wisdom and justice so that they may please him. In this way, the land has good **shepherds**.

### Further explanation of the Testament of Jacob. Chapter 77 [p. 348]

43. Also: **by the God of your fathers, you are helped, and by the Almighty you are blessed.** That is to say, from the God of Abraham—who helped Abraham—you have received wisdom and understanding. This same God helps you against your enemies and against their arrows. You are blessed by the Almighty with blessings from above from Heaven, with blessings of the deep that lies beneath, with blessings of the breast and of the womb. This means that through the protection of the Lord, you shall receive great honor and sustenance; He shall bless you in body and soul, in property and goods, and in all your ways, and give you enough. Thus, you shall not need cunning nor deceit through perverted laws; you shall not need to say anything out of <term>self-will</term> <note>original: *eygenheyd*; in this spiritual context, it refers to the ego-driven desire to possess things for oneself rather than holding them in trust for God</note>, and yet you shall have much and plenty.

44. For a God-fearing person who abandons self-will receives in exchange everything in the Kingdom of Christ: both Heaven and the World are his. The godless, by contrast, must make do with a mere portion, which he has obtained through nothing but cunning and theft, and brought upon himself through deceit. He takes nothing with him from here but hell itself, his false unrighteousness, and the curse of the miserable people whom he plagued on earth. Those same people have, with their curse, ignited for him the hellish fire, which he takes with him.

45. Also: **the blessings of your father prevail above the blessings of my ancestors, unto the desire of the heights of the world, and they shall come upon the head of Joseph, and on the crown of the head of the Nazirite among his brothers.** That is to say, Jacob’s blessing prevailed more strongly than that of his ancestors because the <term>Essence of faith</term> <note>original: *Ens des geloofs*; "Ens" is a philosophical term meaning the inner being or substance. The author suggests that the spiritual seed of the Covenant has fully sprouted and manifested in Jacob</note> had grown out within him and produced many branches and offshoots. The fruit showed itself more than with Abraham and Isaac; for Abraham produced only one branch from the Line of the Covenant, namely Isaac; likewise, Isaac produced only one branch from the Line of the Covenant, namely Jacob. Thereupon the Spirit—after Jacob had fathered twelve sons who all stood together in the root of the Line of the Covenant and grew from it like branches (though the main stem stood in Judah)—said that his blessing prevailed more strongly, just like a tree that has grown from a single trunk into many branches.

46. But regarding what he says—**unto the desire of the heights of the world**—he is pointing to the bliss of the consecrated blessing. Just as the rich of the world desire nothing but high status and goods, so these people receive, with the blessing of God, both temporal and eternal goods. These shall come through the blessing of Jacob upon the head of Joseph, which is to say, upon his children, so that they shall bear good fruits in this generation; for the "head" indicates the blossom and fruit of this tree.

# Chapter 77. Further explanation of the Testament of Jacob

...only in the blessing stood among the children of Jacob, being the tribe of Judah, but on the crown of the head of the Nazirite <note>original: *Nazireer*; referring to Joseph, who in Genesis 49:26 is called "the one separate from his brothers," a term sharing a root with "Nazirite"</note>, that is on the ground of the natural root of the Adamic tree, in them all, so that they all together should be as one fruitful tree. However, regarding their positions and worldly offices, in which they would live wickedly in the future, he presents the figure through **Dan** and the four brothers from the handmaids, Jacob’s concubines; how finally the serpent would lead the government in the Adamic nature, and how their descendants would live in those offices, and what kind of a world would arise therein, just as has happened among the Jews and Christians.

->XII. The Testament of Benjamin.<-

48. **Benjamin is a ravenous wolf, in the morning he shall devour the prey, but in the evening he shall divide the spoil** <note>Genesis 49:27</note>: Benjamin was the physical brother of Joseph, and yet the Spirit says of him that he is a ravenous wolf who shall devour prey in the morning. In this Testament of Benjamin lies the most hidden figure of the entire scripture, and yet in its outward expression it is the most manifest figure, standing so clearly in its fulfillment that one sees it with physical eyes, and yet the <term>intellect</term> <note>original: *vernuft*; often used by mystical writers to describe human reason that is blind to spiritual truths</note> is entirely blind to it.

49. This figure has been fulfilled, is still in operation, and shall yet be fulfilled; it is very hidden and yet as manifest as the brilliance of the sun by day, and yet it is not understood. But to the **wise men** <note>original: *magis*</note> and the learned it is known, who have indeed written much about it, though never rightly unfolded it, because the time of the evening, when Benjamin’s spoil shall be divided, was still far off; but now it is near. Therefore, we shall draft something here and give the meaning to our own to ponder, and yet remain mute for the unwise, while they sit in the darkness and do nothing but gape their jaws for prey.

50. The two brothers, Joseph and Benjamin, are the image of Christendom and of a Christian human, who stands twofold in his figure: namely, the Adamic human who is Benjamin in his nature, and the new human from the covenant in the Spirit of Christ, pointing to Joseph. And the figure stands thus: how Christ has taken the Adamic human upon Himself, so that this human is half Adamic and half Heavenly, and stands there entirely in one person who cannot be separated.

51. Thus he also prefigures Christendom in this image: how they would accept Christ and become Christians, where Christ and also the evil wolf, Adam, would rule in them; that is, when they would accept the faith, they would be as greedy and zealous as a wolf, and would the...

Thus they would bite in a zeal of the <term>ban</term> <note>original: *bannen*; referring to excommunication or formal ecclesiastical condemnation</note> and the sword. This would happen not because they were acting out of zeal for the Spirit of Christ, but out of the wolf of the evil Adam, who would always exalt himself over the Spirit of Christ in both spiritual and worldly statuses.

52. In this way, their zeal would be nothing other than that of the devouring Wolf, where one would strive more for temporal goods, easy living <note>original: *vette dagen*; literally "fat days," meaning a life of luxury or material comfort</note>, and worldly honor under the name of Christ, rather than for love, truth, and salvation. They would not strive in the power of Christ’s love, but in the [power] of the devouring Wolf. Likewise, in the zeal of their customs—in which they do nothing before God but play the hypocrite—they would devour one another like greedy Wolves. Thus the Wolf would rule outwardly; yet, inwardly in the true children, Christ would rule. Outwardly there is Benjamin, being the natural Adam (who is indeed a Christian, but only after his resurrection when he is released from the Wolf), and inwardly there is Joseph, who is hidden beneath the Wolf.

53. Thus the Spirit of Jacob now points within God’s covenant to the time of how things would go. Namely, in the first era of Christendom, they would be zealous and hunger after God in the Spirit of Christ, and yet they would have to hide themselves and conceal themselves from enemies, just like a Wolf that is hunted as an enemy.

54. It would no longer judge and act in the love of Christ, but whoever would not approve of its <term>belly-order</term> <note>original: *buyk-order*; a derogatory term for religious rules designed to serve the physical appetites or material wealth of the clergy</note>, they would devour with bans, sword, fire, and revenge. They would stir up war for the sake of the name of Christ and their institutions, and would force the nations to the confession of Christ with violence, biting around them like a Wolf, always hunting for prey, though mostly aiming only for the goods and the power of foreign peoples.

### Chapter 77. Further explanation of the Testament of Jacob. 351

[When the] Wolf shall cease, then Benjamin—representing the holy, true Christendom—shall distribute the spoil of Christ, which Christ has snatched away from death and hell.

56. This distribution is yet to come, and has already begun; yet it is not yet fully here, although it truly is already present. In this, the whole world is blind, except for the children of the mystery: the time is here, and is not here; yet it is truly so, that this spoil of Christ—and also the spoil of the Wolf—shall be given and distributed through the hand of Joseph into the hand of Benjamin <note>In this mystical interpretation, Joseph represents Christ, while Benjamin represents the spiritualized humanity or the true Church that receives Christ's inheritance.</note>.

57. Babylon <note>original: *Babel*; used here to signify the corrupt, confused state of worldly systems and institutional churches</note>, let this be a wonder to you, and yet no wonder at all; for you have nothing and see nothing at which you could wonder. It is like a young tree growing from a seed into a great tree that produces much beautiful fruit. One might wonder at the corn or seed—how such a precious tree and so much good fruit were hidden in a single little grain, which was neither recognized nor seen. One does not wonder at it because one has no knowledge other than the fact that it is possible for a tree to grow from a seed; for one does not see how it happens or where the great power was hidden. So it is also at present: one sees the little seed that will become the tree, but human reason <note>original: *vernuft*; referring to limited, earthly intellect that cannot perceive spiritual truths</note> despises it and does not believe that such a tree lies within it, or that so much good fruit would come from it, such that Benjamin's Kingdom at the end of time shall be called a distribution of the spoil.

58. But Joseph must first become a Regent in Egypt; then Benjamin comes to him, and Joseph gives him five changes of clothing and five times more food from the fine table than the others. When the time of scarcity famishes the land and the soul of Jacob hungers, know that God intends to lead Israel into Egypt—that is, into penitence <note>original: *boete*; the author interprets the historical famine in Egypt as a spiritual metaphor for the soul's hunger leading it to repentance</note>. This is then the time of temptation. Benjamin carries his predatory sword in his mouth, but the face of Joseph strikes him so that he falls into great terror and fear of death, because the silver cup of Joseph is found in his sack. Because of this, he is ashamed and lets the predatory sword fall with the teeth of the Wolf. Then Joseph reveals himself to him and all his brothers, and from this arises such joy that the Wolf Benjamin becomes a Lamb, willingly giving up his wool. This is the end of the discourse.

Thus the two went together in one being, namely the **spiritual will** and the **fleshly will**, until the time of Moses; there, the worldly and the spiritual divided into two distinct states.

Through this, Christ was pressed down, and the adder and serpent placed themselves in the judicial office of Christ; for then the Holy Spirit was rejected, and the councils were established in its place, and the Antichrist was born. At that same time, the Spirit of Christ spoke: *Lord, I wait now for your salvation*; for my name must now be the cover for the Antichrist here, until you shall release me again under Joseph's time. In this period, the truth has been violently bitten in the heels, so that the rider in the Spirit of Christ had to fall backward.

8. 67. With Gad, who was to be the leader of the host, begins the time of the universities <note>original: *hoge scholen*; literally "high schools," referring to the academic institutions of the time</note> among the Christians, about 800 years ago. There, the Antichrist—equipped with power and military force—was set upon the throne of Christ. He was defended with boasting, twisting, and disputing, where the tail was made into the head, and the power of Christ was forced into the institutions of men, making a worldly kingdom out of the Kingdom of Christ.

### Chapter 77: Further Explanation of the Testament of Jacob

9. 68. With Asher <note>original: *Affer*; referring to Asher, whose blessing in Genesis 49:20 says "his bread shall be fat."</note> begins the time when the King lived to please the Antichrist, when he became God on earth. Then from the high schools <note>referring to the universities and centers of scholastic learning</note> came the hypocrites who flattered this King for the "fat bread"—namely, for good offices, prebends <note>a stipend or portion of revenues granted to a member of a cathedral</note>, and bishoprics. They praised his every deed and did everything to please him, setting Christ and the Antichrist on the same soft cushion, and thus they worshiped the image in the Apocalypse <note>original: *Apocalypsi*; the Book of Revelation</note>, about six hundred years ago and later.

10. 69. With Naphtali begins the time of great wonders, when men dealt with high reasons and deep-seated thoughts regarding the counsel of God. When it was seen that this man, sitting upon the throne of Christ, was not Christ in power, men searched deeply to hang a cloak around him with beautiful, respectable syllogisms <note>original: *Sluytredenen*</note>. Then sharp Logic <note>original: *Logica*</note> arose, through which men disputed. One party said he was Christ in power and might; the other spoke against them. Yet that party and its followers, with a high appearance of sanctity, placed him in the blood of Christ and attributed all power to him, fashioning holy arguments from it. Here, the Spirit of Christ in the inward ground opposed this and said he was the Antichrist; this time has lasted until our own day, in which we live.

11. 70. With Joseph begins the time when Christ is revealed again, where he terrifies and casts down the serpent and adder, Dan <note>In Jacob's blessing, Dan is called "a serpent in the way" (Gen 49:17). In medieval and early modern theology, Dan was often associated with the tribe of the Antichrist.</note>, along with the Antichristian throne and all its power and self-interest, from the Kingdom of Christ on earth. Then Joseph's brothers must be ashamed of the great unfaithfulness they showed toward Joseph, since they threw him into the pit and, moreover, sold him for money. There, all cunning, hypocrisy, and false deceit are made manifest and are cast down by the present face of Joseph; and that is the time of which it is said: "She is fallen, she is fallen, Babylon <note>original: *Babilon*</note>, and has become a dwelling of all devils, and of all loathsome animals and birds." And there Joseph grows in his power, and his daughters <note>A reference to the "branches" or "daughters" (Gen 49:22) of Joseph's fruitful vine.</note> step forth in beauty, and his blessing begins.

12. 71. With Benjamin, the time of the evening begins (during Joseph’s time), for there he shall again distribute the spoil of the first Christianity. He belongs to the first and the last time, especially in the first time of Joseph when Christ begins to reveal himself; thus, at first, he was ready like a wolf and ate far around him when he began to bite and devour the Antichrist. Yet he was still a wolf at that time; but when the face of Joseph is uncovered, he too is ashamed, like a wolf that is captured, and begins to become a lamb and to give his fat wool.

# CHAPTER 78

->*Of the Burial of the Holy Patriarch Jacob in the Land of Canaan, and what is to be understood by it.*<-

<margin>Gen. 50.</margin>
<margin>1.</margin>
The burial of Jacob—the fact that Joseph should lead him back into Canaan after his death and bury him with his fathers, and that Joseph journeyed there with a great army, with all the children of Israel and many Egyptians—prefigures for us the mighty exodus of Christ out of this world. There, the Adamic man <note>The human soul in its fallen state, following the pattern of Adam</note> after his death shall be led out of this Egyptian house of misery back into his first Fatherland in Paradise, where Christ shall lead him in.

<margin>2.</margin>
But the fact that many Egyptians also journeyed with them and accompanied Joseph indicates that Christ, when He shall lead His bride <note>The Church or the soul</note> home into Paradise, shall have many strangers with Him. These are those who in this time did not recognize Him according to His Person and Office, and yet grew up in Him through His Love; all of these shall enter into Paradise with Christ and dwell with Him.

<margin>3.</margin>
Their mourning and weeping indicates the eternal joy which they shall receive in Paradise, just as *Magia* <term>Magia: The divine creative power or the spiritual will that brings internal realities into outward forms</term> always prefigures joy through mourning and weeping. This grave-sign, and what is to be understood by it, was explained previously in the account of Abraham.

<margin>4.</margin>

# Chapter 78. Of Jacob’s burial in the Land of Canaan.

[the brothers saw] that their father was dead, and said, "Joseph might be angry with us, and repay all the evil that we have done to him." Therefore they sent word to him, saying, "Your father commanded before his death, and spoke: 'Thus shall you say to Joseph: Please, forgive your brothers the offense and their sins, for they did so poorly toward you.' Please, now forgive the offense of us, the servants of the God of your father." But Joseph wept when they spoke this with him, and his brothers went and fell down before him and spoke, "Behold, we are your servants." Joseph spoke to them: "Fear not, for I am under God <note>original: "ik ben onder God"; a rendering of the biblical phrase usually translated as "Am I in the place of God?"</note>. You intended to do evil to me, but God intended to make it good, as He did on this day, to preserve many people. Therefore, do not fear now; I shall provide for you and your children." And he comforted them, and spoke kindly to them.

5. This Figure <term>Figure: In traditional biblical interpretation, a "figure" or "type" is an Old Testament person or event that serves as a prophetic symbol or blueprint for a New Testament reality, specifically Christ.</term> is a mighty comfort for the brothers of Joseph; however, since Joseph stands in the image of Christ, and his brothers in the figure of the poor converted sinner, we must also interpret this figure thus: namely, when the poor sinful person, who has committed great sins, has turned toward repentance and received grace, yet now and then commits a fault again, he stands constantly in fear and trembling before the grace of God. He thinks that God will again account the first committed sins to him and take occasion from this new fault. Because of this, he stands in great anxiety and begins again to confess the first committed sins, and falls anew at the Lord’s feet, and enters again into earnest repentance, and bewails his first misdeed, just as David did when he said: *Lord, do not account to me the sins of my youth.* <note>Psalm 25:7</note>

6. But with such new repentance and earnest lamentation, when the poor person shows himself again so completely earnestly and so humbly before God, the Heavenly Joseph <note>The author uses "Heavenly Joseph" as a title for Jesus Christ, emphasizing his role as the one who provides for and forgives his "brothers" (humanity).</note> is moved to such great mercy—just as Joseph was here—that he comforts the poor soul in its conscience. He tells the soul not to fear, for its committed sins shall not only be withheld from its account, but shall even serve for its ultimate good, just as Joseph said: "You intended to do evil, but God intended to make good through it." Thus, in Christ, God not only forgives the humble person for committed sins, but He also provides for him and his children with temporal blessings and sustenance, turning everything for the best, just as Joseph did for his brothers.

Finally, Joseph desired by an oath that when he came to die, they should carry his bones with them out of Egypt to his fathers; which points out to us the oath of God in Paradise: that Christ, God and man, would come again to his brothers and remain eternally with them, and [be] their High Prie-
